title: [Immo] E0 — Discovery & Open Decisions [~3-5 days]
description:
Resolve the six choices that materially change the architecture before building.

**Why:** Each decision branches the design (payments module, auth scope, locales/RTL, static-vs-hybrid rendering, DB ops model, map-tile source). Building before deciding risks expensive rework.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] All six decisions recorded as closed decision beads with rationale
- [ ] Downstream epics (E12 payments, E13 i18n, E15 DB, E11 maps) updated to match

**Spec:** §16, §9, §10
close_reason: all steps complete

title: 0.5 Decide DB ops: self-host Postgres on Hetzner vs managed (Neon/Supabase)
description:
Choose the database operations model given Hetzner has no managed DB.

**Why:** Main operational trade-off of the Hetzner choice; shapes E15.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Decision recorded with ops/cost trade-off; E15 DB tasks updated

**Spec:** §11, §16
close_reason: ADR 0.5 at docs/decisions/00-5-db-ops.md: Self-host Postgres on Hetzner co-located with Phoenix, pgBackRest/WAL-G backups to Hetzner Object Storage. Managed Neon (Frankfurt) as pre-approved escape hatch.

title: 0.1 Decide payments model: B2B subscriptions vs consumer transactions (Stripe vs CMI/Morocco)
description:
Choose who pays and for what, and the provider mix.

**Why:** Drives the entire E12 payments module design and adapter shape.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Model chosen (B2B subscriptions and/or consumer txns)
- [ ] Primary provider chosen (Stripe) + Morocco fallback (CMI/PayZone) confirmed for the legal entity

**Spec:** §10, §16
close_reason: ADR 0.1 at docs/decisions/00-1-payments-model.md: B2B subscription-led, domestic-first (CMI/PayZone primary, Stripe secondary for international). No consumer payments at launch.

title: 0.4 Estimate catalog scale (launch + 2-3yr) -> static vs hybrid
description:
Estimate number of projects/listings now and in 2-3 years.

**Why:** Decides whether E17 hybrid on-demand rendering is ever needed or we stay fully static.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Rough page counts documented; rendering strategy (full-static now) confirmed
- [ ] Threshold defined for when to trigger E17

**Spec:** §5, §16
close_reason: ADR 0.4 at docs/decisions/00-4-catalog-scale.md: Full-static Astro SSG now; E17 hybrid trigger defined (>~50k pages / >15min build / >10min publish latency).

title: 0.3 Decide launch locales & RTL scope (FR / AR / EN)
description:
Pick the locales shipped at launch; Arabic implies RTL theming work.

**Why:** Sizes the E13 i18n epic and the theme layer.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Launch locales fixed; RTL in/out of launch scope decided

**Spec:** §7, §16
close_reason: Decision recorded in docs/decisions/00-3-locales-rtl.md. Launch FR+EN (LTR), French primary; Arabic/RTL deferred to fast-follow Phase 2 but built RTL-ready (Tailwind logical properties, dir-aware, locale-aware data model, Arabic font pre-chosen). Routing: Astro native URL path-prefix i18n with prefixDefaultLocale:true + hreflang/x-default. Amazigh out of scope.

title: 0.6 Decide map tiles: PMTiles on R2 vs hosted provider
description:
Choose serverless PMTiles on R2 (cheap) vs a hosted tile provider (turnkey styles).

**Why:** Shapes E11 maps and R2 usage.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Tile source chosen; E11 task updated

**Spec:** §8, §16
close_reason: ADR 0.6 at docs/decisions/00-6-map-tiles.md: PMTiles on Cloudflare R2 (Morocco vector basemap, MapLibre GL JS). MapTiler as escape hatch.

title: 0.2 Decide public visitor accounts vs inquiry-form-only
description:
Decide whether visitors get logins (saved searches/favorites) or just submit lead forms.

**Why:** Determines whether we build token-based public auth (E2/E5) or skip it.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Decision recorded; auth scope for E2/E5 set accordingly

**Spec:** §9, §16
close_reason: ADR 0.2 at docs/decisions/00-2-visitor-accounts.md: No public visitor accounts at launch. Inquiry-form-only + anonymous localStorage favorites. Phone/WhatsApp-OTP accounts deferred.

title: P4-E4.5 §15.4 e2e: edit published → ssr-dirty ≤ 2 min; unpublish → 404 ≤ 2 min and still 404 post-build; slug change → old URL 301; manual rebuild → headers flip to static
description:
## Why
- This is the epic's Definition of Done (§16 P4-E4 AC): the §15.4 edit/unpublish/slug-301 scenarios green, and headers flipping back to `static` after the next build. It proves R3 end-to-end on staging — including the §3.1 claim that B/C pages collapse back to A automatically after a successful build — and completes the freshness state machine coverage started by P4-E2.4.

## What
On the P4-E2.4 Playwright harness vs staging (§15.4 scenarios):
- **Edit published listing** → page reflects the edit with `x-immo-serving: ssr-dirty` within 2 min; response also carries `cache-control: no-store` (§3.4 state-C headers).
- **Unpublish** → 404 within 2 min; then trigger a rebuild; **still 404 after the build** (no ghost static page — R3's unpublish clause both pre- and post-build).
- **Slug change** → old URL returns 301 to the new path (redirects row + dirty old path + Worker/SSR consultation from P4-E3.3/P4-E4.3).
- **Trigger manual rebuild** (Rebuild-now / `trigger=manual`) → both test pages flip to `x-immo-serving: static` with content correct.

## Out of scope
- §15.4 "plus" list (search facets from custom fields, map bbox, inquiry/Turnstile, AR RTL) — P5/P7/P8 scope; scenario 1 (publish-new) already shipped in P4-E2.4 and stays in the suite.
design:
- Reuses the P4-E2.4 Playwright harness (deadline polling, x-immo-serving asserts, content lifecycle fixtures) against staging
- State-C expectations (§3.4): cache-control: no-store + x-immo-serving: ssr-dirty; post-build expectation: static
- Manual rebuild via Rebuild-now / RebuildSite trigger=manual (P3-E2.1) to make the headers-flip assertion deterministic
- 2 min deadlines per §15.4; KV ~60 s eventual consistency budgeted inside the window (§3.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- Edit published listing -> page reflects the edit with x-immo-serving: ssr-dirty within <= 2 min (§15.4)
- Unpublish -> 404 within <= 2 min; trigger rebuild; STILL 404 after the build (no ghost static page) (§15.4)
- Old URL after slug change -> 301 with correct Location (§15.4)
- Trigger manual rebuild -> previously-SSR pages flip to x-immo-serving: static with content correct (§15.4 + §16 P4-E4 AC "after next build headers flip to static")
- State-C SSR responses carry cache-control: no-store (§3.4)
- Suite green vs staging and wired into CI per §12.3
notes: Spec: §15.4 scenarios 2-4 (verbatim), §16 P4-E4 AC, §3.4 headers. Open decisions: D2 — under the default (ship C at launch) this suite is launch-gating; if C were deferred, it defines the regression to re-enable. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E4.4 RebuildSite re-arm step (real): re-PUT dirty keys for everything changed since last SUCCESSFUL build (self-healing after failed builds) + KV eventual-consistency ~60 s documented as accepted (§3.5)
description:
## Why
- §3.2 step 3, self-healing: a **failed** build means changed content is NOT baked, while the dirty markers protecting those pages keep aging toward TTL expiry (`FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS` = 2× interval). Without re-arming, one failed build + a quiet period = stale statics serving again with no signal — exactly the §14 silent failure mode, now on the R3 path.
- Re-PUTting markers for everything changed since the last **successful** build on every RebuildSite run guarantees changed pages keep serving fresh SSR until a build actually succeeds. Combined with BuildAgeMonitor (P3-E3), failures are both *survived* (this task) and *alerted* (the monitor).

## What
- Replace the P3-E1.2 placeholder with the real step 3: for every record changed since the last successful `content_snapshot_at` (published scope; plus pending redirects' old paths), recompute the public path set via `Immo.Edge.Paths` (§3.5) and re-PUT KV dirty keys via the P4-E4.2 machinery (TTL refreshed).
- Runs before the deploy-hook POST in the §3.2 sequence; no-ops when the skip-if-unchanged path is taken.
- Document **KV eventual consistency (~60 s) as accepted** (§3.5): an edit may serve the stale static at some edge for up to a minute; the stricter alternative (Worker calling `GET /api/v1/internal/freshness?path=` with a 30 s edge cache) stays documented on standby, **not in v1**. Add the editor-facing note (§18 row 3: admin "view live" cache-bust note).
- Tests: simulate failed build → next run re-PUTs the changed set (mocked CF HTTP); successful-build baseline → no spurious re-arms.

## Out of scope
- The `/internal/freshness` consistency upgrade itself (P9 backlog per §3.5/§16); ConfirmBuild semantics (P3-E1.3, unchanged).
design:
- Position: step 3 of the §3.2 RebuildSite algorithm, replacing the P3-E1.2 placeholder, executed before the deploy-hook POST
- Changed set: published-scope records with updated_at > last successful content_snapshot_at (+ pending redirects)
- Re-PUT via the same MarkPathsDirty/mark_dirty machinery — TTL refreshed to FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS so markers outlive consecutive failed builds
- Self-healing rationale (§3.2 step 3): if a previous build FAILED, changed pages keep serving fresh SSR instead of reverting to stale statics when their original markers TTL-expire
- Doc note feeds §18 row 3 mitigation (admin view-live cache-bust note + documented <= 60 s window)
acceptance_criteria:
- After a failed build, the next RebuildSite run re-PUTs dirty keys for ALL records changed since the last SUCCESSFUL content_snapshot_at (simulated failed build in tests, mocked CF HTTP)
- Re-arm path sets come from Immo.Edge.Paths (identical to API paths per the P4-E4.1 property tests)
- Skip-if-unchanged path is unaffected: a quiet run re-arms nothing and still records skipped
- Pending redirects old paths are included in the re-arm set
- KV eventual consistency ~60 s documented as accepted in /docs (editor-facing note: saved changes may show stale at some edge for up to a minute), with the §3.5 GET /api/v1/internal/freshness alternative recorded as on-standby (not v1)
notes: Spec: §3.2 step 3, §3.5 (TTL semantics + eventual-consistency paragraph). Risk register: §18 row 2 (failed builds must not strand stale pages) + row 3 (editor confusion over the ~60 s window). Replaces the placeholder from P3-E1.2. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E4.3 Catalog trigger points (after successful Repo transaction): edit-published → mark paths; unpublish/delete → mark (SSR gets 404 → no-store 404); publish-new → mark parent-project paths; slug change → mark old path + insert redirects row (§3.8)
description:
## Why
- These triggers ARE R3's user-visible behavior: edit → fresh page within ~a minute; unpublish/delete → instant 404 with no ghost page; new unit → parent project page stops missing it; slug change → old URL 301s. Without them the KV layer is plumbing with no water.
- §3.5 fixes the discipline: fire **in context functions, after the successful Repo transaction** — a rolled-back write must never dirty an edge path, and a committed write must never skip its marks.

## What
Wire `Immo.Catalog` publish-state/content transitions (§6.1) to `MarkPathsDirty` per the §3.5 trigger list:
- **Update of a published record** → `mark_dirty(paths(record), record.updated_at)`.
- **Unpublish / delete of a published record** → same (the SSR catch-all will get an API 404 → renders the 404 page with `no-store`, P4-E2.2).
- **Publish of a new record** → no KV write needed for its own path (state B works by asset miss) — **but mark the parent-project paths anyway**, since the parent's static page now misses a unit.
- **Slug change** → mark the **old** path dirty **and** insert a `redirects` row (`old_path`, `new_path`, 301 — §3.8/§5.11); pairs with the Worker/SSR consultation from P4-E3.3 so the old URL 301s immediately.
- Enqueue atomically with the commit (Oban job in the same transaction/Multi) so "after successful Repo transaction" holds under concurrency.

## Out of scope
- Path computation (P4-E4.1) and the PUT mechanics (P4-E4.2); admin slug-lock UI (P1-E3); payment-driven unpublish sweeps (P6-E2 — reuses these triggers).
design:
- Placement (§3.5): in Immo.Catalog context functions, after successful Repo transaction — enqueue the Oban job atomically with the write (job inserted in the same transaction/Ecto.Multi so it runs only on commit)
- Paths exclusively from Immo.Edge.Paths (P4-E4.1 single authority); ts = record.updated_at as unix seconds
- redirects row per §5.11: old_path citext unique, new_path, http_status default 301, reason; slug immutability + admin override per §3.8 is the entry point
- Unpublish flow end state: dirty mark -> Worker SSR -> API 404 (published predicate §5.13) -> no-store 404 (P4-E2.2 contract)
- Billing-driven unpublish (P6 dunning sweep §11) later reuses these same trigger functions
acceptance_criteria:
- Edit of a published listing enqueues MarkPathsDirty with its per-locale detail paths + parent-project paths and ts = updated_at
- Unpublish/delete of a published record marks its paths; subsequent SSR fetch gets API 404 -> real 404 page with no-store (verified at the route level)
- Publish of a NEW record marks parent-project paths only (own detail page is state B by asset miss — no own-path KV write needed)
- Slug change inserts a redirects row (old_path unique, new_path, 301) AND marks the old path dirty (§3.8)
- No marks are enqueued when the transaction fails/rolls back; draft (never-published) edits mark nothing
- Context tests cover all four trigger classes including the developer_user role path
notes: Spec: §3.5 trigger points (all four bullets), §3.8, §5.11, §5.13, §6.1. Open decisions: D2 (these triggers ARE the launch-blocking R3 behavior under the default). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E4.2 Immo.Edge.Freshness.mark_dirty(paths, ts) → CF KV REST PUT (key path:<normalized: lowercase, no trailing slash, no query>, value unix seconds, expiration_ttl=FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS default 7200=2× interval) + MarkPathsDirty Oban job (max_attempts 8, backoff) using CF_ACCOUNT_ID/CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID/CF_KV_API_TOKEN (write-only scoped token)
description:
## Why
- The write side of state C (§3.5): Phoenix marks changed paths dirty in the FRESHNESS namespace; the Worker (P4-E3.1) reads them and bypasses stale statics. R3's "fresh version immediately" is exactly as reliable as these writes — hence a real Oban job with `max_attempts: 8` + backoff, never inline best-effort HTTP inside the request cycle.
- Least-privilege per §10.1 trust path 4: the CF API token is scoped to this single KV namespace, **write-only**, separately rotatable — a leaked token cannot read data or touch anything else.

## What
- `Immo.Edge.Freshness.mark_dirty(paths, ts)`: Cloudflare REST `PUT /accounts/:acct/storage/kv/namespaces/:ns/values/:key?expiration_ttl=:ttl` per path (§3.5).
  - Key: `path:<normalized public path>` (e.g. `path:/fr/projects/casablanca/les-jardins-anfa`); normalization: lowercase, no trailing slash, no query.
  - Value: integer **unix seconds** of the change (`updated_at`).
  - TTL: `FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS` (default **7200** = 2× default rebuild interval). TTL is cleanup only; correctness comes from `dirty_at > built_at`.
- `MarkPathsDirty` Oban job (queue `default`, `max_attempts: 8`, backoff per §6.5) wrapping `mark_dirty`; args = path set + ts; idempotent (re-PUT of same key/value is harmless).
- Config/env: `CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID`, `CF_KV_API_TOKEN` (§12.4); per-environment namespace (prod/staging §3.5); token redacted from logs (§10.1 rules).
- Tests with mocked CF HTTP (§15.1): exact key/value/TTL emitted; retry on 5xx; multi-path batch behavior.

## Out of scope
- When to call it (P4-E4.3 trigger points); re-arm batching (P4-E4.4); Worker reads (P4-E3.1).
design:
- Endpoint (§3.5): PUT /accounts/:acct/storage/kv/namespaces/:ns/values/:key?expiration_ttl=:ttl on the Cloudflare REST API
- Key format: path:<normalized public path> — normalization from Edge.Paths (P4-E4.1): lowercase, no trailing slash, no query
- Value: integer unix seconds of the change (record updated_at) — the Worker multiplies by 1000 and compares against builtAt ms (§3.4)
- TTL: FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS env, default 7200 = 2x default rebuild interval; TTL is CLEANUP ONLY — correctness comes from the dirty_at > built_at comparison (§3.5)
- Oban: queue default, max_attempts: 8, backoff (§6.5 row MarkPathsDirty); namespace per environment (prod/staging, §3.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- PUT issues key path:<normalized>, body value = integer unix seconds of the change (updated_at), query expiration_ttl = FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS (default 7200)
- MarkPathsDirty (queue default) retries up to max_attempts 8 with backoff on CF API failure (§6.5)
- One job invocation can mark a full path set (e.g. listing edit = per-locale detail + parent-project paths)
- Credentials from CF_ACCOUNT_ID / CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID / CF_KV_API_TOKEN; token scoped to the single KV namespace, WRITE-ONLY (§10.1 path 4); token never logged (Logger redaction)
- Job tests green with mocked CF HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test, §15.1): success, 5xx retry, key/value/TTL format assertions
notes: Spec: §3.5 (writer + key/value/TTL contract), §6.5 row MarkPathsDirty, §10.1 trust path 4, §12.4 (CF_* vars + FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS). Risk register: §18 row 3 (KV eventual consistency ~60 s — documented in P4-E4.4). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E4.1 Harden Immo.Edge.Paths as the single path authority (listing → per-locale detail + parent-project paths; project → own paths; developer → own paths; category pages NOT marked §3.6) + property tests: KV keys ≡ API path fields ALWAYS agree
description:
## Why
- §15.1 flags `Edge.Paths` as **correctness-critical**: KV keys and API `path` fields must always agree. A divergence means `mark_dirty` PUTs a key the Worker never looks up — the visitor silently sees the stale static page: an R3 violation with **no error signal anywhere** (worse than a crash).
- One module computes paths for the read API (§6.3 `path` per locale), the sitemap, and KV marking — hardening it here is what makes the whole state-C write side trustworthy.

## What
- `Immo.Edge.Paths.for(record)` per §3.5:
  - **published listing** → its detail path **per locale** + its **parent project's** detail paths per locale (project pages embed unit lists), and nothing else;
  - **project** → its own paths per locale;
  - **developer** → developer paths per locale;
  - **category/index pages are NOT marked** (§3.6: static, ≤ interval lag accepted; instant cards = D4 config flip, not KV marks).
- Normalization shared and exact (§3.5): lowercase, no trailing slash, no query — byte-identical to the Worker `normalize()` (P4-E3.1).
- **Property tests** (§15.1): for arbitrary published records (generated i18n slugs, locales, `url_segment` variants, city values, with/without parent project), `Paths.for(record)` ≡ the `path` fields the API serializers emit. Wire API serializers to call this module so agreement is structural.

## Out of scope
- The KV PUT itself (P4-E4.2); triggers (P4-E4.3); frontend `paths.ts` builders (§4 — kept in lockstep via the OpenAPI `path` field, not duplicated logic).
design:
- Single authority (§6.3 response conventions): path is computed server-side by Immo.Edge.Paths, shared by the read API AND KV marking — one module, zero forks
- Listing detail path shape per §7.1: /{locale prefix}/{type url_segment for locale}/{city}/{slug} (fr at root); project paths /projets/[city]/[slug]; developer paths /promoteurs/[slug]
- Parent-project inclusion rationale (§3.5): project pages embed unit lists, so a listing change dirties its project pages too
- Property-based tests (StreamData) per §15.1: Edge.Paths is correctness-critical — KV keys and API path fields must always agree
- Shared normalization function: lowercase, strip trailing slash, strip query (§3.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- Published listing yields its detail path per locale + its parent-project detail paths per locale, and nothing else; standalone listing (project_id null) yields no project paths
- Project yields its own per-locale paths; developer yields developer per-locale paths
- Category/index/landing paths are never emitted (§3.6 policy)
- Property tests prove Paths.for(record) output ≡ the path fields emitted by the API serializers for arbitrary records (i18n slugs, url_segment per locale, city variations) — §15.1
- Normalization matches §3.5 exactly: lowercase, no trailing slash, no query — and matches the Worker normalize() (P4-E3.1)
- API serializers call Immo.Edge.Paths directly; any duplicate path-building code is removed
notes: Spec: §3.5 path computation bullet, §3.6, §6.3 path field, §7.1, §15.1 (correctness-critical). A mismatch = dirty mark on a key the Worker never reads = silent stale page (R3 violation, no error signal). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P4-E4 — State C: KV dirty layer + redirects (edits/unpublish instant, R3)
description:
## Why
- Serves **R3**: when existing published content is edited, visitors must see the fresh version from the API **immediately** (stale static bypassed), and unpublished content must **immediately 404**, not linger as a ghost static page. After the next scheduled build the page is served statically again.
- State C in the freshness model (§3.1): static asset exists but a KV dirty marker is newer than `built_at` → the Worker (P4-E3) bypasses the stale file and SSRs. This epic builds the **write side**: the single path authority, the KV writer, the catalog trigger points, the RebuildSite re-arm (self-healing, §3.2 step 3), and the slug-change/redirects flow (§3.8).
- §3.9 deliberately ships this last: the most complex piece, isolated behind the working A+B baseline. D2 default says it ships **before launch**.

## What
- `Immo.Edge.Paths` hardened as the single path authority + property tests (KV keys ≡ API `path` fields, §15.1 correctness-critical).
- `Immo.Edge.Freshness.mark_dirty(paths, ts)` → Cloudflare KV REST PUT; `MarkPathsDirty` Oban job (max_attempts 8, backoff) using `CF_ACCOUNT_ID`/`CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID`/`CF_KV_API_TOKEN` (write-only scoped token).
- Catalog trigger points after successful Repo transactions: edit-published / unpublish-delete / publish-new (parent-project paths) / slug change (+ `redirects` row).
- RebuildSite re-arm step made real: re-PUT dirty keys for everything changed since the last SUCCESSFUL build.
- §15.4 e2e: edit → ssr-dirty; unpublish → 404 (and still 404 post-build); slug → 301; manual rebuild → headers flip to static.

## Out of scope
- Worker-side KV reads (P4-E3.1, already shipped dormant); category/index page marking (§3.6 — explicitly not marked); the `/internal/freshness` consistency upgrade (§3.5 alternative — P9 backlog).
design:
- KV contract (§3.5): namespace FRESHNESS per env; key path:<normalized public path> (lowercase, no trailing slash, no query); value integer unix seconds of the change; TTL FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS = 2x rebuild interval (default 7200) — TTL is cleanup only, correctness comes from dirty_at > built_at
- Writer: Immo.Edge.Freshness.mark_dirty(paths, ts) -> CF REST PUT /accounts/:acct/storage/kv/namespaces/:ns/values/:key?expiration_ttl=:ttl, from Oban job MarkPathsDirty (max_attempts 8)
- Path computation (§3.5): listing -> per-locale detail + parent-project paths; project -> own paths; developer -> own paths; category/index pages NOT marked (§3.6)
- Trigger points (§3.5): edit-published, unpublish/delete, publish-new (parent paths), slug change (+ redirects row §3.8) — in context functions after successful Repo transaction
- KV eventual consistency ~60 s accepted; /api/v1/internal/freshness alternative documented on standby (§3.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- §15.4 e2e scenarios green on staging: edit published -> ssr-dirty <= 2 min; unpublish -> 404 <= 2 min and still 404 after rebuild; slug change -> old URL 301 (§16 P4-E4 AC)
- After the next build, headers flip back to x-immo-serving: static (§16 AC)
- Edge.Paths property tests prove KV keys and API path fields ALWAYS agree (§15.1)
- MarkPathsDirty writes key path:<normalized>, value unix seconds, expiration_ttl=FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS (default 7200) with max_attempts 8
- RebuildSite re-arm re-PUTs dirty keys for everything changed since the last SUCCESSFUL build (self-healing after failed builds)
notes: Spec: §3.5 ENTIRE, §3.8, §3.2 step 3, §5.11, §15.1, §15.4, §16 P4-E4 (deps: P4-E3). Open decisions: D2 (ship state C at launch = default YES; if deferred, unpublish lag is the main risk -> interim manual-rebuild stopgap). Risk register: §18 rows 2, 3. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E3.4 Routing-matrix unit tests (state A/B/C × content/non-content paths) + staging chaos test: kill API ⇒ stale-fallback on built pages
description:
## Why
- The Worker entry is pure routing logic guarding R1/R2/R3 simultaneously — a regression here silently mis-serves the whole site (wrong state, stale content, or origin hammering). §16 P4-E3 AC demands the routing matrix be unit-tested and the outage behavior proven by actually killing the staging API.
- Pinning every state transition in tests is what makes later refactors (adapter upgrades, route-variant changes) safe.

## What
- **Unit tests** (frontend test stack, mocked Worker env — ASSETS.fetch, FRESHNESS.get, astroHandler):
  - State A: asset hit + (no marker | marker older than build) → static, no SSR call.
  - State B: asset miss → SSR (explicit "asset 404 falls through to SSR" case).
  - State C: asset hit + marker newer than build → SSR, asset bypassed.
  - SSR throw + asset exists → stale-fallback (200, header set, even when dirty).
  - SSR throw + no asset → 503 with retry-after: 120.
  - Redirect hit → 301 before any asset lookup.
  - Non-content path → assets first, then SSR; CSS/JS/font globs never enter the content branch.
  - Build-info + redirects memoization (60 s window).
- **Staging chaos test:** stop staging Phoenix (or sever the tunnel) → built pages return 200 with `x-immo-serving: stale-fallback`; never-built paths return 503. Document the procedure (consumed by the "site serving stale" runbook, P4-E5.1).

## Out of scope
- Freshness e2e via real publishes (P4-E2.4, P4-E4.5); load testing (§15.5/P8-E3).
design:
- Mock env: ASSETS.fetch (hit/404), FRESHNESS.get (null | older | newer than built_at), astroHandler (ok | throw)
- Matrix dimensions: asset hit|miss x dirty none|older|newer x ssr ok|throw x path content|non-content|redirect-hit
- Expected outcomes pinned per §3.4: A -> static; B -> SSR; C -> SSR; SSR throw + asset -> stale-fallback; SSR throw + no asset -> 503 retry-after 120; redirect -> 301 before assets; non-content -> assets then SSR
- Chaos: stop staging Phoenix (or sever the tunnel) -> request a built page marked dirty -> expect 200 + stale-fallback
acceptance_criteria:
- Routing-matrix unit tests green: states A/B/C x content/non-content paths, plus error branches and redirect ordering (§16 P4-E3 AC)
- Explicit test: asset 404 falls through to SSR (§16 AC)
- Chaos test on staging: killing the API yields x-immo-serving: stale-fallback (HTTP 200) on built pages (§16 AC)
- Memoization tested: /__build.json and redirects.json fetched at most once per 60 s window
- Tests run in CI (frontend Vitest step, §12.3); chaos procedure documented for reuse in the P4-E5.1 runbook
notes: Spec: §16 P4-E3 AC, §3.4, §3.7, §12.3 CI. Chaos procedure feeds the site-serving-stale runbook (P4-E5.1). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E3.3 redirects.json: build-time export from GET /redirects + Worker consultation before asset lookup (single mechanism for static AND SSR, §3.8)
description:
## Why
- §3.8: slug changes must redirect **immediately** (301 served the moment the row exists, via the SSR path) and **permanently** (exported into every subsequent static deployment). One mechanism — the Worker consulting `redirects.json` before asset lookup — covers requests in any page state, static or SSR.
- Serves R3 (an old slug never lingers as a ghost page) and R8 (clean URLs with SEO-correct 301s; link equity preserved).

## What
- **Build-time export:** during `astro build`, fetch `GET /redirects` (build tier, §6.3 — active redirects for the build-time redirects.json) and emit `redirects.json` into the publish dir (§3.8 `_redirects`-equivalent).
- **Worker consultation:** load `redirects.json` via `env.ASSETS.fetch` (memoized alongside build info); in the content-path branch, check the normalized path **before asset lookup**; on hit return `Response` with `http_status` (default 301, §5.11) + `Location: new_path`.
- **Immediate path (pre-build):** the SSR catch-all consults redirects via the API on record-miss (§3.8 "the SSR catch-all consults redirects (via API) to serve 301 immediately") — activates fully once P4-E4.3 inserts rows and marks the old path dirty.
- Path matching uses the same normalization as §3.5 KV keys (lowercase, no trailing slash, no query).

## Out of scope
- Writing redirects rows + marking old paths dirty on slug change (P4-E4.3); admin slug-lock/override UI (P1-E3 scope per §6.2); e2e slug-301 (P4-E4.5).
design:
- Source: GET /redirects build-tier endpoint (§6.3) -> rows old_path citext unique, new_path, http_status default 301, reason (§5.11)
- Export: generated redirects.json in the publish dir (the _redirects-equivalent of §3.8), loaded in the Worker via env.ASSETS.fetch and memoized like build info
- Ordering: redirect consult happens before asset lookup in the content-path branch (§3.8)
- Immediate (pre-build) 301s: slug change marks the old path dirty (P4-E4.3) -> Worker sees dirty -> SSR catch-all -> record miss -> consult redirects via API -> 301 now; next build moves it into redirects.json
- Path matching uses the same §3.5 normalization as KV keys
acceptance_criteria:
- redirects.json generated at build time from GET /redirects (build tier) and deployed with the static assets
- Worker returns the redirect (default 301 with correct Location) BEFORE any asset lookup or SSR delegation
- Mechanism covers both static-era and SSR-era requests (single mechanism, §3.8)
- New deploys pick up newly exported redirects; memoization does not outlive a deployment
- SSR catch-all consults redirects via API on record-miss so a slug change 301s immediately, before the next build bakes redirects.json
- Unit tests: redirect hit, miss, ordering before assets, http_status honored
notes: Spec: §3.8, §5.11, §6.3 (GET /redirects). Pairs with P4-E4.3 (slug change writes the row + marks old path dirty) and P4-E4.5 (e2e slug-301). Serves R3 + R8 (SEO-correct permanent redirects). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E3.2 Stale-beats-error: SSR throw → serve existing static even if dirty (x-immo-serving: stale-fallback); no asset → 503 retry-after 120; islands degrade per §3.7 (site survives total VPS outage — protect in review)
description:
## Why
- §3.7: the public site **surviving a total Hetzner outage** is a primary reason the static layer exists. Without this branch, a VPS outage would 5xx every dirty/missing page even though a perfectly good (slightly stale) static file sits in ASSETS. Stale beats error.
- This is the resilience half of R3: freshness when the origin is up, availability when it is not — and §3.7 explicitly asks reviewers to protect the property (no SSR-only critical path for state-A pages).

## What
- Wrap `astroHandler.fetch` in try/catch per the §3.4 code: on throw → `env.ASSETS.fetch(request)`; if status ≠ 404 → return the asset with `x-immo-serving: stale-fallback` set (rewrap the Response to mutate headers).
- No asset available (state-B path with origin down) → `503` with `retry-after: 120` and body "Temporarily unavailable"; never cached.
- Verify island degradation per §3.7: search/map/inquiry calls surface UI-level error states ("search temporarily unavailable") while static page content remains fully usable — confirm the islands built in P2/P5 handle fetch failure; file follow-ups if any island lacks an error state.
- Add the §3.7 review guard to the team checklist: no SSR-only critical path for state-A pages.

## Out of scope
- Uptime alerting on the 503 path (§14/P8-E2); Worker analytics counting of stale-fallback (P4-E5.1).
design:
- Exact §3.4 catch branch: try astroHandler.fetch -> catch -> env.ASSETS.fetch(request) -> if not 404: rewrap Response, set x-immo-serving: stale-fallback, return -> else 503 body "Temporarily unavailable", header retry-after: 120
- Ordering invariant (§3.7): SSR error -> existing asset (even if dirty) -> 503 only when no asset exists
- Never cache the 503; stale-fallback responses keep asset headers apart from the marker header
- Island degradation is client-side (§3.7) — verify error states exist, no Worker changes needed for them
acceptance_criteria:
- SSR handler throw on a built page -> 200 static response with x-immo-serving: stale-fallback, even when a KV dirty marker exists (stale beats error)
- SSR throw on a never-built path (state B) -> 503 with retry-after: 120 and no caching
- Islands show UI-level error states with the API down (search/map/inquiry per §3.7) while static page content remains fully usable
- Unit tests cover both fallback branches (asset present / absent)
- Review checklist item recorded: no SSR-only critical path for state-A pages (§3.7)
notes: Spec: §3.4 catch branch, §3.7 graceful degradation. Risk register: §18 row 4 (VPS single box dies -> static keeps serving; restore drill covers recovery). Protect in code review per §3.7. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E3.1 Custom Worker entry wrapping Astro SSR handler: isContentPath + run_worker_first globs (content routes only; CSS/JS/fonts stay pure static) + getBuiltAt() from ASSETS /__build.json memoized 60 s + KV FRESHNESS lookup (dirty_at > built_at ⇒ stale)
description:
## Why
- Implements the §3.1 state machine at the edge — the single decision point where every content request is classified A/B/C. State A keeps ~99% of traffic on static assets with zero origin load (R1's economics); the miss/dirty branches deliver R2/R3 by delegating to the SSR catch-alls (P4-E2).
- The `dirty_at > built_at` comparison (not marker deletion) is what lets B/C pages collapse back to A automatically after each successful build (§3.1) — correctness lives in this code.

## What
- `frontend/src/worker/index.ts` custom entry; import the adapter-generated SSR handler (exact export name from the P4-E1 ADR; §3.4 comment "verify exact name in P4").
- `wrangler.jsonc` per §3.4 excerpt: `main: ./dist/_worker.js/index.js`; `assets { directory: ./dist, binding: ASSETS, run_worker_first: [content routes, locale roots, /__health] }`; `kv_namespaces: [{ binding: FRESHNESS }]` (one namespace per environment, §3.5).
- `isContentPath(pathname)` mirroring the `run_worker_first` globs (project/listing/developer families + localized variants).
- `getBuiltAt(env)`: `env.ASSETS.fetch('https://internal/__build.json')`, parse `built_at`, memoize 60 s in module state (§3.3: consumed by the Worker, memoized 60 s).
- KV read `env.FRESHNESS.get('path:' + normalize(pathname))`; `stale = dirtyAt !== null && Number(dirtyAt) * 1000 > builtAt`.
- Flow per §3.4: `!stale` → ASSETS fetch, return unless 404 (state A); otherwise/miss → `astroHandler.fetch` (states B/C); non-content paths reaching the Worker → assets first, then SSR.
- `normalize()`: lowercase, no trailing slash, no query (§3.5) — must agree byte-for-byte with `Immo.Edge.Paths` key normalization (property-tested on the backend in P4-E4.1).
- Dirty path is **dormant** until P4-E4.2 writes keys — ship it tested via mocked KV.

## Out of scope
- try/catch stale-beats-error + 503 (P4-E3.2); redirects.json (P4-E3.3); KV writes (P4-E4.2).
design:
- §3.4 code is the contract: isContentPath(pathname) gate; Promise.all([getBuiltAt(env), env.FRESHNESS.get("path:" + normalize(pathname))]); stale = dirtyAt !== null && Number(dirtyAt) * 1000 > builtAt (KV value = unix SECONDS, builtAt = ms epoch)
- !stale -> ASSETS fetch, return unless 404 (state A); else astroHandler.fetch (states B/C); non-content paths: assets first then SSR
- getBuiltAt: env.ASSETS.fetch("https://internal/__build.json"), Date.parse(built_at) || 0, memoized in module state 60_000 ms
- wrangler.jsonc per §3.4 excerpt: run_worker_first content routes + locale roots + /__health only; kv_namespaces binding FRESHNESS (per-env namespace, §3.5)
- Adapter SSR export imported per the P4-E1 ADR (exact name verified there); /_render/* URL rewrite before delegation if variant B chosen
acceptance_criteria:
- State A: existing asset + no newer dirty marker -> served via env.ASSETS.fetch with no SSR invocation
- Asset 404 -> falls through to the SSR handler (state B path) (§16 AC)
- KV value newer than built_at -> asset bypassed, SSR invoked (state C path code-complete though dormant — no writers yet)
- /__build.json fetched at most once per 60 s per isolate (memoization tested)
- CSS/JS/font requests never invoke the Worker on staging (run_worker_first verified)
- Path normalization identical to §3.5: lowercase, no trailing slash, no query — byte-equal with Immo.Edge.Paths keys
notes: Spec: §3.4 (wrangler excerpt + conceptual code), §3.5 (key format + normalization), §3.1. KV writes do not exist yet (P4-E4.2) so the dirty path is dormant. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P4-E3 — Custom Worker entry (freshness routing + resilience)
description:
## Why
- The custom Worker entry is the request-plane brain of the freshness model (§3.4): per request it decides state A (static asset, ~99% of traffic, zero origin load), B (asset miss → SSR) or C (KV dirty marker newer than build → SSR), composing R1's interval, R2's instant-new and R3's instant-edit semantics at the edge.
- It also embodies §3.7 graceful degradation: **stale beats error** — the public site must survive a total Hetzner outage. That property is a primary reason the static layer exists; this epic implements and tests it.
- `run_worker_first` keeps non-content traffic (CSS/JS/images/fonts) pure-static — free, no Worker CPU (§3.4).

## What
- Custom entry `frontend/src/worker/index.ts` wrapping the Astro-generated SSR handler (adapter export name per the P4-E1 ADR).
- `wrangler.jsonc` per the §3.4 excerpt: ASSETS binding + `run_worker_first` content globs + FRESHNESS KV binding.
- `getBuiltAt()` from ASSETS `/__build.json`, memoized 60 s; KV lookup `path:<normalized>`; `dirty_at > built_at` ⇒ stale.
- Stale-beats-error fallback (`x-immo-serving: stale-fallback`), 503 `retry-after: 120` when no asset exists.
- `redirects.json` build-time export + Worker consultation before asset lookup (§3.8 single mechanism for static AND SSR).
- Routing-matrix unit tests + staging chaos test (kill API ⇒ stale-fallback).

## Out of scope
- KV **writes** (P4-E4 — the dirty path is code-complete here but dormant until Phoenix writes keys); SSR route internals (P4-E2); serving-mode analytics (P4-E5).
design:
- §3.4 conceptual Worker code is THE contract: isContentPath gate -> Promise.all([getBuiltAt, FRESHNESS.get(path:<normalized>)]) -> stale = dirtyAt*1000 > builtAt -> !stale: ASSETS first (state A) -> miss/stale: astroHandler (B/C) -> catch: stale-beats-error -> 503 retry-after 120
- wrangler.jsonc per §3.4 excerpt: main ./dist/_worker.js/index.js, assets binding ASSETS with run_worker_first content globs, kv_namespaces binding FRESHNESS
- Graceful degradation per §3.7: stale beats error; islands degrade; site survives total VPS outage (protect in review)
- redirects.json generated at build from GET /redirects; consulted before asset lookup (§3.8)
acceptance_criteria:
- Routing-matrix unit tests green (state A/B/C x content/non-content paths) (§16 P4-E3 AC)
- Asset 404 falls through to SSR (§16 AC)
- Killing the staging API yields x-immo-serving: stale-fallback on built pages (§16 AC chaos test)
- CSS/JS/fonts never invoke the Worker (run_worker_first limited to content routes)
- /__build.json memoized 60 s; KV FRESHNESS lookup compares dirty_at vs built_at per §3.4 code
- redirects.json consulted before asset lookup (§3.8 single mechanism)
notes: Spec: §3.4 ENTIRE (wrangler excerpt + Worker code), §3.7, §3.8, §16 P4-E3 (deps: P4-E2). Risk register: §18 rows 1 (route variant per P4-E1 ADR) and 4 (VPS dies — static keeps serving). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E2.4 Playwright harness vs staging + e2e: publish new listing → 200 via ssr-new ≤ 2 min, correct JSON-LD
description:
## Why
- This is the epic's Definition of Done (§16 P4-E2 AC): e2e "publish new → live ≤ 2 min" green **with zero KV usage** — proving R2 end-to-end on staging and proving §3.9's claim that state B needs no KV machinery.
- It also establishes the Playwright freshness harness: §15.4 defines the whole state-machine test matrix (edit, unpublish, rebuild-flip, slug-301), and the helpers built here are reused by P4-E4.5 and the full matrix in P8-E3.3.

## What
- Playwright project configured against staging (`PUBLIC_SITE_URL`), runnable locally and in CI (§12.3 frontend CI).
- Fixture path to publish a **new** listing on staging (admin/API test credentials, staging only).
- §15.4 scenario 1: publish new listing → page returns 200 with `x-immo-serving: ssr-new` within **2 min**; JSON-LD correct (validates and matches static expectations).
- Explicit zero-KV assertion: the scenario passes with no FRESHNESS reads or writes (state B works by asset miss alone).
- Harness helpers designed for reuse: serving-mode header asserts, poll-until-deadline, JSON-LD checks, content lifecycle fixtures (publish/edit/unpublish/slug-change — later scenarios consume them in P4-E4.5).

## Out of scope
- Scenarios 2-4 of §15.4 (edit/unpublish/slug-301/rebuild-flip — P4-E4.5); search/map/inquiry/RTL e2e (§15.4 "plus" list — P5/P7/P8 scope).
design:
- Playwright vs staging per §15.4 preamble (E2E Playwright vs staging)
- Deadline: 2 min wall clock from publish to 200 + ssr-new (poll with budget, fail past deadline)
- Content publish via staging admin/API test credentials (never prod)
- Helper inventory: header assertion on x-immo-serving, poll-until-deadline, JSON-LD extraction/validation, publish/edit/unpublish/slug-change fixtures (scenarios 2-4 land in P4-E4.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- e2e green on staging: publish new listing -> page returns 200 with x-immo-serving: ssr-new within <= 2 min, correct JSON-LD (§15.4 scenario 1; §16 P4-E2 AC)
- Zero KV usage demonstrated: state B passes purely by asset miss, no FRESHNESS reads/writes involved (§16 AC "with zero KV usage")
- JSON-LD on the SSR page validates and matches the static-output expectation
- Harness helpers (x-immo-serving assert, deadline polling, publish/unpublish fixtures) are reusable by P4-E4.5 and the full matrix in P8-E3.3
- Suite runs against staging (PUBLIC_SITE_URL) and is wired into CI per §12.3
notes: Spec: §15.4 scenario 1, §16 P4-E2 AC. Harness reused for the full matrix in P8-E3.3 and by P4-E4.5. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E2.3 State-B response headers: cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 + x-immo-serving: ssr-new
description:
## Why
- §3.4: state-B responses get `cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` — **new content can tolerate 60 s edge cache to shield the VPS from hot-new-listing traffic**. This is R2 with origin protection: instant visibility without exposing the single Hetzner box to a traffic spike.
- `x-immo-serving` is the freshness model's observable: §14 samples it for the serving-mode dashboard, and every §15.4 e2e scenario asserts on it. Without this header the state machine is untestable and unmonitorable.

## What
- SSR catch-all responses for found records (state B): set `cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` and `x-immo-serving: ssr-new`.
- Keep 404s on `no-store` (P4-E2.2) — never `s-maxage` a 404.
- Implement header emission behind a small serving-state seam so P4-E4 can flip dirty-path responses to `cache-control: no-store` + `x-immo-serving: ssr-dirty` (§3.4: state C must reflect edits instantly, so it must not be edge-cached) without touching templates.

## Out of scope
- `ssr-dirty`/`no-store` emission for state C (P4-E4) and `stale-fallback` (P4-E3.2 — set by the Worker, not these routes).
design:
- Exact state-B values (§3.4): cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 — new content tolerates 60 s edge cache to shield the VPS from hot-new-listing traffic
- x-immo-serving enum (§3.4 + §3.7): static | ssr-new | ssr-dirty | stale-fallback; this task emits ssr-new
- State C (§3.4): cache-control: no-store + ssr-dirty — NOT implemented here; leave a serving-state seam (e.g. Worker-passed hint) for P4-E4
- Header used by observability sampling (§14 dashboards) and every freshness e2e assertion (§15.4)
acceptance_criteria:
- SSR-rendered found pages carry exactly cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 (§3.4 cache-header paragraph)
- And x-immo-serving: ssr-new
- 404 responses keep cache-control: no-store (never s-maxage)
- Headers assertable by the harness (consumed by P4-E2.4 and §15.4 e2e)
- A forward hook exists so P4-E4 can flip state-C responses to no-store + ssr-dirty without reworking these routes
notes: Spec: §3.4 cache-header paragraph, §14 dashboards bullet, §15.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E2.2 API 404 → real 404 page with cache-control: no-store; canonical always points to prerendered URL; JSON-LD identical to static output
description:
## Why
- R3's unpublish clause ultimately renders through this path: state C → SSR → API 404 → **real 404 page with `no-store`** — unpublished content must immediately 404, not linger as a ghost static page (§3.1 row C). Getting `no-store` wrong would let the edge cache resurrect dead pages.
- R8/SEO correctness: SSR fallback output must be indistinguishable from the static build — **canonical always points to the prerendered URL** (never an internal `/_render/*` path) and **JSON-LD is identical** (§7.6), so crawlers never see a divergent duplicate.

## What
- SSR catch-alls (from P4-E2.1): on render-tier API 404 → render the real 404 page (same design as the prerendered 404, §7.1) with status 404 and `cache-control: no-store`.
- Canonical on every SSR-rendered detail page = the prerendered public URL from the record `path` field (`Immo.Edge.Paths` is the single path authority, §6.3) — identical to what the static page emits.
- JSON-LD via the `JsonLd` component from the view-model (§7.6: `RealEstateListing`/`Residence` + `Offer` + `Organization` + `BreadcrumbList`) — byte-identical between static and SSR output for the same record.
- Tests: 404 + header; canonical equality static vs SSR; JSON-LD snapshot equality from loader-sourced vs SSR-sourced fixtures (§7.3 dual-source pattern extended to these routes).

## Out of scope
- State-B success headers (P4-E2.3); the KV-driven unpublish trigger itself (P4-E4.3) — this task only guarantees the rendering contract once the API answers 404.
design:
- 404 contract: SSR catch-alls render the prerendered 404 page design on API 404, status 404, cache-control: no-store (§3.1 row C note + §7.1)
- canonical source: the record path field computed server-side by Immo.Edge.Paths (§6.3 response conventions) — same authority as sitemap and KV keys
- JsonLd component renders from the view-model only (§7.6) -> static/SSR parity is structural, not coincidental
- SEO fallback chain per §7.6 deterministic fallbacks ({title} - {city} | {site})
acceptance_criteria:
- Unknown/unpublished slug on any catch-all -> HTTP 404 rendering the real 404 page with cache-control: no-store (§7.1 404 row)
- canonical on SSR-rendered detail pages = the prerendered public URL, including when the /_render/* variant is chosen (§7.6)
- JSON-LD emitted via the SSR path is identical to static output for the same record: RealEstateListing/Residence + Offer + Organization + BreadcrumbList (§7.6)
- no-store verified so an unpublished page cannot be cached back into existence at the edge
- Tests: 404 status + header assertion; canonical assertion; JSON-LD snapshot equality static-fixture vs SSR-fixture
notes: Spec: §3.1 row C (API 404 path), §7.1 404 row, §7.6. Serves R3 (unpublish must immediately 404, no ghost pages) + R8 (canonical/JSON-LD parity). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E2.1 SSR catch-all routes /projets/[...fallback] + /{type_segment}/[...fallback] + /promoteurs/[...fallback]: fetch single record via render tier (RENDER_TOKEN), render SAME templates via view-models (R4)
description:
## Why
- This is state B's engine (§3.1 row B): asset miss → SSR catch-all fetches **the one record** from Phoenix and renders **the same template**. R2 is served directly by this task.
- R4 universality is the load-bearing constraint: one view-model, one component set, rendering identically from build-time data or request-time API data — these routes must produce output indistinguishable from the static build (verified by the dual-source render test pattern of §7.3).

## What
- Routes per §7.1 (placement per the P4-E1 ADR — direct catch-all family or `/_render/*` rewrite targets), all `prerender = false`:
  - `/projets/[...fallback].astro` → `GET /projects/:slug`
  - `/{type_segment}/[...fallback].astro` → resolve `property_types.url_segment` (per locale) → `GET /listings/:type_key/:slug`
  - `/promoteurs/[...fallback].astro` → `GET /developers/:slug`
  - locale variants per Astro i18n routing (fr at root, `/ar/`, `/en/`).
- Parse city/slug/type-segment from the fallback path; reject malformed paths early (404 path handled in P4-E2.2).
- Fetch via the single `src/lib/api.ts` client with `RENDER_TOKEN` (Worker secret via `wrangler secret put`; never in the client bundle — §10.1 trust path 2; SSR timeout 5 s §7.3).
- Map via `src/lib/mappers.ts` (`toListingView`, `toProjectView`, developer equivalent) — the only place API shapes become view shapes (§7.3) — and render the same page components as the prerendered routes.

## Out of scope
- 404/canonical/JSON-LD assertions (P4-E2.2); response headers (P4-E2.3); Worker-side routing into these handlers (P4-E3); KV dirty bypass (P4-E4).
design:
- Render-tier endpoints (§6.3): GET /projects/:slug, GET /listings/:type_key/:slug, GET /developers/:slug — single record, all locales, embedded media; 404 if not published
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer RENDER_TOKEN from wrangler secret (§10.1 trust path 2); scopes disjoint from build tier (no list dumps on the SSR path, §6.4)
- One fetch client src/lib/api.ts (timeout 5 s SSR, §7.3); mapping ONLY in mappers.ts toListingView/toProjectView (§7.3)
- Route placement honors the P4-E1 ADR: direct [...fallback] family or /_render/* rewrite targets
- Type-segment resolution: property_types.url_segment per locale drives /{segment}/... parsing (§5.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- Newly published (post-build) listing, project and developer URLs each render via the SSR catch-all with content identical to what the next build would produce (dual-source equality, §7.3)
- All three route families work, including locale variants (fr root, /ar/, /en/) and url_segment-typed listing paths
- RENDER_TOKEN attached server-side only (Worker secret); never present in the client bundle (§10.1 path 2)
- Templates/components consume only *View types; no RENDER_MODE or data-source branching (§2.2 hard rule — PR fails review otherwise)
- Unit tests for path parsing; render tests from SSR-shaped fixtures
notes: Spec: §3.1 row B, §7.1 catch-all rows, §7.3, §6.3 render tier, §10.1 path 2. Depends on P4-E1 ADR for route layout. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P4-E2 — State B: SSR catch-alls (new content live instantly, R2)
description:
## Why
- Serves **R2**: content created between builds (e.g. a new apartment) must be visible **immediately**, served dynamically from the Phoenix API via SSR fallback, until the next scheduled build bakes it into static HTML.
- State B in the freshness model (§3.1): no static asset exists → asset miss → SSR catch-all fetches the one record and renders **the same template**. After the next successful build the page collapses back to state A automatically.
- §3.9 phasing rationale: shipping B before C delivers user value early **with zero KV machinery**, and isolates the most complex piece (state C) behind a working baseline. D2 even allows launching with B only if the timeline demands.
- R4 enforced here: SSR routes render via the same view-models/components as the build — no second template path.

## What
- SSR catch-all routes per §7.1: `/projets/[...fallback]`, `/{type_segment}/[...fallback]`, `/promoteurs/[...fallback]` (+ locale variants), fetching single records via the render tier (`RENDER_TOKEN`).
- API 404 → real 404 page with `cache-control: no-store`; canonical always points to the prerendered URL; JSON-LD identical to static output (§7.6).
- State-B headers per §3.4: `cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` + `x-immo-serving: ssr-new`.
- Playwright harness vs staging + e2e §15.4 scenario 1 (publish new → live ≤ 2 min).

## Out of scope
- KV dirty markers / state C (P4-E4); custom Worker entry routing and stale-beats-error (P4-E3); category/index instant freshness (§3.6 policy: static, ≤ interval lag accepted — D4).
design:
- State B mechanism (§3.1 row B): no static asset exists (published after last build) -> asset miss -> SSR catch-all fetches the ONE record from Phoenix and renders the same template
- Catch-all routes per §7.1: /projets/[...fallback], /{type_segment}/[...fallback], /promoteurs/[...fallback] (placement per the P4-E1 ADR — direct family or /_render/*)
- Render tier auth: RENDER_TOKEN Worker secret, single-record endpoints only (§6.3, §10.1 path 2)
- §3.9 phasing: B before C ships user value with zero KV machinery; C stays isolated behind this working baseline
acceptance_criteria:
- e2e on staging: publish new listing -> page 200 via SSR (x-immo-serving: ssr-new) within <= 2 min, with ZERO KV usage (§16 P4-E2 AC; §15.4 scenario 1)
- Identical templates via view-models: SSR output matches what the next build would produce (R4 dual-source equality)
- API 404 -> real 404 page with cache-control: no-store; canonical always the prerendered URL; JSON-LD identical to static output
- State-B responses carry cache-control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 + x-immo-serving: ssr-new (§3.4)
notes: Spec: §3.1 state table, §3.9 phasing, §7.1 catch-all rows, §7.3, §16 P4-E2 (deps: P4-E1). Open decisions: D2 (if launch pressure, site can ship after P4-E2 only — edits lag <= interval). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P4-E1.1 Spike: validate prerender+catch-all coexistence on pinned Astro/adapter versions; else adopt /_render/* rewrite variant — ADR + staging proof (one route family)
description:
## Why
- R2 and R3 both ride the SSR catch-all (§3.1 states B and C: asset miss or dirty marker → SSR renders from the API). If the prerendered `[slug].astro` family and the `[...slug].astro` catch-all cannot deterministically coexist on the pinned Astro/adapter versions, the freshness model has no delivery mechanism — §18 row 1 rates this M likelihood / H impact, **blocks P4**.
- The fallback is already designed (§3.4): deterministic `/_render/*` internal SSR paths + Worker URL rewrite before delegation. The spike's job is to pick once, prove on staging, and freeze the choice in an ADR so P4-E2/E3 build on solid ground.

## What
- Pin Astro 6 + official Cloudflare adapter versions (record exact versions).
- Minimal staging deployment exercising **one route family** (e.g. `/projets/[city]/[slug]` prerendered + `/projets/[...fallback]` SSR):
  - existing static path → serves the prerendered asset;
  - missing path → SSR catch-all renders;
  - verify the adapter export name for the generated SSR handler (§3.4: `import astroHandler from '../../dist/_worker.js/_astro-entry'` — "verify exact name in P4").
- If precedence is ambiguous/flaky → implement variant B: SSR routes under `/_render/*`; the Worker entry rewrites the request URL before delegating to the Astro handler.
- **If the rewrite variant is chosen: `/_render/*` gets robots.txt `Disallow` + `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`** (§7.6 defense-in-depth) so internal render paths never leak into the index.
- Write the ADR: decision, pinned versions, evidence, consequences for P4-E2 route placement and P4-E3 Worker delegation.

## Out of scope
- Full three-family catch-all implementation (P4-E2.1), KV/dirty logic (P4-E3/E4), production Worker entry hardening (P4-E3).
design:
- Pin exact Astro 6 + official Cloudflare adapter versions; record them in the ADR (the decision is only valid for pinned versions, §18 row 1)
- Variant A: /projets/[city]/[slug] prerendered via getStaticPaths + /projets/[...fallback] SSR in the same family (§7.1 rows)
- Variant B: SSR under /_render/... ; Worker rewrites url.pathname before astroHandler.fetch — deterministic, no precedence dependence (§3.4)
- If B: /_render/* Disallow in robots.txt + X-Robots-Tag: noindex header (§7.6 defense-in-depth)
- Output: ADR + minimal staging deployment proving the chosen variant on one route family
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision made within the 2-day timebox; ADR committed to /docs recording pinned versions, chosen variant, and evidence
- Staging proof for one route family: existing static path serves prerendered HTML; missing path renders via SSR catch-all (§16 P4-E1 AC)
- Exact adapter SSR-handler export name documented for the P4-E3 custom Worker entry (§3.4 code comment)
- If rewrite variant chosen: /_render/* gets robots.txt Disallow + X-Robots-Tag: noindex defense-in-depth, verified on staging (§7.6)
- Test matrix recorded: static hit, asset miss, locale variants, trailing-slash behavior on the pinned versions
notes: Spec: §3.4 route-precedence paragraph, §7.1, §7.6, §16 P4-E1. Risk register: §18 row 1 (blocks P4). Decision-type issue: outcome is an ADR. Gates all of P4-E2..E5 (strictly sequential phase). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P4-E1 — Route-precedence spike (timeboxed 2 days) + ADR
description:
## Why
- §18 risk row 1 (likelihood M, impact **H — blocks P4**): the prerendered `[slug].astro` pages and the SSR catch-all `[...slug].astro` **share a path family**. The entire freshness layer (R2 state B, R3 state C) delegates to the SSR catch-all on asset miss / dirty marker — if route matching on the pinned Astro/adapter versions is ambiguous, nothing downstream of this epic works.
- §3.4 pre-specifies the mitigation: if ambiguous, switch to the **deterministic `/_render/*` rewrite variant** — SSR routes live under internal paths (e.g. `/_render/listings/[slug]`) and the Worker entry **rewrites the request URL before delegating**. Decide once, prove it on staging, write the ADR. P4 epics are strictly sequential; everything after P4-E1 builds on this decision.

## What
- Timeboxed **2-day** spike on pinned Astro 6 + official Cloudflare adapter versions.
- Validate prerender + catch-all coexistence for one route family on staging; else adopt the `/_render/*` rewrite variant.
- Record the exact adapter SSR-handler export name (§3.4 code comment: "verify exact name in P4") for P4-E3.
- ADR in `/docs` per §4 conventions (one ADR per locked-decision change).

## Out of scope
- Production-grade catch-all implementations (P4-E2) and the full custom Worker entry (P4-E3) — this epic proves the routing substrate only.
design:
- Variant A (default): prerendered [slug].astro + SSR [...slug].astro share a path family (§3.4)
- Variant B (fallback): SSR routes under internal /_render/* paths; the Worker entry rewrites the request URL before delegating (deterministic by construction)
- Both variants acceptable; pick ONCE in P4-E1 and document (§3.4 route-precedence paragraph)
- Exact adapter SSR-handler export name must be verified and recorded (§3.4 code comment: verify exact name in P4)
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision made within the 2-day timebox (§16 P4-E1: timeboxed 2 d)
- Working proof on staging for one route family: static hit serves prerendered HTML; asset miss renders via the SSR catch-all (§16 AC)
- ADR written and committed (decision, evidence, pinned Astro/adapter versions, chosen variant)
- If the /_render/* rewrite variant is chosen: robots Disallow + X-Robots-Tag noindex specified for /_render/* (§7.6)
notes: Spec: §3.4 route-precedence risk paragraph, §7.6, §16 P4-E1. Risk register: §18 row 1 (likelihood M, impact H — blocks P4; mitigation = this timeboxed spike with rewrite-variant fallback). P4 epics are STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL — this gates P4-E2..E5. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P8-E4.1 Launch runbook execution: DNS cutover → REBUILD_CRON confirm → BILLING_ENFORCED go/no-go → Search Console + sitemap ping → 48 h hypercare watching serving-mode ratios + Sentry + build dashboard
description:
## Why
Executes §16 P8-E4 — the launch itself. Every prior P8 epic produced evidence; this task performs the cutover, locks the two launch-time decisions (D1, D13), makes the site discoverable for R8, and proves stability through 48 h of supervised production traffic.

## What
- Pre-cutover: verify all three gate epics (P8-E1/E2/E3) are closed; freeze non-launch changes.
- DNS cutover per §12.1: www/apex → Worker, api + admin → Tunnel hostnames, media → R2 custom domain; verify TLS and end-to-end serving on the production domain.
- Confirm `REBUILD_CRON` (D1): record the chosen interval, watch the first scheduled RebuildSite → ConfirmBuild cycle reach `succeeded` with `built_at` captured (§3.2).
- BILLING_ENFORCED go/no-go (D13): default false unless a paying developer is onboarded; record the decision; if enabled, re-verify the §5.13 publish gate and trigger a rebuild.
- SEO activation: verify Search Console ownership, submit sitemap.xml, confirm robots.txt → sitemap pointer (§7.6); ping the sitemap.
- 48 h hypercare: watch the serving-mode ratio dashboard (sustained SSR-share rise = freshness bug or scraping, §14), Sentry on both stacks, and the build dashboard; triage with the §14 runbooks; keep a timestamped log; close hypercare with a go/stay decision and handoff notes.

## Out of scope
- Post-launch backlog (P9); enabling Cloudflare Access on /admin (D9 — recommended follow-up, file separately if adopted).
design:
- Cutover order: confirm staging-parity → switch DNS (§12.1 topology) → smoke the §15.4 happy paths on prod → submit Search Console + sitemap ping
- D1 mechanics: REBUILD_CRON is runtime env (§3.2) — changeable without redeploy; hourly default ≈ 720 builds/month (D3 quota verdict from P0 applies)
- D13 mechanics: BILLING_ENFORCED feature-flags the subscription condition inside published/1 (§5.13); flipping it changes the published set — coordinate a rebuild after flipping
- Hypercare watch surface (§14): x-immo-serving ratio via Workers analytics, Sentry (both SDKs), builds-history dashboard + BuildAgeMonitor alerts
- Escalation: rollback runbook (Worker versions + Coolify) and VPS-down comms runbook on standby
acceptance_criteria:
- DNS records live per §12.1 (www/apex → Worker; api/admin → Tunnel; media → R2); HTTPS green on all hosts; site serves from the production domain
- REBUILD_CRON value confirmed with the product owner and recorded (D1); first post-cutover scheduled build runs to status=succeeded with built_at recorded in the builds table
- BILLING_ENFORCED decision made and applied (D13 default false); if true, publish-gate behavior re-verified against §5.13
- Search Console property verified; sitemap.xml submitted and indexed without errors; robots.txt points at the sitemap (§7.6)
- 48 h hypercare log kept: serving-mode ratio stayed nominal (SSR share near zero between publishes, §14) or deviations triaged via the serving-stale runbook; Sentry triaged; zero unresolved launch-blocking incidents at window close
notes: Spec: §16 P8-E4, §12.1, §3.2, §5.13, §7.6, §14, §15.4 (smoke reference). Open decisions: D1 and D13 are decided inside this task; D3 verdict from P0 constrains D1. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P8-E4 — Launch
description:
## Why
§16 P8-E4 is the final phase gate: put the platform on the real domain, lock the two launch-time open decisions (D1 rebuild interval, D13 billing enforcement), make the site discoverable (Search Console + sitemap per R8), and watch the §14 dashboards through a 48 h hypercare window. It only proceeds once the security (P8-E1), ops (P8-E2), and performance (P8-E3) gates are closed.

## What
- DNS cutover to production: www/apex → Worker, api/admin → Tunnel, media → R2 (§12.1).
- Confirm `REBUILD_CRON` for production (D1, default hourly) and observe the first scheduled build complete.
- Make the BILLING_ENFORCED go/no-go call (D13, default false) and record it.
- Submit the property to Google Search Console; ping the sitemap.
- Run 48 h hypercare watching serving-mode ratios, Sentry, and the build dashboard (§14), with runbooks at hand.

## Out of scope
- Any new feature work; P9 backlog items (second vertical, visitor accounts, PostGIS) remain post-launch.
design:
- §12.1 DNS topology: www/apex → Worker, api + admin → Tunnel, media → R2 custom domain
- D1: REBUILD_CRON runtime env, default 0 * * * * — a cost knob, not a freshness knob (§3.2); relaxing to 0 */3 * * * changes nothing user-visible
- D13: BILLING_ENFORCED=false at launch unless first paying developer onboarded; flag feeds the published/1 predicate (§5.13)
- §14 hypercare watch surface: x-immo-serving ratio (SSR share should hover near zero between publishes; sustained rise = freshness bug or scraping) + Sentry + builds history
- Rollback paths if hypercare goes red: Worker versions + Coolify per the rollback runbook (§14)
acceptance_criteria:
- DNS cutover complete per §12.1 topology (www/apex → Worker; api/admin → Tunnel; media → R2 custom domain); production site serving on the real domain
- REBUILD_CRON confirmed and recorded (D1 default 0 * * * *); first scheduled prod build observed succeeded with built_at captured
- BILLING_ENFORCED go/no-go decided and set (D13 default false); decision logged
- Property submitted to Google Search Console; sitemap pinged and accepted
- 48 h hypercare completed: serving-mode ratios (x-immo-serving dashboard, §14), Sentry, and the build dashboard watched; incidents triaged via runbooks; hypercare log archived
notes: Spec: §16 P8-E4, §12.1, §3.2, §5.13, §14 (dashboards/runbooks), §7.6 (sitemap). Open decisions: D1 (REBUILD_CRON), D13 (BILLING_ENFORCED) — both must be explicitly confirmed at launch. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. Blocked by P8-E1, P8-E2, P8-E3 (gates).

title: P1-E5.5 open_api_spex specs on every controller + mix openapi.spec.json CI generation + drift-fails-CI gate + curl tier matrix doc
description:
## Why
- A9/R4: the OpenAPI contract is what keeps build-time and SSR rendering identical — frontend types are generated from it (P2-E2: openapi-typescript) and the drift gate makes backend/frontend divergence unmergeable (§6.3, §15.2).
- §16 AC also demands an operator-facing curl matrix per tier — the executable documentation of the three trust paths.

## What
- `open_api_spex` ApiSpec (`ImmoWeb.ApiSpec`) + operation specs on every /api/v1 controller shipped in P1-E5 (build, render, public scaffolding) (§6.3).
- CI step: `mix openapi.spec.json --spec ImmoWeb.ApiSpec -o priv/static/openapi.json`; uncommitted diff fails CI (§6.3).
- securitySchemes for the bearer tiers; RFC 9457 problem+json error schemas; envelope + record-convention schemas (§6.3).
- curl tier matrix documentation: build/render/public × success/401/304 (§16 AC).

## Out of scope
- Frontend type generation + types-drift CI gate (P2-E2); schemathesis fuzzing (optional P8, §15.2).
design:
- ImmoWeb.ApiSpec (open_api_spex) + operation specs per controller action (§6.3)
- CI generation exactly per §6.3: mix openapi.spec.json --spec ImmoWeb.ApiSpec -o priv/static/openapi.json; drift gate = git diff --exit-code on the artifact
- Versioning stance encoded in the spec: additive fields non-breaking; breaking → /api/v2 (§6.3)
- curl matrix doc lives with the backend docs and is referenced by the P2-E2 codegen consumer
acceptance_criteria:
- priv/static/openapi.json validates as OpenAPI; every routed /api/v1 endpoint has an open_api_spex operation (§6.3)
- CI step regenerates the spec and fails on uncommitted diff — a controller change without a committed spec update cannot merge (§16 AC: spec drift fails CI)
- securitySchemes document the build/render bearer tiers; problem+json error schemas included
- Envelope and record conventions schematized: {data, meta:{next_cursor, count}}; id, slug, path, updated_at, published_at, i18n maps (§6.3)
- curl matrix per tier documented (§16 AC): build/render/public × success/401/304 examples
notes: Spec: §6.3 (OpenAPI paragraph verbatim), A9, §15.2 (contract tests), §16 P1-E5 AC. Consumed by P2-E2 (openapi-typescript codegen + types-drift gate). Deps: P1-E5.2, P1-E5.3. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E5.3 Render tier: GET /projects/:slug, /listings/:type_key/:slug, /developers/:slug (+/internal/freshness documented alternative) — single records, all locales, embedded media; 404 if unpublished
description:
## Why
- R2/R3: the SSR Worker renders new/edited pages from these single-record lookups between scheduled builds; "404 if not published" is what makes unpublish take effect immediately instead of lingering as a ghost page (R3).
- §10.1: render-tier token protection prevents cache-busting amplification (attackers forcing SSR misses against arbitrary slugs would otherwise hammer the VPS).

## What
- `GET /projects/:slug` — single record, all locales, embedded media + published listings summary; 404 if not published (§6.3).
- `GET /listings/:type_key/:slug` — single record; slug resolved per property_type (§5.4).
- `GET /developers/:slug` — single record (§6.3).
- `GET /internal/freshness?path=` → `{updated_at}` or 404 — the documented KV alternative (§3.5); implemented, unused by default (§6.3).
- ETag/304 on render GETs (§6.3 applies to all build/render GETs).
- All lookups compose `Catalog.published/1` (§5.13).

## Out of scope
- The SSR Worker that calls these (P4); switching freshness from KV to /internal/freshness (P9 backlog, only if KV lag bites).
design:
- Endpoints on the :api_render pipeline (RENDER_TOKEN, §10.1 path 2): GET /projects/:slug, /listings/:type_key/:slug, /developers/:slug, /internal/freshness (§6.3 table)
- Single-record payloads: all locales, embedded media ordered by position (§5.6), path fields via Immo.Edge.Paths (shared with P1-E5.2)
- Lookups compose Catalog.published/1 — a record outside the predicate is a 404, never a leak (§5.13)
- freshness lookup resolves path → entity via the same Edge.Paths authority
acceptance_criteria:
- Published slug → 200 with all locales + embedded media (ordered by position, incl. r2_key/blurhash/dimensions/alt); project responses embed a published-listings summary (§6.3)
- Draft, future-published, unpublished or billing-gated slug → 404 problem+json (§6.3: 404 if not published; powers R3 immediate-404)
- GET /listings/:type_key/:slug resolves the slug within the property_type namespace (slug unique per type, §5.4)
- GET /internal/freshness?path= returns {updated_at} for a published path, 404 otherwise (§6.3/§3.5 documented alternative — implemented, unused by default)
- ETag present on render GETs; If-None-Match → 304 (§6.3: all build/render GETs)
- Build token rejected on render endpoints (disjoint scopes, §6.4)
notes: Spec: §6.3, §3.5 (KV alternative — implemented, unused by default), §5.13, §5.4, §10.1 path 2. Deps: P1-E5.1. Consumed by the SSR Worker in P4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E5.2 Build tier: GET /projects /listings /developers /property_types (cursor, limit≤100, since, ETag/304) + /meta/sitemap + /redirects; response convention: id, slug, per-locale path via Immo.Edge.Paths (single path authority), updated_at, i18n maps; envelope {data, meta:{next_cursor,count}}
description:
## Why
- R1: the scheduled build's content loaders consume these full publishable dumps; `since` powers incremental loader sync and ETag/304 makes hourly re-syncs cheap (§6.3).
- R8/§3.8: /meta/sitemap and /redirects feed the sitemap (lastmod + locale alternates) and the build-time redirects.json.
- `Immo.Edge.Paths` is born here as the **single** path authority (§6.3) — §15.1 makes it correctness-critical: KV keys (P4) and API `path` fields must always agree.

## What
- `GET /projects`, `GET /listings`, `GET /developers` — full publishable dumps with `cursor`, `limit≤100`, `since` (ISO ts → only `updated_at > since`) (§6.3).
- `GET /property_types` — includes `filter_config` (merged with searchable custom fields) and `url_segment` (§6.3).
- `GET /meta/sitemap` — all public paths + lastmod + locale alternates (§6.3).
- `GET /redirects` — active redirects for the build-time redirects.json (§6.3).
- Response convention on every record: `id`, `slug`, `path` (canonical per-locale public path computed server-side by `Immo.Edge.Paths`), `updated_at`, `published_at`, i18n maps as objects keyed by locale; list envelope `{data: [], meta: {next_cursor, count}}` (§6.3).
- Strong ETag from `max(updated_at)+count` of the page; honor `If-None-Match` → 304 (§6.3).
- All queries compose `Catalog.published/1` (§5.13).
- Implement `Immo.Edge.Paths` v1: locale-aware paths from `url_segment` + city + slug (§5.3).

## Out of scope
- Render-tier single records (P1-E5.3); property-test hardening of Edge.Paths (P4-E4.1); frontend loaders consuming this (P2-E3).
design:
- Endpoints on the :api_build pipeline (BUILD_TOKEN, §10.1 path 1): GET /projects, /listings, /developers, /property_types, /meta/sitemap, /redirects (§6.3 table)
- Cursor pagination (keyset over stable ordering; next_cursor in meta) honoring limit≤100 and since on updated_at (§6.3)
- Strong ETag computed from max(updated_at)+count of the page; If-None-Match handling on all build GETs (§6.3)
- Immo.Edge.Paths v1 born here: canonical per-locale public paths from property_type.url_segment + city + slug (§5.3 route shape /{segment}/{city}/{slug}); the SINGLE path authority later shared with KV marking (P4)
- /meta/sitemap feeds the sitemap serializer + redirects export; /redirects feeds build-time redirects.json (§6.3/§3.8)
acceptance_criteria:
- Pagination: limit clamped at 100; cursor pages are stable and complete; since=ISO ts returns only records with updated_at > since (§6.3 — powers incremental loader sync)
- Repeat fetch with If-None-Match returns 304 with empty body (strong ETag from max(updated_at)+count of the page) (§6.3, §16 AC)
- Unpublished, future-published and billing-gated records absent from every dump (Catalog.published/1 composed everywhere, §5.13/§15.1)
- GET /property_types includes filter_config merged with searchable custom fields + url_segment (§6.3)
- GET /meta/sitemap returns all public paths + lastmod + locale alternates; GET /redirects returns active redirect rules (§6.3)
- Every record carries id, slug, path (per locale), updated_at, published_at, i18n maps keyed by locale; lists wrapped in {data, meta:{next_cursor, count}} (§6.3)
- All path values produced exclusively by Immo.Edge.Paths — no inline path building (§6.3)
notes: Spec: §6.3, §5.13, §5.3, §3.8. Edge.Paths v1 is born here and hardened with property tests in P4-E4.1 (§15.1: KV keys and API path fields must always agree). Deps: P1-E5.1. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E5.1 ImmoWeb.Plugs.BearerAuth (+secure_compare, comma-separated token sets for rotation) + api_build/api_render/api_public pipelines + RFC 9457 problem+json errors + Logger redaction of authorization
description:
## Why
- R7: machine trust paths 1–2 (§10.1) — BUILD_TOKEN/RENDER_TOKEN bearers with timing-safe comparison; the comma-separated accepted set is what makes the §10.1 rotation runbook zero-downtime (add new, deploy consumers, remove old).
- §10.1/§13: secrets must never appear in logs — Logger redaction of the authorization header is part of this surface, not an afterthought.

## What
- `ImmoWeb.Plugs.BearerAuth` per the §6.4 code contract: `init(scope)`; `call/2` reads `authorization: Bearer <token>`, guards non-empty expected token, `Plug.Crypto.secure_compare`, assigns `:api_scope`; otherwise 401 + halt.
- Rotation extension (§10.1): `token_for(scope)` returns the comma-separated token set from runtime env; any member matches (constant-time per candidate).
- Router pipelines: `:api_build` (BearerAuth :build), `:api_render` (BearerAuth :render), `:api_public` (CORS + RateLimit + no auth) (§6.4). Scopes disjoint — render is never accepted on build endpoints (§6.4: "No").
- RFC 9457 problem+json error rendering for all /api/v1 errors (§6.3).
- Logger redaction: authorization header + token values filtered (§10.1 rules, §13).

## Out of scope
- The endpoints themselves (P1-E5.2/.3); CORS/rate-limit plug internals (P1-E5.4 — pipeline slot declared here).
design:
- Module shape per the §6.4 contract: init(scope), call/2 reading the authorization header, Plug.Crypto.secure_compare, assign(:api_scope), 401 halt otherwise
- Extension over §6.4 sample per §10.1: token_for(scope) reads a comma-separated set from runtime env (BUILD_TOKEN / RENDER_TOKEN, ≥32 random bytes base64url); each candidate compared constant-time
- Router pipelines: :api_build (BearerAuth :build), :api_render (BearerAuth :render), :api_public (CORS + RateLimit, no auth) (§6.4)
- Shared FallbackController/error view emitting problem+json {type, title, status, detail}
- Logger filter for authorization + token fields (§13)
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid bearer token → request passes with :api_scope assigned; missing/malformed/wrong token → 401 problem+json (§6.4)
- Rotation: with BUILD_TOKEN set to two comma-separated values, both authenticate; removing one immediately disables it (§10.1 rotation runbook)
- Scopes disjoint: render token on a build endpoint → 401, and vice versa (§6.4)
- Empty/unset expected token never authenticates (byte_size guard from §6.4)
- All /api/v1 error responses (401/404/422/429) are application/problem+json per RFC 9457 (§6.3)
- Captured logs never contain authorization header values (Logger redaction test) (§10.1/§13)
notes: Spec: §6.4 (code contract verbatim), §10.1 (token format + rotation), §6.3 (errors), §13 (Logger redaction). Tokens registered in §12.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P1-E5 — Read API v1 + OpenAPI contract (3 auth tiers)
description:
## Why
- This is the contract between the only writer (Phoenix, A3) and every consumer: build-time loaders (R1), the SSR Worker (R2/R3), and browser islands. R4 (universal rendering — identical output from build-time or request-time data) is enforced by the OpenAPI contract (A9): frontend types are generated from it and drift fails CI.
- R7: the three auth tiers (§10.1 paths 1–3) implement least-privilege with separately rotatable credentials. Token-protecting the build firehose limits scraping/availability risk; render-tier protection prevents cache-busting amplification against the VPS (§10.1 rationale).
- Critical path (§16 dependency spine): P1-E2 → **P1-E5** → P2-E2.

## What
- §6.3 endpoint table: build tier (GET /projects, /listings, /developers, /property_types, /meta/sitemap, /redirects), render tier (GET /projects/:slug, /listings/:type_key/:slug, /developers/:slug, /internal/freshness), public-tier pipeline scaffolding (CORS + Hammer rate limits).
- `ImmoWeb.Plugs.BearerAuth` per §6.4 with secure_compare + comma-separated token sets for rotation (§10.1); pipelines :api_build / :api_render / :api_public.
