- §6.3 response conventions: id, slug, per-locale path via Immo.Edge.Paths (single path authority), updated_at, i18n maps; envelope {data, meta:{next_cursor, count}}; strong ETag → 304.
- RFC 9457 problem+json errors; additive changes non-breaking, breaking → /api/v2.
- open_api_spex specs on every controller + CI spec generation + drift gate (A9) + curl tier matrix doc.

## Out of scope
- Public endpoints /search and /listings/geo (P5-E1) and POST /inquiries (P1-E6.1) — this epic ships the pipeline they mount on.
- Frontend codegen consumption (P2-E2); KV freshness writes (P4).
design:
- Auth per §10.1 paths 1–3: BUILD_TOKEN bearer (build tier, full publishable dumps), RENDER_TOKEN bearer (render tier, single-record + freshness), anonymous public tier (CORS exact allowlist + Hammer rate limits)
- BearerAuth plug per the §6.4 code contract with Plug.Crypto.secure_compare; comma-separated token sets for zero-downtime rotation (§10.1 rules)
- Response conventions §6.3: every record carries id, slug, path (per-locale, computed by Immo.Edge.Paths — the single path authority), updated_at, published_at, i18n maps; list envelope {data, meta:{next_cursor, count}}
- Build-tier list contract: cursor, limit≤100, since (updated_at > since); strong ETag + If-None-Match → 304 on all build/render GETs
- Cache-Control: private, no-store on public search; public, s-maxage=60 permissible on geo (§6.3)
- open_api_spex on every controller; mix openapi.spec.json in CI; breaking changes → /api/v2 (§6.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P1-E5 AC: §15.1 API tests green — per-tier controller tests incl. 401s, ETag/304, cursor/since pagination
- §16 P1-E5 AC: curl matrix per tier (build/render/public) documented
- §16 P1-E5 AC: 304 returned on repeat fetch with If-None-Match (strong ETag from max(updated_at)+count)
- §16 P1-E5 AC: OpenAPI spec drift (uncommitted openapi.json diff) fails CI
- Tiers are disjoint: render token rejected on build endpoints and vice versa (§6.4)
- Only published content (Catalog.published/1) is visible on any endpoint (§5.13)
- All /api/v1 errors are RFC 9457 problem+json (§6.3)
notes: Spec: §6.3 (full endpoint table + conventions), §6.4 (BearerAuth contract), §10.1 (tiers + rotation), §5.13, A9, §16 P1-E5 (Deps: E2). CRITICAL PATH (P1-E2 → P1-E5 → P2-E2). Public /search + /listings/geo land in P5-E1; POST /inquiries in P1-E6.1 — scaffolding only here. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P8-E3.3 Full §15.4 Playwright matrix green vs staging: freshness state machine (publish/edit/rebuild/unpublish/301) + search facets from custom field + map bbox + inquiry submit (Turnstile test keys) + AR RTL
description:
## Why
The §15.4 e2e matrix is the behavioral proof of the platform's core differentiator — the R1–R3 freshness state machine — plus the key user journeys (search facets from admin-defined custom fields, map bbox, inquiries, AR RTL). §16 P8-E3 runs it as a launch gate; the harness already exists (P4-E2.4), this is the complete-matrix execution against staging on the launch candidate.

## What
- Freshness state machine end-to-end on staging:
  1. Publish a new listing → page returns 200 via SSR with `x-immo-serving: ssr-new` within 2 min; JSON-LD correct.
  2. Edit a published listing → page reflects the edit with `ssr-dirty` within 2 min.
  3. Trigger manual rebuild ("Rebuild now") → both pages flip to `static` with correct content.
  4. Unpublish → 404 within 2 min; still 404 after rebuild. Slug change → old URL serves 301.
- Search island: facet appears from a searchable custom field and filters results (§7.5/§15.4).
- Map: pan fires `/listings/geo?bbox=` and markers update.
- Inquiry: submit with Turnstile test keys → success UI → row in admin inbox.
- AR pages render RTL.
- Record the green run as launch-gate evidence for P8-E4.

## Out of scope
- Fixing freshness bugs found (file against P4 components, block launch on severity); perf numbers (P8-E3.1/.2).
design:
- §15.4 is the matrix definition; assertions key off the x-immo-serving header contract (§3.4: ssr-new | ssr-dirty | static) and cache headers (no-store for state C, s-maxage=60 for state B)
- 2-minute SLAs come straight from §15.4; rebuild step uses the admin "Rebuild now" button path (§3.2 trigger=manual)
- Slug-change case: redirects row + KV dirty mark → SSR serves 301 immediately (§3.8)
- Turnstile test keys for the inquiry flow (§15.4); honeypot stays untouched by the happy path
- Harness exists from P4-E2.4 — this run extends to the full matrix incl. P5/P6-adjacent surfaces and AR RTL
acceptance_criteria:
- Freshness state machine green per §15.4: publish new listing → 200 via SSR (x-immo-serving: ssr-new) within 2 min with correct JSON-LD; edit published → ssr-dirty within 2 min; manual rebuild → both pages flip to static with correct content; unpublish → 404 within 2 min and still 404 after rebuild; slug change → old URL 301
- Search island renders a facet sourced from a searchable custom field and filters work end-to-end
- Map bbox query: pan triggers /listings/geo and markers update
- Inquiry submit succeeds with Turnstile test keys and appears in the admin inbox
- AR pages render RTL (shared assertion with P7-E1)
- Full matrix runs green as a single suite vs staging; recorded as the launch-gate evidence
notes: Spec: §15.4, §3.4 (header contract), §3.8 (redirects), §3.2 (manual trigger), §7.5 (islands). Open decisions: D2 (if State C were deferred, edit/unpublish cases would shrink — default is shipped, full matrix applies). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. Harness from P4-E2.4; this is the full-matrix run as launch gate.

title: P8-E3.2 k6 smoke on /search + /listings/geo at budget (200 rps sustained, p95 < 300 ms, staging limits relaxed)
description:
## Why
§15.5 sets the load budget for the only two anonymous high-traffic API endpoints; P5-E1 proved it once at build time, and §16 P8-E3 requires it re-proven as a launch gate on the final production-candidate configuration (the VPS also carries SSR fallback + admin + Oban at launch).

## What
- Build/refresh the k6 scenario: 200 rps sustained against staging `/api/v1/search` (realistic mix of q, type, city, price_min/max, surface_min/max, attrs[] facet params per §6.3) and `/api/v1/listings/geo` (varied bboxes within the span guard).
- Relax Hammer/WAF rate limits for the test window per §15.5; restore and verify restoration afterwards.
- Pass criterion: p95 < 300 ms sustained; capture p50/p95/p99, error rates, and VPS CPU/IO; if tuning is required, apply §12.2 starting points and document changes.

## Out of scope
- Rate-limit enforcement testing (P8-E1.1 owns proving the 429s); page-level CWV (P8-E3.1).
design:
- §15.5: k6 smoke on /search and geo — 200 rps sustained, p95 < 300 ms, rate limits relaxed in staging
- §6.3 /search: websearch_to_tsquery over title/description/city, filter params validated against filter_config, page≤50/per_page≤24
- §6.3 /listings/geo: bbox=minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat with max-span guard, limit≤500, GeoJSON FeatureCollection
- Baseline exists from P5-E1 ("k6 budget §15.5 met on staging hardware") — this is the launch-gate rerun on final code/config
- §12.2 starting points if tuning needed: pool size 15, shared_buffers=2GB, work_mem=32MB, pg_stat_statements on
acceptance_criteria:
- k6 scenario sustains 200 rps against staging /api/v1/search and /api/v1/listings/geo with p95 latency < 300 ms (§15.5) and no error-rate spike
- Rate limits relaxed for the test window only (§15.5) and restored afterwards — restoration verified
- Query mix exercises realistic params: q full-text, type/city/price/surface filters, attrs[<key>] facets (§6.3) and bbox-with-span-guard for geo
- Results (p50/p95/p99, error rate, VPS CPU/IO during run) archived; any tuning applied is documented
notes: Spec: §15.5, §6.3 (endpoint contracts), §5.4 (indexes: GIN jsonb_path_ops, partial published, lat/lng btree), §12.2 (PG tuning), P5-E1 AC (baseline). Open decisions: D7 (PostGIS deferred — bbox stays btree ranges). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E7.3 wrangler.jsonc (assets binding ASSETS, kv binding FRESHNESS placeholder) + Git-connected build → staging serves full static site
description:
## Why
- First end-to-end proof of the P2 static MVP: loaders pull the staging catalog, the build emits all prerendered routes + /__build.json, and Workers Static Assets serve it on the staging domain. Everything P3+ builds on (deploy hooks, freshness Worker, KV) extends this deployment.
- Declaring the FRESHNESS KV binding now (placeholder) means the freshness phase changes Worker code, not deployment topology.

## What
- Author frontend/wrangler.jsonc: Static Assets binding ASSETS, KV namespace binding FRESHNESS (staging namespace from the P0 Cloudflare setup), Worker name/routes for staging.
- Connect the repo to Cloudflare Git builds (§12.3); configure staging build env vars/secrets per §12.4.
- Deploy and verify: full static site served on staging across fr/ar/en; /__build.json correct.

## Out of scope
- Custom Worker entry request routing (§3.4) and run_worker_first config tuning for freshness — later phase (plain static-assets serving suffices for P2); production deployment (P8 launch); deploy-hook-triggered content rebuilds (P3).
design:
- wrangler.jsonc per the §4 frontend layout; bindings named for the custom Worker entry that arrives in the freshness phase (§3.4): assets ASSETS, kv FRESHNESS
- §12.3 frontend deploy: code pushes → Cloudflare Git build; content rebuilds via deploy hook arrive in P3 (§3.2)
- Staging environment per §12.3: separate Worker + staging Phoenix + staging KV/R2, REBUILD_CRON=@daily later
- CF build env carries BUILD_TOKEN (secret) + non-secret build vars (§12.4); loaders pull from the staging API (P1-E5)
acceptance_criteria:
- frontend/wrangler.jsonc defines the Static Assets binding ASSETS and a KV namespace binding FRESHNESS (placeholder for the freshness phase)
- Git-connected Cloudflare Workers build: a push to the repo builds and deploys the frontend to staging (§12.3 code pushes → Cloudflare Git build)
- Staging serves the FULL static site (§16 P2-E7 AC): all locales, all prerendered routes from the staging Phoenix seed catalog
- /__build.json on staging has correct fields incl. content_snapshot_at matching staging API data (§16 P2-E7 AC)
- Deploy is reproducible from a clean push; staging env vars set per §12.4 (BUILD_TOKEN secret, PUBLIC_SITE_URL, API_BASE_URL, MEDIA_BASE_URL, RENDER_MODE=static)
notes: Spec: §12.3, §12.4, §3.4 (binding names), §16 P2-E7 AC. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E7.2 render-mode integration (astro:route:setup flips route.prerender): static|hybrid (HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES)|dynamic + CI dual-mode build smoke
description:
## Why
- R4: some deployments are served entirely from the API. §2.2 makes render mode a per-deployment env var implemented at the routing layer, so one codebase serves the flagship static portal and fully-dynamic deployments with zero template changes. The hard rule — page templates and components never know the render mode — is the universality contract this integration protects.
- The CI dual-mode smoke (§12.3: both RENDER_MODE=static and =dynamic must build) prevents the dynamic path from rotting while P2-P5 focus on static.

## What
- Implement src/integrations/render-mode.ts using astro:route:setup to flip route.prerender per the §2.2 table: static (all content routes prerendered), hybrid (HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES env list flips named index routes to SSR), dynamic (no prerendering; loaders skipped per §7.1 — the build runs without BUILD_TOKEN).
- Add the CI dual-mode build smoke (static + dynamic) to the frontend pipeline (§12.3).
- Add a guard (grep/lint step) enforcing the §2.2 hard rule: no RENDER_MODE reads in templates/components.

## Out of scope
- SSR catch-all routes and Worker serving of dynamic/hybrid responses incl. s-maxage caching (§7.1/§3.4, freshness phase); KV freshness checks.
design:
- §2.2: implemented with an Astro integration using the astro:route:setup hook to flip route.prerender at build time — src/integrations/render-mode.ts (§4)
- Mode table (§2.2): static = default flagship; hybrid = HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES env list flips named index routes only; dynamic = no prerendering, every route SSR, aggressive edge caching applied later at the Worker/SSR layer
- Env: RENDER_MODE, HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES (§12.4, build vars via astro:env)
- The universality contract (R4): templates receive a typed view-model (§7.3) and nothing else — the integration is the ONLY place render mode is interpreted
- P2 operates in static mode; dynamic smoke proves the flip without requiring Worker SSR serving yet
acceptance_criteria:
- RENDER_MODE=static: all content routes prerendered; SSR only for the fallback catch-alls (§2.2 table — catch-alls themselves land in a later phase)
- RENDER_MODE=dynamic: integration flips all content routes to prerender = false; loaders are skipped (build needs no BUILD_TOKEN) per the §7.1 note
- RENDER_MODE=hybrid: exactly the routes listed in HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES flip to SSR; all other content routes stay prerendered
- CI dual-mode build smoke green: RENDER_MODE=static and RENDER_MODE=dynamic both build (§12.3)
- §2.2 hard rule check: grep/lint proves zero RENDER_MODE reads in src/pages and src/components — any PR branching template logic on RENDER_MODE fails review
notes: Spec: §2.2, §7.1 (dynamic note), §12.3, §12.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E7.1 build-info integration (astro:build:done) → /__build.json {built_at, content_snapshot_at from loader shared module, git_sha, render_mode, locales}
description:
## Why
- §3.3: /__build.json is the deployment ground truth. The whole scheduled-rebuild confirmation loop (§3.2 step 5: poll until content_snapshot_at in the file ≥ recorded value) and the most important production alert (§14 build-age monitor) read this file. Wrong fields here silently break freshness guarantees.

## What
- Implement src/integrations/build-info.ts with the astro:build:done hook writing /__build.json into the publish dir.
- Fields per the §3.3 example: built_at (now, ISO UTC), content_snapshot_at (from the P2-E3.1 loader shared module), git_sha (short), render_mode (from RENDER_MODE), locales (from config).
- Test with seeded loader data that content_snapshot_at equals the loader-observed max(updated_at).

## Out of scope
- ConfirmBuild polling (P3); Worker-side consumption (§3.4, freshness phase).
design:
- §3.3: emitted by a tiny Astro integration on astro:build:done into the publish dir
- src/integrations/build-info.ts per the §4 layout
- content_snapshot_at: the loader records it; the integration reads it from a shared module (§3.3) — never recomputed independently
- git_sha: short SHA from the CI/build environment
- Contract consumers (§3.3): Worker (memoized 60 s), ConfirmBuild (§3.2 step 5), build-age monitor (§14) — treat the shape as frozen
acceptance_criteria:
- Built dist contains /__build.json with exactly the §3.3 fields: built_at, content_snapshot_at, git_sha, render_mode, locales
- built_at and content_snapshot_at are valid ISO-8601 UTC timestamps
- content_snapshot_at = max(updated_at) observed by the Content Layer loaders during this build (read from the P2-E3.1 shared module) — verified against seeded data
- render_mode reflects RENDER_MODE; locales reflects the configured ["fr","ar","en"]
- Field names match §3.3 byte-for-byte (downstream consumers: ConfirmBuild polling, Worker staleness check, build-age monitor)
notes: Spec: §3.3, §3.2 step 5, §14. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E7 — Build info + render-mode integration + first CF deploy
description:
## Why
- /__build.json (§3.3) is the ground truth for "what data is baked into the current deployment": ConfirmBuild (§3.2 step 5) polls it to mark builds succeeded, the Worker compares against it for staleness, and the build-age monitor (§14) alarms on it. P3 cannot ship without this contract.
- §2.2/R4: render mode is per-deployment configuration — one env var flips prerendering through an integration at build time while templates stay completely ignorant. This epic implements that mechanism and proves it in CI.
- The first Git-connected Cloudflare deploy makes the P2 static MVP real on staging, end to end.

## What
- src/integrations/build-info.ts: astro:build:done hook emits /__build.json into the publish dir with {built_at, content_snapshot_at, git_sha, render_mode, locales} (§3.3); content_snapshot_at read from the loader shared module (P2-E3.1).
- src/integrations/render-mode.ts: astro:route:setup flips route.prerender per RENDER_MODE — static | hybrid (HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES list) | dynamic (§2.2); CI dual-mode build smoke (static + dynamic, §12.3).
- frontend/wrangler.jsonc: Static Assets binding ASSETS + KV binding FRESHNESS placeholder; Git-connected Cloudflare build deploying the full static site to staging.

## Out of scope
- The custom Worker entry + request routing (§3.4) and KV dirty-marker logic (§3.5) — freshness phase; scheduled rebuild jobs (P3); deploy hook wiring from Phoenix (§3.2, P3).
design:
- Spec: §3.3 /__build.json contract, §2.2 render modes, §12.3 frontend deploy, §16 P2-E7. Critical path: P3 (rebuild pipeline) confirms builds by polling /__build.json
- /__build.json consumers: Worker staleness comparison (memoized 60 s), ConfirmBuild (§3.2 step 5), build-age monitor (§14) — field names are a contract, do not rename
- Integrations live in src/integrations/ per §4: build-info.ts, render-mode.ts
- Env (§12.4): RENDER_MODE + HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES build vars; BUILD_TOKEN secret in CF build env; PUBLIC_SITE_URL/API_BASE_URL/MEDIA_BASE_URL on the build
- R4: render mode is per-deployment configuration applied at the routing layer — templates never know (§2.2 hard rule)
acceptance_criteria:
- Staging serves the full static site (§16 P2-E7 AC) — all locales, from Workers Static Assets via Git-connected build
- /__build.json fields correct (§16 P2-E7 AC): built_at, content_snapshot_at, git_sha, render_mode, locales exactly per the §3.3 contract
- content_snapshot_at equals the loader-observed max(updated_at) from the P2-E3.1 shared module
- render-mode integration flips route.prerender per §2.2 (static | hybrid via HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES | dynamic); CI dual-mode build smoke green (RENDER_MODE=static AND =dynamic both build, §12.3)
- §2.2 hard rule verified: zero template/component reads of RENDER_MODE
- wrangler.jsonc carries the ASSETS assets binding and a FRESHNESS KV binding placeholder
notes: Spec: §3.3, §2.2, §12.3, §12.4, §16 P2-E7. Critical path. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P8-E3.1 Lighthouse CI budgets green on prod URLs + CWV field-data plan (CrUX/RUM via Sentry)
description:
## Why
§16 P8-E3 requires the §15.5 lab budgets proven on production (not just PR previews) plus a plan for post-launch field data — lab-only CWV is insufficient evidence for the R8 SEO goal once real Moroccan/diaspora traffic arrives.

## What
- Point the existing Lighthouse CI budget config (§12.3) at production URLs covering each template family in all three locales; run on simulated 4G.
- Verify per-page JS weight: ≤ 100 KB gz detail (MapLibre must remain lazy-loaded, §7.5), ≤ 60 KB gz landings.
- Fix regressions using the §7.6/§8 levers (image dims, preconnects, font-display, hero fetchpriority, blurhash) and re-run to green.
- Write the CWV field-data plan: CrUX origin monitoring + RUM through the Sentry browser SDK shipped in P8-E2.1, owner named, review cadence set.

## Out of scope
- API load testing (P8-E3.2); functional e2e (P8-E3.3).
design:
- §15.5 budget numbers are the contract: LCP < 2.5 s on simulated 4G, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200 ms, 100/60 KB gz JS caps
- §12.3 already runs LHCI on PR previews — reuse the budget config, point at prod URLs
- §7.6 performance levers if budgets fail: explicit image dimensions, preconnect to media.<domain> and api.<domain>, self-hosted fonts with font-display: swap, zero render-blocking third-party JS
- §8: LCP hero uses eager fetchpriority=high with blurhash placeholder
- Field data: CrUX (origin-level) + Sentry browser SDK RUM (release-tagged, from P8-E2.1)
acceptance_criteria:
- Lighthouse CI run against production URLs (landing, category/city index, project detail, listing detail, search shell; fr + ar + en) passes all §15.5 budgets: LCP < 2.5 s (4G), CLS < 0.1, INP < 200 ms
- JS weight budgets hold: ≤ 100 KB gzipped on detail pages (MapLibre lazy per §7.5), ≤ 60 KB on landings
- Regressions found are fixed (or filed with owner + fix-before-launch flag) and the run repeated to green
- CWV field-data plan written: CrUX dashboard + RUM via Sentry browser SDK, with named owner and review cadence (§16 P8-E3)
notes: Spec: §15.5, §16 P8-E3, §12.3 (LHCI), §7.5, §7.6, §8. Open decisions: none blocking. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P8-E3 — Performance gate (§15.5 budgets on prod)
description:
## Why
R8 demands excellent Core Web Vitals; §15.5 turns that into hard budgets and §16 P8-E3 makes meeting them **on production** a launch gate, adding a field-data plan (CrUX/RUM via Sentry) so lab numbers are validated by real users after launch. The full §15.4 e2e matrix is the behavioral regression gate covering the freshness state machine — the product's core mechanism (R1–R3).

## What
- Run Lighthouse CI against production URLs (landing, category index, project detail, listing detail, search shell — fr/ar/en) and bring all §15.5 budgets green.
- k6 smoke: /search and /listings/geo at 200 rps sustained, p95 < 300 ms (staging, rate limits relaxed).
- Execute the complete §15.4 Playwright matrix vs staging as the launch-gate run.
- Document the CWV field-data plan: CrUX monitoring + RUM via the Sentry browser SDK, with owner and review cadence.

## Out of scope
- Wiring monitors (P8-E2) and security load tests of rate limits (P8-E1.1 — note: k6 here runs with limits relaxed; the rate-limit verification belongs to the security gate).
design:
- §15.5 budgets: LCP < 2.5 s (4G) / CLS < 0.1 / INP < 200 ms / ≤ 100 KB JS gz detail pages / ≤ 60 KB landings — enforced by Lighthouse CI (wired in §12.3 CI on previews; this gate runs it against prod)
- §15.5 load: k6 on /search + geo, 200 rps sustained, p95 < 300 ms, staging rate limits relaxed
- §15.4 matrix: freshness state machine (ssr-new ≤ 2 min / ssr-dirty ≤ 2 min / rebuild→static / unpublish 404 / slug 301) + facets from custom field + map bbox + inquiry (Turnstile test keys) + AR RTL, asserted via x-immo-serving headers (§3.4)
- §7.5 JS budget mechanics: MapLibre lazy-loaded only when map scrolls into view
- Field data: CrUX + RUM via the Sentry browser SDK already shipped by P8-E2.1
acceptance_criteria:
- Lighthouse CI green on production URLs against §15.5 budgets: LCP < 2.5 s (4G), CLS < 0.1, INP < 200 ms, ≤ 100 KB gzipped JS on detail pages, ≤ 60 KB on landings
- k6 smoke passes: /search and /listings/geo sustain 200 rps with p95 < 300 ms (rate limits relaxed in staging per §15.5)
- Full §15.4 Playwright matrix green vs staging as the launch-gate run
- CWV field-data plan documented (CrUX/RUM via Sentry per §16 P8-E3) with owner and review cadence
notes: Spec: §15.4, §15.5, §16 P8-E3, §3.4 (x-immo-serving), §7.5 (JS budget), §12.3 (LHCI in CI). Open decisions: D1 (interval affects nothing user-visible — freshness asserts stay ≤ 2 min via SSR). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. P8-E3.3 harness exists from P4-E2.4; here it runs as the full-matrix launch gate.

title: P8-E2.2 Restore drill on prod-sized data (RTO ≤ 4 h per §18) + all /infra/runbooks/ reviewed (deploy, rollback, restore, rotate-secrets, serving-stale triage, VPS-down comms) + on-call/alert routing agreed
description:
## Why
§16 P8-E2 requires the restore drill on prod-sized data, runbook review, and agreed on-call/alert routing before launch. The single-box design (§12.2) is only acceptable because recovery is rehearsed: §18 budgets RTO ≤ 4 h, and §3.7 keeps the static site serving meanwhile.

## What
- Run the scripted restore drill (§12.2) against a production-sized dataset: restore from pgBackRest backups in Hetzner Object Storage into a scratch container, verify checksums, measure wall-clock time against the 4 h RTO; archive the log.
- Confirm the monthly restore-drill calendar task exists and the backup-failure alert (wired in P8-E2.1) fires when a backup is broken.
- Review each /infra/runbooks/ document against current reality: deploy, rollback (Worker versions + Coolify), restore drill, rotate-secrets (updated by P8-E1.2), "site serving stale" triage (from P4-E5), VPS-down comms.
- Agree and document on-call/alert routing: owner + channel per §14 alert, explicitly including who gets paged by BuildAgeMonitor.

## Out of scope
- Building new monitors (P8-E2.1); changing backup architecture (locked per §12.2/D12).
design:
- §12.2: pgBackRest nightly full + WAL archiving (RPO ≤ 5 min) to Hetzner Object Storage (EU, D12); retention 14 d incremental / 90 d weekly; monthly scripted restore drill with checksum verification
- §18: VPS-dies risk accepted because static keeps serving (§3.7) — restore drill ≤ RTO 4 h is the recovery contract
- §14 runbook set lives in /infra/runbooks/; rollback covers both Worker versions and Coolify (D11)
- Routing must name an owner for the BuildAgeMonitor page (§14: "page someone")
acceptance_criteria:
- Restore drill executed against a prod-sized dataset using the §12.2 scripted procedure (scratch container + checksum verification); total time ≤ 4 h RTO (§18); drill log archived and the backup-failure alert path confirmed
- All six §14 runbooks reviewed and updated to match reality: deploy, rollback (Worker versions + Coolify), restore drill, secret rotation, "site serving stale" triage, VPS-down comms
- On-call ownership and alert routing (who is paged for which §14 alert, via which channel) agreed and written into the runbooks
- Monthly restore-drill calendar task in place (§12.2)
notes: Spec: §16 P8-E2, §14 (runbooks list), §12.2 (backup/restore mechanics), §18 (RTO ≤ 4 h), §3.7 (degradation context). Open decisions: D11 (Coolify), D12 (backup target). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. Blocked by P8-E2.1 (alerts must exist before routing is agreed).

title: P3-E1.3 Immo.Jobs.ConfirmBuild: poll PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json (snooze 60 s, max 30 min) — success when content_snapshot_at ≥ recorded value → succeeded + built_at; timeout → failed + alert
description:
## Why
- Closes the R1 loop: triggering a deploy hook is fire-and-forget — without confirmation, a broken hook or failed CF build leaves the site silently stale (§14 failure mode, §18 row 2).
- In the freshness model, `succeeded` + `built_at` is the ground truth that future skip checks and the P4 re-arm step key off ("changed since last SUCCESSFUL build"); a `failed` mark is what keeps the self-healing loop honest.

## What
- `Immo.Jobs.ConfirmBuild` (queue `rebuild`, §6.5), scheduled by RebuildSite step 5.
- Polls `https://<PUBLIC_SITE_URL>/__build.json` (§3.3 contract: `built_at`, `content_snapshot_at`, `git_sha`, `render_mode`, `locales`).
- **Snooze 60 s** between polls, **max 30 min** total window.
- Success when the file's `content_snapshot_at` ≥ the value recorded in the builds row at trigger time → mark `succeeded`, store `built_at` (+ `git_sha` from the file).
- Timeout → mark `failed`, set `error`, dispatch alert (§14: alert on build `failed` status).
- Tests with mocked HTTP: stale file → snooze; fresh file → succeeded; window elapsed → failed; network error → snooze not crash.

## Out of scope
- BuildAgeMonitor cadence/threshold alerting (P3-E3.1) — this task only alerts on the explicit timeout-failure path.
design:
- Queue rebuild; snooze 60 s; absolute timeout 30 min (§6.5 row ConfirmBuild)
- Poll target: PUBLIC_SITE_URL + /__build.json (env §12.4); fields per §3.3: built_at, content_snapshot_at, git_sha, render_mode, locales
- Success predicate: file.content_snapshot_at >= builds.content_snapshot_at recorded at trigger (§3.2 step 5)
- On success: status=succeeded, built_at = file.built_at; on timeout: status=failed + alert
- failed status is consumed by P3-E2 banner and P3-E3 alerting
acceptance_criteria:
- /__build.json with content_snapshot_at >= the recorded builds.content_snapshot_at -> builds row marked succeeded with built_at (and git_sha) captured from the file
- Older content_snapshot_at in the file -> job snoozes 60 s (snooze return asserted)
- 30 min without confirmation -> builds row failed + error set + alert dispatched (§14 build-failed alert)
- Unreachable/erroring site handled as snooze/retry, not a crash loop
- Job tests green with mocked HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test, §15.1)
notes: Spec: §3.2 step 5, §3.3, §6.5, §12.4 (PUBLIC_SITE_URL), §14. Risk register: §18 row 2 (alert, do not discover). /__build.json emission ships in P2-E7. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P8-E2.1 Production monitors live: Sentry Elixir (Phoenix+Oban) + browser/Worker SDK release-tagged with git_sha from /__build.json + uptime checks on /healthz (DB ping) and /__health (Worker) + alerts: build failed, Oban retries exhausted, webhook-signature failure spike, disk > 80%, backup failure
description:
## Why
§14 defines the production observability surface and §16 P8-E2 requires it live before launch. The BuildAgeMonitor is called out as "the alert that matters most": without it, a silently broken build pipeline degrades to stale statics with no error signal once dirty TTLs expire (§18 risk row).

## What
- Configure Sentry in prod: Elixir SDK (Phoenix + Oban) and browser/Worker SDK (islands + SSR), both release-tagged with `git_sha` read from `/__build.json` (§3.3); verify events land with correct release attribution.
- Stand up uptime checks (UptimeRobot/BetterStack): `GET /healthz` on api (DB ping) and `GET /__health` on the site (Worker liveness).
- Wire and test-fire the full §14 alert list: BuildAgeMonitor (built_at age > 2× interval), build `failed`, Oban retries exhausted, webhook-signature failure spike, VPS disk > 80%, backup job failure.
- Publish dashboards: builds history (admin screen from P3-E2) and the serving-mode ratio from sampled `x-immo-serving` headers via Workers analytics — the watch surface for P8-E4 hypercare and the scraping/freshness-bug signal (§14).

## Out of scope
- Restore drill + runbook review + routing agreement (P8-E2.2).
design:
- §14: Sentry Elixir SDK covers Phoenix + Oban; browser/Worker SDK covers islands + SSR; release = git_sha from /__build.json (§3.3)
- §14: GET /healthz does a DB ping on api; /__health is Worker liveness (already in run_worker_first globs §3.4); UptimeRobot/BetterStack as checker
- §6.5/§14: BuildAgeMonitor cron every 15 min; alert if site built_at older than 2× REBUILD_CRON interval
- Alert channels: email/Slack as wired in P3-E3 — extend to the full §14 alert list; agree routing in P8-E2.2
- §12.4: SENTRY_DSN set for backend (VPS) and frontend (build)
acceptance_criteria:
- Sentry receives events from Phoenix, Oban, browser islands, and the SSR Worker in prod, each tagged with the git_sha of the current /__build.json release
- Uptime checks active on api /healthz (DB ping) and site /__health (Worker liveness); a forced failure pages within the provider's check interval
- Every §14 alert test-fired once: BuildAgeMonitor threshold (built_at > 2× interval), build failed, Oban retries exhausted, webhook-signature failure spike, disk > 80%, backup failure
- Serving-mode dashboard live: x-immo-serving ratios from Workers analytics + builds-history screen; baseline ratio recorded (SSR share near zero between publishes per §14)
notes: Spec: §14, §3.3 (/__build.json git_sha), §3.4 (/__health), §6.5 (BuildAgeMonitor), §12.4. Open decisions: none blocking. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P8-E2 — Ops gate (§14 monitors live in prod)
description:
## Why
§16 P8-E2 gates launch on §14 being real in production: error tracking, health checks, the BuildAgeMonitor (the guard against the §18 "build pipeline silently broken → stale site" failure mode, where dirty TTLs lapse and stale statics return with no error signal), alert routing, and a proven restore path. P8-E4 hypercare depends on the serving-mode dashboard this epic makes live.

## What
- Production monitors per §14: Sentry on both stacks release-tagged with `git_sha` from `/__build.json`; uptime checks on `GET /healthz` (DB ping) and site `/__health` (Worker liveness); LiveDashboard admin-gated.
- Alerts wired and test-fired: BuildAgeMonitor (built_at age > 2× interval), build `failed` status, Oban retries exhausted, webhook-signature failure spike, VPS disk > 80%, backup job failure.
- Dashboards: builds history (admin) + `x-immo-serving` ratio via Workers analytics (static / ssr-new / ssr-dirty / stale-fallback).
- Restore drill on prod-sized data against the §18 RTO of ≤ 4 h, using the §12.2 scripted drill (scratch container + checksum verification).
- Review all six runbooks in /infra/runbooks/; agree and document on-call/alert routing.

## Out of scope
- Security controls verification (P8-E1); performance budgets (P8-E3).
- HA/multi-box architecture — single-box SPOF is accepted knowingly per §12.2.
design:
- §14 errors: Sentry Elixir SDK (Phoenix+Oban) + browser/Worker SDK (islands + SSR), releases tagged with git_sha from /__build.json; SENTRY_DSN per §12.4
- §14 health: LiveDashboard admin-gated; GET /healthz (DB ping) + site /__health (Worker liveness) under UptimeRobot/BetterStack
- §14 "alert that matters most": BuildAgeMonitor — built_at age > 2× interval ⇒ page someone (guards the silent-stale failure mode)
- §14 dashboards: builds history (admin) + x-immo-serving sampled via Workers analytics → static/ssr-new/ssr-dirty/stale-fallback ratio
- §14 runbooks: deploy, rollback (Worker versions + Coolify), restore drill, secret rotation, "site serving stale" triage, VPS-down comms
- §12.2 backups: pgBackRest nightly full + WAL (RPO ≤ 5 min) to Hetzner Object Storage; scripted restore into scratch container with checksum verification
acceptance_criteria:
- All §14 monitors and alerts live and test-fired in production: Sentry (Elixir + browser/Worker, release-tagged), uptime checks on /healthz and /__health, BuildAgeMonitor, build-failed / Oban-retries-exhausted / webhook-signature-spike / disk>80% / backup-failure alerts
- Serving-mode dashboard (x-immo-serving ratios via Workers analytics) and builds-history dashboard available — required by P8-E4 hypercare
- Restore drill passed on prod-sized data within RTO ≤ 4 h (§18); evidence archived
- All six /infra/runbooks/ reviewed and current; on-call/alert routing agreed and documented (§16 P8-E2)
notes: Spec: §14 (entire), §16 P8-E2, §6.5 (BuildAgeMonitor), §12.2 (backups/restore), §18 (RTO ≤ 4 h), §12.4 (SENTRY_DSN). Open decisions: D11 (Coolify default — rollback runbook assumes it), D12 (backup target). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P3-E1.2 Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite: skip-if-unchanged (max updated_at across published entities + pending redirects vs last content_snapshot_at) + deploy-hook POST + builds row lifecycle + unique 300 s + trigger cron|manual + re-arm placeholder (real re-arm in P4-E4.4)
description:
## Why
- The heart of R1: scheduled rebuilds that cost **zero build minutes on quiet nights** (skip-if-unchanged) and can never stampede (queue concurrency 1 + unique 300 s).
- In the freshness model this job defines `content_snapshot_at` — the reference point that states B/C compare against (`dirty_at > built_at`) and that ConfirmBuild verifies. Its skip logic shares the single `published/1` predicate (§5.13) so "what is published" never forks.

## What
Implement `Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite` (queue `rebuild`, `unique: [period: 300]`) — the §3.2 algorithm:
1. **Load last successful build** from `builds` (`status = succeeded`, max `content_snapshot_at`).
2. **Skip-if-unchanged:** compute `max(updated_at)` across **published** `projects`, `listings`, `developers`, `property_types`, `media` (via `Catalog.published/1`). If ≤ last `content_snapshot_at` **and** no pending redirects → insert `builds` row `status = skipped`, stop.
3. **Re-arm dirty markers:** placeholder hook only (no-op) — real implementation in P4-E4.4 once the KV layer exists (§3.2 step 3).
4. **Trigger the build:** POST the Cloudflare deploy-hook URL (`DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` secret) via the `Immo.Edge` deploy-hook client. Insert `builds` row `status = running`, `trigger = :cron`, `content_snapshot_at = now()`.
5. **Confirm completion:** schedule `Immo.Jobs.ConfirmBuild` (P3-E1.3).
6. **Manual trigger:** same job with `trigger = :manual` bypasses skip-if-unchanged (admin Rebuild-now button consumes this in P3-E2).
- HTTP mocked in tests (Bypass/Req.Test per §15.1); no live CF calls in the suite.

## Out of scope
- ConfirmBuild polling (P3-E1.3); the admin button (P3-E2.1); real KV re-arm (P4-E4.4); GH Actions trigger transport (P3-E4 behind config).
design:
- Queue rebuild (concurrency 1), unique: [period: 300] (§6.5 row RebuildSite)
- Step 1: last successful build = builds row status=succeeded with max content_snapshot_at
- Step 2 skip check: max(updated_at) over published projects, listings, developers, property_types, media via Catalog.published/1 (§5.13 single predicate — no second definition) AND no pending redirects -> insert status=skipped, stop
- Step 3 re-arm: behaviour/callback no-op placeholder now; P4-E4.4 supplies the real implementation (self-healing after failed builds)
- Step 4: POST DEPLOY_HOOK_URL (trust path 4, §10.1); insert builds row status=running, trigger=:cron|:manual, content_snapshot_at=now()
- Quiet nights cost zero build minutes (§3.2 step 2 rationale)
acceptance_criteria:
- No-change run inserts a builds row status=skipped and does NOT call the deploy hook (asserted via mocked HTTP)
- Changed-content run POSTs the deploy hook and inserts builds row status=running, trigger=cron, content_snapshot_at=now()
- trigger=manual run bypasses skip-if-unchanged (§3.2 step 6)
- Pending redirects alone (no entity change) defeat the skip
- unique period 300 s: double enqueue executes once
- ConfirmBuild scheduled after a triggered build (step 5 handoff)
- Oban job tests green with mocked CF HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test, §15.1)
notes: Spec: §3.2 steps 1-6, §5.13, §6.5, §15.1. Open decisions: D1, D3. Risk register: §18 row 5 (hourly builds vs CF quota — skip keeps spend down). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E2.6 Seeds: ≥3 property types (apartment/land/rental incl. filter_config + schema_hints), ≥40 listings, fr/ar content + EXPLAIN index verification
description:
## Why
- §16 P1-E2 AC requires realistic fixtures (≥3 types, ≥40 listings, ar/fr content) and "GIN/partial indexes verified with EXPLAIN on seed data" — proving R9 polymorphism with three genuinely different verticals (apartment/land/rental) and giving every later epic (admin UI, API, search, frontend) data to develop against.
- fr/ar content exercises the i18n jsonb maps end-to-end (R8) including RTL-relevant Arabic strings.

## What
- Seed ≥3 property_types — apartment, land, rental — with full `filter_config` and `schema_hints` (§5.3).
- ≥40 listings spanning the types: realistic attributes (bedrooms, bathrooms, floor, zoning, buildable_ratio, lease_term per §5.4 examples), MAD prices, price_on_request cases, Moroccan cities; some standalone (project_id null), some under seeded developers/projects.
- fr + ar i18n content in title/description/seo (en optional, D5); mixed publish states and listing statuses for predicate-matrix realism.
- EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) verification on seed data: attributes containment query uses the GIN jsonb_path_ops index; published-only query uses the partial index. Evidence documented.

## Out of scope
- Media fixtures with real R2 objects (P1-E4); inquiry fixtures (P1-E6).
design:
- Seed developers + projects + at least one active subscription so the billing-gate matrix and admin flows run against realistic data
- filter_config exemplars: price range (source column), surface_m2 range (column), bedrooms select (attribute), zoning select (custom_field)
- Custom fields seeded for at least one type to exercise §5.5 (incl. one searchable=true)
- EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) run against seed volume; output captured in PR/docs
acceptance_criteria:
- Seeds run idempotently (mix run priv/repo/seeds.exs) and green in CI
- ≥3 property types seeded (apartment, land, rental) each with filter_config (facets: key, kind range|select|boolean, source column|attribute|custom_field, unit, min/max, options) and schema_hints (§5.3)
- ≥40 listings across the types with realistic attributes, MAD prices, cities; mix of standalone and project-attached; mix of draft/published and statuses (available/reserved/sold)
- fr AND ar i18n content present in title/description/seo maps (§16 AC; en optional per D5)
- EXPLAIN evidence attached: GIN jsonb_path_ops index scan for an attributes containment query AND partial published index usage for a published-only scan (§16 AC)
notes: Spec: §16 P1-E2 AC, §5.3/§5.4/§5.5. Open decisions: D5 (fr+ar required, en optional). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E2.3 Catalog.published/1 — the single composable publish predicate (+BILLING_ENFORCED subscription gate hook) + §15.1 predicate matrix tests
description:
## Why
- §5.13 is explicit: "published" has exactly **one** definition — `published_at IS NOT NULL AND published_at <= now()` and, for projects/listings, the owning developer has an `active|trialing` subscription when `BILLING_ENFORCED`. Implemented once as a composable Ecto query and used by read API, sitemap endpoint, search, geo, and the skip-if-unchanged check. "No second definition anywhere."
- Divergent publish logic is the failure mode behind ghost pages and missing content across the whole R1–R3 freshness machine; R10/D13 require the billing gate to exist and be tested even while the flag is off at launch.

## What
- `Catalog.published/1` composable Ecto query per §5.13.
- Billing gate hook: projects/listings additionally require owning developer subscription status in `active|trialing` when the `BILLING_ENFORCED` feature flag is set (§5.9 statuses).
- §15.1 predicate matrix tests: {published_at: null, future, past} × {subscription: none, trialing, active, past_due, canceled} × {BILLING_ENFORCED: true, false}, for projects and listings; developers gated on published_at only.

## Out of scope
- Wiring into API/sitemap/search/geo/skip-if-unchanged callers (their own tickets compose this function).
design:
- def published(queryable): published_at IS NOT NULL AND published_at <= now(); for projects/listings joins owning developer subscriptions with status in (active, trialing) when BILLING_ENFORCED (§5.13, §5.9)
- BILLING_ENFORCED read from runtime config/env (§12.4; default false per D13)
- Consumers (wired in their own tickets): read API (P1-E5), sitemap + redirects dumps, search/geo (P5), skip-if-unchanged (P3) — grep-able single definition
acceptance_criteria:
- Exactly one implementation: Catalog.published/1 returns a composable Ecto query usable for developers, projects and listings; callers compose it, never re-implement it (§5.13)
- Matrix tests green (§15.1): published_at null → excluded; future published_at → excluded; past published_at → included
- Billing gate matrix: BILLING_ENFORCED=true + owning developer subscription past_due/canceled/none → projects/listings excluded; active|trialing → included; BILLING_ENFORCED=false → gate inert, all past-published included
- Developers themselves are not billing-gated (gate applies to projects/listings per §5.13)
- §16 P1-E2 AC satisfied: predicate matrix incl. billing gate green in CI
notes: Spec: §5.13, §5.9, §15.1, §16 P1-E2 AC. Open decisions: D13 (BILLING_ENFORCED=false at launch — publish gate inert but code path tested). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E2.2 Immo.Catalog context: CRUD + publish/unpublish transitions + slug immutability after first publish (§3.8)
description:
## Why
- §6.1: Immo.Catalog owns developers, projects, listings, property_types, custom_fields, redirects plus publish/unpublish transitions — the write-side API every admin surface (P1-E3) calls; A3 makes Phoenix the only writer.
- §3.8 / R8: slugs are SEO equity — immutable after first publish by default; slug changes must mint 301 redirects so old URLs never die.

## What
- CRUD functions for all §6.1 Catalog-owned entities.
- Publish/unpublish transitions setting/clearing `published_at` (§5.13 semantics; the composable predicate itself is P1-E2.3).
- Slug immutability after first publish; admin-role override; on slug change write a `redirects` row (old_path, new_path, 301) (§3.8, §5.11).
- `listings.attributes` validated against the property type's `schema_hints` + `custom_fields` (§5.4, §5.5) — required custom fields enforced, field_type respected.
- Listing location inheritance from project when fields blank (§5.4).

## Out of scope
- published/1 predicate + billing gate (P1-E2.3); audit wrapper (P1-E2.4); KV dirty-marking on transitions (P4); admin UI (P1-E3).
design:
- Immo.Catalog public API: create/update/delete per entity + publish/2, unpublish/2 transitions on published_at (§6.1)
- Slug lock: changeset rejects slug change once the record has ever been published, unless actor role = admin (§3.8)
- Slug-change side effect: insert redirects row {old_path, new_path, 301} transactionally (§3.8, §5.11); old_path/new_path computed via the path authority (Immo.Edge.Paths once it lands in P1-E5.2)
- attributes validation driven by property_type.schema_hints + custom_fields rows (§5.4/§5.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- CRUD + publish/unpublish for developers/projects/listings/property_types/custom_fields/redirects covered by context tests
- Slug change on a once-published record rejected for non-admin actors; admin override succeeds AND writes a redirects row (old_path, new_path, 301) in the same transaction (§3.8)
- listings.attributes rejected when violating schema_hints/custom_fields (unknown keys, wrong field_type, missing required)
- Listing location inheritance honored: blank address/city/region fall back to project values when project_id set (§5.4)
- Ecto changeset validation on every write; no raw SQL with interpolation (§13)
notes: Spec: §6.1, §3.8, §5.2/§5.4/§5.5/§5.11. KV dirty-marking on slug change is P4 scope — only the redirects row + transitions land here. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E2.1 Migrations: all §5 tables + indexes (uuid v7 PKs, citext, timestamptz, enums, GIN jsonb_path_ops on listings.attributes, partial published index, (lat,lng) btree, slug-unique-per-type)
description:
## Why
- R9: the polymorphic schema (property_types + listings.attributes JSONB + custom_fields) is what makes new verticals data-not-schema-rewrites.
- Critical path: every other P1 epic (admin, media, API, CRM) reads/writes these tables; index correctness here is what the §16 EXPLAIN acceptance verifies.

## What — enumerated §5.1–§5.12 tables
- **§5.1 developers**: name, slug (citext unique, immutable after publish §3.8), description jsonb i18n, logo_media_id fk → media nullable, contact jsonb, seo jsonb i18n, published_at timestamptz nullable.
- **§5.2 projects**: developer_id fk required; title jsonb i18n / slug citext unique; status enum `preselling|under_construction|delivered`; description jsonb; address, city, region, country (ISO-3166 alpha-2, default `MA`); lat/lng float nullable; delivery_date date; amenities jsonb; seo jsonb; featured boolean default false; published_at. Indexes: (published_at), (city, status), (developer_id).
- **§5.3 property_types**: key citext unique; label jsonb i18n; url_segment jsonb i18n; filter_config jsonb; schema_hints jsonb; position integer.
- **§5.4 listings**: project_id fk nullable (null = standalone); property_type_id fk required; title jsonb / slug citext unique **per property_type**; description jsonb; price numeric(14,2) nullable; price_on_request boolean default false; currency char(3) default `MAD`; status enum `available|reserved|sold|rented|hidden`; address, city, region; lat/lng; surface_m2 numeric(10,2); attributes jsonb; seo jsonb; published_at. Indexes: GIN `jsonb_path_ops` on attributes; (property_type_id, status, published_at); (city); (price); (lat,lng) btree pair; partial index WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL.
- **§5.5 custom_fields**: property_type_id fk; key citext unique per type; label jsonb; field_type enum `string|integer|decimal|boolean|select|multiselect|date`; options jsonb; searchable boolean; required boolean; position integer.
- **§5.6 media**: attachable_type + attachable_id (polymorphic: Project, Listing, Developer); kind enum `photo|floorplan|brochure|document|logo`; r2_key; content_type, byte_size, width, height; blurhash nullable; alt jsonb i18n; position. Index (attachable_type, attachable_id, position).
- **§5.7 inquiries**: listing_id fk nullable, project_id fk nullable, name, email, phone, message text, locale, consent boolean, source, status enum `new|contacted|closed`, handled_by_user_id fk nullable.
- **§5.8 users**: phx.gen.auth columns + role enum + developer_id fk (coordinate with P1-E1.1 if already created there).
- **§5.9 subscriptions**: developer_id fk, plan enum `basic|featured|enterprise`, status enum `trialing|active|past_due|canceled`, provider enum `stripe|cmi|manual`, provider_subscription_id, current_period_start/end, cancel_at_period_end. **payments**: subscription_id fk, amount numeric(14,2), currency, status enum `pending|succeeded|failed|refunded`, provider, provider_payment_id unique (idempotency), invoice_url, paid_at, raw_event jsonb.
- **§5.10 builds**: status enum `queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped`, trigger enum `cron|manual`, content_snapshot_at, started_at, finished_at, built_at, error text, git_sha.
- **§5.11 redirects**: old_path citext unique, new_path, http_status int default 301, reason.
- **§5.12 audit_log**: user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, diff jsonb, at.
- All tables: id uuid (v7) PK, inserted_at/updated_at timestamptz; citext extension (§5 preamble).

## Out of scope
- Context functions/changesets beyond what migrations need (P1-E2.2/.5); seeds (P1-E2.6).
design:
- §5.1 developers: name, slug citext unique, description jsonb i18n, logo_media_id fk media nullable, contact jsonb, seo jsonb, published_at timestamptz nullable
- §5.2 projects: developer_id fk required, title jsonb/slug citext unique, status enum preselling|under_construction|delivered, address/city/region/country, lat/lng float, delivery_date, amenities jsonb, seo jsonb, featured bool, published_at
- §5.4 listings: project_id fk nullable, property_type_id fk required, price numeric(14,2), price_on_request bool, currency char(3) MAD, status enum available|reserved|sold|rented|hidden, surface_m2 numeric(10,2), attributes jsonb, published_at
- §5.3/§5.5: property_types (key citext unique, label/url_segment jsonb, filter_config, schema_hints, position) + custom_fields (field_type enum string|integer|decimal|boolean|select|multiselect|date, options, searchable, required, position, key unique per type)
- §5.6–§5.12: media (polymorphic attachable, kind enum photo|floorplan|brochure|document|logo, r2_key, blurhash, alt jsonb, position), inquiries, users role columns, subscriptions/payments, builds, redirects, audit_log
- PostGIS deferred (D7): bbox queries = simple range predicates over the (lat,lng) btree pair
acceptance_criteria:
- mix ecto.migrate up AND down run clean on an empty database
- All §5.1–§5.12 tables exist with the exact fields, enums and defaults (country default MA, currency char(3) default MAD, http_status default 301, featured default false)
- listings slug uniqueness is per property_type (§5.4); developers/projects slugs globally unique citext
- Indexes present and named: GIN jsonb_path_ops on listings.attributes; partial index WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL; (lat,lng) btree pair; (property_type_id,status,published_at); (city); (price); projects (published_at), (city,status), (developer_id); media (attachable_type,attachable_id,position); payments.provider_payment_id unique; redirects.old_path unique citext
- uuid v7 PKs + timestamptz inserted_at/updated_at on every table; citext extension enabled (§5 preamble)
notes: Spec: §5.1–§5.12 (field-exact). Open decisions: D7 (no PostGIS). users.role/developer_id may already exist from P1-E1.1 — coordinate so migrations stay idempotent. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P1-E2 — Schema & contexts (catalog core)
description:
## Why
- Serves R9 (polymorphic catalog: configurable property_types + JSONB attributes + admin-defined custom fields — new verticals are data, not schema rewrites) and underpins R1–R3 (the publish state drives builds/freshness), R8 (slugs/SEO fields), R10 (subscription-gated publishing).
- On the critical path / dependency spine (§16): P0-E2/E3 → **P1-E2** → P1-E5 → P2-E2 → … Every downstream epic consumes these schemas and contexts.
- §5.13 makes this epic the home of the single most load-bearing function in the system: `Catalog.published/1`, the one publish predicate shared by read API, sitemap, search, geo, and skip-if-unchanged.

## What
- All §5 migrations (§5.1–§5.12): developers, projects, property_types, listings, custom_fields, media, inquiries, users(+role), subscriptions, payments, builds, redirects, audit_log — uuid v7 PKs, citext, timestamptz, enums and indexes exactly per §5.
- Context modules per §6.1 bounded responsibilities: Immo.Catalog (CRUD, publish/unpublish transitions, published/1, slug rules §3.8), plus Media/CRM/Billing/Edge skeletons.

## Out of scope

title: P0-E4.1 Create all §12.4 vars/secrets in every store (VPS/Coolify, CF build env, Worker secrets, CI) + rotation runbook draft
description:
## Why
§12.4 is the single authoritative registry for all environment variables and secrets across the four stores; R7/§10.1 requires each of the five trust paths to have its own separately rotatable credential. This task turns the table into reality and drafts the runbook that makes rotation routine.

## What
- Create every §12.4 row in its designated store(s):
  - VPS/Coolify: DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY_BASE, PHX_HOST, BUILD_TOKEN, RENDER_TOKEN, DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID, CF_KV_API_TOKEN, REBUILD_CRON, FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS, PUBLIC_SITE_URL, R2_* (endpoint, bucket, access key/secret), TURNSTILE_SECRET, STRIPE_SECRET, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CMI_*, BILLING_ENFORCED, GRACE_DAYS, INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS, SENTRY_DSN, RESEND_API_KEY.
  - CF build env: BUILD_TOKEN (astro:env server secret), PUBLIC_SITE_URL, MEDIA_BASE_URL, API_BASE_URL, RENDER_MODE, HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES, THEME, LOCALES, TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, frontend SENTRY_DSN.
  - Worker secrets: RENDER_TOKEN via `wrangler secret put` (never in client bundle).
  - CI: secrets the §12.3 workflows need.
- Use placeholder values where the consumer doesn't exist yet (e.g. Stripe/CMI until P6) — the rows must still exist.
- Draft `infra/runbooks/rotate-secrets`: §10.1 comma-separated token-set rotation (add new → deploy consumers → remove old, zero downtime; quarterly + on personnel change).
- Document the §12.4 rule: adding an env var without updating the table fails review.

## Out of scope
- BearerAuth plug consuming the tokens (§6.4, P1-E5); executing the rotation drill (P8-E1, §13); real payment-provider credentials (P6).
design:
- Store mapping follows the §12.4 "Where" column exactly: VPS · VPS + CF build env / VPS + Worker secret (BUILD_TOKEN/RENDER_TOKEN) · build + Worker (MEDIA_BASE_URL, API_BASE_URL) · build only (RENDER_MODE, HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES, THEME, LOCALES, TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY) · VPS only (the rest)

- Inputs produced by P0-E2/P0-E3: DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID, CF_KV_API_TOKEN, TURNSTILE_*, R2_*, DATABASE_URL
acceptance_criteria:
- VPS/Coolify store holds: DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY_BASE, PHX_HOST, BUILD_TOKEN, RENDER_TOKEN, DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID, CF_KV_API_TOKEN, REBUILD_CRON, FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS, PUBLIC_SITE_URL, R2_* (endpoint/bucket/access key/secret), TURNSTILE_SECRET, STRIPE_SECRET, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CMI_* (placeholders until P6), BILLING_ENFORCED, GRACE_DAYS, INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS, SENTRY_DSN, RESEND_API_KEY
- CF build env holds: BUILD_TOKEN (astro:env server secret), PUBLIC_SITE_URL, MEDIA_BASE_URL, API_BASE_URL, RENDER_MODE, HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES, THEME, LOCALES, TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, SENTRY_DSN (frontend), RESEND placeholder not required
