title: P3-E1.1 Oban config (queues default:10, rebuild:1, media:5, mailers:5, payments:5; Pruner; Cron from REBUILD_CRON runtime env) + builds table migration + Immo.Edge context
description:
## Why
- Foundation of the R1 scheduled-rebuild pipeline: the Oban runtime config (cron interval changeable without redeploy — the R1 "configurable at runtime" clause), the `builds` bookkeeping table, and the `Immo.Edge` context that owns build/freshness machinery (§6.1).
- Everything downstream (RebuildSite, ConfirmBuild, dashboard, BuildAgeMonitor, P4 re-arm) reads/writes through these pieces.

## What
- `config/runtime.exs` Oban config exactly per §3.2: repo `Immo.Repo`; plugins `[Oban.Plugins.Pruner, {Oban.Plugins.Cron, crontab: [{System.get_env("REBUILD_CRON", "0 * * * *"), Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite}]}]`; queues `[default: 10, rebuild: 1, media: 5, mailers: 5, payments: 5]`.
- Migration for `builds` per §5.10: status enum `queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped` · trigger enum `cron|manual` · `content_snapshot_at` timestamptz · `started_at` · `finished_at` · `built_at` (from `/__build.json`) · `error` text · `git_sha`.
- `Immo.Edge` context skeleton (§6.1): create/query functions for builds (last successful build = `status = succeeded`, max `content_snapshot_at`; record `skipped`/`running`/`succeeded`/`failed`), deploy-hook client module location.
- Env registry (§12.4) entries used here: `REBUILD_CRON` (no secret, default `0 * * * *`), `DEPLOY_HOOK_URL` (secret), `PUBLIC_SITE_URL`.

## Out of scope
- The RebuildSite/ConfirmBuild job logic itself (P3-E1.2 / P3-E1.3).
design:
- Queues: default:10, rebuild:1 (concurrency 1 serializes builds), media:5, mailers:5, payments:5
- Crontab entry: {System.get_env("REBUILD_CRON", "0 * * * *"), Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite} in config/runtime.exs (§3.2)
- builds.status enum queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped; builds.trigger enum cron|manual; uuid v7 PK + timestamptz per §5 conventions
- Immo.Edge context owns builds, freshness (KV writes arrive in P4), path computation, deploy-hook client (§6.1)
- REBUILD_CRON + DEPLOY_HOOK_URL + PUBLIC_SITE_URL documented in the §12.4 env registry (registry-update rule)
acceptance_criteria:
- Oban starts with the five queues and Pruner + Cron plugins exactly per the §3.2 snippet
- Changing REBUILD_CRON env (runtime.exs) changes the schedule without redeploy; default "0 * * * *"
- builds migration applies and rolls back cleanly; fields match §5.10 exactly (status, trigger, content_snapshot_at, started_at, finished_at, built_at, error, git_sha)
- Immo.Edge exposes last-successful-build lookup (status=succeeded, max content_snapshot_at) used by RebuildSite step 1
- Tests cover builds row lifecycle transitions (queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped)
notes: Spec: §3.2 (config snippet), §5.10, §6.1, §12.4. Open decisions: D1 (interval). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P8-E1.3 Pen-test pass: ZAP baseline minimum + manual auth checks (admin session, API tier 401s, webhook signatures, developer_user scoping)
description:
## Why
§16 P8-E1 requires a pen-test pass — "at minimum ZAP baseline + manual auth checks" — as part of the §13 release gate. Automated checklist verification (P8-E1.1) proves controls exist; this task attacks them.

## What
- Run OWASP ZAP baseline against the public site (Worker) and `api.<domain>`; triage every alert; fix highs/criticals; re-scan to clean.
- Manual auth matrix:
  - Admin: CSRF token enforcement on LiveView mutations, 24 h idle-timeout expiry, argon2 in use, no session fixation.
  - API tiers (§6.4): no token → 401; wrong token → 401; render token on build-tier endpoint → 401 (disjoint scopes); timing-safe comparison in code.
  - Webhooks (§6.6): tampered Stripe-Signature / CMI MAC rejected before parsing; replayed event id processed exactly once.
  - developer_user (§5.8): attempt cross-developer reads/writes through admin LiveView and any reachable API path — must be fully scoped to own developer_id.
- Probe the public tier abuse cases §10.1 calls out: firehose endpoints must not be reachable anonymously; SSR cache-busting amplification blocked by render-tier auth.
- Archive the report + remediations as evidence on the §13 gate.

## Out of scope
- Commissioning an external pen-test firm (beyond the spec minimum; recommend post-launch if budget allows).
design:
- Minimum tooling per §16 P8-E1: OWASP ZAP baseline scan; manual checks on the auth surfaces
- §6.4: BearerAuth per tier with secure_compare; pipelines api_build / api_render / api_public — scopes disjoint by design ("No" to render-on-build)
- §5.8: developer_user role carries developer_id; all queries scoped to own projects — test horizontal-privilege escalation
- §6.6: signature over raw body before parsing (Stripe-Signature / CMI MAC); replay-safe via unique provider event id
- §15.2 optional extension: schemathesis fuzz against staging if time allows
acceptance_criteria:
- ZAP baseline scan run against the public site + api host; findings triaged, highs/criticals fixed and re-scanned clean
- Manual auth checks pass: admin session CSRF + 24 h idle timeout enforced; build-tier and render-tier endpoints return 401 without/with-wrong bearer token and scopes are disjoint (render token rejected on build tier per §6.4)
- Webhook endpoints reject tampered signatures and replayed events (§6.6)
- developer_user account cannot read or mutate another developer's projects/listings via admin UI or any API surface (§5.8/§6.2 scoping)
- Pen-test report archived as §13 gate evidence
notes: Spec: §16 P8-E1 (pen-test minimum), §6.4, §6.6, §5.8, §6.2, §13, §15.2 (optional schemathesis at P8). Open decisions: D9 (CF Access would add a second factor — note in findings if recommended). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. Blocked by P8-E1.1.

title: [Immo] P0-E4 — Secrets registry instantiated + rotation runbook
description:
## Why
R7 demands a secure, least-privilege scheme with separately rotatable credentials per trust path (§10.1's five paths); §12.4 is the authoritative env/secret registry. Instantiating every variable in every store now means P1–P4 consume ready credentials instead of inventing them ad hoc, and the rotation runbook makes the §13 rotation drill (P8-E1) executable.

## What
- Create all §12.4 vars/secrets in their designated stores: VPS/Coolify env, Cloudflare build env, Worker secrets (`wrangler secret put`), CI secrets.
- Generate BUILD_TOKEN / RENDER_TOKEN (≥ 32 random bytes, base64url, distinct); capture DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID, CF_KV_API_TOKEN (namespace-scoped, write-only), Turnstile keys, R2_* credentials from P0-E2/E3 outputs.
- Draft the rotation runbook in `infra/runbooks/` per §10.1: plugs accept a comma-separated token set → add new token, deploy consumers, remove old — zero downtime; quarterly + on personnel change.
- Record the registry rule: adding an env var without updating the §12.4 table fails review.

## Out of scope
- The BearerAuth plug that consumes the tokens (§6.4, P1-E5); executing the rotation drill (§13, P8-E1); Stripe/CMI live values (P6 — placeholders now).
design:
- §12.4 registry verbatim: DATABASE_URL · SECRET_KEY_BASE, PHX_HOST · BUILD_TOKEN / RENDER_TOKEN · DEPLOY_HOOK_URL · CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID, CF_KV_API_TOKEN · REBUILD_CRON · FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS · PUBLIC_SITE_URL · R2_* (endpoint, bucket, access key/secret) · MEDIA_BASE_URL · API_BASE_URL · RENDER_MODE, HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES, THEME, LOCALES · TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY / TURNSTILE_SECRET · STRIPE_SECRET, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CMI_* · BILLING_ENFORCED, GRACE_DAYS, INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS · SENTRY_DSN (backend+frontend), RESEND_API_KEY
- Stores per §12.4 "Where" column: VPS (Coolify secrets), CF build env (astro:env server secret schema), Worker secrets (wrangler secret put — RENDER_TOKEN never in client bundle), CI
- Five trust paths, separately rotatable credentials (§10.1): build/BUILD_TOKEN, render/RENDER_TOKEN, public/anonymous, Phoenix→CF (DEPLOY_HOOK_URL + scoped CF_KV_API_TOKEN), staff sessions
- Defaults: REBUILD_CRON=0 * * * * (D1), FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS=7200, BILLING_ENFORCED=false (D13), GRACE_DAYS=7, INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS=365
- Never in code or logs; Logger filters authorization (§10.1)
acceptance_criteria:
- Every row of the §12.4 table exists in its designated store(s) — VPS/Coolify, CF build env, Worker secrets, CI — with placeholder values where the consumer does not exist yet
- BUILD_TOKEN and RENDER_TOKEN are distinct, ≥ 32 random bytes base64url each (§10.1 paths 1–2)
- CF_KV_API_TOKEN is scoped to the single FRESHNESS KV namespace, write-only (§10.1 path 4)
- Rotation runbook drafted in infra/runbooks/ covering the §10.1 comma-separated token-set procedure (add new → deploy consumers → remove old, zero downtime; quarterly + on personnel change)
- The §12.4 rule is documented and enforced going forward: adding an env var without updating the table fails review
notes: Spec: §12.4, §10.1, §16 P0-E4, §13 (rotation drill executed in P8-E1). Open decisions: D1 (REBUILD_CRON default), D13 (BILLING_ENFORCED=false). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P3-E1 — builds table + RebuildSite/ConfirmBuild (scheduled rebuilds, R1)
description:
## Why
- Serves **R1**: the static site is rebuilt on a **schedule** (default hourly, runtime-configurable, e.g. 3 h) — not on every content change. This epic is the Phoenix half of that pipeline (§3.2).
- Role in the freshness model: until P4 ships states B/C, site freshness = the rebuild interval (§3.9 step 1 — acceptable interim). Once P4 lands, the interval becomes a **cost knob, not a freshness knob** (§3.2 interval semantics); this epic builds the knob.
- The `builds` table (§5.10) + `ConfirmBuild` make the pipeline observably stateful (`queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped`), feeding the admin dashboard (P3-E2) and BuildAgeMonitor (P3-E3) so a silently broken pipeline is alerted, not discovered (§14, §18 row 2).

## What
- Oban runtime config per §3.2 snippet: queues `default: 10, rebuild: 1, media: 5, mailers: 5, payments: 5`; plugins `Oban.Plugins.Pruner` + `Oban.Plugins.Cron` with crontab `{System.get_env("REBUILD_CRON", "0 * * * *"), Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite}` in `config/runtime.exs`.
- `builds` table migration per §5.10: status enum `queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped`, trigger enum `cron|manual`, `content_snapshot_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `built_at` (from `/__build.json`), `error`, `git_sha`.
- `Immo.Edge` context (§6.1): builds bookkeeping + deploy-hook client (trust path 4, §10.1).
- `Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite` (queue `rebuild`, `unique: [period: 300]`, §6.5): the 6-step algorithm of §3.2 — load last successful build; skip-if-unchanged; re-arm dirty markers (placeholder until P4-E4.4); POST deploy hook + insert `running` row; schedule ConfirmBuild; manual trigger bypass.
- `Immo.Jobs.ConfirmBuild` (§3.2 step 5, §6.5): poll `PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json`, snooze 60 s, max 30 min; on confirmation mark `succeeded` + store `built_at`; on timeout mark `failed` + alert.

## Out of scope
- Admin build dashboard + Rebuild-now UI (P3-E2); BuildAgeMonitor (P3-E3); GH Actions executor fallback (P3-E4, conditional on D3 verdict).
- Real re-arm of KV dirty keys (P4-E4.4 — the KV layer does not exist yet).
- `/__build.json` emission (P2-E7 build-info integration).
design:
- Queues: default:10, rebuild:1 (serializes builds), media:5, mailers:5, payments:5; plugins Pruner + Cron (§3.2 config snippet)
- builds fields per §5.10: status queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped, trigger cron|manual, content_snapshot_at, started_at, finished_at, built_at, error, git_sha
- Skip-if-unchanged: max(updated_at) across published projects/listings/developers/property_types/media (Catalog.published/1, §5.13) + pending-redirects check, vs last successful content_snapshot_at
- ConfirmBuild: snooze 60 s, max 30 min; success when /__build.json content_snapshot_at >= value recorded at trigger (§3.3)
- Deploy hook: POST DEPLOY_HOOK_URL secret (trust path 4, §10.1)
acceptance_criteria:
- Cron fires hourly on staging (REBUILD_CRON default "0 * * * *", changeable at runtime without redeploy)
- No-change run records a builds row with status=skipped and triggers no CF build (deploy hook not called)
- Change run goes running -> succeeded with built_at captured from /__build.json
- Manual trigger (trigger=manual) bypasses skip-if-unchanged; duplicate enqueues within 300 s execute once
- ConfirmBuild timeout (30 min) marks the build failed and raises an alert (§14)
notes: Spec: §3.2, §3.3, §5.10, §6.5, §16 P3-E1 (phase dep: P2-E7). Open decisions: D1 (interval default 0 * * * *), D3 (executor default = deploy hook). Risk register: §18 row 2 (build pipeline silently broken). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P8-E1.2 Credential rotation drill across all 5 trust paths (§10.1): add-new → deploy consumers → remove-old, zero downtime; quarterly cadence documented
description:
## Why
§13 requires "all five trust paths use distinct credentials; rotation drill executed once". R7's value is that each path is *separately rotatable* — this drill proves the runbook works under real conditions before an incident forces it.

## What
- For each rotatable credential in the §10.1 table, run the full cycle: add the new credential alongside the old (plugs accept a comma-separated set), deploy/update every consumer, then remove the old:
  - Path 1 BUILD_TOKEN: update VPS env + CF build env; verify the next scheduled build succeeds.
  - Path 2 RENDER_TOKEN: update VPS env + `wrangler secret put`; verify SSR (state B/C) pages still render.
  - Path 4 deploy-hook URL + CF KV API token: regenerate hook, re-issue the namespace-scoped write-only token; verify RebuildSite trigger + MarkPathsDirty writes.
  - Path 5 staff session credentials: rotate an admin password (argon2) and confirm session invalidation behavior.
  - Path 3 (browser islands): confirm anonymous-by-design — no credential exists; nothing to rotate.
- Prove old credentials are rejected (401) after removal; confirm zero downtime throughout.
- Capture the executed procedure in the rotate-secrets runbook (§14) with the quarterly + personnel-change cadence (§10.1).

## Out of scope
- Rotating SECRET_KEY_BASE/DATABASE_URL and other §12.4 secrets not on a §10.1 trust path (runbook may note them, drill not required by §13).
design:
- §10.1 rotation contract: plugs accept a comma-separated token set → add new token to env list → deploy consumers (CF build env / Worker secret via wrangler secret put / VPS-Coolify secrets) → remove old token
- Path-to-store map (§10.1/§12.4): BUILD_TOKEN in VPS + CF build env (astro:env server secret); RENDER_TOKEN in VPS + Worker secret; DEPLOY_HOOK_URL + CF_KV_API_TOKEN (single-namespace, write-only) in VPS/Coolify; path 5 = phx.gen.auth argon2 sessions
- Verify with §6.4 BearerAuth: rotated-out token → 401; secure_compare in place
- Cadence: quarterly + on personnel change (§10.1 rules)
acceptance_criteria:
- Drill executed once per §10.1 rotatable credential: BUILD_TOKEN (path 1), RENDER_TOKEN (path 2), deploy-hook URL + KV-scoped CF API token (path 4), staff credential rotation for an admin account (path 5); path 3 confirmed anonymous-by-design with no credential to rotate
- Zero downtime observed during each rotation: builds, SSR, KV dirty writes, and admin sessions keep working through the add-new → deploy-consumers → remove-old window
- Old credentials verified dead after removal (401 on use)
- rotate-secrets runbook updated with the executed steps, quarterly cadence + on-personnel-change trigger documented (§10.1)
notes: Spec: §10.1 (five trust paths + rotation rules), §6.4, §12.4 (secret registry), §14 (rotate-secrets runbook in /infra/runbooks/). Open decisions: none blocking. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. Blocked by P8-E1.1 (baseline checklist verified first).

title: P8-E1.1 Execute §13 checklist end-to-end + CSP report-only (2 weeks) → enforce + HSTS preload + security headers verified
description:
## Why
This is the execution arm of the §13 release gate: walk every checklist line in the epic body against the production configuration and produce evidence, including the time-boxed CSP report-only → enforce transition (§7.6).

## What
- Verify origin lockdown: external port scan of the VPS shows only hardened SSH; api/admin reachable solely through the tunnel (§10.2).
- Confirm the five trust paths carry distinct credentials (§10.1 table) and Logger redacts authorization/tokens/card-adjacent fields.
- Run the CSP soak: collect report-only violations for 2 weeks, fix or whitelist by nonce, then enforce; confirm islands (SearchFilter, ListingMap, InquiryForm, Turnstile) work under enforcement.
- Verify HSTS preload, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy on site + api responses.
- Load-test rate limits at the §10.1 thresholds until 429; verify CORS exact-origin allowlist (no wildcard); Turnstile server-side verification + honeypot rejection.
- Exercise upload guards (§8), webhook signature + replay safety (§6.6), changeset-only writes / no interpolated SQL (code audit), LiveView CSRF + 24 h idle timeout + argon2, audit_log coverage on all admin mutations (§5.12).
- Confirm hex.audit/npm audit gates in CI, backup encryption at rest (object-storage SSE), and §13 privacy items (consent flag, retention sweeps, EU/MA residency, P7-E3 pages live).

## Out of scope
- The rotation drill itself (P8-E1.2) and the pen-test (P8-E1.3) — both depend on this task's verified baseline.
design:
- §7.6: csp:true in Astro config, nonce-compatible islands; report-only first 2 weeks, then enforce
- §13 header set: CSP + HSTS preload + X-Content-Type-Options + Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin
- §10.2: tunnel-only origin; verify no inbound port except hardened SSH (key-only, non-standard port, fail2ban) via external port scan
- §8 upload guards: allowlist jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf, 25 MB cap, presign 15 min — test expired presign + forbidden type server-side
- §6.6 webhooks: tampered signature rejected, replayed event processed once (unique provider_payment_id/event id)
- CI: mix hex.audit + npm audit jobs blocking (§13)
acceptance_criteria:
- Each §13 line item (see epic body checklist) executed and evidenced; failures fixed and re-verified
- CSP report-only soak completed (2 weeks, §7.6) with violation reports triaged to zero actionable, then switched to enforce — islands still hydrate (nonce-compatible)
- Live responses carry: enforced Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security with preload, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
- Rate-limit load test demonstrates 429s at the §10.1 thresholds (search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP); Turnstile server-side rejection + honeypot verified
- CORS preflight from a non-allowlisted origin rejected; allowlisted exact origins succeed
notes: Spec: §13, §7.6 (CSP soak), §10.1, §10.2, §8, §6.6, §5.12, §12.3 (CI). Open decisions: D9, D10. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator. Note: schedule the CSP flip 2 weeks after report-only goes live — start the soak early in P8.

title: P0-E3.4 pgBackRest → Hetzner Object Storage: nightly full + WAL (RPO ≤ 5 min) + retention (14 d/90 d) + restore-drill script green on empty DB
description:
## Why
R6's co-located single-box design is only acceptable with real backups: §12.2 sets nightly full + WAL archiving with RPO ≤ 5 min, and §13's release gate requires encrypted backups plus a passed restore drill. The drill script written here is also the §16 P0-E3 acceptance check and the basis for the P8-E2 prod-sized drill.

## What
- Configure the pgBackRest sidecar (`infra/pgbackrest/` per §4) against the `postgres:17` service.
- Point the repository at a Hetzner Object Storage bucket (EU, D12) with server-side encryption (§13).
- Schedule nightly full backups + continuous WAL archiving (RPO ≤ 5 min); set retention 14 d incremental / 90 d weekly (§12.2).
- Write the scripted restore drill: restore into a scratch container with checksum verification; commit the runbook to `infra/runbooks/` and note the monthly calendar task (§12.2).
- Run the drill against the empty DB and make it pass.

## Out of scope
- Prod-sized restore drill and on-call alert routing (P8-E2); §14 alerting on backup failure (P3-E3 wires alerting infrastructure); moving Postgres off-box (P9, DATABASE_URL one-line change).
design:
- pgBackRest sidecar (infra/pgbackrest/ per §4) against the postgres:17 service from P0-E3.2
- Repo target: Hetzner Object Storage bucket, EU (D12; alternative R2 requires a jurisdiction check first); SSE at rest (§13)
- Schedule/semantics (§12.2): nightly full + continuous WAL archiving → RPO ≤ 5 min; retention 14 d incremental / 90 d weekly
- Monthly scripted restore drill into a scratch container with checksum verification — runbook + calendar task (§12.2); the same drill runs on prod-sized data in P8-E2
- Backup-job failure is an alert condition in §14 — note the hook in the runbook (alert wiring lands P3-E3/P8-E2)
acceptance_criteria:
- Nightly full backup object appears in the Hetzner Object Storage bucket (§16 P0-E3 AC)
- WAL archiving continuous: archive_command healthy with lag well under the RPO ≤ 5 min target (§12.2)
- Restore-drill script exists and passes against the empty DB: restore into a scratch container + checksum verification green (§16 AC)
- Retention configured: 14 d incremental / 90 d weekly (§12.2)
- Backups encrypted at rest via object-storage SSE (§13); runbook committed at infra/runbooks/restore-drill with the monthly calendar task noted
notes: Spec: §12.2, §13, §14, §4, §16 P0-E3. Open decisions: D12 (default Hetzner Object Storage EU). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator (P8-E2 re-runs the drill on prod-sized data).

title: P2-E3.2 Failure policy: non-2xx after 3 retries FAILS the build (partial catalog never deploys) + wire collections projects/listings/developers/property_types + delta-fetch verification
description:
## Why
- §7.2: a partial catalog must never deploy — silent data loss in a build would publish a broken site for an hour or more (until the next scheduled rebuild, R1). Failing the build keeps the previous deployment live, which is the safe state.
- The §16 P2-E3 acceptance (delta-only second build, verified via API logs) proves the incremental mechanism actually works against the real API, not just in unit tests.

## What
- Wrap the factory fetch path so any non-2xx response, after 3 retries, throws and fails astro build.
- Wire the four collections — projects, listings, developers, property_types — through phoenixLoader in the content config (§7.2).
- Run two consecutive builds against a seeded backend (P1-E2 fixtures via the P1-E5 build-tier API) and verify via API logs that the second build issues only since/delta requests; document the evidence.

## Out of scope
- Skip-if-unchanged build avoidance (that is the Phoenix RebuildSite job, §3.2/P3-E1); alerting on failed builds (§14, P3-E3).
design:
- §7.2 failure policy verbatim: any non-2xx after 3 retries fails the build — a partial catalog must never deploy
- Retry behavior built on the api client (P2-E2.2) error surface; the loader converts exhausted retries into a thrown build error
- Collections wired in the content config via the factory (P2-E3.1) — projects, listings, developers, property_types (§7.2)
- Delta verification against a seeded staging/dev Phoenix (P1-E2 fixtures + P1-E5 API)
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulated persistent 5xx on any one collection → astro build exits non-zero (no partial catalog deploys; previous deployment stays live)
- Transient failure recovered within 3 retries → build succeeds
- All four collections (projects, listings, developers, property_types) populate from the P1-E2 seed catalog (≥3 types, ≥40 listings, ar/fr content)
- property_types records carry filter_config and url_segment (§6.3) for downstream route generation (P2-E4.1)
- §16 P2-E3 AC verified end-to-end: second consecutive build fetches only deltas, confirmed via API logs and documented in the PR
notes: Spec: §7.2, §6.3, §16 P2-E3 AC. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E3.1 phoenixLoader factory: cursor pagination + since high-water mark from persisted loader meta + store-by-id + digest=updated_at + global max(updated_at) shared module (consumed by build-info integration §3.3)
description:
## Why
- §7.2: incremental syncs keep hourly builds fast as the catalog grows (R1 cost knob); the digest/updated_at contract avoids re-rendering unchanged content.
- The shared max(updated_at) module is the bridge between the loaders and the /__build.json contract (§3.3) — without it the rebuild pipeline (§3.2 step 5) cannot confirm builds.

## What
- src/loaders/phoenixLoader.ts: generic Content Layer loader factory taking {collection, endpoint}.
- Pagination: cursor + limit (≤ 100, §6.3); incremental: since = stored high-water mark read from the loader persisted meta, updated after each successful run.
- Uses src/lib/api.ts (P2-E2.2) with the build trust path: Bearer BUILD_TOKEN from astro:env (10 s build timeout, ETag support).
- Store-by-id; digest from updated_at.
- Shared module (e.g. src/loaders/snapshot.ts) accumulating global max(updated_at) across all collections, exported for the build-info integration (P2-E7.1, §3.3).

## Out of scope
- Failure policy + collection wiring + delta verification (P2-E3.2); the build-info integration that reads the shared module (P2-E7.1).
design:
- §7.2: phoenixLoader({collection, endpoint}) generic factory — one implementation, four collections
- since semantics per §6.3: only records with updated_at > since; cursor pagination with the {data, meta:{next_cursor, count}} envelope
- High-water mark persisted in the Content Layer loader meta store (survives builds via CI cache)
- ETag/If-None-Match passthrough makes repeat syncs cheap (§6.3 304s)
- Shared module is the §3.3 contract: content_snapshot_at = max(updated_at) observed by the loader during this build
acceptance_criteria:
- First build performs a full fetch (cursor-paginated, limit ≤ 100 per §6.3) and persists the high-water mark in loader meta
- Second no-change build sends since=<high-water mark> requests only and leaves digests untouched
- Records stored by id; digest set from updated_at (unchanged records skip re-processing)
- Shared module exposes global max(updated_at) across all collections after the loader run — unit-tested; matches §3.3 content_snapshot_at semantics
- Authorization: Bearer BUILD_TOKEN injected from the astro:env server secret schema via the one api client (P2-E2.2)
notes: Spec: §7.2, §6.3, §3.3. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E3 — Content Layer loaders (incremental, fail-safe)
description:
## Why
- R1 economics: the site rebuilds on a schedule (hourly default); incremental syncs via the since high-water mark keep those builds fast as the catalog grows (§7.2).
- Build correctness: a partial catalog must never deploy — any non-2xx after retries fails the build and the previous deployment simply stays live (§7.2 failure policy).
- Freshness pipeline dependency: the loader records the global max(updated_at) that becomes content_snapshot_at in /__build.json (§3.3), which ConfirmBuild (§3.2 step 5) and the Worker staleness comparison rely on. This epic is load-bearing for P3.

## What
- src/loaders/ (§4): one generic factory phoenixLoader({collection, endpoint}) used for projects, listings, developers, property_types.
- Cursor pagination + since = stored high-water mark from the loader persisted meta; Bearer BUILD_TOKEN from the astro:env server secret schema (§7.2).
- Store records by id; set digest from updated_at; track global max(updated_at) in a shared module read by the build-info integration (§3.3).
- Failure policy: any non-2xx after 3 retries fails the build.
- Wire the four content collections and verify delta-only behavior on a second consecutive build via API logs.

## Out of scope
- The build-info integration itself (P2-E7.1 — it only reads the shared module); pages consuming the collections (P2-E4); scheduled rebuild triggering (P3).
design:
- Spec: §7.2 Content Layer loaders (build time); endpoint contract §6.3 (cursor, limit ≤ 100, since = updated_at > since, ETag/304)
- Auth: build trust path (§10.1) — BUILD_TOKEN server secret via astro:env (§12.4)
- content_snapshot_at consumed downstream: /__build.json (§3.3) → ConfirmBuild polling (§3.2 step 5) → build-age monitor (§14)
- Incremental sync is the R1 cost mechanism: hourly builds stay fast as the catalog grows
- Uses the ONE api client (P2-E2.2) — no loader-private fetch logic
acceptance_criteria:
- Second consecutive build fetches only deltas, verified via API logs (§16 P2-E3 AC)
- One generic factory phoenixLoader({collection, endpoint}) powers all four collections: projects, listings, developers, property_types (§7.2)
- since = stored high-water mark from persisted loader meta; cursor pagination; Authorization: Bearer BUILD_TOKEN from astro:env
- Records stored by id with digest = updated_at; global max(updated_at) tracked in a shared module for the build-info integration (§3.3)
- Any non-2xx after 3 retries FAILS the build — a partial catalog never deploys; the previous deployment stays live (§7.2)
notes: Spec: §7.2, §6.3, §3.3, §16 P2-E3. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P8-E1 — Security gate (execute §13 checklist)
description:
## Why
§13 is the named security release gate for P8 and operationalizes R7 (least-privilege, separately rotatable trust paths). Launch (P8-E4) must not happen until every item below is executed and evidenced — most controls were built in earlier phases; this epic proves them in production configuration.

## What — execute the full §13 checklist
- [ ] Cloudflare Tunnel up; zero inbound ports except SSH (key-only, non-standard port, fail2ban) (§10.2)
- [ ] All five trust paths (§10.1) use distinct credentials; rotation drill executed once
- [ ] CSP enforced after report-only soak (report-only first 2 weeks per §7.6, then enforce)
- [ ] HSTS preload + X-Content-Type-Options + Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin
- [ ] CORS exact origins, no wildcard (public tier allowlist, §10.1 path 3)
- [ ] Rate limits verified by load test (search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP — Hammer + CF WAF)
- [ ] Turnstile verified server-side; honeypot live on the inquiry form (§6.3, §7.5)
- [ ] Upload allowlist + size caps + presign expiry 15 min (§8: jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf, 25 MB, presigned PUT)
- [ ] Webhook signature verification with raw body; replay-safe (§6.6: unique provider event id)
- [ ] Ecto changeset validation on every write; no raw SQL with interpolation
- [ ] LiveView CSRF; admin session idle timeout 24 h; argon2 password hashing
- [ ] audit_log on all admin mutations (§5.12 thin context wrapper)
- [ ] Logger redaction: authorization, tokens, card-adjacent fields
- [ ] Dependency audit in CI: mix hex.audit + npm audit
- [ ] Backups encrypted at rest (object-storage SSE) + restore drill passed
- [ ] Privacy: consent flag stored, retention sweeps on, data stays EU/MA (Hetzner EU, R2 EU jurisdiction setting), privacy policy + Law 09-08/GDPR notice pages live (delivered by P7-E3)

## Out of scope
- Production monitor/alert wiring (P8-E2); performance budgets (P8-E3).
- Enabling Cloudflare Access on /admin (D9 — default off; recommend post-launch).
design:
- Headers: Content-Security-Policy via Astro csp:true with nonce-compatible islands (§7.6); Strict-Transport-Security with preload; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (§13)
- Rotation contract (§10.1): plugs accept a comma-separated token set → add new credential → deploy consumers → remove old; zero downtime; quarterly + on personnel change
- Rate limits to load-verify (§10.1): search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP via Hammer + Cloudflare WAF
- Token comparison via Plug.Crypto.secure_compare (§6.4); build/render scopes disjoint
- Upload guards (§8): type allowlist jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf, max 25 MB, presign expiry 15 min
- Webhooks (§6.6): signature over raw body before parsing; replay-safe via unique provider event id
acceptance_criteria:
- Every §13 checklist line item verified with linked evidence (test output, config, screenshot, or drill log)
- CSP flipped from report-only to enforce after the 2-week soak (§7.6); HSTS preload + X-Content-Type-Options + Referrer-Policy verified on live responses
- Credential rotation drill executed once across the five §10.1 trust paths with zero downtime; quarterly cadence documented in the rotate-secrets runbook
- Pen-test pass complete (ZAP baseline minimum + manual auth checks); all findings triaged, highs/criticals fixed
- P8-E4 launch is unblocked only when this epic closes
notes: Spec: §13 (entire checklist), §10.1, §10.2, §7.6 (CSP), §6.4, §6.6, §8, §5.12, §12.2 (backups). Open decisions: D9 (Cloudflare Access on /admin — default off, recommended after launch), D10 (tunnel is default lockdown). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E3.3 Cloudflare Tunnel live: api.<staging> reaches stub; zero inbound ports except SSH
description:
## Why
R7's origin lockdown (§10.2): with the tunnel as the only path in, Cloudflare's WAF/DDoS/rate-limits actually bind, and the VPS needs no inbound ports beyond SSH. This is also the transport for the LiveView admin (WebSockets through the tunnel).

## What
- Configure the `cloudflared` container (compose service from P0-E3.2) with `infra/cloudflared/config.yml` (§4); outbound-only connection.
- Route `api.<staging-domain>` — and `admin.<staging-domain>` or `/admin` on the api host per §12.1 — through the tunnel to the placeholder stub.
- Create the api/admin DNS records against the tunnel, completing the §12.1 DNS plan from P0-E2.1.
- Verify zero inbound ports except SSH and that WebSocket upgrades pass (LiveView readiness).

## Out of scope
- Real Phoenix behind the tunnel (P1); Cloudflare Access in front of /admin (D9, off by default, post-launch); WAF rule content (P0-E2.3).
design:
- cloudflared container in the compose stack; outbound-only connection — no inbound firewall holes (§10.2)
- DNS: api and admin CNAMEs → tunnel, completing the §12.1 DNS plan started in P0-E2.1
- Result (§10.2): nobody reaches Phoenix except via Cloudflare, so WAF, DDoS protection and the P0-E2.3 rate limits actually bind
- Fallback if tunnel rejected (D10): Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS) + firewall allowing only Cloudflare IP ranges — tunnel is the default
- WebSockets (LiveView) must work through the tunnel (§10.2)
acceptance_criteria:
- https://api.<staging-domain> returns the placeholder stub response through the tunnel (§16 P0-E3 AC)
- admin route established per §12.1 plan (admin.<domain> or /admin on the api host) through the same tunnel
- External port scan confirms zero inbound ports except SSH (§10.2)
- WebSocket upgrade succeeds through the tunnel (LiveView readiness, §10.2)
- cloudflared config committed at infra/cloudflared/config.yml (§4)
notes: Spec: §10.2, §12.1, §12.2, §4. Open decisions: D10 (default tunnel). Depends on the CF zone from P0-E2.1 (wired). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E2.4 Dual-source render-equality test: render ListingPage from loader fixture and SSR fixture ⇒ byte-identical HTML (modulo build hash)
description:
## Why
- §7.3/R4: the universality contract needs a regression net — this CI test is the executable guarantee that one template renders identically from build-time data and request-time API data. Any future template or mapper change that breaks universality goes red immediately.

## What
- Check in two fixtures of the same logical listing: one shaped like the build-tier list endpoint record, one like the render-tier single-record endpoint (§6.3).
- Vitest test renders the listing detail page template through the mappers from both fixtures and asserts byte-identical HTML, normalizing only build-hash differences (§7.3).
- HTML diff on failure; wire into CI (§12.3).

## Out of scope
- The full E2E freshness state machine (§15.4, later phase); equality coverage for every route (listing page is the §7.3-specified canary; extend opportunistically).
design:
- §15.3: the dual-source render test — loader fixture vs SSR fixture ⇒ identical HTML; the CI-enforced proof of R4
- Fixtures mirror real shapes: GET /listings (build tier) record vs GET /listings/:type_key/:slug (render tier) record (§6.3)
- Render via the Astro container API inside Vitest; data flows through mappers (P2-E2.3) only
- Fixtures live in the frontend test fixtures dir; the types-drift gate (P2-E2.1) forces awareness when the contract changes
acceptance_criteria:
- Vitest CI test renders the listing detail template from a loader-sourced fixture and an SSR-sourced fixture of the same logical record → byte-identical HTML modulo build hash (§7.3, §15.3)
- Only build-hash differences may be normalized; whitespace and attribute order must match exactly
- Failure output shows an HTML diff
- Demonstrated red: a template branch on data source makes the test fail
- Wired into the §12.3 PR pipeline
notes: Spec: §7.3, §15.3, §6.3, §12.3. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E2.3 src/lib/mappers.ts — toListingView/toProjectView/toDeveloperView: locale fallback chain (requested→fr→en→first), price formatting, media URL building, path building; the ONLY place API shapes become view shapes
description:
## Why
- §7.3/R4: mappers are the single seam where API shapes become view shapes; everything downstream (templates, components, JSON-LD) consumes only *View types, which is what makes static and SSR rendering identical.
- Deterministic locale fallback is also SEO correctness (R8): the same record must yield the same metadata on every render path.

## What
- src/lib/mappers.ts exporting toListingView(apiRecord, locale), toProjectView(...), toDeveloperView(...) and the *View types.
- Locale resolution with fallback chain: requested → fr → en → first available, applied to i18n maps (title, description, seo, ...).
- Price formatting incl. price_on_request awareness (consumed by PriceTag, §7.4).
- Media URL building per §8 (MEDIA_BASE_URL + /cdn-cgi/image/... pattern — shared contract with Media.astro, P2-E6).
- Path building per locale honoring the server-computed canonical path field (§6.3 response conventions).
- Vitest unit tests per §15.3: locale fallback chains, price/edge cases, path builders.

## Out of scope
- Components consuming the views (P2-E4.2); JSON-LD serialization (P2-E5.2); the Media component itself (P2-E6.1).
design:
- §7.3: toListingView(apiRecord, locale), toProjectView(...), toDeveloperView(...) — the ONLY place API shapes become view shapes (R4)
- The API path field is computed server-side by Immo.Edge.Paths, the single path authority (§6.3) — client path building must never contradict it
- Mappers are pure functions: no fetch, no env reads beyond documented URL bases (MEDIA_BASE_URL, PUBLIC_SITE_URL)
- Output view-models feed every §7.4 component and the JSON-LD serializers (P2-E5.2)
acceptance_criteria:
- *View types exported; templates/components can import only these (never api-types directly)
- Locale fallback chain requested → fr → en → first available unit-tested incl. missing-locale and empty-map edge cases (§15.3)
- price_on_request listings render without leaking a numeric price (feeds PriceTag, §7.4)
- Media URLs built per the §8 pattern from MEDIA_BASE_URL; paths respect the server-computed path field (§6.3)
- Mapper output is byte-stable for identical input — determinism that the P2-E2.4 equality test relies on
notes: Spec: §7.3, §6.3, §8, §15.3. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E2.2 src/lib/api.ts — ONE fetch client: base URL, token injection, ETag support, retry, timeouts 5 s SSR / 10 s build; used by loaders AND SSR routes AND (token-free) islands
description:
## Why
- §7.3/R4: one client shared by all three consumers (loaders, SSR routes, islands) guarantees identical wire behavior across build-time and request-time rendering — the data half of the universality contract.
- ETag support (§6.3 strong ETags + If-None-Match → 304) keeps the hourly incremental re-syncs cheap (R1 economics).

## What
- src/lib/api.ts: typed client over api-types.ts; base URL from API_BASE_URL via astro:env (§12.4).
- Token injection per trust path: BUILD_TOKEN (build/loaders), RENDER_TOKEN (SSR Worker, consumed in a later phase), none for public island endpoints (/search, /listings/geo, POST /inquiries).
- ETag store/propagation: send If-None-Match, expose 304-aware results.
- Retry with backoff on transient failures for idempotent GETs; per-call timeout — 5 s SSR / 10 s build defaults.
- Typed error surface (RFC 9457 problem+json per §6.3) so loaders and SSR routes can apply their failure policies.

## Out of scope
- Loader pagination/high-water-mark logic (P2-E3.1); Worker SSR wiring of RENDER_TOKEN (later phase).
design:
- §7.3: one fetch client — base URL from API_BASE_URL (§12.4), token injection, ETag support, retry, timeout 5 s SSR / 10 s build
- Trust paths (§10.1): build = BUILD_TOKEN bearer (loaders), render = RENDER_TOKEN bearer (Worker SSR, later phase), public = anonymous (islands)
- Typed over api-types.ts (P2-E2.1) paths/responses
- Error surface feeds the loader failure policy (P2-E3.2: non-2xx after 3 retries fails the build)
acceptance_criteria:
- Single module importable from loader context, SSR context, and island context (token-free) — BUILD_TOKEN never reaches client bundles (astro:env server secret enforced)
- Timeouts default 5000 ms in SSR context and 10000 ms in build context (§7.3), overridable per call
- Sends If-None-Match when an ETag is known; surfaces 304 results to callers (powers cheap hourly re-syncs, §6.3)
- Retries transient failures on idempotent GETs before surfacing a typed error
- Handles the §6.3 list envelope {data, meta:{next_cursor, count}} and RFC 9457 problem+json errors
- grep/review check: no other fetch call to the API anywhere in frontend/
notes: Spec: §7.3, §6.3, §10.1, §12.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E2.1 openapi-typescript codegen from backend/priv/static/openapi.json → src/lib/api-types.ts + CI types-drift gate (drift fails build)
description:
## Why
- A9/§7.3: the OpenAPI contract is what keeps build-time and request-time data shapes identical (R4); typed drift detection turns silent contract breaks into red CI.

## What
- Add openapi-typescript devDependency + codegen script reading backend/priv/static/openapi.json → src/lib/api-types.ts (path per §4 monorepo layout).
- Commit the generated file; mark as generated (header + linter ignore as needed).
- CI job: run codegen, then git diff --exit-code on src/lib/api-types.ts — drift fails the build (§12.3 frontend types-codegen drift check).

## Out of scope
- The fetch client (P2-E2.2); backend OpenAPI generation (P1-E5, exists).
design:
- Source of truth: backend/priv/static/openapi.json — generated by open_api_spex and committed (§6.3, A9)
- Generated file is never hand-edited; header comment marks it generated
- Backend side already CI-gates spec drift (§6.3); this is the frontend half of the contract
acceptance_criteria:
- src/lib/api-types.ts generated, committed, and type-checks under tsc strict
- npm script (codegen) regenerates from backend/priv/static/openapi.json
- CI step regenerates and fails on uncommitted diff (git diff --exit-code) — demonstrated once with an intentional spec change
- Gate wired into the §12.3 PR pipeline (replaces the P0 types-drift placeholder)
notes: Spec: §7.3, §6.3, §12.3. Cross-phase dep on P1-E5 wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E2 — API client + view-models (the R4 universality contract)
description:
## Why
- R4: some deployments of this codebase are served entirely from the API (no prerendering); all layouts, templates, and data shapes must be universal — one view-model, one set of components, rendering identically from build-time data or request-time API data. §7.3 names this the universality contract; this epic IS the mechanism.
- A9: the OpenAPI contract (open_api_spex → openapi-typescript) shared by backend and frontend prevents drift between the static and SSR paths.
- Critical path: loaders (P2-E3), pages/components (P2-E4), and build integrations (P2-E7) all consume these modules.

## What
- src/lib/api-types.ts — generated from backend/priv/static/openapi.json via openapi-typescript; regenerated in CI; drift fails the build (§7.3).
- src/lib/api.ts — ONE fetch client: base URL, token injection, ETag support, retry, timeout 5 s SSR / 10 s build; used by loaders and SSR routes and (token-free) islands.
- src/lib/mappers.ts — toListingView / toProjectView / toDeveloperView: locale fallback chain (requested → fr → en → first available), price formatting, media URL building (§8), path building. The only place API shapes become view shapes.
- CI dual-source render-equality test (§7.3, §15.3): ListingPage from loader fixture vs SSR fixture → byte-identical HTML modulo build hash.

## Out of scope
- The Content Layer loaders themselves (P2-E3); page templates and the component inventory beyond the equality-test harness (P2-E4); RENDER_TOKEN Worker SSR runtime (later phase — the client supports the trust path, the Worker wires it).
design:
- Spec: §7.3 (the universality contract — R4); A9 OpenAPI contract shared by backend and frontend
- Locale fallback chain: requested → fr → en → first available
- Client contract: base URL from API_BASE_URL (§12.4), token injection per trust path (§10.1: build=BUILD_TOKEN, render=RENDER_TOKEN, public=anonymous), retry, ETag, timeouts 5 s SSR / 10 s build
- R4/§2.2 hard rule on every artifact: templates never know the render mode or data source — any PR that branches template logic on RENDER_MODE or data source fails review
- Critical path: P2-E3/E4/E7 all consume these modules
acceptance_criteria:
- types-drift CI gate live: regenerating src/lib/api-types.ts from backend/priv/static/openapi.json in CI with any uncommitted diff fails the build (§16 P2-E2 AC)
- render-equality test green: ListingPage rendered from a loader-sourced fixture and an SSR-sourced fixture produces byte-identical HTML modulo build hash (§16 P2-E2 AC, §7.3)
- src/lib/api.ts is the ONE fetch client used by loaders AND SSR routes AND (token-free) islands — no other fetch path to the API exists in frontend/
- src/lib/mappers.ts is the only place API shapes become view shapes; templates/components import only *View types
- Timeouts enforced: 5 s SSR / 10 s build; ETag If-None-Match support demonstrated (304 on repeat fetch)
notes: Spec: §7.3, §15.3, §6.3, §16 P2-E2. Critical path. Cross-phase dep on P1-E5 (Read API + OpenAPI) wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E3.2 Coolify + compose stack: postgres:17 (localhost-only, scram-sha-256, tuning) + cloudflared + placeholder app
description:
## Why
Coolify (D11) provides push-deploys, env/secret management and TLS for its own UI; the compose stack realizes the R6/A4 co-location design — Phoenix + PostgreSQL 17 + cloudflared on one box, with Postgres hardened to localhost-only from day zero (§12.2).

## What
- Install Coolify on the VPS; manage the stack defined in `infra/compose.yml` (§4) through it.
- Services per §12.2: `phoenix` (placeholder stub HTTP responder for the tunnel test; real Elixir release image arrives in P1), `postgres:17` with a data volume, `cloudflared` (configured/activated in P0-E3.3).
- Postgres hardening per §12.2: `listen_addresses='localhost'`, published on 127.0.0.1 only (never 0.0.0.0), scram-sha-256, unix-socket/localhost connections only.
- Apply tuning starting points: `shared_buffers=2GB`, `effective_cache_size=4GB`, `work_mem=32MB`; enable pg_stat_statements.

## Out of scope
- Tunnel routing + DNS (P0-E3.3); pgBackRest sidecar (P0-E3.4); real Phoenix deploy pipeline (§12.3 backend deploy, P1); Ecto pool config (P1, noted at 15).
design:
- infra/compose.yml in the monorepo (§4) is the source of truth; Coolify deploys it (D11: push-deploys, env/secret management, TLS for the Coolify UI itself)
- Postgres co-location hardening (§12.2): listen_addresses=localhost; unix-socket/localhost connections only; scram-sha-256 auth
- Tuning starting points (§12.2): shared_buffers=2GB, effective_cache_size=4GB, work_mem=32MB; pg_stat_statements on; Ecto pool size 15 noted for P1
- DATABASE_URL env-driven (§12.4, §12.2) so Postgres can move to its own VPS later with a one-line change
- phoenix service: placeholder stub now; replaced by the Elixir release image with migrations-on-boot in P1 (§12.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- Coolify installed; its UI reachable over TLS; the stack deploys from Coolify
- Compose stack from infra/compose.yml runs three services healthy: phoenix placeholder (stub HTTP responder), postgres:17 (with volume), cloudflared (config activated in P0-E3.3)
- Postgres unreachable from any external interface (connection attempt from outside fails); psql over localhost authenticates via scram-sha-256
- SHOW shared_buffers / effective_cache_size / work_mem return 2GB / 4GB / 32MB; pg_stat_statements extension available
- Port published on 127.0.0.1 only — never 0.0.0.0 (§12.2)
notes: Spec: §12.2, §4, §12.3, §12.4. Open decisions: D11 (default Coolify; Kamal alternative = runbooks change only). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E3.1 Hetzner CPX31 + Ubuntu 24.04 + SSH hardening (key-only, non-standard port, fail2ban) + unattended-upgrades
description:
## Why
The single Hetzner box is the entire backend plane (R6/A4: Phoenix + co-located Postgres). §10.2's lockdown model only works if the host itself exposes nothing but hardened SSH before any service goes on it.

## What
- Provision Hetzner CPX31 (4 vCPU / 8 GB) with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (§12.2), EU location (§13: data stays EU/MA).
- SSH hardening per §10.2: key-only auth, non-standard port, fail2ban.
- Enable unattended-upgrades (§12.2).
- Host firewall: no inbound ports except the SSH port (all app traffic comes via the outbound-only tunnel from P0-E3.3).

## Out of scope
- Docker/Coolify/compose stack (P0-E3.2); tunnel (P0-E3.3); backups (P0-E3.4).
design:
- Size per §12.2: CPX31 launch; documented upgrade path to CPX41 if geocoding/media jobs contend
- §10.2 SSH rules verbatim: key-only, non-standard port, fail2ban; all app traffic will arrive outbound-only via cloudflared (P0-E3.3), so the host firewall allows inbound SSH only
- EU location: data stays EU/MA (§13 privacy line)
- OS baseline: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS + unattended-upgrades (§12.2)
acceptance_criteria:
- CPX31 (4 vCPU/8 GB) running Ubuntu 24.04 LTS in an EU location
- Password SSH auth rejected; key-only login works on the non-standard port
- fail2ban active with sshd jail enabled
- unattended-upgrades enabled and verified (dry-run applies security updates)
- External port scan shows only the SSH port open — no other inbound ports (§10.2 precondition for the tunnel)
notes: Spec: §12.2, §10.2, §13. Open decisions: none. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P0-E3 — VPS provisioning (Hetzner + Coolify + tunnel + pgBackRest)
description:
## Why
R6 mandates PostgreSQL co-located with Phoenix on a single Hetzner VPS (A4), and R7/§10.2 mandates origin lockdown so the VPS is reachable only through Cloudflare. This epic provisions the entire backend runtime substrate — host, Coolify-managed compose stack, tunnel, and backups — before any Phoenix code exists (P1 deploys onto it; the single-box SPOF is accepted knowingly per §12.2 because the static layer survives outages per §3.7).

## What
- Hetzner CPX31 (4 vCPU/8 GB), Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, SSH hardening (key-only, non-standard port, fail2ban), unattended-upgrades (§12.2).
- Coolify (D11) managing the Docker Compose stack from `infra/compose.yml`: `phoenix` placeholder, `postgres:17` (localhost-only, scram-sha-256, §12.2 tuning), `cloudflared`.
- Cloudflare Tunnel live: `api.<staging-domain>` reaches the stub; zero inbound ports except SSH (§10.2, D10).
- pgBackRest → Hetzner Object Storage (EU, D12): nightly full + WAL archiving (RPO ≤ 5 min), retention 14 d incremental / 90 d weekly, scripted restore drill green against the empty DB.

## Out of scope
- Real Phoenix release deploys via GH Actions → Coolify webhook (§12.3, P1).
- Populating the full §12.4 secret registry across stores (P0-E4).
- Email provider setup (Swoosh/Resend — P1-E6) and §14 monitors (P3-E3/P8-E2).
design:
- Host: Hetzner CPX31 (4 vCPU/8 GB) at launch, CPX41 if geocoding/media jobs contend; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS; unattended-upgrades (§12.2)
- Runtime: Docker Compose managed by Coolify (D11 — push-deploys, env/secret management, TLS for the Coolify UI); services: phoenix (placeholder now, Elixir release image later), postgres:17 (volume), cloudflared (§12.2)
- Postgres hardening (§12.2): listen_addresses=localhost, published on 127.0.0.1 only (never 0.0.0.0), scram-sha-256, unix-socket/localhost only; tuning starting points shared_buffers=2GB, effective_cache_size=4GB, work_mem=32MB; pg_stat_statements on; Ecto pool size 15 (P1)
- Origin lockdown (§10.2): Cloudflare Tunnel outbound-only; api.<domain>/admin.<domain> via tunnel; fallback if tunnel rejected = Authenticated Origin Pulls + CF IP allowlist (D10)
- Backups: pgBackRest sidecar → Hetzner Object Storage (EU, D12); nightly full + WAL archiving (RPO ≤ 5 min); retention 14 d incremental / 90 d weekly; monthly scripted restore drill; DATABASE_URL env-driven for a future one-line DB move
acceptance_criteria:
- api.<staging-domain> reaches a stub through the tunnel (§16 P0-E3 AC)
- Nightly backup object appears in the Hetzner Object Storage bucket (§16 AC)
- Restore-drill script exists and passes against the empty DB (§16 AC)
- SSH hardened: key-only, non-standard port, fail2ban; external port scan shows zero inbound ports except SSH (§10.2, §12.2)
- Coolify manages the compose stack: postgres:17 localhost-only with scram-sha-256 + §12.2 tuning, cloudflared, placeholder app — all healthy
notes: Spec: §12.2, §10.2, §12.1 (DNS), §13 (encrypted backups), §14 (runbooks), §16 P0-E3. Open decisions: D10 (default tunnel), D11 (default Coolify; Kamal = runbooks change only), D12 (default Hetzner Object Storage). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E2.4 D3 verdict: Workers Builds monthly quota vs ~720 builds → ADR
description:
## Why
R1's hourly rebuild schedule means ~720 builds/month (§3.2 build-minutes note). §12.1 and §16 P0-E2 require verifying in P0 that the Workers Builds monthly quota on the chosen Cloudflare plan covers this; the verdict gates the conditional epic P3-E4 (GH Actions build path) and defuses the §18 risk "hourly builds exceed CF quota mid-month".

## What
- Determine the Workers Builds monthly quota/limits on the chosen Cloudflare plan (verified against current plan docs/account, not assumed).
- Compare against ~720 builds/month from `REBUILD_CRON` default `0 * * * *`, plus headroom for code-push builds, PR previews, and manual "Rebuild now" triggers.
- Record the D3 verdict as an ADR in /docs: keep Workers Builds via deploy hook (default) or switch the build executor to the GH Actions path (`astro build && wrangler deploy` triggered via GitHub API `workflow_dispatch` — P3-E4).

## Out of scope
- Implementing the GH Actions path itself (P3-E4, only if the verdict demands it); changing the rebuild interval (D1 is a runtime knob, §3.2).
design:
- §3.2 build-minutes note: hourly = ~720 builds/month; D3 override trigger is quota < ~750/mo on the chosen plan
- Fallback architecture unchanged (§3.2): GitHub Actions runs astro build && wrangler deploy, triggered by Phoenix via GitHub API workflow_dispatch; ConfirmBuild polling of /__build.json identical; free minutes
- Cost knob independent of the verdict: REBUILD_CRON can relax to 0 */3 * * * with zero user-visible freshness change once the P4 freshness layer exists (D1, §3.2 interval semantics)
- One ADR markdown file per locked-decision change (§4 convention)
acceptance_criteria:
- ADR committed in /docs recording: the Workers Builds quota numbers on the chosen Cloudflare plan, the comparison vs ~720 builds/month (hourly cron) plus headroom for code pushes and manual rebuilds, and the verdict
- Verdict states either: keep Workers Builds via deploy hook (D3 default) OR activate the GH Actions fallback — which makes P3-E4 mandatory instead of conditional
- §16 P0-E2 AC satisfied: "D3 quota verdict documented"
notes: Spec: §3.2 (build-minutes note), §12.1, §17 D3, §18 (quota risk). Open decisions: D3 (default Workers Builds; this issue produces the verdict), D1 (interval default 0 * * * *). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator (P3-E4 is the conditional consumer).

title: P0-E2.3 Deploy hook created+tested + Turnstile site keys + WAF & rate-limit baseline rules
description:
## Why
The deploy hook is the trigger of the scheduled-rebuild pipeline (R1, §3.2 step 4 — `RebuildSite` POSTs it hourly), and Turnstile + WAF/rate-limits are the trust-path protections for the anonymous public tier (R7, §10.1 path 3, §10.2). All three are §12.1 P0 checklist items that later phases consume as ready-made resources.

## What
- Create the deploy hook on the Workers project; test it manually (POST → build runs); hand the URL to the §12.4 registry as `DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`.
- Create Turnstile site keys (`TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` / `TURNSTILE_SECRET`) for the inquiry form (§6.3 `POST /inquiries` verifies server-side).
- Configure WAF baseline per §10.2: managed ruleset on `api.*`, bot-fight mode on public endpoints, country-agnostic.
- Create rate-limit baseline rules mirroring §10.1: search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP (Cloudflare-side complement to the Phoenix Hammer limits).

## Out of scope
- Storing secrets in all stores + rotation runbook (P0-E4); the Phoenix-side Hammer rate limiting and Turnstile verification code (P1-E5/P1-E6); load-test verification of limits (P8-E1, §13).
design:
- Deploy hook is trust path 4 (§10.1): Phoenix → Cloudflare; URL is a secret stored VPS-side (DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, §12.4); consumed by Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite step 4 (§3.2)
- Rate limits are enforced twice by design (§10.1): Hammer in Phoenix + Cloudflare WAF rules — this task ships the CF half
- Turnstile verification is server-side in POST /inquiries (§6.3, P1-E6); keys: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY (build store) / TURNSTILE_SECRET (VPS) per §12.4
- WAF: managed ruleset on api.*, bot-fight on public endpoints, country-agnostic — Moroccan diaspora traffic from EU expected (§10.2)
acceptance_criteria:
- Manual POST to the deploy hook produces a build/deploy on the Workers project — "deploy hook tested manually" (§16 P0-E2 AC)
- Hook URL captured for the DEPLOY_HOOK_URL secret (handed to P0-E4; stored on VPS per §12.4)
- Turnstile widget/site created; TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY + TURNSTILE_SECRET captured; test widget validates on a scratch page
- WAF managed ruleset active on api.* hostname; bot-fight enabled on public endpoints; configuration is country-agnostic (§10.2)
- Rate-limit rules created matching §10.1 path-3 budgets: search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP
notes: Spec: §12.1, §3.2, §10.1, §10.2, §6.3, §12.4. Open decisions: D3 (hook is the default executor trigger), D9 (Cloudflare Access on /admin off by default — not part of this task). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E2.2 KV namespaces FRESHNESS (prod+staging) + R2 buckets + media.<domain> custom domain + CORS range rule + Image Transformations enabled
description:
## Why
FRESHNESS KV is the substrate of the state-C dirty-marker layer (R3, §3.5) consumed by the P4 Worker entry, and R2 + `media.<domain>` + Image Transformations is the entire media delivery path (R5, A6, §8) plus the PMTiles basemap host (A7, §9). These must exist in P0 so namespace IDs/bucket names can flow into the §12.4 registry.

## What
- Create KV namespaces `FRESHNESS` for prod and staging (§12.1, §3.5); record namespace IDs.
- Create R2 buckets `immo-media-prod` + staging equivalent (§8).
- Attach custom domain `media.<domain>` (proxied, first-party).
- Add the R2 CORS rule allowing range GET from site origins (PMTiles, §9).
- Enable Image Transformations on the zone and verify the pricing tier fits expected volume (§8 explicitly requires this check in P0).

## Out of scope
- KV writer code (`Immo.Edge.Freshness.mark_dirty`, P4-E4); presigned uploads (P1-E4); `Media.astro` URL building (P2-E6); uploading the actual basemap PMTiles (P5-E3).
design: - KV contract this namespace must serve (§3.5): keys path:, values integer unix seconds, per-key expiration_ttl = FRESHNESS_TTL_SECONDS (default 7200 = 2× rebuild interval) - R2 buckets: immo-media-prod + staging equivalent (§8); keys content-addressed media/{attachable_type}/{attachable_id}/{sha256}.{ext}; object cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable — updates create new keys, no purging ever - media. proxied custom domain → first-party, edge-cached, no CORS needed for (§8); MEDIA_BASE_URL=https://media. (§12.4) - CORS rule: range GET from site origins for tiles/basemap.pmtiles (§9 PMTiles over HTTP range requests) - Transformation URL shape (§8): https://media./cdn-cgi/image/width={w},quality=82,format=auto/
acceptance_criteria:
- KV write+read round-trip verified on both FRESHNESS namespaces (prod+staging), including a PUT with expiration_ttl (§3.5 TTL semantics)
- Namespace IDs recorded for CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID and the wrangler.jsonc kv_namespaces binding FRESHNESS (§3.4)
- Test object uploaded to the staging bucket is served via https://media.<staging-domain>/... proxied and edge-cached (§8)
- Range GET against an R2 object succeeds from the site origin (CORS rule for PMTiles, §9)
- /cdn-cgi/image/ transformation URL returns a resized variant; Image Transformations pricing tier verified against expected volume and documented (§8)
notes: Spec: §12.1, §3.5, §3.4, §8, §9, §12.4. Open decisions: D8 (PMTiles on R2 default — the CORS range rule serves it), D12 (backup target is Hetzner Object Storage, not these buckets). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E2.1 Zone + DNS plan + Workers project + Git builds + preview deployments + hello-world Worker on staging domain
description:
## Why
Establishes the Cloudflare zone and the Workers project that will host the public site (A2: Workers Static Assets with Git builds + previews). Every other CF resource (KV, R2, hooks, WAF) and the P2-E7 first deploy hang off this project, and PR preview deployments are a §12.3 CI dependency.

## What
- Configure the zone(s) for staging + prod.
- Document and create the DNS plan per §12.1: `www`/apex → Worker; `api`, `admin` → Tunnel (records completed when the tunnel lands in P0-E3.3); `media` → R2 custom domain (completed in P0-E2.2).
- Create the Workers project (name `immo-frontend` per §3.4) with Git-connected builds from the monorepo `/frontend` and preview deployments on PRs.
- Deploy a hello-world Worker and verify it serves on the staging domain.

## Out of scope
- KV/R2/Image Transformations (P0-E2.2); deploy hook, Turnstile, WAF (P0-E2.3); tunnel DNS activation (P0-E3.3).
design:
- Worker name "immo-frontend", compatibility_date 2026-05-01, assets binding ASSETS (§3.4 wrangler.jsonc excerpt)
- Workers Static Assets, not Pages — Pages is maintenance mode (A2)
- Git-connected Workers Builds watch the monorepo /frontend directory; preview deployments on PRs feed Lighthouse CI (§12.3)
- DNS plan per §12.1: www/apex → Worker; api, admin → Tunnel; media → R2 custom domain
acceptance_criteria:
- Staging domain returns the hello-world Worker response over HTTPS (§16 P0-E2 AC)
- Workers project is Git-connected: a push builds and deploys; a PR produces a preview deployment URL (§12.1)
- DNS plan documented and records created where possible now: www/apex → Worker; api, admin reserved for Tunnel (CNAMEs land with P0-E3.3); media reserved for R2 custom domain (P0-E2.2)
- Both staging and prod zone/Worker environments exist per §12.3 staging-env requirement
notes: Spec: §12.1, §3.4, §12.3, §1.4 (A2). Open decisions: D3 (Git builds are the default executor under test here). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P0-E2 — Cloudflare account setup (zone, Workers, KV, R2, hooks)
description:
## Why
The Cloudflare edge is half the architecture (A2 Static Assets, A5 KV freshness, A6 R2 media): R1–R3 (scheduled builds + freshness), R5 (R2 media) and R7 (WAF/Turnstile protections) all require these account resources to exist before any feature work. This epic executes the §12.1 P0 checklist for staging and prod.

## What
- Zone + DNS plan (§12.1): `www`/apex → Worker; `api`, `admin` → Tunnel; `media` → R2 custom domain.
- Workers project with Git-connected builds and preview deployments on PRs; hello-world Worker on the staging domain.
- KV namespaces `FRESHNESS` prod+staging (§3.5).
- R2 buckets (`immo-media-prod` + staging) with custom domain `media.<domain>`, CORS range-GET rule for PMTiles (§8/§9), Image Transformations enabled with pricing-tier check (§8).
- Deploy hook created and tested; Turnstile site keys; WAF + rate-limit baseline rules (§10.1/§10.2).
- D3 verdict: Workers Builds monthly quota vs ~720 builds/month, documented as ADR (§3.2 build-minutes note).

## Out of scope
- VPS-side cloudflared container and tunnel routing (P0-E3.3).
- Populating all secrets into every store + rotation runbook (P0-E4).
- Real frontend deploys (P2-E7) and the GH Actions build path itself (P3-E4, conditional on D3).
design:
- DNS plan (§12.1): www/apex → Worker; api, admin → Tunnel; media → R2 custom domain
- KV: FRESHNESS namespace per environment (prod+staging, §3.5); IDs feed CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID and the wrangler.jsonc kv_namespaces binding "FRESHNESS" (§3.4)
- R2: buckets immo-media-prod + staging (§8); media.<domain> proxied; CORS allows range GET for PMTiles (§9); Image Transformations enabled, pricing tier verified (§8)
- Secrets produced here feed §12.4: DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID, CF_KV_API_TOKEN (scoped to single namespace, write-only), TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY/TURNSTILE_SECRET, MEDIA_BASE_URL
- WAF managed ruleset on api.*; bot-fight on public endpoints; rate-limit baselines per §10.1 (search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP)
acceptance_criteria:
- Deploy hook tested manually: a POST to the hook triggers a build (§16 P0-E2 AC)
- KV and R2 reachable: write+read round-trip verified on FRESHNESS namespaces and staging bucket (§16 AC)
- Hello-world Worker serves on the staging domain (§16 AC)
- D3 quota verdict documented as ADR: Workers Builds monthly quota vs ~720 builds/month (§16 AC)
- Full §12.1 checklist executed for staging+prod: DNS plan, Git builds + PR previews, media.<domain> custom domain, PMTiles CORS range rule, Image Transformations, WAF + rate-limit rules, Turnstile site keys
notes: Spec: §12.1, §8, §9, §10.1, §10.2, §3.2 (build-minutes note), §3.4, §3.5, §16 P0-E2. Open decisions: D3 (default Workers Builds, fallback GH Actions P3-E4), D10 (tunnel default), D8 (PMTiles default). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E1.2 CI workflows: backend+frontend gates + OpenAPI/types-drift placeholders + dual render-mode build smoke
description:
## Why
§12.3 CI gates are the enforcement arm of the global DoD (§15.6) and of R4's universality contract: the dual render-mode build smoke guarantees no PR ships code that only builds in one mode, and the drift gates (once activated) keep backend OpenAPI and frontend types in lockstep (A9).

## What
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running on all PRs with:
  - Backend gates: `mix format --check-formatted`, Credo, Dialyzer, `mix test`, OpenAPI-drift check placeholder (real spec arrives P1-E5).
  - Frontend gates: types-codegen drift check placeholder (real codegen arrives P2-E2), ESLint, `tsc`, Vitest.
  - Build smoke: `astro build` with `RENDER_MODE=static` AND `RENDER_MODE=dynamic` — both must build (§12.3).
  - Lighthouse CI on preview deployments noted/stubbed (budgets per §15.5; previews come from P0-E2 Git builds).
- Placeholder workflows per §4 tree: `backend-deploy.yml` (release image → Coolify webhook) and `frontend-build.yml` (D3 fallback).

## Out of scope
- Real OpenAPI generation (P1-E5) and `openapi-typescript` codegen (P2-E2) — placeholders must be wired so activation is a small diff.
- Backend deploy wiring to a live Coolify instance (needs P0-E3).
design:
- §12.3 CI gate list verbatim — backend: format check, Credo, Dialyzer, mix test, OpenAPI drift check; frontend: types-codegen drift check, ESLint, tsc, Vitest, build smoke (RENDER_MODE=static and =dynamic both must build), Lighthouse CI on preview
- OpenAPI drift mechanics (§6.3): mix openapi.spec.json --spec ImmoWeb.ApiSpec -o priv/static/openapi.json then fail on git diff (placeholder until P1-E5)
- RENDER_MODE consumed via the render-mode integration (§2.2 astro:route:setup); dynamic build skips loaders and must not require BUILD_TOKEN (§7.1)
- backend-deploy.yml (GH Actions builds release image → Coolify webhook, §12.3) and frontend-build.yml (D3 GH Actions fallback: astro build && wrangler deploy) committed as placeholders per §4
acceptance_criteria:
- PR to main runs all gates green (epic AC, §16 P0-E1)
- Introducing a format/Credo/Dialyzer/test failure in backend or an ESLint/tsc/Vitest failure in frontend fails the PR
- Build smoke job runs astro build twice: once with RENDER_MODE=static and once with RENDER_MODE=dynamic; both must succeed
- OpenAPI-drift placeholder (uncommitted diff of backend/priv/static/openapi.json fails CI) and types-drift placeholder (openapi-typescript regen vs committed src/lib/api-types.ts) exist, marked to activate in P1-E5 / P2-E2
- Lighthouse CI on preview deployments noted/stubbed with §15.5 budgets (LCP < 2.5 s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200 ms, ≤ 100 KB JS gz detail / ≤ 60 KB landings)
notes: Spec: §12.3, §15.5, §15.6, §6.3, §2.2, §7.1, §4. Open decisions: D3 (default Workers Builds; frontend-build.yml is the fallback path). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P0-E1.1 Monorepo scaffold + tooling baseline (/backend /frontend /infra /docs)
description:
## Why
A10's monorepo is the substrate for atomic cross-cutting changes and a single CI pipeline; the §4 tooling conventions (format/lint/types) must exist before any feature code so every later phase inherits them.

## What
- Create the §4 directory layout verbatim:
  - `backend/` — Phoenix app (Elixir 1.18 / OTP 27, Phoenix 1.8): `lib/immo/`, `lib/immo_web/`, `lib/immo/jobs/`, `priv/repo/migrations/`, `priv/static/openapi.json` placeholder (generated+committed per A9 from P1-E5), `test/`
  - `frontend/` — Astro 6: `src/pages/`, `src/loaders/`, `src/lib/`, `src/components/`, `src/islands/`, `src/worker/index.ts` (stub custom entry, real impl P4-E3), `src/integrations/`, `astro.config.mjs`, `wrangler.jsonc`
  - `infra/` — `compose.yml`, `cloudflared/config.yml`, `pgbackrest/`, `runbooks/` (deploy, restore-drill, rotate-secrets, incident placeholders)
  - `docs/` — plan, ADR template
  - `.github/workflows/` — empty placeholders for ci.yml, backend-deploy.yml, frontend-build.yml (filled in P0-E1.2)
- Tooling baseline: mix format, Credo strict, Dialyzer configured; TypeScript strict mode, ESLint, Prettier; conventional commits documented; ADR template in /docs.

## Out of scope
- CI workflow content (P0-E1.2). Any real Phoenix/Astro features (P1/P2).
design:
- Versions pinned: Elixir 1.18 / OTP 27 / Phoenix 1.8; Astro 6 + official Cloudflare adapter (A1/A2)

title: [Immo] P0-E1 — Repo & CI skeleton (monorepo + quality gates)
description:
## Why
Foundation everything else depends on (§16 P0). The monorepo (locked decision A10) enables atomic cross-cutting changes and a single CI; the quality gates enforce the global DoD (§15.6) and protect the R4 universality contract (OpenAPI/types drift, dual render-mode builds) from the first PR onward.

## What
- Monorepo scaffold exactly per §4: `/backend` (Phoenix app, Elixir 1.18 / OTP 27, Phoenix 1.8), `/frontend` (Astro 6), `/infra` (compose.yml, cloudflared/, pgbackrest/, runbooks/), `/docs` (plan, ADRs), `.github/workflows/` (ci.yml, backend-deploy.yml, frontend-build.yml).
- Tooling baseline per §4 conventions: mix format + Credo strict + Dialyzer; TypeScript strict + ESLint + Prettier; conventional commits; ADR template in /docs.
- CI pipelines per §12.3 wired even while trivial: backend gates (format check, Credo, Dialyzer, mix test, OpenAPI drift placeholder), frontend gates (types-drift placeholder, ESLint, tsc, Vitest, build smoke with RENDER_MODE=static and =dynamic), Lighthouse CI on previews noted.

## Out of scope
- Real application features: Phoenix contexts/auth (P1), Astro pages/loaders (P2). Gates may run against trivial scaffolds.
- Live OpenAPI spec generation (P1-E5) and types codegen (P2-E2) — this epic ships the drift-gate placeholders only.
- Cloudflare account resources (P0-E2) and VPS (P0-E3).

**Notes**: video code is full of 'works on my machine' traps. The critic's job here is to surface the things you'll only see on a real device with throttled network and a low battery.

title: 6.2 Vertical full-screen feed + prefetch + HLS
description:
The player. `PageView` (vertical) with a small pool of `video_player` / `better_player` controllers, aggressive prefetch of the next 2-3 clips, HLS adaptive bitrate so playback never stalls on a bandwidth dip.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_page.dart` — the `PageView` + controller pool.
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_item.dart` — single-item widget with overlay (caption, like, follow).
- `app/lib/features/feed/prefetch.dart` — next-N prefetch logic.
- `app/lib/core/video/` — controller lifecycle helpers.

**Validation (the hard ones)**
- Smooth scroll: 60fps on a mid-range Android (Pixel 5 / Galaxy A52 era) when swiping through 20+ clips. Profile with `flutter run --profile` and DevTools.
- No stalls on throttled 3G: Fast 3G profile in DevTools, swipe 10 times → every clip plays without a buffering spinner longer than ~250ms.
- Fast first frame: from swipe to visible first frame < 300ms when the next clip is already prefetched.
- Memory: scrolling 50 clips doesn't blow past ~250 MB on the same device.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is THE task. If you only have time to do one thing well, do this. Single-controller-per-clip is the most common Flutter video mistake — it leaks memory and stutters on scroll. A pool of 3-4 controllers is the right shape.

title: 6.1 Mux integration: signed direct-upload + webhook
description:
Server-side: a Supabase Edge Function that creates a signed Mux direct-upload URL, plus a webhook handler that updates `videos` with the `playback_id` and `status` on `asset.ready`.

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/functions/mux-upload/index.ts` — Edge Function: create Mux direct upload, persist a `videos` row in `uploading` state, return the signed URL to the client.
- `backend/supabase/functions/mux-webhook/index.ts` — Edge Function: verify Mux signature, update `videos.status` and `videos.playback_id` on `video.upload.asset_created` / `video.asset.ready`.
- `app/lib/features/upload/` — Flutter upload widget that PUTs the file to the signed URL with progress + retry.

**Validation**
- End-to-end: pick a clip on device → progress UI shows upload → within ~30s the `videos` row flips to `ready` and a `playback_id` is present.
- Webhook signature verification: a forged webhook returns 401.
- Failed upload (e.g. Mux rejects the file) flips the row to `errored` and is visible in a 'your uploads' debug screen.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: use Mux's signed direct upload (not the public upload) — the whole point is that the Supabase service-role key never leaves the server. Webhook signing-key verification is non-negotiable.

title: E7 — Phase 6: Video feed end-to-end (MAKE-OR-BREAK) (Part B · app) [~2-4 weeks]
description:
**Phase 6 (Part B · app) — ~2-4 weeks · priority HIGH · MAKE-OR-BREAK**

The defining feature of the app. TikTok-style vertical full-screen feed, video uploads via Mux signed direct-upload, HLS playback with a controller pool and aggressive prefetch. If this phase doesn't ship, the app doesn't ship.

**Why this is high priority and big-effort**: video is the hard part. Networking, codecs, scroll perf, prefetch, signed URLs, webhooks, error states, and analytics all collide here. A 'simple feed' prototype is achievable in a week; a *smooth* feed that doesn't stall on throttled 3G is a multi-week effort.

**Ordering note**: depends on E6. Children 6.1 and 6.2 are the critical path; 6.3 (ranking) and 6.4 (review) are parallel-friendly.

**Inputs**

- Constraints passed as flags/env: `--max-depth=4`, `--node-budget=200`, `--target-stack=flutter,supabase,mux`.

**Outputs**
- `docs/backlog/index.md` + per-epic Markdown files + `docs/backlog/backlog.json`.
- A `docs/backlog/critic_report.md` with the bounded critic's findings.

**Validation**
- Every leaf in the produced tree has `estimate_days <= 1.0` and a clear done-condition in `description`.
- The tree covers all the E0..E10 epics in this roadmap (i.e. the agent agrees with the structure you had in mind, possibly with renames).
- The critic report has no open P0/P1 findings; if it does, they are either resolved or escalated.
- Re-running the agent produces zero diff in `docs/backlog/`.

**Agent**: code-puppy (running the agent CLI).
**Notes**: this is a milestone, not a routine task. If the leaves aren't atomic or the critic finds structural problems, **fix the agent first** (loop back into E2-E4), do NOT 'just continue and clean up the backlog manually'.

**Bridge Milestone (A -> B) — ~1-2 days · priority HIGH**

The whole point of building the agent first: feed it the locked architecture spec and let it produce the day-sized backlog for the app, written to `docs/backlog/` with human approval.

**Why this is a separate epic**: it is the only moment in the project where Part A and Part B connect. If it works, the rest of the project is a backlog. If it doesn't, the agent isn't actually useful and you need to fix it before building the app on top of a shaky foundation.
