title: P4-E5.1 Serving-mode analytics (static/ssr-new/ssr-dirty/stale-fallback ratios) + 'site serving stale' triage runbook in /infra/runbooks/
description:
## Why
- §14: the serving-mode ratio is the single request-plane health signal for the whole freshness mechanism — SSR share hovering near zero between publishes proves states are collapsing back to A (builds succeeding, markers comparing correctly); a sustained rise means a freshness bug (KV writes failing, routing regression, build silently stale) **or scraping** (§18 row 7: monitor serving-mode ratio is a named mitigation).
- The runbook turns the signal into action: when someone reports "the site is serving stale", on-call needs a deterministic triage path through the §3 machinery instead of re-deriving it at 3 a.m.

## What
- **Instrumentation:** in the custom Worker entry (P4-E3.1), sample `x-immo-serving` outcomes (static / ssr-new / ssr-dirty / stale-fallback) into Workers analytics (§14: "sampled via Workers analytics"); ensure state-A responses are attributable (header or sampling default) so ratios are complete.
- **Dashboard/query:** ratios over time, per environment (staging/prod); document how to read it (SSR share ~0 between publishes; publish/edit events appear as short blips; stale-fallback indicates origin failures being absorbed per §3.7).
- **Runbook** `/infra/runbooks/site-serving-stale.md` (§14 runbooks list): symptom → checks: `/__build.json` `built_at` age + BuildAgeMonitor state (P3-E3), builds table `failed`/`skipped` history (P3-E1/E2), KV dirty keys vs `built_at`, deploy-hook reachability, ConfirmBuild logs, Worker routing regression; cross-link the P4-E3.4 chaos procedure, the rollback runbook (Worker versions + Coolify, §14), and the manual Rebuild-now escape hatch (P3-E2.1).

## Out of scope
- Alert wiring on ratio thresholds (observe first; BuildAgeMonitor P3-E3 remains the paging alert); Sentry/uptime monitors (P8-E2).
design:
- Source header: x-immo-serving set by the Worker for content routes (§3.4 + §3.7 values: static | ssr-new | ssr-dirty | stale-fallback)
- Sink: Workers analytics sampling (Analytics Engine binding or equivalent Workers analytics, §14) — sampled, not per-request logging
- Health semantics (§14): SSR share ~0 between publishes is healthy; stale-fallback > 0 means origin failures are being absorbed (§3.7)
- Runbook lives in /infra/runbooks/ alongside deploy/rollback/restore/rotation/incident docs (§4, §14)
acceptance_criteria:
- Ratios static / ssr-new / ssr-dirty / stale-fallback queryable per environment over time, sourced from sampled x-immo-serving (§14)
- Staging freshness e2e runs (P4-E2.4 / P4-E4.5) visibly register as ssr-new / ssr-dirty blips that settle to static after the next build
- Sustained-rise interpretation documented (freshness bug or scraping, §14 / §18 row 7) with a suggested watch threshold
- Runbook /infra/runbooks/site-serving-stale.md walks symptom -> causes: /__build.json age (BuildAgeMonitor), builds table failed/skipped history, KV dirty keys vs built_at, deploy-hook reachability, ConfirmBuild logs, Worker routing regression — and cross-links the P4-E3.4 chaos procedure and the rollback runbook
- Hypercare usage noted: watched during the 48 h launch window (§16 P8-E4)
notes: Spec: §14 dashboards + runbooks bullets, §16 P4-E5. Risk register: §18 row 7 (scraping shows as serving-mode shift; tiered tokens + WAF are the control, this is the monitor). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E4.1 Billing admin: per-developer subscription status + payment history + manual mark-paid UI
description:
## Why
§6.2: offline CMI onboarding (§11: Manual = day-one path) needs an operator UI — without mark-paid the first paying customer cannot be activated, and without status/history visibility, publish-gate failures (§5.13) are undebuggable for staff.

## What
- Developer billing tab/screen: subscription card — plan (basic|featured|enterprise), status (trialing|active|past_due|canceled), provider (stripe|cmi|manual), current_period_start/end, cancel_at_period_end (§5.9).
- Payment history table: amount, currency, status (pending|succeeded|failed|refunded), provider, provider_payment_id, invoice_url link, paid_at — newest first.
- Manual mark-paid form: period covered + amount/currency → the P6-E1.2 context op → payment (provider=manual, succeeded) + subscription activation; confirmation UX + audit-log entry (§5.12).
- Subscription-gate feedback on publish screens: when BILLING_ENFORCED=true and the gate blocks publishing, show the reason + link here (§6.2).
- RBAC via on_mount hooks: admin write, manager read-only, others no access (§6.2).

## Out of scope
- Initiating Stripe/CMI checkout sessions from admin (separate flow once adapters land); refunds workflow beyond displaying status.
design:
- LiveView components in the existing admin shell (P1-E3 patterns); on_mount role gating (§6.2: admin write, manager billing-read)
- Mark-paid form (period covered + amount/currency) → Immo.Billing context op from P6-E1.2 — no billing logic in the UI layer
- Gate feedback derives from Catalog.published/1 (§5.13 single predicate) — no duplicated rule
- Flag-aware copy: with BILLING_ENFORCED=false show informational status only (no scary blocked-state warnings)
acceptance_criteria:
- Mark-paid creates the payment row (provider=manual, succeeded) and activates the subscription; UI reflects it without reload (LiveView)
- Status card and history table render exactly the §5.9 fields; invoice_url opens when present; history newest-first
- Role matrix test: admin can mark paid; manager sees read-only; editor has no route to billing screens
- A publish attempt blocked by the billing gate (flag on) shows actionable feedback linking to the billing screen
- The mutation appears in audit_log with actor + diff (§5.12)
notes: Spec: §6.2 billing bullet, §5.9, §5.12, §5.13, §11. Open decisions: D13 (default flag off; screens must be useful in both states). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E3.1 CMI adapter: hosted page redirect + MAC verification (reject tampered) + invoice/manual-recurring mode + sandbox tests
description:
## Why
§18: if Stripe cannot serve the MA entity (P6-E2.1 verdict), CMI is the primary card rail — it must be production-grade, not a stub. §11 constrains v1 scope honestly: hosted payment page + MAC-signature verification now; recurring later (needs bank-side setup), bridged by invoice/manual-recurring mode so revenue is never blocked on the bank.

## What
- Adapter module implementing all four P6-E1.1 Provider callbacks (§11):
  - `create_checkout_session/2`: build the CMI hosted-payment-page redirect (merchant id, amount, currency MAD, order id, ok/fail callback URLs) with the MAC computed over the canonical param string.
  - `verify_webhook/2`: recompute the MAC over the raw callback params with the CMI store key; constant-time compare; reject tampered (§16 AC).
  - `normalize_event/1`: CMI approval/decline callbacks → normalized `payment_succeeded`/`payment_failed` events; `provider_payment_id` = CMI transaction id.
  - `cancel/1`: local cancel semantics (no provider-side recurring in invoice mode).
- `POST /webhooks/cmi` wired through the §6.6 contract: raw verification → raw event insert → `PaymentWebhookProcessor` (queue `payments`) → idempotent processing (reuse P6-E2.2 plumbing).
- Invoice/manual-recurring mode: a succeeded CMI payment opens/extends `current_period_start/end`; renewal = a new hosted payment or admin mark-paid; operator flow documented.
- Tests: sandbox run against the CMI test environment + unit tests with recorded fixtures (tampered MAC, wrong amount, replayed callback).

## Out of scope
- Bank-side recurring billing (follow-up once enabled); refund tooling beyond recording status=refunded.
design:
- MAC: HMAC per CMI spec over the canonical sorted param string with the store key (CMI_* env §12.4); Plug.Crypto constant-time compare; verify on RAW callback params before parsing (§6.6)
- create_checkout_session/2 builds the hosted-page redirect: merchant id, amount, currency MAD (§5.4 default), order id, ok/fail callback URLs + computed MAC
- normalize_event/1: approval/decline callbacks → payment_succeeded/payment_failed normalized events (P6-E1.1 struct)
- Reuses the P6-E2.2 webhook plumbing (raw-body/raw-params reader + PaymentWebhookProcessor on queue payments) — adapter-only differences; hosted page only, SAQ-A posture (§11)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 AC: tampered callback (any param or the MAC altered) rejected with 4xx and zero state change
- Sandbox happy path: redirect → pay on the CMI test page → callback verified → payment row (succeeded) + subscription period opened/extended
- Replayed callback processed exactly once (provider_payment_id = CMI transaction id, unique index)
- CMI_* env vars present in the §12.4 registry; secrets never logged (Logger redaction per §13)
- Invoice/manual-recurring operator flow documented (how a period is opened, renewed, and reconciled)
notes: Spec: §11 CMI bullet, §6.6, §5.9, §12.4, §13 redaction, §16 P6-E3 AC, §18 risk row. Open decisions: D13; recurring mode pending bank-side setup — invoice/manual mode is the v1 deliverable. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P6-E3 — CMI adapter (Morocco interbank gateway)
description:
## Why
R10 names CMI the Morocco adapter, and §18 ranks "Stripe unavailable for MA entity" a top risk with the explicit mitigation that CMI + Manual are first-class (P6-E1/E3), not afterthoughts — if the P6-E2.1 verdict goes against Stripe, CMI is the primary card rail. §11 scopes it realistically: hosted payment page + MAC-signature verification now; manual/invoice mode FIRST because CMI recurring billing requires bank-side setup.

## What
- `Immo.Billing.Providers.CMI` implementing the P6-E1.1 behaviour: hosted payment page redirect (`create_checkout_session/2` → signed redirect params), MAC verification of callbacks (`verify_webhook/2` — reject tampered, §16 AC), `normalize_event/1` mapping CMI approval/decline callbacks to normalized events, `cancel/1` with local semantics (invoice mode has no provider-side recurring to cancel).
- Invoice/manual-recurring mode first (§11): subscription periods opened/extended via one-off hosted payments or admin mark-paid until bank-side recurring exists.
- `POST /webhooks/cmi` callback wired through the §6.6 endpoint contract (raw verification → raw event insert → `PaymentWebhookProcessor`, idempotent).
- Sandbox-tested against the CMI test environment; `CMI_*` env vars registered (§12.4).

## Out of scope
- Bank-side recurring billing setup (follow-up once CMI/the bank enables it); admin UI (P6-E4).
design:
- Hosted payment page redirect: merchant params + MAC over the canonical param string; callback MAC recomputed over raw params with the CMI store key (CMI_* env, §12.4); constant-time compare
- provider enum cmi (§5.9); provider_payment_id = CMI transaction id (unique index → replay-safe)
- Manual/invoice mode FIRST (§11): CMI recurring billing requires bank-side setup — periods opened/extended by one-off hosted payments or admin mark-paid
- Same PaymentWebhookProcessor pipeline as Stripe (§6.5/§6.6) — differences live in the adapter only
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P6-E3 AC: signature verification rejects tampered callbacks (MAC mismatch → 4xx, zero state change)
- Sandbox: hosted-page payment completes and activates/extends a subscription period
- Invoice/manual-recurring mode works and is documented — no bank-side recurring setup required to take money
- CMI webhook path reuses the §6.6 contract: raw-payload verification, raw event insert, idempotent async processing
notes: Spec: §11 CMI bullet, §6.6, §5.9, §12.4 CMI_*, §16 P6-E3, §18 Stripe-MA risk (CMI/Manual first-class). Open decisions: D13; CMI recurring mode pending bank-side setup. Cross-phase deps (P6-E1) wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E2.3 Dunning: past_due grace GRACE_DAYS=7 → daily sweep auto-unpublish → MarkPathsDirty (freshness covers visibility ≤ 1 min; no immediate rebuild needed)
description:
## Why
§11: when payment fails, content must come down — but with a humane grace window (`GRACE_DAYS=7`) and through the existing freshness machinery: unpublish → KV dirty marks → SSR serves API-404 → real 404 page within ~a minute. No immediate rebuild is needed; the next cron build bakes the change (§11 explicitly relies on the freshness layer here).

## What
- `past_due` entry: driven by normalized provider events (e.g. `invoice.payment_failed` from P6-E2.2 processing); grace clock starts at the transition.
- Daily Oban cron sweep: find subscriptions `past_due` longer than `GRACE_DAYS` (default 7, §12.4) → auto-unpublish the developer projects/listings via Catalog unpublish transitions → `MarkPathsDirty` fires for all affected paths (§3.5 unpublish trigger: SSR gets API 404 → renders 404 with no-store).
- Recovery semantics: payment succeeds during grace → status back to `active`, no unpublish; after unpublish, re-activation enables re-publish — document the chosen policy (manual vs automatic re-publish).
- E2e: expiry scenario hides content ≤ 2 min after the sweep (§16 P6-E2 AC).

## Out of scope
- Dunning emails/notifications to developers (file separately if product wants them); payment retry orchestration (Stripe Billing handles its own retries).
design:
- Daily Oban cron sweep (default queue); GRACE_DAYS env, default 7 (§12.4)
- past_due entry driven by normalized provider events (invoice.payment_failed → subscription_past_due)
- Unpublish via Catalog transitions so the §3.5 MarkPathsDirty triggers fire — no bespoke path computation in the sweep
- Recovery: payment success during grace → active, no unpublish; post-unpublish re-activation enables re-publish — document the chosen re-publish policy (manual vs automatic)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 AC: expiry e2e hides content ≤ 2 min after the sweep (pages 404 via the freshness layer)
- Sweep only unpublishes after the full GRACE_DAYS window has elapsed; a successful payment during grace prevents unpublish
- All affected public paths marked dirty per Edge.Paths (listing detail + parent project + developer paths, per-locale)
- Sweep is idempotent — re-running it changes nothing — and unpublish actions are audit-logged (§5.12)
- No rebuild is triggered by the sweep (next cron build bakes the 404s; §11)
notes: Spec: §11 dunning bullet, §3.5 unpublish trigger, §12.4 GRACE_DAYS, §16 P6-E2 AC. Open decisions: D13; re-publish-on-recovery policy (manual vs automatic) to confirm with PO — default manual. Cross-phase deps (P4-E4 freshness layer) wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E2.2 POST /webhooks/stripe: Stripe-Signature verify on raw body → insert raw event → enqueue PaymentWebhookProcessor (queue payments, idempotent on provider event id / unique provider_payment_id)
description:
## Why
§6.6: webhooks are the only externally-driven write path in the system — the signature must be verified against the RAW body before any parsing, the endpoint must answer 200 fast (providers retry aggressively), and replays must be harmless (R10 "idempotent webhooks"). Getting this wrong corrupts billing state or loses payments.

## What
- `POST /webhooks/stripe` controller per §6.6:
  - Custom body-reader plug caches the raw body for the webhooks scope (Plug.Parsers must not consume it first).
  - Call adapter `verify_webhook/2` with the `Stripe-Signature` header against the raw body; invalid → 400, zero side effects.
  - On valid: insert the raw event row, enqueue `PaymentWebhookProcessor` (queue `payments`, §6.5), respond 200 immediately — all processing async.
- `PaymentWebhookProcessor`: `normalize_event/1` → upsert payment (unique `provider_payment_id`) / transition subscription status; idempotent on the provider event id — duplicate delivery is a no-op; publish-affecting transitions (activation/expiry) → enqueue `MarkPathsDirty` for the developer content (§11).
- Tests (§15.1): signature pass/fail, duplicate replay, out-of-order events, unique-violation-as-no-op.

## Out of scope
- Stripe event semantics/mapping (P6-E2.1 normalize_event); CMI callback wiring (P6-E3.1 reuses this plumbing); dunning (P6-E2.3).
design:
- Raw-body caching reader plug mounted on the /webhooks scope so Plug.Parsers does not consume the body; verification BEFORE any parsing (§6.6)
- Verification delegated to adapter verify_webhook/2 with the Stripe-Signature header + STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (§12.4)
- PaymentWebhookProcessor on queue payments (concurrency 5, §3.2 queue config); Oban unique on provider event id; payments.provider_payment_id unique index (§5.9)
- Signature-failure spike feeds the §14 alert (webhook signature failures spike)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 AC: events replayed via Stripe CLI are processed exactly once — second delivery changes nothing (payment count and subscription status stable)
- Tampered body or invalid Stripe-Signature → 4xx, no event row inserted, no job enqueued
- Endpoint responds fast (verify + insert + enqueue only; all processing async in Oban)
- Unique-constraint hits on provider_payment_id / event id handled as success-no-op, not job failure (idempotency)
- Publish-affecting transitions (activation/expiry) enqueue MarkPathsDirty for the developer content (§11)
- §15.1 webhook signature + idempotency tests green
notes: Spec: §6.6 (raw body, 200 fast, replay-safe), §6.5 PaymentWebhookProcessor row, §5.9, §11 flow, §15.1, §14 alerts. Open decisions: none. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E2.1 Stripe adapter (stripity_stripe): hosted Checkout sessions (PCI SAQ-A) + subscription lifecycle + document MA-entity availability verdict (else EU entity or CMI-primary)
description:
## Why
R10 makes Stripe primary; §11 mandates hosted checkout only so raw card data never touches the stack (PCI SAQ-A). §18 flags the open risk that Stripe cannot serve a Moroccan entity — this task must produce the documented verdict deciding whether Stripe operates via MA entity, via an EU entity, or CMI becomes the primary rail.

## What
- `Immo.Billing.Providers.Stripe` implementing the P6-E1.1 behaviour via stripity_stripe:
  - `create_checkout_session/2` → Stripe Billing hosted Checkout session (subscription mode; plan basic|featured|enterprise → Price ID mapping); returns the redirect URL.
  - `cancel/1` → cancel at period end or immediate per args; mirrors `cancel_at_period_end` (§5.9).
  - `verify_webhook/2` → Stripe-Signature verification with `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (consumed by P6-E2.2).
  - `normalize_event/1` → map `checkout.session.completed`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `customer.subscription.updated|deleted` to normalized events driving §5.9 status transitions (trialing|active|past_due|canceled).
- Persist `provider_subscription_id`, `current_period_start/end` from Stripe subscription objects.
- Document the MA-entity availability verdict (ADR/notes per §11/§18): Stripe via MA entity? else EU entity or CMI-primary.

## Out of scope
- The webhook HTTP endpoint + processor (P6-E2.2); dunning sweep (P6-E2.3); customer self-serve portal.
design:
- stripity_stripe client; env STRIPE_SECRET, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (§12.4 registry)
- Plan mapping basic|featured|enterprise → Stripe Price IDs via config (§5.9 plan enum)
- normalize_event/1 maps checkout.session.completed / invoice.paid / invoice.payment_failed / customer.subscription.updated|deleted → the P6-E1.1 normalized event struct — processor stays provider-agnostic
- Persist provider_subscription_id, current_period_start/end, cancel_at_period_end from Stripe objects (§5.9)
acceptance_criteria:
- Checkout session created in Stripe test mode redirects to the Stripe-hosted page; completing it activates the subscription (status active, current_period_start/end set)
- Lifecycle events map to the correct §5.9 statuses (active, past_due, canceled) in adapter tests with recorded fixtures
- No card-data fields anywhere in the stack — hosted checkout only (PCI SAQ-A posture)
- cancel/1 honors cancel_at_period_end vs immediate; flag mirrored from the Stripe subscription object
- MA-entity availability verdict documented with the chosen operating path (MA entity / EU entity / CMI-primary)
notes: Spec: §11 Stripe bullet, §5.9, §12.4, §18 Stripe-MA risk row. Open decisions: D13; the MA-entity verdict is a deliverable of this task (§11: confirm MA entity availability in P6). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P6-E2 — Stripe adapter + webhooks + dunning
description:
## Why
R10 names Stripe the primary provider — hosted Checkout only (PCI SAQ-A), idempotent webhooks. §6.6 fixes the webhook contract (signature over the RAW body before parsing, fast 200, replay-safe unique index) and §11 the lifecycle: publish-affecting events (activation/expiry) flow through MarkPathsDirty so the freshness layer makes visibility changes live within ~1 minute — no rebuild coupling.

## What
- Stripe adapter (stripity_stripe) implementing `Immo.Billing.Provider`: hosted Checkout sessions + subscription lifecycle mapping; document the MA-entity availability verdict (§11: else operate via EU entity or make CMI primary).
- `POST /webhooks/stripe` (§6.6): verify `Stripe-Signature` against the raw body before parsing; insert raw event; enqueue `PaymentWebhookProcessor` (queue `payments`, §6.5); respond 200 fast; replay-safe via unique provider event id / `provider_payment_id`.
- Dunning (§11): `past_due` grace `GRACE_DAYS=7` → daily sweep auto-unpublishes the developer content → `MarkPathsDirty` → pages 404/hidden within a minute via the freshness layer.

## Out of scope
- CMI adapter (P6-E3); admin billing UI (P6-E4); self-serve developer checkout portal (admin-initiated for v1, §11).
design:
- stripity_stripe; env: STRIPE_SECRET + STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (§12.4)
- §6.6 contract: verify Stripe-Signature against the RAW body before parsing (body-caching reader plug); insert raw event; enqueue; respond 200 fast
- PaymentWebhookProcessor on Oban queue payments (§6.5; queues payments: 5 per §3.2), idempotent on provider event id; payments.provider_payment_id unique (§5.9)
- Dunning: GRACE_DAYS=7 (§12.4) → daily sweep auto-unpublish → MarkPathsDirty → freshness layer covers visibility ≤ 1 min, no immediate rebuild (§11)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P6-E2 AC: Stripe CLI replayed events are processed exactly once (no duplicate payments or duplicate status transitions)
- §16 P6-E2 AC: expiry e2e hides content ≤ 2 min after the dunning sweep
- Signature failure → 4xx, no event row, no job; webhook signature failures feed the §14 spike alert
- Checkout reaches the Stripe-hosted page; raw card data never touches the stack (hosted checkout only, PCI SAQ-A)
notes: Spec: §11 flow + dunning, §6.6 webhook contract, §6.5 PaymentWebhookProcessor, §12.4, §16 P6-E2. Open decisions: D13 (gate flag default); MA-entity verdict documented in P6-E2.1 (§18 fallback = CMI/Manual). Cross-phase deps (P6-E1, P4-E4) wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E1.2 Manual adapter (admin marks paid) + BILLING_ENFORCED gate wired into Catalog.published/1 (flag off, §5.13) + tests both flag states
description:
## Why
§11: Manual is the day-one onboarding path (offline/bank-transfer customers, pre-gateway CMI onboarding), and D13 launches with `BILLING_ENFORCED=false` — but R10 requires the publish gate to be real, wired and tested now ("publish gate inert but code path tested"), not bolted on when the first paying customer arrives.

## What
- `Manual` adapter implementing `Immo.Billing.Provider`: `create_checkout_session/2` → no-op/instructional result; `cancel/1` → local cancel; `verify_webhook/2` / `normalize_event/1` → not-applicable stubs (no external webhooks exist for manual).
- Mark-paid context operation: admin marks a subscription period paid (provider = manual) → payment row (status `succeeded`, `paid_at`) + subscription activated with `current_period_start/end` set (§5.9).
- `BILLING_ENFORCED` gate inside `Catalog.published/1` (§5.13): when true, projects/listings count as published only if the owning developer has an `active|trialing` subscription; when false, the predicate is unchanged. Flag from runtime env (§12.4), default false (D13).
- Tests for BOTH flag states across the §15.1 predicate-matrix consumers: read API, sitemap endpoint, search, geo, skip-if-unchanged.

## Out of scope
- The mark-paid LiveView UI (P6-E4.1 — this task ships the context op it calls); Stripe/CMI adapters.
design:
- Gate = composable exists/join on subscriptions with status in (active, trialing) inside Catalog.published/1 (§5.13) — applied only when BILLING_ENFORCED
- BILLING_ENFORCED in the §12.4 env registry; default false (D13); GRACE_DAYS listed alongside for P6-E2.3
- Manual adapter: create_checkout_session/2 → instructional no-op result; cancel/1 → local cancel; verify_webhook/2 + normalize_event/1 → not-applicable stubs (no external webhooks)
- Mark-paid is an admin-scope context fn (RBAC §6.2: manager billing-read only); audit-logged (§5.12)
acceptance_criteria:
- Mark-paid creates a payment row (status succeeded, provider=manual, paid_at set) and flips the subscription to active with current_period_start/end set
- BILLING_ENFORCED=true: a developer without an active|trialing subscription has projects/listings excluded everywhere published/1 is consumed (read API, sitemap, search, geo, skip-if-unchanged); =false: behavior identical to pre-gate — both proven by the §15.1 predicate matrix
- Flag flips via runtime env without code change (runtime.exs read)
- Publish-state rule stays single-sourced: no second published definition introduced (§5.13 rule upheld in review)
notes: Spec: §11 Manual = day-one onboarding path, §5.13, §12.4, §15.1 predicate matrix, §16 P6-E1. Open decisions: D13 (default BILLING_ENFORCED=false; flips when first paying developer onboards). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P6-E1.1 Immo.Billing.Provider behaviour: create_checkout_session/2, cancel/1, verify_webhook/2, normalize_event/1 + Billing context over subscriptions/payments tables (§5.9)
description:
## Why
R10: every provider (Stripe, CMI, Manual) must plug into one contract so webhook processing, admin screens and the publish gate stay provider-agnostic. The §18 mitigation ("CMI + Manual adapters are first-class") depends on this seam existing before any concrete gateway adapter is written.

## What
- `Immo.Billing.Provider` behaviour with the §11 callbacks: `create_checkout_session/2` (subscription/plan + opts → hosted-checkout session/URL), `cancel/1`, `verify_webhook/2` (raw body + signature material → verified | rejected), `normalize_event/1` (provider payload → normalized internal event struct).
- Migrations for §5.9:
  - `subscriptions`: developer_id fk · plan enum `basic|featured|enterprise` · status enum `trialing|active|past_due|canceled` · provider enum `stripe|cmi|manual` · provider_subscription_id · current_period_start/end · cancel_at_period_end boolean.
  - `payments`: subscription_id fk · amount numeric(14,2) · currency · status enum `pending|succeeded|failed|refunded` · provider · provider_payment_id **unique** (idempotency) · invoice_url · paid_at · raw_event jsonb.
- `Immo.Billing` context (§6.1): subscription/payment CRUD, status transitions, adapter dispatch by `subscription.provider`; mutations through the §5.12 audit_log wrapper.

## Out of scope
- Manual adapter + gate wiring (P6-E1.2); any concrete gateway (P6-E2/E3); webhook endpoint (P6-E2.2).
design:
- @callback create_checkout_session/2 (subscription/plan + opts → hosted checkout URL/session), cancel/1, verify_webhook/2 (raw body + signature header → verified|rejected), normalize_event/1 (provider payload → normalized event struct)
- Normalized event struct: type (payment_succeeded|payment_failed|subscription_activated|subscription_past_due|subscription_canceled), provider ids, amount/currency, occurred_at, raw
- Adapter resolution: provider enum stripe|cmi|manual → module map in config (§5.9)
- payments.raw_event jsonb retains the original payload for forensics (§5.9)
acceptance_criteria:
- Behaviour compiles with the four §11 callbacks exactly as named; a test adapter exercises the full dispatch path
- subscriptions + payments tables match §5.9 field-for-field; provider_payment_id carries a unique index (replay-safety backbone for §6.6)
- Context tests: subscription lifecycle transitions (trialing|active|past_due|canceled), payment insert, adapter dispatch by provider field
- Billing mutations audit-logged via the §5.12 wrapper
- Migrations reversible
notes: Spec: §11 adapter behaviour, §5.9 schema, §5.12 audit_log, §6.1. Open decisions: D13. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P6-E1 — Billing provider behaviour + Manual adapter
description:
## Why
R10: B2B subscriptions gate publishing for developers/agencies — behind a provider-adapter so Stripe, CMI and Manual are interchangeable (§11). `BILLING_ENFORCED=false` at launch (D13) but the publish-gate code path must exist and be tested from day one ("publish gate inert but code path tested", §11). §18 ranks Stripe-unavailable-for-MA a real risk: Manual is the day-one onboarding path and the behaviour contract is what keeps CMI/Manual first-class rather than afterthoughts.

## What
- `Immo.Billing.Provider` behaviour (§11): callbacks `create_checkout_session/2`, `cancel/1`, `verify_webhook/2`, `normalize_event/1`.
- `Immo.Billing` context (§6.1) over the §5.9 tables: `subscriptions` (developer_id, plan basic|featured|enterprise, status trialing|active|past_due|canceled, provider stripe|cmi|manual, provider_subscription_id, current_period_start/end, cancel_at_period_end) and `payments` (subscription_id, amount numeric(14,2), currency, status pending|succeeded|failed|refunded, provider, provider_payment_id unique, invoice_url, paid_at, raw_event jsonb).
- Manual adapter: admin marks paid (provider = manual) — zero external calls; the day-one onboarding path (§11).
- `BILLING_ENFORCED` flag wired into `Catalog.published/1` (§5.13): published ⇒ owning developer has an active|trialing subscription when the flag is on; flag off at launch (D13); both states tested.

## Out of scope
- Stripe adapter + webhooks + dunning (P6-E2); CMI adapter (P6-E3); admin billing screens beyond the context op (P6-E4).
design:
- Behaviour callbacks (§11 verbatim): create_checkout_session/2, cancel/1, verify_webhook/2, normalize_event/1
- Adapter dispatch by subscriptions.provider enum stripe|cmi|manual (§5.9)
- BILLING_ENFORCED from runtime env (§12.4), default false (D13); gate composed into the single Catalog.published/1 predicate (§5.13) — no second definition anywhere
- Subscription statuses trialing|active|past_due|canceled; plans basic|featured|enterprise (§5.9)
acceptance_criteria:
- Immo.Billing.Provider behaviour defines exactly create_checkout_session/2, cancel/1, verify_webhook/2, normalize_event/1; Manual adapter implements it
- §5.9 migrations live: subscriptions + payments field-for-field, incl. unique index on provider_payment_id (idempotency backbone)
- published/1 matrix (§15.1) covers the billing gate: BILLING_ENFORCED=true excludes content of developers without active|trialing subscription from read API, sitemap, search, geo; =false leaves behavior unchanged — both states tested
- Manual flow: admin mark-paid creates a succeeded payment row and activates the subscription
notes: Spec: §11, §5.9, §5.13, §6.1 Billing context, §12.4 env registry, §16 P6-E1. Open decisions: D13 (default BILLING_ENFORCED=false until first paying developer). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E6.4 RetentionSweeper daily cron: purge closed inquiries after INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365)
description:
## Why
- Privacy/data-minimization (Law 09-08/GDPR): leads are PII; §5.7 mandates "Retention job purges closed inquiries after INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365)" and the §13 release gate checks "retention sweeps on".

## What
- Oban cron worker `RetentionSweeper`, daily, on the default queue (§6.5).
- Deletes inquiries with `status=closed` older than `INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS` (env, default 365) (§5.7).
- Logged purge counts; failure visibility via Oban retries/alerts (§14).

## Out of scope
- Retention for other PII stores (none specified for v1); audit_log retention (unspecified).
design:
- Oban.Plugins.Cron daily schedule → RetentionSweeper on the default queue (§6.5)
- Purge = hard delete of status=closed inquiries past INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS (§5.7 says purges — not soft-delete)
- Age measured from the closed-state timestamp (updated_at at close)
- INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS sourced from runtime env (§12.4 registry, VPS-scoped flag)
acceptance_criteria:
- Closed inquiry older than the threshold is hard-deleted; closed-but-younger, new and contacted inquiries retained (§5.7)
- INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS env respected; default 365 when unset (§5.7)
- Daily cron entry registered in the Oban config (§6.5)
- Purge counts logged; failures surface via Oban retry/alerting (§14)
- Job test covers threshold boundary cases
notes: Spec: §5.7 (retention rule), §6.5 (RetentionSweeper: default queue, daily cron), §13 (retention sweeps on), §12.4 (INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E6.3 Admin inquiries inbox: status new|contacted|closed + assignment + CSV export
description:
## Why
- §6.2: "Inquiries inbox: status workflow, assignment, CSV export" — where staff actually work leads. Per the §6.2 role matrix, CRM belongs to admin + manager (editor is catalog-only; developer_user sees own projects/listings only).

## What
- LiveView inbox at /admin/inquiries: filterable list (status, assignee, listing/project) + detail view (§6.2).
- Status workflow `new → contacted → closed` (§5.7 enum).
- Assignment to staff (`handled_by_user_id`, §5.7).
- CSV export of the filtered set (§6.2).
- Mutations audit-logged via the P1-E2.4 wrapper (§13: audit_log on all admin mutations).

## Out of scope
- Email notification (P1-E6.2); retention (P1-E6.4); any developer_user lead visibility (not granted by §6.2).
design:
- /admin/inquiries LiveView under the role-gated live_session (P1-E1.2 hooks; CRM = manager+admin per §6.2)
- Status/assignment mutations via Immo.CRM context functions wrapped by the audit layer (P1-E2.4)
- CSV streamed from the filtered query (no temp files)
- Detail view shows message, consent, source, locale and the related listing/project
acceptance_criteria:
- Status transitions new → contacted → closed persist and are audit-logged (§5.7/§5.12)
- Assignment to a staff user persists in handled_by_user_id and is visible in list + detail (§5.7)
- CSV export downloads the currently filtered set with the §5.7 fields in stable column order
- Access per the §6.2 matrix: admin + manager allowed (CRM); editor and developer_user denied
- List filterable by status, assignee and listing/project; paginated
notes: Spec: §6.2 (inquiries inbox: status workflow, assignment, CSV export), §5.7, §5.12. Deps: P1-E6.1 (rows exist). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E6.2 InquiryNotifier Oban job (queue mailers): Swoosh + Resend/SES email to assigned staff
description:
## Why
- Lead response time is the business value of the inquiries feature; §6.5 specifies async notification (queue `mailers`) so the public endpoint stays fast and mailer outages never block lead capture.

## What
- Oban worker `InquiryNotifier` on queue `mailers`, triggered on inquiry insert (§6.5).
- Swoosh with Resend/SES adapter per environment config (§6.5).
- Email to assigned staff (`handled_by_user_id`) when present; configured default staff recipient otherwise (spec says "assigned staff" — at insert time assignment is usually empty, so a default recipient is required for the trigger-on-insert flow to be useful).
- Content: lead fields + admin deep link.

## Out of scope
- Inbox/assignment UI (P1-E6.3); digest/secondary notifications (not specified).
design:
- Oban worker on queue :mailers, trigger = inquiry insert (§6.5 catalog row)
- Swoosh mailer with Resend or SES adapter selected by runtime env (§6.5)
- Recipient default configurable (env) since assignment usually happens after notification
- Job tests per §15.1 (Oban testing + Swoosh test adapter)
acceptance_criteria:
- Inquiry insert enqueues InquiryNotifier on queue mailers; job sends exactly one email (asserted via Swoosh test adapter)
- Email contains lead name/contact/message and a link to the admin inquiry
- Recipient resolution: assigned staff (handled_by_user_id) when set, else configured default staff address
- Transient mailer failure retries via Oban; a retry after success does not double-send
- Exhausted retries surface for alerting (§14: Oban job retries exhausted)
notes: Spec: §6.5 (InquiryNotifier: queue mailers, Swoosh email to assigned staff), §15.1, §14 (alert on retries exhausted). Deps: P1-E6.1. Mailer credentials in the §12.4 registry. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E6.1 POST /api/v1/inquiries: Turnstile token verified server-side + honeypot + 5/min/IP + consent flag (Law 09-08/GDPR) + source/locale capture
description:
## Why
- The only anonymous write endpoint in the system (R7, §10.1 path 3) — every §13 abuse control applies: "Turnstile verified server-side; honeypot live", rate limits, changeset validation on every write.
- Consent capture (Law 09-08/GDPR) at the moment of submission is what legitimizes storing lead PII at all (§5.7).

## What
- `POST /api/v1/inquiries` on the `:api_public` pipeline (§6.3): fields per §5.7 (listing_id/project_id optional, name, email, phone, message, locale, consent, source) + `turnstile_token`.
- Server-side Turnstile verification (siteverify) before insert (§6.3, §13); Turnstile test-keys path for staging E2E (§15.4).
- Honeypot field handling: silently drop/flag (§13).
- 5/min/IP rate limit via the P1-E5.4 Hammer scaffolding (§10.1 path 3).
- On insert: enqueue `InquiryNotifier` (§6.5).
- RFC 9457 problem+json validation errors (§6.3).

## Out of scope
- Email delivery (P1-E6.2); inbox workflow (P1-E6.3); the public form island markup (frontend phases).
design:
- Route mounted on the :api_public pipeline using the 5/min/IP bucket from P1-E5.4 (§6.4/§10.1)
- Body per §5.7 + turnstile_token (§6.3); locale + source captured for attribution
- Server-side Turnstile siteverify call before insert; Turnstile test keys path for staging E2E (§15.4)
- Insert via Immo.CRM context; InquiryNotifier Oban insert transactional with the row
- consent boolean stored per Law 09-08/GDPR (§5.7/§13)
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid submission → 2xx; inquiry row created with status=new, consent, source, locale, optional listing_id/project_id (§5.7); InquiryNotifier enqueued (§6.5)
- Missing/invalid turnstile_token → rejected via server-side siteverify — client-side checks alone never suffice (§6.3/§13)
- Filled honeypot field → submission silently dropped/flagged, no notification (§13)
- 6th request within one minute from the same IP → 429 problem+json (5/min/IP, §10.1 path 3)
- Ecto changeset validation on every field; validation errors as problem+json (§13/§6.3)
- Turnstile verification tested with mocked HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test) incl. failure modes (§15.1)
notes: Spec: §6.3 (POST /inquiries), §5.7, §10.1 path 3, §13, §15.1/§15.4. Deps: P1-E5.4 public pipeline (epic-level dep on P1-E5 covers). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P1-E6 — Inquiries (leads) + email
description:
## Why
- Inquiries are the v1 conversion mechanism — §1.3 rules out visitor accounts ("inquiry forms only"), so leads + fast staff notification are how the platform produces business value.
- R7 path 3 (§10.1): POST /inquiries is one of only three anonymous endpoints; Turnstile (server-side verified) + honeypot + 5/min/IP keep it abuse-resistant per the §13 release gate.
- Privacy: consent flag (Law 09-08/GDPR, §5.7) and retention sweeps (§13 "retention sweeps on") keep PII handling lawful and minimal.

## What
- `POST /api/v1/inquiries` on the public tier: Turnstile verified server-side, honeypot, 5/min/IP, consent flag, source/locale capture (§6.3, §5.7).
- `InquiryNotifier` Oban job (queue `mailers`): Swoosh + Resend/SES email to staff (§6.5).
- Admin inquiries inbox: status `new|contacted|closed`, assignment (handled_by_user_id), CSV export (§6.2, §5.7).
- `RetentionSweeper` daily cron: purge closed inquiries after `INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 365) (§5.7, §6.5).

## Out of scope
- The frontend inquiry form island (P2/P5 frontend work); Turnstile widget embedding (frontend); WAF-level rate rules (infra, §10.1).
design:
- inquiries per §5.7: listing_id fk nullable, project_id fk nullable, name, email, phone, message text, locale, consent boolean, source string, status enum new|contacted|closed, handled_by_user_id fk nullable
- POST /inquiries rides the :api_public pipeline with the 5/min/IP Hammer bucket from P1-E5.4 (§10.1 path 3); Turnstile verified server-side (§6.3)
- Oban jobs per §6.5: InquiryNotifier (queue mailers, on insert, Swoosh + Resend/SES) and RetentionSweeper (default queue, daily cron)
- CRM surfaces role-gated per §6.2: CRM = admin + manager
acceptance_criteria:
- Anonymous POST /api/v1/inquiries with valid Turnstile token creates an inquiry (status new, consent/source/locale stored) and a staff email is sent (§6.3/§6.5)
- Invalid/missing Turnstile token, filled honeypot, or >5 req/min/IP → request rejected (401/422/429 per case, problem+json) (§10.1 path 3/§13)
- Admin inbox: status workflow new → contacted → closed, assignment to staff, CSV export (§6.2)
- RetentionSweeper purges closed inquiries older than INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365); open/contacted untouched (§5.7)
- inquiries table matches §5.7 field-for-field incl. consent boolean (Law 09-08/GDPR)
notes: Spec: §5.7, §6.3 (POST /inquiries row), §6.5 (InquiryNotifier, RetentionSweeper), §6.2 (inquiries inbox), §10.1 path 3, §13, §16 P1-E6 (Deps: E2, E5). INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS in the §12.4 registry. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E4.2 Admin MapLibre mini-map in forms: geocode button + drag-to-correct writes lat/lng
description:
## Why
§6.2: Moroccan addressing makes pure geocoding unreliable — admins need the visual confirm/correct loop the spec mandates: see the pin on a MapLibre mini-map, drag it to the true location, and have that correction stick (P5-E4.1 honors the manual-pin override).

## What
- MapLibre mini-map embedded in the project and listing LiveView forms (§6.2), showing the current lat/lng pin (city-level default center when coords empty).
- "Geocode" button: enqueues the §6.5 Geocode job and reflects the async result in the form (LiveView update).
- Drag-to-correct: dragging the pin writes lat/lng into the changeset and marks the record manually pinned, so future geocode runs never overwrite (§6.5 contract).
- Reuse the P5-E3.1 basemap (tiles/basemap.pmtiles + brand-tinted style); extend the R2 CORS rule to the admin origin if required.

## Out of scope
- Public map islands (P5-E3); bulk pin-editing tools.
design:
- LiveView JS hook wrapping MapLibre; pin dragend pushes {lat, lng} → changeset fields + sets the manual-pin marker consumed by P5-E4.1
- Basemap reuse: tiles/basemap.pmtiles + brand style from P5-E3.1; admin origin added to the R2 CORS range-GET rule if needed
- Geocode button → enqueue Immo.Jobs.Geocode (§6.5); async result pushed back into the form
- Empty coords: map centers on city-level default; no pin until set
acceptance_criteria:
- Form shows the pin at stored lat/lng; dragging updates the lat/lng fields and persists on save
- After a manual drag, a later geocode run (button or address re-save) does not move the pin — override wins end to end
- Geocode button enqueues the job and the form reflects resulting coords via LiveView update, no full reload
- Works on both project and listing forms (§6.2)
notes: Spec: §6.2 map-pin bullet, §6.5, §9 basemap reuse. Open decisions: D6/D8 defaults apply. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E4.1 Geocode Oban job: triggered on address save + admin button; Nominatim w/ UA + ≤ 1 rps; manual pin override always wins
description:
## Why
§6.5: lat/lng powers the detail map, the search map and /listings/geo. Geocoding must be polite — Nominatim usage policy requires an identifying User-Agent and ≤ 1 rps — and must never clobber a human correction (§6.2 drag-to-correct implies a durable manual-pin override).

## What
- `Immo.Jobs.Geocode` Oban worker on queue `default` (§6.5 jobs catalog).
- Triggers: Catalog context hook when address fields (address/city/region/country, §5.2/§5.4) change on save; admin "geocode" button enqueue (§6.2).
- Nominatim client: configured `User-Agent` header on every request; global throttle ≤ 1 rps across all executions (not per-job).
- Result handling: write lat/lng unless the record is manually pinned (manual pin override always wins); no result → coords stay null + admin feedback; transient HTTP errors → Oban retry with backoff.
- Tests with mocked HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test, §15.1): success, pin-override skip, no-result, retry, throttle behavior.

## Out of scope
- The mini-map UI that sets the pin flag (P5-E4.2); provider swap implementation (D6 override — keep the seam only).
design:
- Immo.Jobs.Geocode, queue default (§6.5; queues config §3.2); trigger points in Catalog context after successful save when address/city/region/country changed
- ≤ 1 rps: global throttle (serialize via unique args + snooze, or shared 1 rps limiter) — document the chosen mechanism
- Provider behind a small module seam so the D6 override (LocationIQ/Geoapify key) is a config swap
- Coords precedence: manual-pin flag (e.g. coords pinned marker set by P5-E4.2) short-circuits the write
acceptance_criteria:
- Address change on save enqueues exactly one job (deduplicated); admin button enqueues on demand
- Every HTTP request carries the configured User-Agent; sustained load never exceeds 1 rps to Nominatim (throttle test)
- Manually pinned records: job runs but does not modify lat/lng (pin override test)
- Job tests green with mocked provider HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test per §15.1): success, no-result, 5xx-retry paths
- No-result leaves coords null and surfaces feedback in admin rather than failing silently
notes: Spec: §6.5 Geocode row, §6.2, §15.1 Oban job tests with mocked HTTP. Open decisions: D6 (default Nominatim; UA + ≤1 rps are policy requirements). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P5-E4 — Geocoding
description:
## Why
Maps (P5-E3) and `/listings/geo` (P5-E1.2) are only as good as the coordinates: §5.2 specifies `lat`/`lng` filled by the Geocode job with an admin map-pin override. §6.5 defines the job contract (Nominatim, User-Agent set, ≤ 1 rps, writes lat/lng unless manually pinned); §6.2 defines the admin correction loop (mini-map, geocode button, drag-to-correct). D6 picks Nominatim with a hard rate cap as the default geocoder.

## What
- `Geocode` Oban job (§6.5): queue `default`; triggered on address save and by an admin button; Nominatim with a proper `User-Agent` and a global ≤ 1 rps throttle; writes lat/lng unless the record is manually pinned — the manual pin always wins.
- Admin map-pin UX (§6.2): MapLibre mini-map in project/listing forms; geocode button enqueues the job; manual drag-to-correct writes lat/lng directly and flags the record as manually pinned.

## Out of scope
- Public map rendering (P5-E3); PostGIS/radius queries (D7); bulk re-geocoding tooling (file later if needed).
design:
- Immo.Jobs.Geocode on Oban default queue (§6.5 catalog); triggers: address save + admin button
- Nominatim client with mandatory User-Agent header and a global ≤ 1 rps throttle (Nominatim usage policy; D6 default)
- Coords precedence contract: manual pin > geocode result — pin flag set by the admin mini-map drag
- D6 override path: LocationIQ/Geoapify key behind the same provider seam (config swap, no job rewrite)
acceptance_criteria:
- Saving an address enqueues Geocode; job writes lat/lng on success
- Job never exceeds 1 request/second to Nominatim and always sends the configured User-Agent (§6.5 row / D6 constraints)
- A manually pinned record is never overwritten by subsequent geocode runs (manual pin always wins)
- Admin can drag the pin to correct; saved lat/lng match the dragged position; geocode button re-enqueues on demand (§6.2)
notes: Spec: §6.5 Geocode row, §6.2 map-pin bullet, §5.2 lat/lng fields, §16 P5-E4. Open decisions: D6 (default Nominatim w/ rate cap; override on volume/quality → LocationIQ/Geoapify). Cross-phase deps (P1-E3) wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E5.4 Public pipeline scaffolding: CORS exact-origin allowlist + Hammer rate limits (search 60, geo 120, inquiries 5 per min/IP) — endpoints themselves land in P5-E1/P1-E6
description:
## Why
- R7 trust path 3 (§10.1): browser islands are anonymous — their entire safety story is CORS exact-origin allowlisting + per-IP rate limits (Hammer in-app, Cloudflare WAF at the edge) + Turnstile on inquiries. §13 release gate: "CORS exact origins, no wildcard; rate limits verified by load test".
- Building the pipeline now (with E5) keeps P5-E1 and P1-E6.1 endpoint work from re-opening auth plumbing.

## What
- `:api_public` pipeline: CORS with exact-origin allowlist (site origins from config; no wildcard) (§10.1, §13).
- Hammer-based rate-limit plug with per-route buckets keyed by IP: search 60/min, geo 120/min, inquiries 5/min (§10.1 path 3).
- 429 problem+json on limit exceeded (§6.3 error convention).
- Cache-Control conventions wired: `private, no-store` for search responses; `public, s-maxage=60` permissible on geo (§6.3).

## Out of scope
- The public endpoints themselves: /search and /listings/geo (P5-E1), POST /inquiries (P1-E6.1); Cloudflare WAF rule configuration (infra/§10.1).
design:
- :api_public pipeline = CORS plug (exact-origin allowlist from runtime config, site origins only) + RateLimit plug (Hammer, per-route buckets keyed by IP) + no auth (§6.4/§10.1 path 3)
- Limits configurable per route with §10.1 defaults (60/120/5 per min per IP)
- 429s rendered via the shared problem+json error path (P1-E5.1)
- Cloudflare WAF rules complement at the edge (§10.1) — infra scope, not app scope
acceptance_criteria:
- Allowed exact origin passes CORS preflight; any other origin receives no CORS allow headers — no wildcard anywhere (§10.1/§13)
- Exceeding a per-IP limit returns 429 problem+json; under-limit requests pass (RFC 9457, §6.3)
- Per-route limit configuration proven with the spec defaults: search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP, inquiries 5/min/IP (§10.1 path 3)
- Pipeline mounts cleanly so P5-E1 (/search, /listings/geo) and P1-E6.1 (POST /inquiries) attach without rework
- Cache-Control conventions available: private, no-store for search; public, s-maxage=60 permissible for geo (§6.3)
notes: Spec: §10.1 path 3, §6.4 (api_public pipeline), §6.3 (cache-control + errors), §13 (CORS exact origins, rate limits verified). Endpoints land in P5-E1 (/search, /listings/geo) and P1-E6.1 (POST /inquiries). Deps: P1-E5.1. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E3.4 RTL map labels: mapbox-gl-rtl-text plugin for Arabic locale
description:
## Why
R8/i18n: Arabic is a first-class locale with full RTL treatment (§7.6). Without the RTL text plugin, MapLibre renders Arabic labels with disconnected, left-to-right glyphs — §9 explicitly mandates loading `mapbox-gl-rtl-text` for the Arabic locale. §18 lists RTL/Arabic regressions as a top risk.

## What
- Load the `mapbox-gl-rtl-text` plugin via `setRTLTextPlugin` when the active locale is `ar` (§9) — lazily, only on Arabic pages, so fr/en JS budgets are untouched.
- Apply through the shared map bootstrap so both surfaces get it: detail ListingMap (P5-E3.2) and the search map (P5-E3.3).
- Host the plugin asset in a CSP-compatible way (§7.6: CSP enabled; avoid new third-party script origins).
- Extend the §15.4 "AR pages render RTL" e2e with a map-label assertion.

## Out of scope
- General RTL/logical-properties work (P7-E1 audit); style/label-language changes beyond shaping.
design:
- maplibregl.setRTLTextPlugin(<plugin url>, lazy: true) gated on active locale === ar
- Plugin asset self-hosted (or pinned) to satisfy CSP (§7.6: csp true, nonce-compatible islands; no surprise third-party origins)
- Wired into the shared map bootstrap so both ListingMap modes inherit it
acceptance_criteria:
- On /ar/ pages, Arabic basemap labels render with correct glyph shaping and direction on both map surfaces (detail + search)
- Plugin not loaded for fr/en locales (network assertion — zero extra bytes outside ar)
- §15.4 RTL e2e extended with a map-label assertion (AR pages render RTL incl. maps)
notes: Spec: §9 RTL bullet, §7.6 i18n/CSP, §15.4 RTL e2e. Open decisions: none. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E3.3 Search map: MapLibre cluster source from /listings/geo + moveend → bbox fetch + abort stale requests + marker click → card popover with path link
description:
## Why
§9/§7.5: the search map is the spatial complement to the SearchFilter island — clustered markers over the public geo endpoint, refreshed per viewport move. §16 P5-E3 binds it to a hard latency budget (pan → bbox results ≤ 500 ms p95 on staging), and §7.5 mandates aborting stale requests so fast pans stay correct.

## What
- Search-page mode of the ListingMap island: MapLibre GeoJSON source with clustering (`cluster: true`) fed by `GET /api/v1/listings/geo` (§9).
- On `moveend`: compute the visible viewport bbox → fetch `/listings/geo?bbox=minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat` (+ `type` when a type filter is active) → swap source data.
- AbortController cancels in-flight requests superseded by a newer move (§7.5 "abort stale requests").
- Marker click → card popover (title, price, thumb) linking to the Feature `path` property (§9).
- Respect the server contract: `limit ≤ 500` results per fetch; render clusters + unclustered points from the FeatureCollection.
- MapLibre lazy-loaded per the shared island loader (budget rules §7.5/§15.5).

## Out of scope
- Two-way binding with SearchFilter facet state (follow-up if product asks); server-side clustering (client clusters per §9).
design:
- MapLibre GeoJSON source with cluster: true over the P5-E1.2 FeatureCollection; cluster + unclustered-point layers
- moveend (not move) triggers fetch — avoids fetch storms; AbortController per request cancels stale ones (§7.5)
- Popover content from Feature properties: id, title, price, path, thumb (§6.3 geo contract)
- Token-free public fetch via api.ts (§7.3); server-side limit≤500 + 120/min/IP rate limit already bound (§10.1)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P5-E3 AC: pan loads bbox results ≤ 500 ms p95 on staging
- Rapid panning never renders out-of-order results — superseded fetches aborted (test under throttled network)
- Clusters expand on zoom; clicking an individual marker opens a card popover whose link navigates to the listing path
- bbox param matches the visible viewport in minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat order (§6.3); type filter forwarded when set
- Geo responses benefit from public, s-maxage=60 edge caching (§6.3) — no cache-busting query noise from the client
notes: Spec: §9 clustering bullet, §7.5 ListingMap search mode, §6.3 geo row, §16 P5-E3 AC. Open decisions: D8. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P3-E3.1 BuildAgeMonitor (every 15 min cron): alert if site /__build.json built_at age > 2× rebuild interval + alerts for build failed status + Oban retries exhausted; wire email/Slack
description:
## Why
- The freshness model fails *silently*: dirty TTLs expire → stale statics return → no error signal anywhere (§14). This job converts that silence into a page. §18 row 2 mitigation = "BuildAgeMonitor + ConfirmBuild + skipped/failed states — alert, don't discover".
- Guards R1 directly and is the long-run backstop for R2/R3 once the KV layer (P4) exists.

## What
- `Immo.Jobs.BuildAgeMonitor`: cron every 15 min, queue `default` (§6.5).
- Fetch `PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json` (§3.3); compute `built_at` age; alert when age > **2× rebuild interval** (derive interval from `REBUILD_CRON`; default 1 h → threshold 2 h).
- Alert on `builds.status = failed` transitions (ConfirmBuild timeout path feeds this).
- Alert on Oban retries exhausted (telemetry hook).
- Wire delivery: Swoosh email (Resend/SES per §12.2) and/or Slack webhook; alert content includes age, threshold, last build row.
- Note: `skipped` builds are fine — age is measured against `built_at` of the deployed site, and a skipped run means content has not changed, so a correct implementation must not false-alarm on quiet days. Use last successful build + last content change to suppress false positives while still catching a dead pipeline. Document the chosen predicate.

## Out of scope
- Admin-facing banner (P3-E2.1 reads the same failed state); broader ops alerts (disk, backups — P8-E2).
design:
- Cron: every 15 min, queue default (§6.5 row BuildAgeMonitor)
- Threshold: built_at age > 2x rebuild interval (default interval 1 h -> alert past 2 h age); interval parsed from REBUILD_CRON
- Age source: GET PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json built_at field (§3.3)
- Delivery: Swoosh email via Resend/SES (§12.2 email stack) + optional Slack webhook; both behind a small notifier module
- Oban telemetry handler for retries-exhausted; ConfirmBuild failure path reuses the same notifier
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulated deploy-hook outage on staging alerts within 15 min of crossing the 2x-interval threshold (§16 P3-E3 AC verbatim)
- built_at age computed from PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json; threshold = 2x rebuild interval derived from REBUILD_CRON
- builds row entering failed status (e.g. ConfirmBuild timeout) triggers an alert
- Oban retries-exhausted events trigger an alert (telemetry handler tested)
- Unreachable /__build.json is itself alertable, not a monitor crash
- Alert payload includes built_at age, threshold, and the last builds row
notes: Spec: §6.5 row BuildAgeMonitor, §14, §16 P3-E3 AC. Risk register: §18 row 2 (silent pipeline breakage -> stale site after TTLs lapse). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E3.2 Detail-page ListingMap: single marker from baked coords (zero fetch), client:visible, MapLibre lazy-loaded
description:
## Why
§7.5 ListingMap (detail mode): the map must add zero data cost — coordinates are already baked into the page view-model (build-time or SSR, identically per R4), and MapLibre only loads when the user actually scrolls the map into view. That lazy-load is what keeps the ≤ 100 KB gz detail-page JS budget achievable (§7.5/§15.5).

## What
- ListingMap island, detail-page mode: props `lat`/`lng` (+ title) from the page view-model (§7.3) — zero fetch for listing data.
- Hydration `client:visible`; MapLibre GL JS + pmtiles protocol dynamically imported only when the island hydrates.
- Single marker at the baked coords on the P5-E3.1 basemap (brand-tinted style).
- Listings without coords: island renders nothing/a hidden state — no broken map.
- Render-mode agnostic (R4): the island receives view-model props only; identical from static and SSR output.

## Out of scope
- Search-page clustered mode (P5-E3.3); RTL plugin wiring (P5-E3.4); admin mini-map (P5-E4.2).
design:
- client:visible hydration + dynamic import(): MapLibre GL JS + pmtiles protocol registered only on hydrate (§7.5 lazy-load mandate)
- Props: {lat, lng, title} from the typed *View model (§7.3) — island never knows the data source (R4)
- Basemap + brand style from P5-E3.1; style URL configurable (D8 swap path)
- No interaction cost before hydrate: static placeholder/poster keeps CLS at 0 (explicit dimensions, §7.6 perf rules)
acceptance_criteria:
- Island makes zero data requests for listing info (coords are props); only tile range requests occur, and only after scroll-into-view
- MapLibre chunk absent from initial page JS; loads on intersection (verified via network panel / Lighthouse trace)
- Detail page total JS ≤ 100 KB gz with the map present (Lighthouse CI budget §15.5)
- Marker renders at the listing lat/lng; records without coords render no broken map (island skipped or hidden)
- Identical behavior on a statically-built page and an SSR-rendered page (R4 dual-source check)
notes: Spec: §7.5 ListingMap row (detail mode), §9, §15.5 JS budget, §7.3 view-models. Open decisions: D8. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E4.4 Alt-text publish gate: photos require alt (i18n) before attachable can publish (SEO/a11y)
description:
## Why
- R8 SEO-first + accessibility: §5.6 marks `alt` (jsonb i18n) as "required for photos before publish (SEO/a11y gate)"; §6.2 lists "alt-text enforcement before publish" in the media manager. Images without alt undermine both image SEO and a11y on every public page.

## What
- Publish-transition check: an attachable (developer/project/listing) cannot publish while any of its `kind=photo` media lacks alt for the required locales (§5.6).
- Actionable admin feedback: which photos, which locales.
- Alt editing UI in the media manager (i18n-tabbed, reusing the P1-E3.3 component).

## Out of scope
- Alt rendering on the public site (P2-E6 Media.astro); enforcement for non-photo kinds (exempt per §5.6).
design:
- Validation added to the Catalog publish transition (P1-E2.2) — same single enforcement point as the §5.13 subscription gate
- Required locales follow the active locale set (fr + ar, en optional — D5)
- Alt editing UI in the media manager reuses the i18n-tabbed component from P1-E3.3 (alt is jsonb i18n, §5.6)
acceptance_criteria:
- Publish of a developer/project/listing blocked with an actionable error while any kind=photo media lacks alt for the required locales; succeeds once alt present (§5.6)
- Gate applies to photos only — floorplan/brochure/document/logo exempt (§5.6)
- Admin UI lists which photos are missing alt and for which locale
- Covered by context tests + LiveView test
notes: Spec: §5.6 (alt required for photos before publish), §6.2 (alt-text enforcement before publish), R8. Open decisions: D5 (locale set). Deps: P1-E4.2. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E4.3 MediaDerivatives Oban job (queue media): content-type allowlist (jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf), dimensions+byte_size via HEAD, blurhash LQIP
description:
## Why
- §6.5: server-side validation of what actually landed in R2 (defense in depth against presign tampering) + the metadata that powers R8 Core Web Vitals: explicit width/height for zero-CLS images and blurhash LQIP placeholders (§8 delivery).

## What
- Oban worker `MediaDerivatives` on queue `media`, triggered after upload confirm (§6.5).
- HEAD the R2 object → store byte_size + content_type; validate against allowlist jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf — violations mark/remove the media row (§16 AC server-side rejection).
- Download once → image dimensions (width/height) + blurhash; persist on the media row (§5.6).
- PDFs (brochures/floorplans-as-pdf): metadata only; served inline from R2 (§8).
- Job tests with mocked R2 HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test, §15.1).

## Out of scope
- Image resizing/derivative files — delivery uses Cloudflare Image Transformations on originals (§8, A6); only metadata + blurhash are computed here.
design:
- Oban worker on queue :media, enqueued by the P1-E4.2 confirm callback (§6.5)
- HEAD R2 object → byte_size + content_type validation; single GET (download once) → dimensions + blurhash computation (§6.5)
- Allowlist exactly: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/avif, application/pdf
- blurhash string persisted to media.blurhash for LQIP placeholders (§5.6, consumed by Media.astro in P2-E6)
acceptance_criteria:
- After the job runs, image media rows carry width/height/byte_size/blurhash; pdf rows carry byte_size/content_type (no blurhash/dims) (§5.6/§8)
- Object with content-type outside jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf → media row rejected/flagged and unusable by attachables (server-side rejection half of the §16 AC)
- Job is idempotent and retry-safe: re-running converges to the same row state
- Tests use mocked R2 HTTP (Bypass/Req.Test) per §15.1 — no live R2 in CI
notes: Spec: §6.5 (MediaDerivatives row), §5.6, §8, §15.1 (Oban tests with mocked HTTP). Deps: P1-E4.2 confirm flow. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E4.2 Admin drag-drop multi-upload direct to R2 + confirm callback → media rows (content-hashed keys media/{type}/{id}/{sha256}.{ext}) + reorder + kinds
description:
## Why
- §6.2 media manager + §8 upload flow: editors need bulk photo workflows (drag-drop multi-upload, reorder, kinds) and the bytes must go browser → R2 directly (R5/R6).
- Content-addressed keys mean updates create new keys → **no purging ever** (§8/A6) — the delivery cache strategy depends on this invariant being enforced here.

## What
- LiveView drag-drop multi-upload on developers/projects/listings forms: client computes sha256 → presign (P1-E4.1) → direct PUT to R2 → confirm callback → `Immo.Media` creates the media row (§5.6).
- Client-side validation mirroring server constraints: ≤25 MB, allowlisted types — rejected before upload (§16 AC "client- AND server-side").
- Kinds: photo | floorplan | brochure | document | logo (§5.6).
- Reorder via position (drag handle); delete (row removal; objects remain).
- Enqueue `MediaDerivatives` on confirm (§6.5/§8).

## Out of scope
- Derivative computation itself (P1-E4.3); alt-text enforcement (P1-E4.4); rendering on the public site (P2-E6).
design:
- LiveView drag-drop multi-upload component on developer/project/listing forms: client computes sha256, requests presign (P1-E4.1), PUTs direct to R2, then confirm callback
- Client-side validation mirror: size ≤ 25 MB + type allowlist before upload (§16 AC)
- Confirm: Immo.Media creates row {attachable_type, attachable_id, kind, r2_key, content_type, position} then Oban-inserts MediaDerivatives (queue media) — row + job in one transaction
- Delete removes the row only; content-addressed objects remain (no purging ever, §8/A6)
acceptance_criteria:
- 10-photo drag-drop: all land in R2 under content-hashed keys; media rows created with correct kind and position (§16 epic AC)
- Oversized/forbidden file rejected client-side before any PUT; tampered direct PUT (wrong type/size) rejected server-side by presign constraints (§16 AC: client- AND server-side)
- Reorder persists position and round-trips to gallery order via the (attachable_type, attachable_id, position) index (§5.6)
- Kind selectable per upload: photo|floorplan|brochure|document|logo (§5.6)
- Confirm callback creates the media row AND enqueues MediaDerivatives (§8/§6.5)
- Uploads attach to developers, projects and listings (polymorphic, §5.6)
notes: Spec: §8 (upload flow steps 2–3), §5.6, §6.2 (media manager). Deps: P1-E4.1. Alt-text editing UI hooks in via P1-E4.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E4.1 POST /admin/media/presign: presigned R2 PUT via ex_aws_s3 (15 min expiry, content-type + 25 MB constraints)
description:
## Why
- §8 upload flow step 1: bytes never transit the VPS (R5/R6). The presign constraints (expiry 15 min, content-type, 25 MB cap) are the server-side half of upload abuse prevention required by the §13 release gate ("upload allowlist + size caps + presign expiry 15 min").

## What
- `POST /admin/media/presign` (staff-session authenticated, role-gated): accepts attachable_type/attachable_id, kind, content_type, sha256, extension.
- Returns a presigned PUT URL via ex_aws_s3 against the R2 bucket: 15 min expiry, content-type constrained, max size 25 MB (§8).
- Key computed server-side: `media/{attachable_type}/{attachable_id}/{sha256}.{ext}` (§8/§5.6); object cache-control `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (§8).
- Content-type allowlist enforced up front: jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf (§6.5/§8).

## Out of scope
- The upload UI and confirm callback (P1-E4.2); derivative processing (P1-E4.3).
design:
- ex_aws_s3 presigned PUT against the R2 bucket (immo-media-prod / staging, §8) with 15 min expiry, content-type and max-size 25 MB constraints
- Endpoint lives under the admin (browser session) pipeline, not /api/v1 — §8 says LiveView admin requests it
- Server computes/validates the key from client-supplied sha256 + extension; attachable existence + authorization checked
- Object metadata set so stored objects carry cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable (§8)
acceptance_criteria:
- Presign requires an authenticated staff session with media rights; anonymous/unauthorized → 401/403
- Returned URL expires at 15 min; PUT with mismatched content-type or body >25 MB is refused by R2 (constraints baked into the signature) (§8/§13)
- Returned key matches media/{attachable_type}/{attachable_id}/{sha256}.{ext} computed server-side (§8/§5.6)
- Disallowed content types (outside jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf) rejected at presign time (§6.5)
- developer_user can only presign for own attachables (§5.8 scoping)
notes: Spec: §8 (upload flow step 1), §13 (allowlist + size caps + presign expiry 15 min), §5.6, §6.5 allowlist. R2 credentials/bucket from P0 (§12.1, §12.4 registry). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P1-E4 — Media pipeline (presigned direct-to-R2 + derivatives)
description:
## Why
- R5: all images and public media stored in and served from Cloudflare R2 (edge-cached, first-party domain, on-the-fly resizing); A6 locks content-hashed keys + originals only.
- Presigned direct-to-R2 PUT (§8) keeps media bytes off the single Hetzner VPS (R6 ops posture) — uploads scale independently of Phoenix.
- Blurhash + stored dimensions power R8 Core Web Vitals rendering downstream (explicit width/height, LQIP placeholders via Media.astro in P2-E6).

## What
- `POST /admin/media/presign` returning presigned R2 PUT URLs (ex_aws_s3, 15 min expiry, content-type + 25 MB constraints) (§8).
- Admin drag-drop multi-upload direct to R2; confirm callback creates media rows (§5.6) with content-hashed keys `media/{attachable_type}/{attachable_id}/{sha256}.{ext}`; reorder; kinds photo|floorplan|brochure|document|logo.
- `MediaDerivatives` Oban job (queue `media`): content-type allowlist jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf, dimensions + byte_size via HEAD, blurhash LQIP (§6.5).
- Alt-text publish gate: photos require alt (i18n) before their attachable can publish (§5.6, §6.2).

## Out of scope
- Delivery/transformation component `Media.astro` + CF Image Transformations (P2-E6); R2 bucket/domain provisioning (P0, §12.1); PMTiles basemap objects (§9, P5).
design:
- Upload flow per §8: LiveView requests POST /admin/media/presign → presigned PUT (ex_aws_s3, 15 min, content-type + 25 MB constrained) → browser PUTs direct to R2 (bytes never transit the VPS) → confirm callback creates media row → MediaDerivatives job
- media schema per §5.6: polymorphic attachable (Project/Listing/Developer), kind enum, r2_key, content_type/byte_size/width/height, blurhash, alt jsonb i18n, position; index (attachable_type, attachable_id, position)
- MediaDerivatives on Oban queue media: allowlist jpeg/png/webp/avif/pdf, HEAD for metadata, blurhash LQIP (§6.5)
- Content-addressed keys → updates create new keys, no purging ever (A6/§8)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P1-E4 AC: a 10-photo drag-drop lands in R2 with content-hashed keys; blurhash + dimensions populated
- §16 P1-E4 AC: oversized (>25 MB) or forbidden-type file rejected client-side AND server-side
- Keys follow media/{attachable_type}/{attachable_id}/{sha256}.{ext}; objects carry cache-control public, max-age=31536000, immutable (§8)
- Presigned PUT URLs expire at 15 min with content-type + size constraints (§8, §13)
- Photos without alt (i18n) block publish of their attachable (§5.6 gate)
- Reorder persists position; kinds photo|floorplan|brochure|document|logo supported (§5.6)
notes: Spec: §8, §5.6, §6.5 (MediaDerivatives), §6.2 (media manager), §13 (upload limits), §16 P1-E4 (Deps: E2). Bucket immo-media-prod (+staging) and media.<domain> provisioned in P0 (§12.1/§8). Delivery component Media.astro is P2-E6. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P3-E3 — BuildAgeMonitor + alerting (the alert that matters most)
description:
## Why
- §14 calls this **"the alert that matters most"**: the freshness model's worst failure mode is *silent* — if the build pipeline breaks, KV dirty TTLs eventually expire and stale statics quietly return **with no error signal anywhere**. Visitors see old data; nobody knows. This monitor is the guard (§18 risk row 2: likelihood M, impact H).
- Protects R1 (the schedule actually runs) and, after P4, backstops R2/R3 (dirty markers only protect freshness while builds keep succeeding).

## What
- `BuildAgeMonitor` Oban job (queue `default`, every-15-min cron per §6.5).
- Alert if site `/__build.json` `built_at` age > **2× rebuild interval** (§14).
- Also alert on: build `failed` status, Oban job retries exhausted (§14 "also alert on" list).
- Wire email/Slack delivery.

## Out of scope
- VPS disk / backup-failure / webhook-signature-spike alerts (§14 list — P8-E2 ops gate scope).
- Serving-mode dashboards (P4-E5).
design:
- Immo.Jobs.BuildAgeMonitor on a 15-minute cron, queue default (§6.5 row BuildAgeMonitor)
- Threshold: built_at age > 2x rebuild interval (interval derived from REBUILD_CRON; default 1 h -> alert past 2 h)
- Age source: PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json built_at (§3.3)
- Delivery: Swoosh email (Resend/SES, §12.2) and/or Slack webhook
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulated deploy-hook outage on staging produces an alert within 15 min of crossing the threshold (§16 P3-E3 AC)
- Alert fires when site /__build.json built_at age > 2x rebuild interval (§14)
- Alerts also fire on build failed status and on Oban job retries exhausted (§14 also-alert list)
- Alerts delivered via email/Slack and verified end-to-end on staging
notes: Spec: §14 (the alert that matters most), §6.5, §16 P3-E3 (deps: P3-E1). Risk register: §18 row 2 — alert, do not discover. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E3.1 Protomaps PMTiles extract (Morocco + neighbors, ~z14) → R2 tiles/basemap.pmtiles + CORS range-GET rule + brand-tinted Protomaps light style + quarterly refresh task documented
description:
## Why
A7: the serverless basemap is the foundation every P5-E3 surface renders on — PMTiles on R2 means zero tile-server ops, first-party delivery, and edge caching. Without the CORS range-GET rule the pmtiles protocol cannot fetch tile ranges from the browser at all.

## What
- Produce a Protomaps `.pmtiles` extract covering Morocco + neighbors at ~zoom 14 (§9).
- Upload to R2 as `tiles/basemap.pmtiles` (media bucket / custom domain, §12.1).
- Add the R2 CORS rule allowing range GET from the site origins (staging + prod) — required by the pmtiles HTTP range protocol (§9; §12.1 P0 checklist names this rule, verify/extend it for tiles).
- Style: start from the Protomaps light style; brand-tint via theme tokens (tokens.css theme layer, §7.4) so re-skinning a vertical re-tints the map for free.
- Document the quarterly refresh task (§9): regenerate the extract, re-upload, verify — runbook entry + recurring reminder.

## Out of scope
- Map islands (P5-E3.2/.3); MapTiler account setup (only keep the style URL configurable per D8).
design:
- Extract: Protomaps/pmtiles tooling, coverage Morocco + neighbors, max ~zoom 14 (§9)
- R2 object key tiles/basemap.pmtiles on the media bucket/custom domain (§12.1); long-cache headers fine — refresh replaces the object
- CORS: allow GET + Range header from exact site origins only (§9/§12.1 range-GET rule)
- D8 fallback designed in: style URL kept configurable so MapTiler hosted tiles are a config swap, zero code change
acceptance_criteria:
- MapLibre on staging renders the basemap from tiles/basemap.pmtiles via HTTP range requests (206 partial responses observed; no tile server)
- Cross-origin range GET succeeds from site origins (staging + prod); other origins blocked by the CORS rule
- Style is Protomaps light brand-tinted through theme tokens; swapping tint = token change only
- Quarterly refresh task documented: regenerate extract, re-upload, verify steps + owner + recurring reminder mechanism
notes: Spec: §9, §12.1 (R2 + CORS range GET checklist item), §7.4 theme tokens. Open decisions: D8 (default PMTiles on R2; override trigger = cartographic polish → MapTiler style URL). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P3-E2.1 Build dashboard: builds table + current /__build.json snapshot + Rebuild-now button (trigger=manual, bypasses skip-if-unchanged) + last-failure alert banner + REBUILD_CRON display
description:
## Why
- §6.2 names the build dashboard an explicit admin feature; §3.2 step 6 makes the manual trigger part of the rebuild algorithm itself. Together they keep R1 operable: editors confirm freshness state, ops spots failures, anyone can force a bake-in without touching the VPS.

## What
- LiveView screen in the admin (role-gated via `on_mount` hooks per §6.2):
  - **builds table**: rows with status (`queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped`), trigger (`cron|manual`), `content_snapshot_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `built_at`, `error`, `git_sha` (§5.10).
  - **Current `/__build.json` snapshot**: `built_at`, `content_snapshot_at`, `git_sha`, `render_mode`, `locales` (§3.3) fetched live from `PUBLIC_SITE_URL`.
  - **Rebuild-now button**: enqueues `Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite` with `trigger = :manual` — bypasses skip-if-unchanged (§3.2 step 6).
  - **Last-failure alert banner** when the most recent build `failed`.
  - **`REBUILD_CRON` display** (current schedule).

## Out of scope
- Email/Slack alert wiring (P3-E3.1); audit-log viewer; serving-mode ratios (P4-E5.1).
design:
- Button -> Oban.insert(Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite, %{trigger: "manual"}); unique: [period: 300] still applies (§6.5) so double-clicks are no-ops
- Snapshot fetched server-side from PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json with short timeout; render gracefully when unreachable
- Banner predicate: most recent builds row status == failed
- REBUILD_CRON read from runtime env for display (cost knob per §3.2 interval semantics)
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard lists builds (paginated) with status queued|running|succeeded|failed|skipped, trigger cron|manual, content_snapshot_at, started_at, finished_at, built_at, error, git_sha (§5.10)
- Rebuild-now enqueues RebuildSite trigger=manual; a run with unchanged content still POSTs the deploy hook (skip bypass proven)
- Banner appears when the latest build has status=failed and clears after the next succeeded build
- Current /__build.json snapshot (built_at, content_snapshot_at, git_sha, render_mode, locales) and REBUILD_CRON value rendered
- Role gating per §6.2 RBAC verified in tests
notes: Spec: §6.2 build dashboard bullet, §3.2 step 6, §3.3, §5.10. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P5-E3 — Maps: MapLibre + PMTiles on R2
description:
## Why
A7 (locked decision): MapLibre GL JS + Protomaps PMTiles on R2 — serverless basemap, no tile server to operate, first-party tile delivery that fits the Cloudflare frontend. §7.5 defines both map surfaces (detail page: single marker, zero fetch; search page: clustered, bbox-driven via /listings/geo). R8 performance: maps must not blow the JS budget — MapLibre lazy-loads only when a map scrolls into view (§7.5 budget note, enforced by Lighthouse CI §15.5).

## What
- Basemap (§9): Protomaps `.pmtiles` extract (Morocco + neighbors, ~zoom 14) in R2 at `tiles/basemap.pmtiles`; MapLibre + `pmtiles` protocol over HTTP range requests; R2 CORS rule allowing range GET from site origins; Protomaps light style brand-tinted via theme tokens; quarterly refresh task documented.
- Detail-page ListingMap: `client:visible`, single marker from baked coords — zero data fetch.
- Search map: MapLibre cluster source over the /listings/geo GeoJSON endpoint; `moveend` → bbox fetch; abort stale requests; marker click → card popover with `path` link (§9).
- RTL labels: `mapbox-gl-rtl-text` plugin for the Arabic locale (§9).

## Out of scope
