- The geo endpoint itself (P5-E1.2); admin mini-map (P5-E4.2 reuses the basemap); MapTiler integration beyond keeping the style URL configurable (D8 override path).
design:
- A7 locked: MapLibre GL JS + Protomaps PMTiles on R2; D8 fallback = MapTiler hosted tiles via style-URL config swap only
- pmtiles protocol over HTTP range requests against tiles/basemap.pmtiles; R2 CORS rule allows range GET from site origins (§9/§12.1)
- Search map clustering: MapLibre GeoJSON cluster source over GET /listings/geo; marker click → card popover with path link (§9)
- Style: Protomaps light, brand-tinted via theme tokens (tokens.css layer, §7.4)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P5-E3 AC: pan loads bbox results ≤ 500 ms p95 on staging
- JS budget holds: ≤ 100 KB gz per detail page — MapLibre lazy-loaded only when the map scrolls into view (Lighthouse CI, §15.5/§7.5)
- Basemap renders on staging from R2 tiles/basemap.pmtiles via HTTP range requests — no tile server anywhere
- Arabic locale pages render map labels correctly via the RTL text plugin (§9)
notes: Spec: §9 (entire), §7.5 ListingMap row, §15.5 budgets, §12.1 R2/CORS, §16 P5-E3. Open decisions: D8 (default PMTiles on R2; MapTiler style URL if cartographic polish demanded). Cross-phase deps (P5-E1) wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E3.5 Audit-log viewer (admin only)
description:
## Why
- §6.2 lists "Audit log viewer (admin only)"; §5.12 rationale: compliance + debugging "why did this page change" — essential when published pages are baked into scheduled static builds (R1–R3) and content provenance questions arise.

## What
- Admin-only LiveView listing audit_log entries: user, action, entity_type, entity_id, diff, at (§5.12).
- Filters by entity, user, action; pagination.
- Readable diff rendering (changed fields old → new from the diff jsonb).

## Out of scope
- Audit export/retention tooling (not specified in v1).
design:
- /admin/audit LiveView behind admin-only on_mount hook (P1-E1.2)
- Reads via the P1-E2.4 audit query API (filter + paginate); no direct Repo in the view
- Columns per §5.12: user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, diff, at
acceptance_criteria:
- Only admin role can access; manager/editor/developer_user denied (§6.2)
- Entries listed with user, action, entity_type/id, at; filterable by entity, user, action; paginated
- diff jsonb rendered readably as changed fields old → new
- A catalog mutation performed in the admin UI appears in the viewer
notes: Spec: §6.2 (audit log viewer, admin only), §5.12. Deps: P1-E2.4 (epic-level dep covers). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E3.4 Publish/unpublish UI + subscription-gate feedback + slug lock with admin-role override (§3.8)
description:
## Why
- R1–R3: `published_at` transitions are the events the entire build/freshness machine reacts to — this UI is where they happen.
- R10/D13: publishing is subscription-gated (§5.13); editors need clear feedback instead of silent failures while BILLING_ENFORCED is toggled on.
- §3.8/R8: slug immutability protects SEO equity; the admin override must mint a 301 redirect, never a dead URL.

## What
- Publish/unpublish actions on developers/projects/listings calling the P1-E2.2 Catalog transitions.
- Subscription-gate feedback (§6.2): when BILLING_ENFORCED and the owning developer lacks an active|trialing subscription, publish is blocked with an explanatory message (§5.13).
- Slug lock UI: read-only after first publish; admin-role unlock; on change show the created redirects row (§3.8, §5.11).

## Out of scope
- KV dirty-marking on publish-state transitions (P4); billing screens / subscription management (P6); alt-text publish gate condition (P1-E4.4 adds it to the same transition).
design:
- Publish/unpublish buttons call Catalog.publish/2 / unpublish/2 (P1-E2.2); no view-level logic
- Gate feedback derived from the same subscription-status logic used by Catalog.published/1 (§5.13) — single source, no duplicate check
- Slug lock UI: disabled input once ever-published; admin sees explicit unlock control (§3.8)
- Redirect insertion happens in the context transaction; UI confirms old → new path
acceptance_criteria:
- Editor publishes a draft project/listing (active sub or flag off): published_at set; record now matches Catalog.published/1
- With BILLING_ENFORCED=true and owning developer lacking active|trialing subscription, publish is blocked with explanatory feedback (§6.2/§5.13)
- Unpublish clears published_at; record drops out of published/1
- Slug field read-only after first publish for non-admin; admin override edits slug AND surfaces the created redirects row (old_path → new_path, 301) (§3.8)
- All transitions audit-logged (§5.12)
notes: Spec: §6.2, §3.8, §5.13. Open decisions: D13 (BILLING_ENFORCED=false at launch — feedback path still exercised via flag in tests/staging). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E3.3 i18n field tabs (fr/ar/en) + per-locale completeness indicators + SERP-style SEO preview
description:
## Why
- R8 (SEO-first, i18n fr/ar/en with hreflang) depends on editors actually filling per-locale content; §6.2 specifies "i18n field tabs (fr/ar/en) with completeness indicators; per-locale SEO preview snippet (SERP-style)". The frontend auto-fallback (§5.1 seo note) only works well when editors can see what is missing.

## What
- Tabbed locale editing (fr default, ar, en) for all jsonb i18n fields — title, description, seo (and reusable for media alt in P1-E4.4) — on developers/projects/listings forms.
- Per-locale completeness indicators showing which locales lack required content.
- SERP-style preview per locale from the seo jsonb (title, meta_description) (§6.2).
- RTL-correct text entry on the ar tab.

## Out of scope
- Frontend locale fallback chains (P2); hreflang emission (P2-E5).
design:
- Shared LiveComponent for i18n-tabbed inputs over jsonb maps {fr, ar, en}; locale set fr/ar/en per D5
- SEO preview component reads the seo jsonb i18n fields: title, meta_description, og fields (§5.1)
- Completeness derived per locale from required i18n fields of the entity
- ar tab sets dir=rtl on inputs
acceptance_criteria:
- Editing fr/ar/en values round-trips into jsonb i18n maps keyed by locale (§5.1 shape)
- Completeness indicator per tab reflects missing locale content for required fields
- SERP-style preview renders seo title + meta_description per locale (§6.2)
- Arabic tab inputs handle RTL text entry correctly
- Component reused across developers/projects/listings forms (title, description, seo)
notes: Spec: §6.2, §5.1/§5.2/§5.4 (jsonb i18n + seo fields). Open decisions: D5 (en droppable if content capacity short). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E3.2 property_types admin + custom-fields builder (instantly reflected in listing forms + filter_config)
description:
## Why
- R9 is the product's universality bet: admins define new categories and fields without schema rewrites. §6.2: "Custom-fields builder per property type (creates §5.5 rows; instantly reflected in admin listing forms and search facets)."

## What
- CRUD for property_types (§5.3): key, label i18n, url_segment i18n, filter_config, schema_hints, position.
- Custom-fields builder per type (§5.5): key, label i18n, field_type (`string|integer|decimal|boolean|select|multiselect|date`), options for selects, searchable, required, position.
- Instant reflection: new/changed custom field immediately renders in listing forms; searchable fields surface as facets in the merged filter_config at read time (§5.5).
- Values stored inside `listings.attributes` under the field key — no EAV tables (§5.5).

## Out of scope
- The public GET /property_types endpoint that serves the merged filter_config (P1-E5.2); search facet rendering (P5).
design:
- Builder writes §5.5 custom_fields rows: key citext unique per type, label jsonb, field_type enum string|integer|decimal|boolean|select|multiselect|date, options jsonb, searchable, required, position
- Listing-form renderer merges schema_hints + custom_fields at render time (single merge function reused by API filter_config merge)
- filter_config facet shape per §5.3: {key, kind: range|select|boolean, source: column|attribute|custom_field, unit, min, max, options}
- url_segment jsonb drives public routes /{segment}/{city}/{slug} (§5.3) — editable here, consumed by Edge.Paths
acceptance_criteria:
- Creating a custom field then reloading a listing form of that type renders the new input with correct field_type widget and required flag — no deploy/migration (§6.2)
- searchable=true custom field appears in the merged filter_config as consumed later by GET /property_types (§5.5/§6.3)
- select/multiselect options editable; key uniqueness per property_type enforced (§5.5)
- property_types CRUD covers key, label i18n, url_segment i18n, filter_config, schema_hints, position (§5.3)
- Values persist into listings.attributes under the field key — no EAV tables (§5.5)
notes: Spec: §5.3, §5.5, §6.2. No EAV — values live in listings.attributes (§5.5). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E3.1 LiveView admin shell + role-gated nav + CRUD for developers/projects/listings
description:
## Why
- §6.2 first bullet: CRUD for §5 entities with role gating — developers, projects and listings are the core catalog entities staff manage daily; this shell is the frame every other E3 screen mounts into (R9 content production).

## What
- Admin layout/shell: navigation, flash, current-user display, role-gated menu items.
- LiveView CRUD for developers (§5.1), projects (§5.2), listings (§5.4): index with filters + form views.
- Listing form renders type-specific attribute inputs from `property_type.schema_hints` + `custom_fields`, writing into `listings.attributes` (§5.4/§5.5).
- developer_user scoping applied throughout (P1-E1.2 query scoping; §6.2 "own projects/listings only").
- All mutations via Immo.Catalog (P1-E2.2) wrapped with audit logging (P1-E2.4).

## Out of scope
- property_types/custom-fields screens (P1-E3.2), i18n tabs polish (P1-E3.3), publish controls (P1-E3.4), media manager (P1-E4.2).
design:
- live_session :admin with on_mount RBAC hooks from P1-E1.2
- Routes: /admin/developers, /admin/projects, /admin/listings (+ /new, /:id/edit)
- Index views with filters (city, status, property_type) and pagination over Catalog queries
- Listing form renders §5.4 columns + dynamic attribute inputs from schema_hints + custom_fields
acceptance_criteria:
- CRUD flows (index/new/edit/delete) for developers, projects, listings pass LiveView tests for admin/manager/editor
- developer_user sees and edits only own projects/listings; foreign rows invisible and write-rejected (§6.2/§5.8)
- Nav items render per role (no links to surfaces the role cannot mount)
- Listing form attribute inputs adapt when property_type changes (schema_hints-driven, §5.3)
- Invalid changesets render inline errors; all writes go through Immo.Catalog + audit wrapper (no direct Repo in views)
notes: Spec: §6.2, §5.1/§5.2/§5.4. Deps: P1-E1.2 hooks, P1-E2.2 context (epic-level deps cover this). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P1-E3 — Admin CRUD (LiveView) for the catalog
description:
## Why
- The management application is where staff produce the catalog (A3: Phoenix LiveView admin is the only writer). Everything the build/freshness pipeline (R1–R3) serves originates in these screens, with SEO-grade fields (R8) over the polymorphic schema (R9).
- §6.2 defines the admin feature list; per §16 P1-E3 this epic delivers it **minus** media manager (P1-E4), build dashboard (P3) and billing screens (P6).

## What
- LiveView admin shell + role-gated nav + CRUD for developers/projects/listings (§6.2 first bullet, role gating from P1-E1).
- property_types admin + custom-fields builder, instantly reflected in listing forms and search facets (§5.5, §6.2).
- i18n field tabs (fr/ar/en) with per-locale completeness indicators + SERP-style SEO preview (§6.2).
- Publish/unpublish UI with subscription-gate feedback + slug lock with admin override (§3.8, §6.2).
- Audit-log viewer, admin only (§6.2, §5.12).

## Out of scope
- Media manager drag-drop (P1-E4.2), inquiries inbox (P1-E6.3), billing screens (P6), build dashboard (P3).
- Map pin / geocode button (§6.2) — not in this epic's task set; Geocode job is §6.5 (flagged to orchestrator).
design:
- LiveView screens mounted under role-gated live_session using the P1-E1.2 on_mount hooks (§6.2 matrix)
- All writes go through Immo.Catalog (P1-E2.2) wrapped by the audit layer (P1-E2.4) — no direct Repo calls from views
- i18n jsonb editing via a shared tabbed LiveComponent (fr/ar/en per D5)
- Listing forms render type-specific inputs from property_type.schema_hints + custom_fields; values land in listings.attributes (§5.4/§5.5)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P1-E3 AC: an editor takes a project from draft → published end-to-end in the UI, incl. i18n tabs (fr/ar/en)
- §16 P1-E3 AC: developer_user sees only own data on every E3 screen (projects/listings scoped to own developer_id)
- Custom field created in the builder appears instantly in listing forms and in filter_config (§6.2)
- Slug locked after first publish with admin-role override; subscription-gate feedback shown on publish (§3.8, §6.2)
- Audit-log viewer accessible to admin only; all E3 mutations appear in it (§5.12)
notes: Spec: §6.2 (minus media manager, build dashboard, billing screens), §3.8, §5.3/§5.4/§5.5, §5.12, §16 P1-E3 (Deps: E1, E2). Map-pin/geocode UI from §6.2 is NOT covered by E3.1–E3.5 (Geocode job is §6.5) — placement owned by orchestrator. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P3-E2 — Admin build dashboard + Rebuild-now
description:
## Why
- Serves R1 operationally: staff need visibility into the scheduled-rebuild pipeline (did my change get baked? did last night's build fail?) and a sanctioned manual escape hatch — §3.2 step 6 makes "Rebuild now" part of the core algorithm, not an afterthought.
- In the freshness model this is the human console over the `builds` state machine: the failure banner surfaces the same `failed` state that ConfirmBuild and BuildAgeMonitor (P3-E3) alert on, so editors see pipeline health without shell access.

## What
- Admin LiveView build dashboard per §6.2: builds table, current `/__build.json` snapshot, **"Rebuild now"** button, last-failure alert banner, current `REBUILD_CRON` display.
- Rebuild-now enqueues `Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite` with `trigger = :manual` (bypasses skip-if-unchanged per §3.2 step 6).

## Out of scope
- Alert delivery (email/Slack) — P3-E3.
- Serving-mode analytics dashboard — P4-E5.
design:
- LiveView screen per the §6.2 build-dashboard bullet: builds table, current /__build.json snapshot, Rebuild-now button, last-failure banner, REBUILD_CRON display
- Rebuild-now -> Oban insert of Immo.Jobs.RebuildSite with trigger=:manual (unique 300 s still applies, §6.5)
- Snapshot fetched server-side from PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json (§3.3 fields)
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard lists builds history with all §5.10 fields (status, trigger, content_snapshot_at, started/finished/built_at, error, git_sha)
- Rebuild-now enqueues RebuildSite with trigger=manual and bypasses skip-if-unchanged (§3.2 step 6)
- Last-failure alert banner shows when the most recent build failed; clears on next succeeded build
- Current /__build.json snapshot and current REBUILD_CRON value are displayed
- Screen is role-gated per §6.2 RBAC
notes: Spec: §6.2 build dashboard bullet, §3.2 step 6, §5.10, §16 P3-E2 (deps: P3-E1). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E6.2 Gallery component + brochure/floorplan PDF direct R2 links (content-disposition: inline)
description:
## Why
- §7.4 lists Media/Gallery in the universal component inventory; project/listing detail pages need multi-image presentation plus brochure/floorplan downloads, all on the single §8 delivery path.

## What
- Gallery component composing Media.astro for image sets from the media view-model (hero-first ordering, lazy thumbnails).
- Brochure/floorplan PDF links: direct R2 URLs (media.<domain>), expected to serve content-disposition: inline (§8); verify headers on staging.

## Out of scope
- Lightbox/zoom JS beyond minimal behavior (JS budget §7.5: ≤ 100 KB gz per detail page); PDF upload/metadata (P1-E4).
design:
- §8: PDFs (brochures/floorplans-as-pdf) = direct R2 links with content-disposition: inline
- Gallery composes Media.astro (P2-E6.1) — single URL-building path preserved
- Render-mode agnostic, props-only (R4); media view-models from mappers
- content-disposition is object/serving metadata on the R2 side (P1-E4 upload flow) — frontend just links
acceptance_criteria:
- Gallery renders n images from the media view-model list, each through Media.astro with correct srcsets (no bespoke img tags)
- First gallery image usable as the LCP hero (eager); the rest lazy
- Brochure/floorplan PDF links point directly at R2 objects and open inline in the browser (content-disposition: inline verified via response headers)
- PDFs are NOT routed through /cdn-cgi/image/ transformation URLs
- Component passes the logical-properties lint and stays within the JS budget (no heavy lightbox dependency)
notes: Spec: §8, §7.4 (Media/Gallery). Cross-phase dep on P1-E4 wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E6.1 Media.astro: /cdn-cgi/image/width={w},quality=82,format=auto URL builder + srcset 400/800/1200/1600 + sizes + explicit dims + lazy default / eager+fetchpriority=high LCP hero + blurhash placeholder
description:
## Why
- §8/R5: one delivery component over Cloudflare Image Transformations gives on-the-fly responsive variants from immutable R2 originals — zero build-time image work, identical output from static and SSR renders (R4 one-path hard rule).
- R8 CWV: the hero LCP strategy (eager + fetchpriority=high + explicit dims + blurhash) is what keeps LCP < 2.5 s and CLS < 0.1 (§15.5 budgets).

## What
- src/components/Media.astro: builds /cdn-cgi/image/width={w},quality=82,format=auto/<key> URLs on MEDIA_BASE_URL; emits srcset 400/800/1200/1600 w + sizes; explicit width/height; loading=lazy default; hero mode = eager + fetchpriority=high; blurhash placeholder background until load.
- Consume media view-models (key, dims, blurhash, alt) from mappers (P2-E2.3).
- Verify AVIF negotiation (format=auto) against the staging media domain; Lighthouse check that the hero is the LCP element.

## Out of scope
- Gallery + PDFs (P2-E6.2); backend derivatives/blurhash computation (P1-E4); zone-level Image Transformations enablement (P0).
design:
- §8 delivery contract verbatim: width={w},quality=82,format=auto; widths 400/800/1200/1600
- Inputs: media view-model from mappers (P2-E2.3) — key, width/height, blurhash, alt (alt-text publish gate guarantees presence, P1-E4)
- Keys are content-addressed media/{attachable_type}/{attachable_id}/{sha256}.{ext} with immutable cache-control (§8) — URL building only, never derive or mutate keys
- Render-mode agnostic component: pure props → markup, identical in static and SSR (R4)
- URL-builder helper shared with mappers media URL building to avoid two implementations
acceptance_criteria:
- URL builder emits exactly https://media.<domain>/cdn-cgi/image/width={w},quality=82,format=auto/<key> per §8 (base from MEDIA_BASE_URL)
- srcset contains exactly the 4 widths 400/800/1200/1600 w plus a sizes attribute
- Every emitted img has explicit width/height from the media record dimensions
- Default loading=lazy; hero variant eager + fetchpriority=high — Lighthouse confirms the hero is the LCP element with explicit dims (§16 AC)
- AVIF served to supporting UAs via format=auto (Accept-header check against staging media domain)
- blurhash placeholder background rendered until image load
- Guard in place (lint/review note) preventing astro:assets usage for catalog media (§8 hard rule)
notes: Spec: §8, §7.6, §12.4, §16 P2-E6 AC. Cross-phase dep on P1-E4 wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E6 — Media.astro (CF Image Transformations + blurhash)
description:
## Why
- R5: all images served from R2 via the first-party media.<domain> with on-the-fly resizing (Cloudflare Image Transformations) — no build-time processing, no CORS, edge-cached.
- R4 one-path rule (§8): SSR-rendered pages cannot use the Astro build-time image pipeline, so catalog media must not use it anywhere — one Media.astro URL builder serves static and SSR output identically.
- R8 Core Web Vitals: explicit dimensions (CLS), lazy/eager strategy + fetchpriority (LCP), blurhash placeholders.

## What
- Media.astro building https://media.<domain>/cdn-cgi/image/width={w},quality=82,format=auto/<key> URLs; emits img srcset at 400/800/1200/1600 w + sizes, explicit dimensions, lazy by default, eager + fetchpriority=high for the LCP hero, blurhash placeholder background (§8).
- Gallery component composing Media; brochure/floorplan PDFs as direct R2 links with content-disposition: inline.

## Out of scope
- Upload/presign/derivatives (P1-E4, backend); enabling Image Transformations on the zone (P0 checklist, §8/§12.1); maps tiles in R2 (§9).
design:
- Spec: §8 delivery; URL pattern https://media.<domain>/cdn-cgi/image/width={w},quality=82,format=auto/<key> on MEDIA_BASE_URL (§12.4)
- srcset widths 400/800/1200/1600 + sizes; explicit width/height from media-record dimensions (CLS guard, §7.6)
- blurhash + dimensions are computed by the P1-E4 MediaDerivatives job and arrive via the media view-model (mappers P2-E2.3)
- R5: media on first-party media.<domain>, edge-cached, immutable content-addressed keys — no purging ever
- §8 hard rule: do NOT use the Astro build-time image pipeline for catalog media — SSR-rendered pages cannot, and R4 demands one path
acceptance_criteria:
- Hero is the LCP element with explicit dimensions (§16 P2-E6 AC)
- srcset has the 4 widths 400/800/1200/1600 w (§16 P2-E6 AC)
- AVIF served to supporting UAs via format=auto (§16 P2-E6 AC) — verified with Accept-header requests against the media domain
- Images lazy by default; LCP hero eager + fetchpriority=high; blurhash placeholder background until load
- HARD RULE upheld (§8): catalog media never goes through the Astro build-time image pipeline — one Media.astro URL-builder path for static AND SSR (R4)
- PDFs (brochures/floorplans) served as direct R2 links with content-disposition: inline
notes: Spec: §8, §7.6, §12.4, §16 P2-E6. Cross-phase dep on P1-E4 (media pipeline) wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E2.2 Results grid (card view-models from /api/v1/search) + UI error states ('search temporarily unavailable' §3.7) + prerendered page shell stays static
description:
## Why
§3.6: /search results are permanently the island's job — the page shell is prerendered ("prerender shell; island does the work", §7.1) and must stay cacheable. §3.7 makes graceful degradation a protected property: when the VPS is down, islands show UI-level error states while static page content remains fully usable. This task delivers the visible half of that contract.

## What
- Results grid rendering card view-models returned by `/api/v1/search`, reusing the §7.4 render-mode-agnostic components (ListingCard, PriceTag, Pagination).
- Pagination controls honoring the §6.3 caps (`page ≤ 50`, `per_page ≤ 24`).
- Island-internal states: loading skeleton, empty ("no results"), and error — error copy "search temporarily unavailable" (§3.7) with a retry affordance; the static shell never breaks.
- Verify /recherche remains a prerendered static asset: no SSR dependency introduced; shell serves even with the API down.

## Out of scope
- Facet rendering/state (P5-E2.1); map view of results (P5-E3.3).
design:
- Consume the §6.3 list envelope {data, meta}; card fields: id, slug, path, title, price, currency, thumb
- Reuse §7.4 render-mode-agnostic components (ListingCard, PriceTag, Pagination) inside the island grid
- Loading/empty/error are island-internal states; prerendered shell content untouched in every state
- AbortController from P5-E2.1 ensures no out-of-order result rendering
acceptance_criteria:
- Cards render from API card view-models incl. path links, price/price_on_request via PriceTag, thumb
- Killing the staging API yields the search temporarily unavailable state; the rest of the page still renders and works (§3.7)
- Empty result set shows a designed empty state, not an error
- /recherche served as a static asset (x-immo-serving: static); data fetching happens only inside the island
- Pagination respects page≤50/per_page≤24 caps; out-of-range pages handled gracefully
notes: Spec: §3.6, §3.7, §6.3, §7.1 /recherche row, §7.4. Open decisions: none. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E2.1 SearchFilter island (client:load on /recherche, client:visible embeds): facet renderer from filter_config (range/select/boolean kinds) + 300 ms debounce + URL state sync
description:
## Why
R9 — facets are configuration, not code: the island renders whatever ordered facet list `property_types.filter_config` declares (§5.3), including admin-defined searchable custom fields merged server-side (§6.3 GET /property_types). New verticals and new fields need zero island changes (§7.5).

## What
- Island component in `frontend/src/islands/` (§4 layout): hydrate `client:load` on `/recherche`, `client:visible` when embedded on other pages (§7.5).
- Props: filter_config + property-type list baked at build as static props from the property_types collection (§7.2 loader; §6.3: GET /property_types includes filter_config merged with searchable custom fields + url_segment).
- Facet renderer by `kind`: `range` (min/max inputs honoring unit/min/max bounds), `select` (options), `boolean` (toggle) — rendered in filter_config order.
- Emits /api/v1/search query params exactly per §6.3: `q`, `type`, `city`, `price_min/max`, `surface_min/max`, `attrs[<key>]`, `sort`, `page`, `per_page`.
- 300 ms debounce on input changes before fetch; AbortController cancels in-flight requests superseded by new input.
- URL state sync: filters serialize to the query string; initial state parsed from the URL; history back/forward works (shareable searches, §7.5).

## Out of scope
- Results grid, empty/error states (P5-E2.2); the search-page map (P5-E3.3).
design:
- filter_config shape (§5.3): [{key, kind: range|select|boolean, source: column|attribute|custom_field, unit, min, max, options}] — ordered list drives render order
- Emits §6.3 param convention: q, type, city, price_min/max, surface_min/max, attrs[<key>]=value, sort, page, per_page
- Fetch via shared token-free api.ts client (§7.3); API_BASE_URL public const (§12.4); AbortController cancels superseded requests
- URL = canonical state store; island state rebuilt from query params on init — no state survives reload outside the URL
acceptance_criteria:
- Facets render purely from a filter_config fixture: adding a {key, kind} entry renders a new facet with no island code change (unit test)
- A searchable custom field present in build-time filter_config appears as a facet (feeds §15.4 e2e: search island facets from a custom field)
- Typing pauses 300 ms before exactly one /api/v1/search call fires; rapid changes never stack requests (debounce + abort test)
- Copy-pasting the URL reproduces the exact filter state; back/forward navigates previous filter states
- Hydration verified: client:load on /recherche, client:visible when embedded
notes: Spec: §7.5 row 1, §5.3, §6.3, §7.2, §7.3, §15.4. Open decisions: none. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E5.3 sitemap.xml (@astrojs/sitemap + custom serializer fed by GET /meta/sitemap: lastmod + hreflang alternates incl. x-default) + robots.txt + rss.xml
description:
## Why
- R8: the sitemap with accurate lastmod is how the hourly-rebuild model communicates freshness to crawlers; hreflang alternates make the fr/ar/en cluster indexable without duplicate-content penalties.
- Feeding from GET /meta/sitemap (§6.3) keeps the sitemap consistent with the server-side path authority — the same source that drives KV dirty-marking later.

## What
- Integrate @astrojs/sitemap with a custom serializer consuming GET /meta/sitemap at build time (lastmod + per-locale alternates incl. x-default).
- robots.txt allowing all + sitemap pointer; rss.xml feed of recent published content.
- Cross-check sitemap contents vs the API response for the seed catalog in CI or a build assertion.

## Out of scope
- redirects.json export from GET /redirects (slug-change phase, §3.8); X-Robots-Tag headers on SSR-internal paths (Worker phase).
design:
- §7.6: @astrojs/sitemap + custom serializer fed by GET /meta/sitemap (build tier, BUILD_TOKEN via the ONE api client P2-E2.2) — all public paths + lastmod + locale alternates (§6.3)
- /meta/sitemap is server-authoritative for paths (Immo.Edge.Paths) — do not recompute paths client-side
- robots.txt: allow all + Sitemap pointer; SSR-internal Disallow noted as defense-in-depth only if the /_render/* variant is chosen (Worker phase)
- PUBLIC_SITE_URL (§12.4) as URL base
acceptance_criteria:
- sitemap.xml lists ALL published paths with lastmod (§16 P2-E5 AC), cross-checked against GET /meta/sitemap output for the seed catalog
- Each sitemap URL carries hreflang alternates for fr/ar/en incl. x-default (§7.6)
- robots.txt allows all and points to the sitemap URL
- rss.xml of recent published content validates against the RSS spec
- All three emitted as build artifacts per the §7.1 route table
notes: Spec: §7.6, §6.3, §7.1, §16 P2-E5 AC. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E5.2 JsonLd component from view-models: RealEstateListing/Residence + Offer (status-mapped availability) + Organization + BreadcrumbList (+FAQPage on landings) — identical in static and SSR output
description:
## Why
- R8: JSON-LD structured data is what earns rich results for listings and projects.
- R4: structured data must not degrade when a page is served by the SSR fallback (states B/C) — emitting from view-models through one component guarantees parity (§7.6).

## What
- src/components JsonLd (serializer logic in src/lib/seo.ts per §4 layout): RealEstateListing for listings, Residence for projects, Offer (price, currency, availability mapped from status), Organization for developers, BreadcrumbList on detail pages, FAQPage on landings where content exists.
- Status → availability mapping table; price_on_request handling consistent with PriceTag.
- Vitest serializer tests (§15.3); validate fixtures with the Rich-results test and record evidence.

## Out of scope
- FAQ landing content authoring (data); meta tags (P2-E5.1); sitemap (P2-E5.3).
design:
- §7.6: emitted by JsonLd from the view-model → identical in static and SSR output (R4)
- Schema types: RealEstateListing (listings) / Residence (projects) + Offer + Organization (developer) + BreadcrumbList; FAQPage on landings with content
- Offer.availability: explicit status → schema.org mapping documented in the component
- price_on_request: respect the no-numeric-leak rule from PriceTag/mappers in Offer emission
- Input is exclusively *View types (P2-E2.3); no API shapes, no fetch
acceptance_criteria:
- Google Rich-results test passes for a listing fixture and a project fixture (§16 P2-E5 AC)
- Listing detail emits RealEstateListing + Offer (price, currency, availability mapped from listing status — mapping table covers ALL statuses); project detail emits Residence; developer data emits Organization; all detail pages emit BreadcrumbList
- FAQPage emitted on landings where FAQ content exists; omitted otherwise
- JSON-LD output identical from loader-fixture and SSR-fixture view-models (extends the P2-E2.4 equality guarantee)
- Serializer unit tests green (§15.3)
notes: Spec: §7.6, §15.3, §16 P2-E5 AC. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E5.1 Per-page title/meta/canonical/OG/Twitter with deterministic fallbacks ({title} – {city} | {site}); canonical always the prerendered URL
description:
## Why
- R8: unique, deterministic metadata per URL is table stakes; duplicate or empty titles across a 40+ listing catalog torpedo indexing.
- The canonical rule (§7.6) is what keeps SSR-served state B/C pages from competing with their future static selves — one URL identity regardless of render path (R4).

## What
- Wire Seo (P2-E1.3) into every E4.1 route with entity seo i18n via the mappers fallback chain.
- Implement the fallback pattern {title} – {city} | {site} and canonical construction from PUBLIC_SITE_URL + canonical path.
- Feed real hreflang alternates (per-locale paths from view-models) into the BaseLayout cluster incl. x-default.
- Dist-crawl check for uniqueness across the seed catalog.

## Out of scope
- JSON-LD (P2-E5.2); sitemap/robots/rss (P2-E5.3).
design:
- Wires the Seo component (P2-E1.3) on every route via view-model seo data (mappers P2-E2.3 locale fallback chain)
- §7.6 rule: canonical always the prerendered URL — the SSR fallback emits the same canonical (templates identical, R4)
- OG image slots from media view-models (final image URLs via P2-E6 contract)
- PUBLIC_SITE_URL from §12.4 is the canonical base
acceptance_criteria:
- Every prerendered page of the seed catalog emits unique title + description + canonical + OG + Twitter tags (crawl over dist verifies no duplicates)
- Missing seo fields fall back deterministically to {title} – {city} | {site} (§7.6) — same input, same output, unit-tested
- canonical equals the prerendered locale URL on every route, built from PUBLIC_SITE_URL + the canonical path (§6.3 path field)
- hreflang cluster (fr/ar/en + x-default) emitted with real alternate URLs on all content pages
notes: Spec: §7.6, §6.3, §12.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E5 — SEO pack (meta, JSON-LD, sitemap, feeds)
description:
## Why
- R8 is a core product requirement: unique metadata, JSON-LD structured data, sitemap, clean URLs, hreflang — organic search is the acquisition channel for a property portal.
- R4: SEO output must be byte-identical whether a page was prerendered or SSR-rendered (state B/C pages must not lose rich results); deriving everything from view-models via the Seo/JsonLd components is the mechanism (§7.6).

## What
- Per-page title/meta/canonical/OG/Twitter from entity seo i18n with deterministic fallbacks ({title} – {city} | {site}); canonical always the prerendered URL (§7.6).
- JsonLd component emitting RealEstateListing/Residence + Offer (status-mapped availability) + Organization + BreadcrumbList, plus FAQPage on landings where content exists — from view-models, identical static/SSR.
- sitemap.xml via @astrojs/sitemap + custom serializer fed by GET /meta/sitemap (lastmod + hreflang alternates incl. x-default); robots.txt; rss.xml (§7.1 build artifacts row, §7.6).

## Out of scope
- The hreflang/i18n routing base (P2-E1); SSR-internal path Disallow/X-Robots-Tag hardening (only relevant if the /_render/* variant is chosen — Worker phase); Lighthouse CI budgets (§15.5, CI epic territory).
design:
- Spec: §7.6 SEO implementation (R8); sitemap fed by GET /meta/sitemap (build tier, §6.3)
- Fallback pattern: {title} – {city} | {site}; canonical always the prerendered URL (SSR fallback emits the same canonical)
- JSON-LD types: RealEstateListing (listings) / Residence (projects) + Offer (availability mapped from status) + Organization (developer) + BreadcrumbList; FAQPage on landings where content exists
- R4: all SEO output derives from view-models (P2-E2.3) so static and SSR renders are identical
- Serializer unit tests per §15.3 (SEO/JSON-LD serializers)
acceptance_criteria:
- Google Rich-results test passes for listing + project fixtures (§16 P2-E5 AC)
- sitemap lists all published paths with lastmod (§16 P2-E5 AC) and hreflang alternates incl. x-default
- Every page has unique title/meta/canonical/OG/Twitter with deterministic fallbacks; canonical always the prerendered URL
- JSON-LD emitted by the JsonLd component from view-models — identical in static and SSR output (R4)
- robots.txt allows all and points to the sitemap; rss.xml validates
notes: Spec: §7.6, §6.3, §15.3, §16 P2-E5. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P5-E2 — SearchFilter island
description:
## Why
R9: the search UI must be configuration-driven — facets render from `property_types.filter_config` fetched at build time (static prop), so a new searchable custom field defined in admin appears as a facet after the next build with NO code change (§7.5 row 1; §16 P5-E2 AC verbatim). §3.6: /search results are always client-side against /api/v1/search — never stale, never indexed for content; the page shell stays static and cacheable.

## What
- `SearchFilter` island (§7.5): hydration `client:load` on `/recherche`, `client:visible` for embeds elsewhere.
- Facet renderer driven by filter_config kinds (range | select | boolean over sources column | attribute | custom_field, §5.3) — ordered facet list, zero hardcoded facets.
- Calls `GET /api/v1/search` (token-free public tier via the shared `api.ts` client, §7.3); 300 ms debounce.
- URL-synced state — shareable searches: copy-paste a URL reproduces filters + results; back/forward navigates filter history.
- Results grid renders card view-models from the API; §3.7 UI error state ("search temporarily unavailable") on API failure — the prerendered shell never breaks.

## Out of scope
- Backend endpoints (P5-E1); the map on the search page (P5-E3.3); visitor accounts/saved searches (§1.3 non-goal).
design:
- filter_config arrives as a static prop baked at build from GET /property_types (build tier merges searchable custom fields server-side, §6.3) — island never fetches config at runtime
- Facet kinds per §5.3 filter_config shape: [{key, kind: range|select|boolean, source: column|attribute|custom_field, unit, min, max, options}]
- URL query string is the single source of truth for filter state
- Calls token-free public tier via shared api.ts (§7.3); base URL from API_BASE_URL (§12.4); no secrets in client bundle (§10.1 path 3)
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P5-E2 AC: adding a searchable custom field in admin surfaces a facet after next build with no code change
- /recherche page shell prerendered/static; island hydrates client:load there, client:visible in embeds (§7.5)
- Input changes debounce 300 ms before calling /api/v1/search; filter state round-trips through the URL (shareable searches, back/forward safe)
- API failure shows the §3.7 UI error state (search temporarily unavailable); static page content remains fully usable
- Lighthouse CI JS budgets hold: ≤ 60 KB gz landings, ≤ 100 KB gz detail pages (§15.5)
notes: Spec: §7.5 row 1, §3.6, §3.7, §5.3, §6.3, §16 P5-E2. Open decisions: none. Cross-phase deps (P5-E1, P2) wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E2.5 Media/CRM/Billing/Edge context module skeletons (bounded responsibilities per §6.1)
description:
## Why
- §6.1 fixes bounded responsibilities up front so P1-E4 (Media), P1-E6 (CRM), P3/P4 (Edge) and P6 (Billing) build into pre-agreed module boundaries instead of inventing their own — keeping the single-app/single-writer architecture (A3) coherent.

## What
- `Immo.Media` skeleton: media records, presigned R2 uploads, derivative jobs (§6.1).
- `Immo.CRM` skeleton: inquiries, retention.
- `Immo.Billing` skeleton: subscriptions, payments, provider adapters, webhooks.
- `Immo.Edge` skeleton: builds, freshness (KV writes), path computation, deploy-hook client.
- Ecto schema modules + base changesets for media (§5.6), inquiries (§5.7), subscriptions/payments (§5.9), builds (§5.10) under their owning contexts.
- Stubs/typespecs only — compiling contracts, not behavior.

## Out of scope
- Any actual upload/notification/billing/build behavior (P1-E4, P1-E6, P6, P3/P4 respectively).
design:
- §6.1 ownership map: Immo.Media → media records, presigned R2 uploads, derivative jobs; Immo.CRM → inquiries, retention; Immo.Billing → subscriptions, payments, provider adapters, webhooks; Immo.Edge → builds, freshness (KV writes), path computation, deploy-hook client
- Immo.Edge.Paths placeholder declared here; born for real in P1-E5.2 as the single path authority
- Redirect ROWS stay Catalog-owned (§6.1); Edge owns path computation
acceptance_criteria:
- Immo.Media, Immo.CRM, Immo.Billing, Immo.Edge modules compile with @moduledoc stating responsibilities matching the §6.1 table verbatim
- Each owned §5 table (media, inquiries, subscriptions, payments, builds) has an Ecto schema module + base changeset under its owning context
- No cross-context ownership leaks: Catalog does not touch media/inquiries/subscriptions tables and vice versa (review or boundary check)
- Function stubs carry typespecs so P1-E4/P1-E6/P3/P4/P6 implement against agreed signatures
notes: Spec: §6.1, §5.6/§5.7/§5.9/§5.10. Fleshed out by P1-E4 (Media), P1-E6 (CRM), P3/P4 (Edge), P6 (Billing). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E2.4 audit_log thin context wrapper for all admin mutations (user, action, entity, diff)
description:
## Why
- §5.12: audit_log exists for compliance + debugging "why did this page change" — vital in a system where published content is baked into static builds on a schedule (R1–R3) and an edit's provenance matters.
- §13 release gate requires audit_log on all admin mutations.

## What
- audit_log writes via a thin context wrapper (§5.12): user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, diff jsonb, at.
- Wrap Catalog admin mutations now; designed so Media/CRM/Billing mutations (P1-E4/E6, P6) plug into the same wrapper.
- Field-level diff computation (changed fields, old → new values).
- Read/query API for the admin viewer (P1-E3.5).

## Out of scope
- Viewer UI (P1-E3.5); retention/rotation policy for audit rows (not specified in v1).
design:
- Thin wrapper (e.g. Immo.Audit.log_mutation/4 or a Catalog-level with_audit/3) invoked by context mutation functions; same Repo transaction
- Schema exactly per §5.12: user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, diff jsonb, at
- Later contexts (Media/CRM/Billing) reuse the same wrapper — §13 requires audit_log on ALL admin mutations
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Catalog admin mutation (create/update/delete/publish/unpublish) produces an audit_log row with user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, diff, at (§5.12)
- diff jsonb contains changed fields old → new
- Audit row written in the same transaction as the mutation: rollback removes both
- Query API exists for the P1-E3.5 viewer (filter by entity, user, action; paginated)
notes: Spec: §5.12, §13 (audit_log on all admin mutations). Viewer UI is P1-E3.5. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E4.3 Arabic RTL pass on all templates (dir=rtl, logical CSS properties)
description:
## Why
- R8 names AR with RTL as a first-class locale; half-mirrored RTL is worse than none. The lint rule (P2-E1.2) catches properties, but composition issues (icon direction, ordering, truncation, numeral formatting) need an explicit pass over real templates with real ar content.

## What
- Audit every route (E4.1) and component (E4.2) rendered under /ar/ with the seed catalog.
- Fix violations: physical properties that slipped through, direction-sensitive icons/ordering, ar number/price/date formatting.
- Confirm dir="rtl" propagation from BaseLayout on all ar pages; document with screenshots.

## Out of scope
- Map RTL labels (mapbox-gl-rtl-text — §9, maps phase); ar content authoring (data, P1-E2 seeds suffice).
design:
- §7.6: RTL = dir="rtl" on html + logical CSS properties throughout (lint rule from P2-E1.2 enforces; this pass audits and fixes what lint cannot see)
- Seed ar/fr content from P1-E2 fixtures is the test corpus
- Mechanical sweep: lint + manual route-by-route review of /ar/ output
acceptance_criteria:
- §16 P2-E4 AC: ar pages RTL-correct across the entire seed catalog (all routes from E4.1, all components from E4.2)
- html dir="rtl" on every /ar/ page (via BaseLayout); layout mirrors correctly — navigation, cards, breadcrumbs, pagination, tables
- Logical-properties lint clean across templates/components; any remaining physical-property violations fixed
- Directional details verified: chevrons/arrows, pagination order, number/price/date formatting in ar locale
- Visual evidence (screenshots of key ar pages) attached to the PR
notes: Spec: §7.6, §16 P2-E4 AC. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E4.2 Component inventory: ListingCard, ProjectCard, PriceTag (price_on_request aware), AttributesTable (from schema_hints + custom-field labels — universal), Breadcrumbs, LocaleSwitcher, Pagination
description:
## Why
- §7.4 fixes the shared UI inventory; building it once, render-mode agnostic, is what makes static pages, SSR fallbacks, and future verticals share one component set (R4/R9).
- AttributesTable is the R9 lynchpin: admin-defined custom fields and per-type schema_hints surface in the UI with zero component edits.

## What
- src/components per §7.4: ListingCard, ProjectCard, PriceTag (price_on_request aware), AttributesTable (renders rows from property_type schema_hints + custom-field labels — universal), Breadcrumbs, LocaleSwitcher, Pagination; footer/nav from config.
- All props are *View types (P2-E2.3); styling via tokens (P2-E1.2); logical properties only.
- Component-level Vitest coverage where logic exists (PriceTag formatting paths, AttributesTable row derivation).

## Out of scope
- Media/Gallery (P2-E6); JsonLd (P2-E5.2); InquiryForm island wrapper (§7.5, later phase).
design:
- §7.4: all components render-mode agnostic; props are *View types from src/lib/mappers.ts (R4)
- AttributesTable input: property_type schema_hints + custom field labels (R9, §6.3 property_types payload)
- Styling via tokens only (P2-E1.2); no physical CSS properties
- footer/nav driven from config (§7.4)
- PriceTag behavior feeds JSON-LD Offer mapping later (P2-E5.2) — keep formatting logic in mappers, presentation here
acceptance_criteria:
- AttributesTable renders a listing of ANY seeded property_type from schema_hints + custom-field labels — zero per-type component code (R9); covered for all 3+ seed types
- PriceTag: price_on_request renders the request-price label with no numeric leak; numeric prices format per locale/currency
- ListingCard/ProjectCard consume card view-models from mappers only; render identically from loader-fixture and SSR-fixture data (equality harness covers components transitively)
- LocaleSwitcher links to the correct localized alternate paths of the current page
- Breadcrumbs + Pagination functional on index/detail routes; all components pass the logical-properties lint (RTL-safe)
notes: Spec: §7.4, §16 P2-E4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E4.1 Prerendered routes: home + locale roots, /projets/ index + [city] + [city]/[slug] via getStaticPaths, /{type_segment}/ routes from url_segment, /promoteurs/[slug], /recherche shell, contact/legal stubs, 404 page
description:
## Why
- R8: clean, localized, crawlable URLs for the whole catalog are the SEO foundation; §7.1 fixes the exact URL space.
- R9: routing driven by property_types url_segment means new catalog verticals appear as routes without code changes.
- R4: these templates are the single source of markup — the SSR catch-alls added in the freshness phase render the very same components from request-time data.

## What
- src/pages per §7.1 (prerendered rows only):
  - / and locale roots (fr at root, /ar/, /en/)
  - /projets/ index and /projets/[city]/ city indexes
  - /projets/[city]/[slug] detail via getStaticPaths over the projects collection
  - /{type_segment}/[city]/[slug] listing details — segments from property_types url_segment (§6.3)
  - /promoteurs/[slug] developer pages
  - /recherche prerendered shell (island excluded here)
  - /contact + legal pages from content files
  - prerendered 404 page
- All data flows collections → mappers → *View props; pagination on index routes.

## Out of scope
- [...fallback] SSR catch-alls (§7.1, freshness phase); islands (§7.5); per-page SEO wiring beyond the BaseLayout/Seo basics (P2-E5.1).
design:
- §7.1 route table is the contract; prerender mode (RENDER_MODE=static) via output: static — flipping is P2-E7.2 territory, templates stay ignorant (R4/§2.2)
- Data: collections (P2-E3) → mappers (P2-E2.3) → props
- /recherche is a prerendered shell only; the SearchFilter island (§7.5) attaches in a later phase
- 404 is a prerendered page; SSR catch-alls will render it on API 404 with no-store (§7.1, later phase)
- Localized segments via Astro i18n routing + url_segment (e.g. fr /projets/, type-specific segments per locale)
acceptance_criteria:
- All §7.1 prerendered rows build from the seed catalog in fr/ar/en: /, locale roots, /projets/ + /projets/[city]/ + /projets/[city]/[slug], /{type_segment}/[city]/[slug], /promoteurs/[slug], /recherche shell, /contact + legal, 404
- Type-segment routes are generated from property_types url_segment data (§6.3) — adding a seeded type yields routes with zero code change
- Generated page paths agree with the API path field for every record (server-computed canonical, §6.3)
- Index routes paginate via the Pagination component
- getStaticPaths reads collections only — no network at page level; templates import only *View types
notes: Spec: §7.1, §6.3, §16 P2-E4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E4 — Pages & components (all prerendered routes)
description:
## Why
- This is the product surface: every prerendered route of the flagship portal with clean localized URLs (R8).
- R9: AttributesTable renders from property_type schema_hints + admin-defined custom-field labels — new verticals become data + templates + theme, not schema or component rewrites.
- R4: every template/component built here is reused verbatim by the SSR catch-alls in the freshness phase; they consume only *View types (§7.3) and never branch on render mode (§2.2 hard rule).

## What
- Prerendered routes per §7.1: home + locale roots; /projets/ index + /projets/[city]/ + /projets/[city]/[slug] (getStaticPaths); /{type_segment}/[city]/[slug] driven by property_types url_segment; /promoteurs/[slug]; /recherche prerendered shell (island does the work — later phase); /contact + legal pages from content files; prerendered 404.
- Component inventory per §7.4: ListingCard, ProjectCard, PriceTag (price_on_request aware), AttributesTable (schema_hints + custom-field labels — universal), Breadcrumbs, LocaleSwitcher, Pagination; footer/nav from config.
- Arabic RTL pass across all templates (dir="rtl", logical CSS properties).

## Out of scope
- SSR catch-all routes ([...fallback], §7.1 — freshness phase); islands SearchFilter/ListingMap/InquiryForm (§7.5, later phase); JSON-LD/sitemap (P2-E5); Media/Gallery internals (P2-E6 — use placeholder media slots until E6 lands).
design:
- Spec: §7.1 route table (prerendered rows), §7.4 component inventory, §16 P2-E4
- Data path: content collections (P2-E3) → mappers (P2-E2.3) → *View props → templates; getStaticPaths sources from collections only
- Localized URLs: Astro i18n routing (P2-E1.1) + url_segment from property_types (§6.3); paths must agree with the API path field (server-computed by Immo.Edge.Paths)
- R4 hard rule (§2.2): page templates and components never know the render mode — the SSR catch-alls (later phase) will reuse these exact templates
- Styling exclusively via tokens (P2-E1.2); logical properties only
acceptance_criteria:
- Seed catalog (P1-E2: ≥3 property types, ≥40 listings, ar/fr content) renders all locales (§16 P2-E4 AC)
- ar pages RTL-correct (§16 P2-E4 AC): dir="rtl", logical CSS properties, mirrored UI
- Every prerendered route of the §7.1 table exists: home + locale roots, /projets/ index + [city] + [city]/[slug], /{type_segment}/ routes from url_segment, /promoteurs/[slug], /recherche shell, contact/legal, 404
- AttributesTable renders any seeded property_type from schema_hints + custom-field labels with zero per-type code (R9)
- Templates and components consume only *View types from src/lib/mappers.ts — no api-types imports, no RENDER_MODE reads (R4, §2.2 hard rule)
notes: Spec: §7.1, §7.4, §16 P2-E4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E1.3 tsvector + trigram + supporting indexes + k6 load test meeting §15.5 budgets
description:
## Why
§16 P5-E1's acceptance criterion is purely a performance budget: k6 §15.5 (200 rps sustained, p95 < 300 ms) on staging hardware. Without dedicated tsvector/trigram indexes the §6.3 predicates (websearch_to_tsquery over i18n jsonb, attribute filters, bbox ranges) will seq-scan and the budget fails as the catalog grows.

## What
- Migration(s): tsvector coverage (stored generated column or expression GIN index) over title/description/city across locales for `websearch_to_tsquery`; `pg_trgm` extension + trigram index where partial/fuzzy matching needs it (city/title).
- Verify the §5.4 baseline indexes serve the search/geo predicates: GIN on `attributes` (jsonb_path_ops), `(price)`, `(city)`, `(lat, lng)` btree pair, partial index `WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL`.
- EXPLAIN ANALYZE evidence on the P1-E2 seed catalog (≥ 3 types, ≥ 40 listings — scale up synthetically if needed for meaningful plans) for representative /search and /listings/geo queries.
- k6 scripts for both endpoints per §15.5; run on staging hardware with rate limits relaxed; record and commit results.

## Out of scope
- Endpoint behavior changes (P5-E1.1/.2); Lighthouse budgets (frontend, §15.5 — P5-E2/E3 concern).
design:
- tsvector strategy: stored generated column or expression GIN index covering title/description/city across locales, feeding websearch_to_tsquery (§6.3)
- pg_trgm GIN trigram index for fuzzy city/title matching
- Verify §5.4 indexes actually used: GIN attributes jsonb_path_ops, (price), (city), (lat,lng) btree pair, partial WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL
- Staging k6 run with Hammer limits relaxed (explicitly allowed by §15.5); budgets 200 rps sustained, p95 < 300 ms
acceptance_criteria:
- EXPLAIN ANALYZE on seed data shows index scans (no seq scan on listings) for q-only, attrs-filtered, and bbox query shapes
- k6: /search and /listings/geo sustain 200 rps with p95 < 300 ms on staging hardware, rate limits relaxed (§15.5 verbatim)
- Migrations reversible; pg_trgm and any extensions created idempotently
- k6 scripts + recorded results committed/documented for reuse by the P8-E3 performance gate
notes: Spec: §15.5 k6 budgets, §6.3, §5.4 index list, §16 P5-E1 AC. Open decisions: D7 (no PostGIS — btree ranges must hold the budget). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E1.2 GET /api/v1/listings/geo: bbox=minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat with max-span guard + type + limit≤500 → GeoJSON FeatureCollection (id, title, price, path, thumb); public, s-maxage=60 permissible
description:
## Why
Feeds the clustered search map (§7.5 ListingMap: `moveend` → `GET /listings/geo?bbox=`; §9 cluster source). Public-tier abuse resistance requires the max-span guard + limit cap so a single giant bbox cannot dump the catalog (§10.1: tiered tokens keep the firehose private; this endpoint must stay narrow).

## What
- `GET /api/v1/listings/geo` on `:api_public` (§6.4).
- Params: `bbox=minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat` (required; numeric validation, ordering check, max-span guard rejection), `type` (property_type key filter), `limit ≤ 500` (cap enforced, sensible default).
- Query: published listings (`Catalog.published/1`, §5.13) with lat/lng inside bbox using simple range predicates on the §5.4 `(lat, lng)` btree pair (PostGIS explicitly deferred — D7).
- Response: GeoJSON `FeatureCollection`; each Feature = Point geometry `[lng, lat]` + properties `id`, `title` (locale-resolved), `price`, `path` (via `Immo.Edge.Paths`), `thumb`.
- Cache headers: `public, s-maxage=60` permissible per §6.3 — set it so the edge shields the VPS from pan storms.

## Out of scope
- Clustering (client-side, MapLibre cluster source — P5-E3.3); radius/polygon search (D7 override only).
design:
- bbox predicate: lat BETWEEN minLat AND maxLat AND lng BETWEEN minLng AND maxLng over the §5.4 (lat,lng) btree pair — D7 default, no PostGIS
- Max-span guard: configured degree threshold validated before query — blocks scrape-the-world bboxes (§10.1 abuse rationale)
- path + thumb built server-side (Immo.Edge.Paths + §8 media URL convention); geometry Point [lng, lat]
- Pipeline :api_public, Hammer 120/min/IP + CF WAF (§10.1)
acceptance_criteria:
- bbox exceeding the max-span guard → 422 problem+json; malformed/mis-ordered bbox → 422
- limit > 500 capped/rejected; results strictly inside bbox; only published records (Catalog.published/1)
- Output is valid GeoJSON FeatureCollection (schema-checked); Feature properties exactly id, title, price, path, thumb
- Rate limit 120/min/IP enforced (§10.1); responses carry public, s-maxage=60 cache header
- OpenAPI documented; drift gate green
notes: Spec: §6.3 geo row, §9 clustering consumer, §7.5 ListingMap, §5.4 indexes, §10.1. Open decisions: D7 (default lat/lng btree ranges; PostGIS deferred). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P5-E1.1 GET /api/v1/search: q via websearch_to_tsquery over title/description/city + filters type/city/price_min/max/surface_min/max + attrs[key] validated against filter_config (incl. searchable custom fields) + sort price_asc/desc|newest + page≤50/per_page≤24 → card view-models; Cache-Control: private, no-store
description:
## Why
R9: search must be data-driven — `attrs[<key>]` params validate against `property_types.filter_config` merged with searchable custom fields (§5.5), so an admin-defined field becomes filterable with zero code change. §3.6 routes all search traffic here permanently (results never baked), making correctness + abuse caps load-bearing.

## What
- Controller on `:api_public` (§6.4) at `GET /api/v1/search`.
- `q`: `websearch_to_tsquery` over title/description/city (i18n jsonb text + city column).
- Scalar filters: `type` (property_type key), `city`, `price_min`/`price_max`, `surface_min`/`surface_max`.
- `attrs[<key>]=...`: accept only keys present in the resolved filter_config (sources column|attribute|custom_field, §5.3); apply per kind (range/select/boolean); unknown key → 422 problem+json (RFC 9457).
- `sort`: `price_asc` | `price_desc` | `newest` (default newest).
- Pagination caps: `page ≤ 50`, `per_page ≤ 24` — enforced, behavior documented in OpenAPI.
- Response: card view-models (id, slug, `path` per locale via `Immo.Edge.Paths`, title, price, price_on_request, currency, city, thumb, key attributes) in the §6.3 `{data, meta}` envelope.
- `Cache-Control: private, no-store` on every response (§6.3: page shell caches, results must not).
- Scope: `Catalog.published/1` only (§5.13).

## Out of scope
- Indexes + k6 (P5-E1.3); geo endpoint (P5-E1.2); island UI (P5-E2).
design:
- Pipeline :api_public (§6.4): CORS exact-origin allowlist + Hammer 60/min/IP (§10.1 path 3)
- Filter resolution: filter_config merged with searchable custom_fields (§5.3/§5.5) resolved per request; kinds range|select|boolean over sources column|attribute|custom_field drive predicate building
- Attribute predicates hit listings.attributes JSONB via GIN jsonb_path_ops (§5.4)
- Card view-model per §6.3 conventions: id, slug, path (Immo.Edge.Paths), title, price/price_on_request/currency, city, thumb; list envelope {data, meta}
acceptance_criteria:
- q= matches words in title, description and city across locales with websearch_to_tsquery semantics (quoted phrases, - exclusion)
- attrs[key] for a searchable custom field filters results; unknown attrs key → 422 problem+json
- page > 50 or per_page > 24 rejected/clamped per documented contract; both caps covered by tests
- sort=price_asc|price_desc|newest orders correctly; price_on_request/null prices handled deterministically
- Every response carries Cache-Control: private, no-store; unpublished or billing-gated records never appear (Catalog.published/1)
- 61st request in a minute from one IP → 429 (Hammer 60/min/IP); OpenAPI updated, drift gate green
notes: Spec: §6.3 /search row, §6.4, §5.3, §5.5, §5.13, §10.1. Open decisions: none blocking (D7 applies to geo only). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E1.3 Role-matrix integration tests (4 roles × admin surfaces incl. developer_user scoping)
description:
## Why
- §16 P1-E1 acceptance criterion is literally "role matrix integration-tested" — this task is the epic's Definition of Done.
- R7: locks in least-privilege on the staff path (§10.1 path 5) and prevents privilege-escalation or tenant-leak regressions as P1-E3 adds surfaces.

## What
- Integration tests crossing the 4 roles (admin, manager, editor, developer_user) × admin surface groups (catalog, CRM, billing-read, billing-write, audit-log/admin-only) per §6.2.
- developer_user scoping cases: own projects/listings visible; foreign developer's data invisible and write-rejected (§5.8).
- Session idle-timeout test (24 h, §13).
- Role fixtures (with/without developer_id) reusable by later epics.

## Out of scope
- Surface-specific behavior tests (land with each P1-E3 surface); this matrix asserts access control only.
design:
- ExUnit + Phoenix.LiveViewTest; fixtures for each role (developer_user fixtures carry developer_id)
- Table-driven test over the §6.2 role-to-surface matrix (surfaces: catalog, CRM, billing-read, billing-write, audit/admin-only)
- Two developers seeded to prove cross-tenant isolation
acceptance_criteria:
- Matrix coverage: every role × surface combination asserted (allow or deny) per the §6.2 matrix
- developer_user cross-tenant read and write attempts rejected; own-data access succeeds
- 24 h idle-timeout behavior covered (§13)
- Suite green in CI; failures pinpoint role+surface combination
notes: Spec: §6.2, §5.8, §13, §15.1, §16 P1-E1 AC (role matrix integration-tested). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E1.2 RBAC on_mount hooks: admin=all, manager=catalog+CRM+billing-read, editor=catalog, developer_user=own data only + 24 h session idle timeout
description:
## Why
- R7 least-privilege on the staff trust path (§10.1 path 5): every admin surface must be role-gated; developer_user is an external, tenant-scoped role that must never see other developers' data (§5.8).
- §13 security checklist mandates the 24 h admin session idle timeout.

## What
- LiveView `on_mount` RBAC hooks per §6.2: admin = everything; manager = catalog + CRM + billing-read; editor = catalog only; developer_user = own projects/listings only.
- Query-level scoping for developer_user: catalog queries filtered to `current_user.developer_id` (§5.8 "scopes all queries to own projects") — enforced in context functions, not just UI.
- 24 h session idle timeout for admin sessions (§13).
- Graceful denial UX: redirect + flash on unauthorized mount/navigation.

## Out of scope
- The admin CRUD surfaces themselves (P1-E3 mounts onto these hooks).
- Cloudflare Access second factor (D9).
design:
- Parameterized on_mount hooks (e.g. on_mount {ImmoWeb.UserAuth, {:ensure_role, scope}}) implementing the §6.2 matrix
- developer_user scoping applied at the query layer keyed on current_user.developer_id (§5.8: scopes all queries to own projects)
- Idle timeout: session/token validity window of 24 h (§13)
- Surfaces grouped: catalog, CRM, billing-read, billing-write, admin-only (audit log, users)
acceptance_criteria:
- on_mount hooks deny manager access to billing-write and admin-only surfaces; allow catalog + CRM + billing-read (§6.2)
- editor restricted to catalog surfaces only
- developer_user catalog queries return only rows belonging to their developer_id; cross-tenant reads and writes denied (§5.8)
- Session idle beyond 24 h forces re-login (§13)
- admin role passes through to all surfaces
- Unauthorized access redirects with flash, does not crash
notes: Spec: §6.2, §5.8, §10.1 path 5, §13. Open decisions: D9 (CF Access second factor — default off). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P1-E1.1 Phoenix 1.8 app in /backend + phx.gen.auth (argon2) + users.role enum + developer_id fk + seed admin
description:
## Why
- R7/A8: the staff trust path (§10.1 path 5) requires phx.gen.auth sessions with argon2; the users table (§5.8) is the substrate for all RBAC and for developer_user tenant scoping.
- The `/backend` Phoenix app is the single-source-of-truth application (A3) that every other P1 epic builds in.

## What
- Generate Phoenix 1.8 app in `/backend` (monorepo layout §4; Elixir conventions: mix format, Credo strict, Dialyzer in CI per §4).
- Run `mix phx.gen.auth` with **argon2** (§10.1 path 5, §13).
- Migration adding `users.role` enum: `admin | manager | editor | developer_user` (§5.8).
- `users.developer_id` uuid fk → developers, nullable; invariant: required iff role = developer_user (§5.8) — DB check constraint + changeset validation.
- Seed admin user (priv/repo/seeds.exs).

## Out of scope
- on_mount role gating (P1-E1.2).
- The developers table itself (P1-E2.1) — if this task runs first, add the column and defer the fk constraint to the E2 migration chain.
design:
- users: phx.gen.auth columns + role (Ecto.Enum: admin|manager|editor|developer_user) + developer_id uuid fk nullable (§5.8)
- argon2 as the hash lib (not bcrypt) per §10.1 path 5 / §13
- HttpOnly Secure session cookies (phx.gen.auth default, verified)
- Seed: one admin user via priv/repo/seeds
acceptance_criteria:
- Phoenix app boots in /backend; mix test green; mix format/Credo conventions wired (§4)
- phx.gen.auth flows (register/login/logout/reset) pass generated tests using argon2 hashing
- users.role accepts exactly admin|manager|editor|developer_user; invalid role rejected
- developer_id required iff role=developer_user, enforced at changeset AND database level (§5.8)
- Seed admin exists after seeding and can log in
notes: Spec: §5.8, §10.1 path 5, §13, A8, §4. The developers table lands in P1-E2.1 — coordinate fk constraint timing (column may precede fk). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P1-E1 — Phoenix app + auth/RBAC (staff)
description:
## Why
- Serves R7 (secure, least-privilege auth with separately rotatable credentials per trust path): implements trust path 5 of §10.1 — Staff → Phoenix admin via phx.gen.auth session (argon2), RBAC roles, HttpOnly Secure cookies.
- Locked decision A8: `mix phx.gen.auth` + RBAC for staff.
- Foundation of the management plane: the Phoenix app in `/backend` is the single writer (A3) hosting LiveView admin, JSON API, and Oban — every other P1 epic builds inside it.

## What
- Phoenix 1.8 app under `/backend` (monorepo layout §4, A10).
- phx.gen.auth (argon2) staff users per §5.8: `role` enum `admin|manager|editor|developer_user`; `developer_id` fk nullable, required iff role = developer_user (scopes all queries to own projects).
- `on_mount` RBAC hooks per §6.2: admin = everything; manager = catalog + CRM + billing-read; editor = catalog only; developer_user = own projects/listings only.
- 24 h admin session idle timeout (§13).
- Seed admin user.
- Role-matrix integration tests (§16 AC).

## Out of scope
- Machine bearer tokens / API tiers (P1-E5).
- Cloudflare Access in front of /admin (D9 — default off).
- Admin CRUD surfaces themselves (P1-E3); this epic delivers the auth/RBAC substrate they mount on.
design:
- users = phx.gen.auth columns + role enum admin|manager|editor|developer_user + developer_id fk nullable, required iff role=developer_user (§5.8)
- RBAC enforced via LiveView on_mount hooks per the §6.2 role-to-surface matrix
- argon2 password hashing; HttpOnly Secure session cookies; staff trust path = §10.1 path 5
- 24 h admin session idle timeout per §13 security checklist
acceptance_criteria:
- Role matrix integration-tested (§16 P1-E1 AC): all 4 roles (admin/manager/editor/developer_user) exercised against admin surfaces, allow AND deny cases
- developer_user sessions are scoped to their own developer_id data; cross-tenant access denied
- phx.gen.auth login/logout works with argon2 hashes; sessions are HttpOnly Secure cookies (§10.1 path 5)
- Seed admin can sign in on a fresh database
- Admin session idle timeout of 24 h enforced (§13)
notes: Spec: §5.8, §6.2, §10.1 path 5, §13, A8, §16 P1-E1. Open decisions: D9 (Cloudflare Access on /admin — default off, post-launch). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P5-E1 — Search backend (/search + /listings/geo)
description:
## Why
The two anonymous public read endpoints (§6.3) power the never-stale search experience (§3.6: /search results are always a client island against /api/v1/search) and both map surfaces (P5-E3). R9 demands attribute filters be driven by `property_types.filter_config` including admin-defined searchable custom fields — zero code change per new field. These endpoints are the only anonymous read surface besides POST /inquiries, so abuse resistance (caps, span guards, rate limits) is part of the contract.

## What
- `GET /api/v1/search` (§6.3): `q` via `websearch_to_tsquery` over title/description/city; filters `type`, `city`, `price_min/max`, `surface_min/max`, `attrs[<key>]` validated against filter_config (incl. searchable custom fields); `sort` price_asc/desc|newest; `page≤50`, `per_page≤24`; returns card view-models; `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- `GET /api/v1/listings/geo` (§6.3): `bbox=minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat` with max-span guard, `type`, `limit≤500` → GeoJSON FeatureCollection (id, title, price, path, thumb); `public, s-maxage=60` permissible.
- Both on the `:api_public` pipeline (§6.4: CORS + RateLimit, no auth) and scoped by the single `Catalog.published/1` predicate (§5.13 — billing gate included when enforced).
- Supporting indexes (tsvector, trigram, §5.4 GIN/btree) + k6 load test proving §15.5 budgets on staging hardware.

## Out of scope
- The SearchFilter island and results UI (P5-E2); map islands (P5-E3); PostGIS (D7, deferred).
design:
- Public tier (§10.1 path 3): anonymous, CORS exact-origin allowlist, Hammer rate limits search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP + CF WAF rules
- Cache-Control: private, no-store on /search; public, s-maxage=60 permissible on /listings/geo (§6.3 conventions)
- path field computed server-side by Immo.Edge.Paths (single path authority shared with KV marking)
- Geo via lat/lng btree range predicates on the §5.4 (lat,lng) pair — PostGIS explicitly deferred (D7)
acceptance_criteria:
- k6 budget §15.5 met on staging hardware: /search and /listings/geo sustain 200 rps with p95 < 300 ms (rate limits relaxed in staging)
- Both endpoints in OpenAPI (open_api_spex); drift gate green
- Only published records returned (single Catalog.published/1 predicate, §5.13)
- Invalid params yield RFC 9457 problem+json 4xx, never 500
- Rate limits enforced: search 60/min/IP, geo 120/min/IP (§10.1)
notes: Spec: §6.3 /search + /listings/geo rows, §6.4 pipelines, §10.1, §5.13, §15.5, §16 P5-E1. Open decisions: D7 (default lat/lng btree ranges; PostGIS only if radius/polygon search demanded). Cross-phase deps (P1-E5) wired by orchestrator.

title: P7-E3.1 Privacy policy (Law 09-08 + GDPR) + terms + about pages (3 locales) + consent text on inquiry form
description:
## Why
Delivers the §13-mandated privacy/legal surface (Law 09-08 + GDPR notice pages, consent capture) so the P8-E1 security gate can check off its privacy line item with live evidence.

## What
- Write and ship the privacy policy: enumerate §5.7 inquiry fields (name, email, phone, message, locale, consent), processing purpose (lead handling by staff/assigned developer), retention via `INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 365) enforced by the RetentionSweeper (§6.5), data residency EU/MA (Hetzner EU VPS, R2 EU jurisdiction, EU backup bucket), and rights under Law 09-08 and GDPR with a contact channel.
- Write terms and about pages.
- Localize all three pages into fr, ar, en; wire into nav/footer; prerendered per §7.1; hreflang clusters per §7.6.
- Add consent text + required checkbox to the InquiryForm island, persisted to `inquiries.consent` (§5.7); link to the privacy page in the visitor's locale.

## Out of scope
- Changing retention defaults or the sweeper (already specified/built); legal counsel review cycle.
design:
- Pages are prerendered from content files (§7.1 "/contact, legal pages — prerender — content files"); no API dependency
- §5.7 inquiries: consent boolean (GDPR/Law 09-08), locale captured; RetentionSweeper purges closed inquiries after INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS (§6.5, default 365)
- Residency facts to state: Hetzner EU VPS (§12.2), R2 EU jurisdiction setting, backups in Hetzner Object Storage EU (D12) — per §13 privacy bullet
- Consent UX: checkbox + text inside the InquiryForm island; POST /inquiries body carries consent (§6.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- /privacy (localized paths) renders in fr, ar, en; covers data collected (§5.7 inquiry fields), purpose, retention (INQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS default 365), EU/MA residency (Hetzner EU, R2 EU jurisdiction), and Law 09-08 + GDPR notices
- Terms + about pages render in all 3 locales as prerendered pages (§7.1) with correct hreflang per §7.6
- InquiryForm shows consent text linking to the privacy page; consent is required and persisted to inquiries.consent (§5.7)
- AR versions render RTL-correct (consistent with P7-E1)
notes: Spec: §16 P7-E3, §13, §5.7, §6.5 (RetentionSweeper), §7.1, §12.2, §12.4. Open decisions: D5, D12. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P7-E3 — Content & legal pages
description:
## Why
The §13 security release gate explicitly requires "privacy policy + Law 09-08/GDPR notice pages", a stored consent flag, active retention sweeps, and EU/MA data residency. P8-E1 verifies these; this epic produces the user-facing pages and consent text that make that verification possible. Also completes the §7.1 content/legal route set for launch.

## What
