title: P2-E1.3 BaseLayout (head mgmt, hreflang cluster skeleton, preconnect media./api.) + Seo component (title/meta/OG/Twitter from seo i18n with deterministic fallbacks)
description:
## Why
- §7.4 component inventory: BaseLayout (head mgmt, hreflang, CSP-safe) and Seo are the head/SEO substrate for every page (R8).
- R4: both are render-mode agnostic — they receive view/seo data as props and emit identical markup whether the page is prerendered or SSR.

## What
- BaseLayout: html lang + dir per locale; head management (title/meta slots+props); hreflang cluster skeleton emitting fr/ar/en + x-default alternates from a prop (§7.6); preconnect to media.<domain> and api.<domain> derived from MEDIA_BASE_URL / API_BASE_URL (§12.4, §7.6 performance).
- Seo component: title/meta/OG/Twitter from entity seo i18n maps with deterministic fallbacks ({title} – {city} | {site}, §7.6); OG image wiring left pluggable for Media URLs (P2-E6).
- Vitest unit tests for the fallback chain.

## Out of scope
- Per-route canonical correctness and full page wiring (P2-E5.1); JSON-LD (P2-E5.2).
design:
- Props-only contract: BaseLayout/Seo never read RENDER_MODE and never fetch — render-mode agnostic (R4, §2.2 hard rule)
- Fallback pattern per §7.6: {title} – {city} | {site}; per-route canonical wiring finished in P2-E5.1
- hreflang alternates fed later by mappers/path builders (P2-E2.3) and route/SEO wiring (P2-E4/E5)
- §7.4: BaseLayout = head mgmt, hreflang, CSP-safe
acceptance_criteria:
- Pages using BaseLayout emit correct html lang + dir for fr/ar/en
- preconnect links to media.<domain> and api.<domain> present in head (built from MEDIA_BASE_URL / API_BASE_URL)
- Seo: full seo data emitted verbatim; missing fields fall back deterministically to the {title} – {city} | {site} pattern — unit-tested in Vitest
- hreflang cluster incl. x-default rendered when alternates prop provided
notes: Spec: §7.4, §7.6, §12.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E1.2 Design tokens src/styles/tokens.css + THEME env override file + logical-properties lint rule (RTL) + self-hosted fonts (font-display: swap)
description:
## Why
- R9/§7.4: new verticals are re-skinned via tokens + logo + content with zero component edits; the tokens file + THEME override is that contract.
- R8 AR RTL correctness depends on logical CSS properties everywhere — a lint rule makes it structural rather than best-effort (§7.6).
- Core Web Vitals: self-hosted fonts with font-display: swap remove render-blocking third-party requests (§7.6).

## What
- src/styles/tokens.css: CSS custom properties (color palette, typography scale, spacing, radii, shadows) — the single styling source for all components.
- Per-deployment theme override file (e.g. src/styles/themes/<THEME>.css) selected by THEME env (§12.4), loaded after tokens.css; ship a default theme.
- Lint rule (stylelint/ESLint) banning physical properties in favor of logical equivalents; wired into CI frontend lint (§12.3).
- Self-hosted fonts: woff2 assets in-repo, @font-face with font-display: swap; no font CDN.

## Out of scope
- Component styling itself (P2-E4.2); logo/content theming of a second vertical (data work, post-v1).
design:
- §7.4 theme layer: tokens.css + per-deployment override file selected by THEME env (§12.4) — re-skinning a vertical = tokens + logo + content, zero component edits (R9)
- Logical-properties rule is the §7.6 RTL lint rule; wired into frontend lint CI (§12.3)
- Fonts: woff2 self-hosted, font-display: swap, preload only LCP-critical faces; zero render-blocking third-party JS (§7.6)
acceptance_criteria:
- Two builds with different THEME values yield different token values in output CSS with zero component diffs
- Lint fails a fixture using physical properties (margin-left, padding-right, text-align: left); passes logical equivalents (margin-inline-start etc.)
- All @font-face rules self-hosted with font-display: swap; no external font origins in built HTML
- tokens.css covers color palette, typography scale, spacing, radii — components reference tokens only (no raw values)
notes: Spec: §7.4 theme layer, §7.6, §12.4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P2-E1.1 Astro 6 + Cloudflare adapter + output:'static' + built-in i18n routing (fr root, /ar RTL, /en) + csp:true + astro:env schema (BUILD_TOKEN server secret etc.)
description:
## Why
- Substrate for all of P2. i18n routing and CSP are config-level concerns, keeping templates render-mode agnostic (R4, §2.2 hard rule).
- R8: FR-default/AR-RTL/EN URL structure is SEO-load-bearing and painful to change after launch.

## What
- Create frontend/ with Astro 6 per §4 layout (src/pages, src/loaders, src/lib, src/components, src/islands, src/integrations, astro.config.mjs; src/worker placeholder dir).
- Install @astrojs/cloudflare adapter; set output: static (§2.2 static is the default flagship mode).
- Configure built-in i18n routing (§7.6): defaultLocale fr at root; locales ar (/ar/, RTL) and en (/en/).
- Set csp: true (§7.6), nonce-compatible islands.
- Define astro:env schema (§12.4): server secret BUILD_TOKEN; build vars PUBLIC_SITE_URL, API_BASE_URL, MEDIA_BASE_URL, RENDER_MODE (default static), HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES, THEME, LOCALES.
- Placeholder locale index pages so the build emits /, /ar/, /en/.

## Out of scope
- Tokens/fonts (P2-E1.2), BaseLayout/Seo (P2-E1.3), real routes (P2-E4), render-mode flipping integration (P2-E7.2).
design:
- Astro 6 + @astrojs/cloudflare adapter; output: static — the P2-E7 integration later flips prerender per RENDER_MODE (§2.2)
- i18n routing per §7.6: defaultLocale fr at root (no prefix), /ar/ and /en/ prefixed
- BUILD_TOKEN consumed only by loaders/SSR server code (§7.2, §10.1 build path)
- csp: true with nonce-compatible islands (§7.6)
acceptance_criteria:
- astro build succeeds; dist contains /, /ar/, /en/ index HTML with correct html lang and dir="rtl" on ar pages
- csp: true set in astro.config.mjs and reflected in built output
- astro:env schema: BUILD_TOKEN declared as server secret — client-side import fails the build; RENDER_MODE / HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES / THEME / LOCALES / PUBLIC_SITE_URL / API_BASE_URL / MEDIA_BASE_URL declared per §12.4
- Directory layout matches §4 (src/pages, src/loaders, src/lib, src/components, src/islands, src/integrations)
- CI build smoke runs astro build on PRs (§12.3)
notes: Spec: §7.6, §2.2, §12.4, §4. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P2-E1 — Astro scaffold + theme tokens + RTL base

title: P7-E2.1 Verify completeness indicators + missing-locale fallback chains end-to-end + hreflang audit vs sitemap (every published path's alternates consistent)
description:
## Why
Closes §16 P7-E2: the three i18n-completeness contracts (§6.2 indicators, §7.3 fallback chain, §7.6 hreflang-vs-sitemap consistency) must be demonstrated working together, end-to-end, as a launch precondition for R8.

## What
- Seed/curate records with partial translations (e.g. fr-only, fr+ar, missing seo map per locale) and verify admin completeness indicators match stored data on the fr/ar/en tabs (§6.2).
- Render those records in each locale and verify the §7.3 chain: requested → fr → en → first available, for title, description, SEO meta/OG, and media alt — no blanks anywhere in HTML or head.
- Run an hreflang audit across **every published path**: fetch each page, extract the hreflang cluster (fr/ar/en + x-default), and diff against the alternates `GET /meta/sitemap` feeds into sitemap.xml. Every mismatch is a defect; fix and re-run to zero.
- Verify SSR fallback pages (state B/C) emit the identical hreflang cluster and canonical as their static twins (§7.6 / R4).

## Out of scope
- Writing the missing translations themselves; RTL layout defects (P7-E1.1).
design:
- §7.3: locale resolution lives only in mappers.ts (toListingView/toProjectView) — fallback requested → fr → en → first available
- §6.2: admin i18n tabs per locale with completeness indicators; per-locale SEO preview snippet
- §7.6: hreflang cluster includes x-default; @astrojs/sitemap custom serializer fed by GET /meta/sitemap (lastmod + locale alternates)
- Audit mechanics: crawl published paths from /meta/sitemap, parse link rel=alternate hreflang, diff against sitemap.xml entries
acceptance_criteria:
- Completeness indicators verified against seeded records with partial translations: indicator state matches stored i18n jsonb for each of fr/ar/en (§6.2)
- Fallback-chain test cases pass for each missing-locale combination: requested → fr → en → first available (§7.3); no blank field reaches rendered HTML or meta tags
- Automated audit over every published path: rendered hreflang cluster (incl. x-default) matches sitemap alternates from GET /meta/sitemap; zero mismatches
- Canonical on SSR-served pages equals the prerendered URL (§7.6)
notes: Spec: §16 P7-E2, §6.2, §7.3, §7.6, §6.3. Open decisions: D5. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P7-E2 — Translation completeness workflow
description:
## Why
R8 requires i18n with hreflang as an SEO-first feature. Three spec contracts make partial translation safe — admin completeness indicators (§6.2), the mapper fallback chain (§7.3), and the full hreflang cluster incl. x-default consistent with the sitemap (§7.6) — and §16 P7-E2 requires all three verified end-to-end before launch. Inconsistent hreflang/sitemap alternates silently waste the entire i18n SEO investment.

## What
- Verify the admin LiveView i18n field tabs (fr/ar/en) show completeness indicators that reflect actual stored jsonb i18n maps, on developers, projects, listings and SEO fields (§6.2).
- Exercise the §7.3 fallback chain end-to-end with deliberately partial records: requested → fr → en → first available, across titles, descriptions, SEO meta, alt text.
- hreflang audit vs sitemap: for every published path, the rendered hreflang cluster (incl. x-default) must agree with the locale alternates emitted by `GET /meta/sitemap` into sitemap.xml.

## Out of scope
- Visual RTL correctness (P7-E1).
- Authoring missing translations (content work; file gaps as separate content issues).
design:
- §7.3 mappers are the single locale-resolution point: requested → fr → en → first available; verify no template does its own fallback
- §6.2: i18n field tabs (fr/ar/en) with completeness indicators + per-locale SERP-style SEO preview in admin
- §7.6: full hreflang cluster incl. x-default on every page; canonical always the prerendered URL (SSR emits the same canonical)
- §6.3 GET /meta/sitemap is the source of paths + lastmod + locale alternates feeding @astrojs/sitemap — audit alternates against rendered hreflang
acceptance_criteria:
- Admin i18n field tabs show accurate completeness indicators (§6.2) for records with partial fr/ar/en translations
- A page whose requested locale is missing renders via the §7.3 fallback chain (requested → fr → en → first available) with no blank titles/descriptions/SEO fields
- hreflang audit: every published path emits the full hreflang cluster incl. x-default (§7.6), and the alternates are consistent with the sitemap for every published path
- Global DoD §15.6 met
notes: Spec: §16 P7-E2, §6.2 (completeness indicators), §7.3 (fallback chain), §7.6 (hreflang cluster incl. x-default), §6.3 (GET /meta/sitemap). Open decisions: D5 (drop en if content capacity short — audit must still pass for whichever locales ship). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P7-E1.1 Full AR visual pass: mirrored layouts, Arabic typography, islands RTL (search facets, map labels via RTL plugin), fixes filed/applied
description:
## Why
Executes the §16 P7-E1 audit — the named §18 mitigation for RTL/Arabic regressions — so the launch gates (P8) start from a verified-RTL baseline.

## What
- Walk every template on /ar/: mirrored layout (nav, breadcrumbs, cards, pagination, footer), spacing/icon direction, Arabic typography (font stack, line-height, numeral rendering in PriceTag/AttributesTable).
- Islands: SearchFilter facet controls and URL-synced state in RTL; ListingMap Arabic labels via the mapbox-gl-rtl-text plugin (§9) on both detail and clustered search maps; InquiryForm field order, Turnstile widget placement, validation messages.
- Confirm `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` for AR routes and zero logical-properties lint violations (§7.6); convert any stragglers to logical properties.
- Spot-check an SSR catch-all page (state B/C) in AR against its prerendered equivalent — must be identical per R4.
- File one issue per defect; land fixes; re-run the §15.4 AR RTL e2e check to close.

## Out of scope
- hreflang/fallback-chain checks (P7-E2.1); legal page copy (P7-E3.1).
design:
- §7.6: dir="rtl" set on <html> for /ar/ pages via Astro i18n routing
- §7.6: physical CSS properties replaced by logical equivalents; lint rule is the regression guard
- §9: load mapbox-gl-rtl-text plugin for the Arabic locale so MapLibre renders Arabic labels correctly (detail map + clustered search map)
- R4 invariant: templates are render-mode agnostic, so verify one SSR-served page in AR matches its static twin
acceptance_criteria:

- Logical-properties lint passes with zero violations (§7.6)
- Visual pass evidenced for all page templates (home, indexes, project/listing/developer detail, search shell, contact/legal, 404) and all three islands in AR
- All RTL defects found are filed; fixes merged and verified on staging

title: [Immo] P7-E1 — AR/RTL full audit
description:
## Why
R8 demands SEO-first i18n with FR default and **AR with RTL** as a first-class locale. The risk register (§18) rates RTL/Arabic regressions medium-likelihood / medium-impact, and names its mitigation explicitly: the logical-properties lint rule, **this dedicated P7-E1 audit**, and the §15.4 e2e RTL check. P2-E4 only required "ar pages RTL-correct" for the seed catalog; this epic is the full sweep across everything built since (freshness SSR pages, search, maps, inquiry, billing-gated states) before the P8 launch gates.

## What
- Full AR visual pass per §16 P7-E1: mirrored layouts and Arabic typography on every page template (home/landings, category and city indexes, project/listing/developer detail, search shell, contact + legal pages, 404).

- File an issue per defect found; apply fixes.

acceptance_criteria:

- Every page template and all three islands (SearchFilter, ListingMap, InquiryForm) visually verified in AR: mirrored layout, Arabic typography; all defects filed and fixes merged

title: E10 — Phase 9: Polish & cross-cutting (Part B · app) [~2-4 weeks, ongoing]
description:
**Phase 9 (Part B · app) — ~2-4 weeks, ongoing · priority normal**

The catch-all for things that are explicitly **not** launch blockers. Done iteratively as time allows, alongside the other phases — none of these gate a release.

**Why a separate phase**: the spec is explicit that the recommendation model, store-submission polish, and offline tolerance are not launch blockers. Putting them in their own epic signals 'park here, don't let it expand the launch scope.'

**Ordering note**: depends on E9. Children 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 are independent and can ship in any order.

title: 8.2 Social: follow / like / comment / view (RLS-protected)
description:
The follow / like / comment / view interactions, all backed by the `follows` and `engagements` tables from E6. RLS is the source of truth — every interaction is server-validated.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/social/follow_button.dart`
- `app/lib/features/social/engagement_bar.dart` — like, comment, share, view-count.
- `app/lib/features/social/comments_sheet.dart`
- `backend/supabase/functions/engagement/index.ts` — single Edge Function for all four engagement types (router pattern); enforces `auth.uid()` server-side.
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0004_engagement_views.sql` — a view that joins `videos` + `engagements` for fast feed rendering.

**Validation**
- Follow a user → their videos appear in your 'Following' feed within the next refresh.
- A like is idempotent (liking twice doesn't double-count).
- A forged `user_id` in a like/comment payload is rejected at the Edge Function layer (not the client).
- View counts increment on a clip after 2+ seconds of visible playback (not on every page impression).

**Agent**: code-puppy + code-critic (RLS review).
**Notes**: the engagement bar is the second-most visible UI element after the video. Don't make it look like 2014 Twitter.

title: 8.1 Calendar: dated events + local reminders + FCM push
description:
A simple dated list (NOT a full calendar grid in v1) of `calendar_events`: planned workouts, classes, goals. Local reminders via the platform scheduler; FCM push for server-side reminders.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/calendar/event_list_page.dart` — dated list view.
- `app/lib/features/calendar/event_create_page.dart`
- `app/lib/features/calendar/local_reminders.dart` — wraps `flutter_local_notifications`.
- `backend/supabase/functions/calendar-reminders/index.ts` — Edge Function: a scheduled job (via `pg_cron` or Supabase scheduled functions) that fires FCM at the configured lead time.

**Validation**
- Create an event for 'tomorrow at 8am' → a local notification fires at the device's local 7:50am (10-min default lead).
- FCM reminder reaches a device that has been backgrounded for an hour.
- Deleting an event cancels its local reminder.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: the spec says 'keep it a simple dated list' — that's a deliberate scope cut. A full calendar grid is a v2 problem.

title: E9 — Phase 8: Calendar + social graph (Part B · app) [~2-3 weeks]
description:
**Phase 8 (Part B · app) — ~2-3 weeks · priority normal**

Two distinct features in one phase: a simple dated calendar of workouts/classes/goals, and the follow/like/comment/view social graph. Both already have data model support from E6; this phase is UI + state + RLS-backed interactions.

**Why they're grouped**: they share the social identity model (who you follow, what you can see) and the FCM push wiring. Doing them together avoids two passes through the same cross-cutting concerns.

**Ordering note**: depends on E8 (you'll want to test calendar/social interactions with real activity data). Children 8.1 and 8.2 are parallel.

title: 7.2 Link a clip to an activity (the distinguishing feature)
description:
The feature that distinguishes this app from a generic short-video app: when you upload a clip of a run, the clip carries the run's stats (distance, pace, splits, elevation).

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0003_video_activity_link.sql` — `videos.activity_id` is already a column; this adds the index + a join view.
- `app/lib/features/upload/attach_activity_step.dart` — upload wizard step: 'link to which workout?'.
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_item_overlay.dart` — overlay shows the linked activity's stats below the caption.
- `app/lib/features/activity/activity_detail_page.dart` — tap a workout → see all clips linked to it.

**Validation**
- Upload a clip with an activity attached → feed shows the activity stats in the overlay.
- A clip uploaded without an activity shows a 'no stats' placeholder (not an error).
- Tapping the overlay opens the activity detail page; activity detail page lists the clip.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is the bit that makes the app *not* another TikTok clone. Spend time on the overlay design — it should be glanceable, not a wall of numbers.

title: 7.1 HealthKit (iOS) + Health Connect (Android) + GPS
description:
Platform entitlements, permissions UX, and the recording loop. `health` package for HealthKit/Health Connect; `geolocator` for GPS. On-device only; sync is a separate concern (E10).

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/activity/recorder.dart` — the recording loop.
- `app/lib/features/activity/summary.dart` — the summary record shape.
- `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — `NSHealthShareUsageDescription`, `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`, `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`.
- `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` — Health Connect permissions, foreground service for ongoing workouts.
- `app/pubspec.yaml` — `health`, `geolocator`, `permission_handler`.

**Validation**
- iOS: a real device run of a 20-min walk → HealthKit shows the activity → app shows the same summary.
- Android: same, against Health Connect.
- Permission denial flow is graceful — clear message, no crash, can re-request from settings.
- App-killed-mid-workout case: foreground service keeps recording on Android; iOS uses HealthKit's own workout session, which is robust to kills.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: the platform permissions UX is half the work. The first build of this task will be a lot of plist/manifest churn. Budget for it.

title: E8 — Phase 7: Activity tracking (Part B · app) [~1.5-3 weeks]
description:
**Phase 7 (Part B · app) — ~1.5-3 weeks · priority normal**

HealthKit on iOS, Health Connect on Android, via the Flutter `health` package. GPS via `geolocator`. Record on-device; sync **summary** records only — raw GPS points stay on the device in v1.

**Why summaries only**: uploading raw GPS is a privacy / cost / battery triple-threat. Summaries (distance, duration, splits, elevation gain, average pace) are what the social feed actually displays anyway.

**Ordering note**: depends on E7 (you'll want to test activity-to-video linking against a real feed). Children 7.1 and 7.2 are tightly coupled (7.2 is the point of 7.1).

title: 6.3 Simple ranking (chronological 'following' + 'discover' by recency × engagement)
description:
Two feed sources. NO recommendation model — that's explicitly NOT a launch blocker (it's parked in E10).

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/functions/feed-following/index.ts` — Edge Function: returns the latest `ready` videos from accounts the user follows, paginated.
- `backend/supabase/functions/feed-discover/index.ts` — Edge Function: returns the latest `ready` videos from accounts the user doesn't follow, sorted by `recency * engagement_score`.
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_source.dart` — toggles between the two sources.

**Validation**
- 'Following' is empty for a new user with no follows → shows a friendly empty state.
- 'Discover' is non-empty on a fresh DB (you'll need to seed it manually for testing).
- A new video uploaded to a followed account appears in 'Following' within ~5 seconds (no aggressive polling; consider a Realtime channel).

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: keep the engagement score dead simple — `(likes*1 + comments*2 + views*0.1) / hours_since_post`. No ML. The point is to launch.

title: 5.3 Auth via Supabase Auth (no custom auth!)
description:
Wire email + Apple + Google sign-in through Supabase Auth. Do not roll your own auth.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/auth/` — sign-in screens, OAuth callbacks.
- `backend/supabase/config.toml` — auth providers enabled.

**Validation**
- Email/password sign-up creates a `users` row via a Postgres trigger on `auth.users`.
- Sign in with Apple and Sign in with Google work on iOS and Android respectively (manual device test).
- Sign-out clears the Supabase session and the local cache; restart of the app lands on the sign-in screen.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is a 600-line task, not a 60-line task. The 'thin slice' is about scope (just auth), not about effort. Apple Sign-In in particular has annoying config in both Xcode and Supabase.

title: 5.2 Supabase migrations: full data model + RLS
description:
Migrations for the full relational model and the RLS policies that gate every read/write. **This is the security surface — review it twice.**

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql` — schema for: `users` (extends `auth.users`), `activities`, `videos` (with `activity_id` FK), `calendar_events`, `follows`, `engagements` (likes/comments/views).
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0002_rls.sql` — RLS policies for every table.
- `backend/rls/README.md` — one-paragraph rationale per policy.

**Critical RLS rules**
- A user can read another user's **public** video metadata but NOT their activity GPS points (those are private, server-side summary only — see E8).
- A user can only INSERT an engagement with their own `user_id`; the `auth.uid()` check is non-negotiable.
- Follows are mutual-readable; only the follower can create/delete their own follow.
- Calendar events are owner-only; no public calendar feed in v1.

**Validation**
- `supabase db reset` runs migrations cleanly.
- A test script hits each table as anon, as authenticated user A on A's rows, and as authenticated user B on A's rows — only the expected combinations succeed.
- A write with a forged `user_id` is rejected at the DB layer, not at the client.

**Agent**: code-puppy + code-critic (security review of the RLS file before merge).
**Notes**: Postgres, not Firestore, was chosen for exactly this — RLS is a first-class feature. Use it.

title: 5.1 Flutter scaffold + Supabase client + env config + Sentry
description:
Scaffold the Flutter app, feature-first folder layout, wire the Supabase client, env config, and Sentry from day one.

**Files**
- `app/lib/core/` — `supabase_client.dart`, `env.dart`, `sentry.dart`, `router.dart`.
- `app/lib/features/auth/` — auth feature module (UI + state, real implementation in 5.3).
- `app/pubspec.yaml` — `supabase_flutter`, `flutter_dotenv`, `sentry_flutter`, etc.
- `app/.env` (gitignored) + `app/.env.example` (committed).

**Validation**
- `flutter run` boots a hello-world that initializes Supabase and Sentry on startup (visible in logs).
- A throwaway unhandled exception in dev shows up in Sentry's dashboard within a minute.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: feature-first (`features/<name>/{ui,state,data}/`) not layer-first (`screens/`, `widgets/`, `services/`). It's the boring choice for a small app but the only one that scales when the video feed lands.

title: E6 — Phase 5: App foundation — Auth + thin slice (Part B · app) [~1-2 weeks]
description:
**Phase 5 (Part B · app) — ~1-2 weeks · priority normal**

The first app code. Scaffold the Flutter project, wire the Supabase client, get a real auth flow working end-to-end, and stand up the full data model with RLS. Nothing user-facing is impressive yet — the goal is to prove the foundation is solid before the make-or-break video phase.

**Why this is its own phase**: the data model + RLS policies are the **entire authz surface**. Get them wrong here and you've shipped a security hole that you can't easily unwind after launch.

**Ordering note**: depends on E5 (the agent-generated backlog). Children 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 can run mostly in parallel; 5.2 must land before 5.3 if you want auth to talk to a real schema.

title: 4.3 Self-review: delegate planning-agent/ to code-critic
description:
Before declaring Part A done, hand the `planning-agent/` tree to `code-critic` for a self-review. This is the meta-loop: the agent that produces backlogs gets one too.

**Files**
- `docs/reviews/planning-agent-review.md` — the review output.
- Any issues raised → new tasks filed under this epic and resolved before closing E4.

**Validation**
- `code-critic` runs against `planning-agent/src/**/*.py` + prompts.
- Output covers: prompt injection surface, error paths, the human gate's default-deny behavior, idempotency of the writer, and the termination guards' correctness.
- No P0/P1 findings open at the end of E4.

**Agent**: code-critic
**Notes**: this is the moment to surface design problems, not after you've started building the app. A weak critic here is a weak foundation for the bridge milestone.

title: 4.2 Idempotent writer: local files (docs/backlog/)
description:
After the human gate approves, write the tree to LOCAL files. Stable IDs and content hashes so re-runs don't duplicate or churn.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/writers/local_md.py` — emits `docs/backlog/index.md`, `docs/backlog/<epic-id>.md`, per-task sections.
- `planning-agent/src/writers/local_json.py` — emits `docs/backlog/backlog.json` with the full tree + critic report.
- `planning-agent/src/writers/github_issues.py` — OPTIONAL, behind a feature flag. Uses GitHub Issues REST, not the (unavailable) MCP.

**Why local files, not Jira/Linear**: the original spec assumed MCP for Jira/Linear. This env has no MCP. For a solo dev, a clean `docs/backlog/` is genuinely enough for v1.

**Idempotency**
- Each node's content includes a stable hash of (id, title, description, estimate_days, depends_on). If a re-run produces the same hash for a node, do NOT rewrite that file.
- If a node was removed since last run, leave a tombstone (or delete; document the choice).

**Validation**
- First run: produces `docs/backlog/index.md` and one file per epic + a `backlog.json`.
- Second run with NO spec change: zero diff in `docs/backlog/` (`git status` clean).
- Re-run with a spec edit: only the changed node's file differs; all other files are byte-identical.
- `github_issues.py` is reachable but is OFF by default; turning it on requires an explicit `--sync-github` flag and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is also a security boundary. The writer must NEVER touch files outside `docs/backlog/` (no path-traversal, no symlink escapes).

title: 4.1 Human-approval gate (BEFORE any write)
description:
A non-optional gate that blocks any write to disk or any external tracker until a human has approved the assembled tree.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/review_gate.py` — `request_approval(tree, critic_report) -> ApprovalResult`.

**Behavior**
- Renders a human-readable preview of the tree (Markdown) and the critic report.
- Explicit prompt: 'Approve / Reject / Edit-then-Approve'. In CI / non-interactive mode, default to REJECT (never silently approve).
- Audit log: timestamp, decision, what was changed if 'Edit'.

**Validation**
- Non-interactive run (no TTY, no `--yes`) → writes are blocked; clear log entry explains why.
- Interactive run with `--yes` for the case 'we already reviewed this offline' → proceeds and logs that the human gate was bypassed by explicit flag.
- A pure-CI run (e.g. in a PR) cannot accidentally write to `docs/backlog/`.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is a security boundary, not a UX nicety. Treat it like one. Default-deny is the only safe default.

title: E4 — Phase 4: Backlog writer + human gate (Part A · agent) [~3-5 days]
description:
**Phase 4 (Part A · agent) — ~3-5 days · priority normal**

The last agent-only phase. Adds the **non-optional human gate** and an **idempotent writer** to local files. The env has no MCP/web-search, so the v1 target is local Markdown + JSON in `docs/backlog/`; GitHub Issues sync is optional.

**Why the human gate is non-optional for v1**: the spec is explicit. A planning agent that writes to a tracker without a human in the loop is a footgun. v1 keeps humans in the loop; v2 can revisit.

**Ordering note**: depends on E3 (critic + graph). Children 4.1 → 4.2 → 4.3 in sequence (gate must exist before writer; review follows writes).

title: 3.2 Build depends_on edges + compute build order
description:
Wire the `depends_on` edges from the tree (some are explicit in node fields; others are inferred from parent-child relationships and from the critic's findings) and compute a build order + critical path.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/task_graph.py` (extend, or merge with the E2 module)
- `planning-agent/src/build_order.py` — topological sort + critical-path computation.

**Validation**
- Given a tree, produces a deterministic build order (e.g. lexicographic, or by depth-first on the `id` tree — pick one and document it).
- Critical-path output: list of node ids on the longest dependency chain, with total `estimate_days`.
- A cycle in `depends_on` → raises a clear error (not a hang). `bd dep cycles` is a good cross-check.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: use Python's `graphlib.TopologicalSorter` rather than hand-rolling topo sort. Boring is good.

title: 3.1 Critic persona (bounded, 1-2 passes)
description:
Build the Critic-LLM that audits the task tree the orchestrator produced. Bounded re-planning: at most 2 re-plan passes; after that, write the open concerns into a `critic_open_questions.md` and stop.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/prompts/critic.md` — the critic persona + rubric.
- `planning-agent/src/critic.py` — `audit(tree: list[Node]) -> CriticReport`.

**Critic rubric (must check)**
- **Gaps**: anything in the spec that no node addresses (look for verbs like 'secure', 'authenticate', 'log', 'monitor' that imply cross-cutting work).
- **Ordering**: dependencies that are wrong (B depends on A but is listed before A).
- **Cross-cutting**: explicit checks for auth, CI, observability, error handling, rate-limiting — if any are missing from the tree, flag them.
- **Granularity**: any leaf over 1 day that should have been decomposed.

**Validation**
- Feed it the E2 output for the architecture spec → produces a critic report with concrete, actionable findings (not vague 'looks good').
- Run critic → orchestrator → critic a second time → either clean or new findings are minor; never a third re-plan.
- Adversarial input (a deliberately incomplete spec) → critic catches the gap in one pass.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: the critic's output should be *structured* too (a Pydantic `CriticReport`), not free-text. The writer (E4) will render it as a section in the human-gate review.

title: E3 — Phase 3: Critic pass + dependency mapping (Part A · agent) [~4-6 days]
description:
**Phase 3 (Part A · agent) — ~4-6 days · priority normal**

Add a bounded Critic-LLM that reviews the assembled task tree for gaps, wrong ordering, and missing cross-cutting work (auth, CI, observability). Plus the dependency-edge + build-order logic.

**Why the critic is bounded**: an unbounded critic will keep finding 'one more thing' and the agent will spiral. Hard cap of 1-2 re-plan passes; after that, escalate to a human.

**Ordering note**: depends on E2 (needs a finished tree to critique). Children 3.1 and 3.2 can run in parallel.

title: 2.1 Deterministic orchestrator + stop guards
description:
Implement the orchestrator loop and the three termination guards. The loop is plain Python — only the planner call itself is an LLM.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/orchestrator.py` — `run(spec: str) -> list[Node]` (in-memory; writer comes in E4).
- `planning-agent/src/task_graph.py` — Node collection, `id` generation, parent/child wiring.

**Stop guards (all three must trip before recursion halts)**
1. **Max depth 4** — refuse to recurse past depth 4 regardless of `needs_decomposition`.
2. **Granularity test** — if a node is at the leaf-eligible depth AND `estimate_days <= 1.0` AND has a clear done-condition in `description`, stop.
3. **Total node budget** — hard cap on total nodes (e.g. 200) to prevent runaway on adversarial specs.

**Logging requirement**
- Every planner call logged: depth, node id being decomposed, resulting children ids, which guard (if any) stopped the recursion.
- Log format: structured (JSON lines), not free-text, so the writer (E4) can render a clean audit trail.

**Validation**
- Run on the architecture spec → produces a multi-level tree where leaves are atomic (≤1 day) and the tree respects all three guards.
- Manually flip a leaf's `needs_decomposition` to True and re-run → guard (1) or (2) kicks in, no infinite loop.
- Hit guard (3) on a synthetic spec that asks for unlimited decomposition → stops with a clear log message.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is the *core* of the agent. Time-box it. If the loop logic isn't clean by day 2, that's the signal to redesign before going further.

title: E2 — Phase 2: Recursion loop + termination conditions (Part A · agent) [~4-6 days]
description:
**Phase 2 (Part A · agent) — ~4-6 days · priority normal**

Add a **deterministic** orchestrator (plain code, not LLM) that loops over nodes from E1, recurses into any node with `needs_decomposition=True`, and stops on **all three** termination guards.

**Why the orchestrator is plain code, not an LLM**: the loop, the guards, and the logging are not decisions — they're a state machine. Putting them in the LLM is exactly the kind of 'we'll figure it out at runtime' that creates the runaway recursion the spec explicitly warns against.

**Ordering note**: depends on E1 (needs the planner and the schema). Single-task epic; subtask is one larger piece of work.

title: 1.2 Planner persona + prompt (one-level, no recursion)
description:
Build the Planner-LLM wrapper: a prompt + a thin Python function that calls the LLM, parses JSON output into `Node`s, validates, and prints.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/prompts/planner.md` — the planner persona + instructions.
- `planning-agent/src/planner.py` — `decompose_one_level(spec: str) -> list[Node]`.

**Prompt contract (must enforce)**
- Output **structured JSON only** — an array of `Node` objects, depth 0/1.
- Hard instruction: do NOT recurse, do NOT write to disk, do NOT call any tool.
- Refuse to break the schema; emit a refusal message rather than a malformed node.

**Validation**
- Feed it the architecture spec → produces a list of clean top-level epics (one per phase 0-9 plus the bridge).
- Each epic is a valid `Node` (no `ValidationError`).
- No nested children beyond depth 1 (one-level deep only).
- An obviously-garbage spec produces a clean refusal, not a stack trace.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this phase deliberately has NO orchestrator and NO writer. Output goes to stdout. The next phase (E2) wires the loop.

title: 1.1 Define node schema (Pydantic)
description:
Define the `Node` Pydantic model — the contract every phase of the planning agent will share.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/schema.py`

**Schema fields (per spec)**
- `id: str` — stable, slugified, e.g. `E1-1.1`.
- `title: str`
- `description: str`
- `parent_id: Optional[str]` — null for epics at depth 0.
- `estimate_days: float` — must be > 0 when `needs_decomposition=False` (i.e. at leaves).
- `depends_on: list[str]` — other `id`s.
- `needs_decomposition: bool` — true when the planner wants the orchestrator to recurse.

**Validation**
- `from schema import Node; Node(id='E1-1.1', title='x', description='y', parent_id=None, estimate_days=1.0, depends_on=[], needs_decomposition=False)` succeeds.
- `Node(... estimate_days=-1 ...)` raises `ValidationError`.
- `Node(... depends_on=['nope'] ...)` is permitted (string IDs are not FK-validated at the Pydantic layer — that's the orchestrator's job).

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is the only schema in v1. Keep it strict — no optional extras, no 'we might need this later' fields. The Zen of Python applies: 'There should be one — and preferably only one — obvious way to do it.'

title: E1 — Phase 1: One-shot planner with strict schema (Part A · agent) [~3-5 days]
description:
**Phase 1 (Part A · agent) — ~3-5 days · priority normal**

The simplest version of the planning agent: a Planner-LLM that decomposes a spec **one level deep** into epics. No recursion, no orchestrator, no writer — just `prompt + LLM + parse + print`. Goal is to lock the **schema** (the contract every later phase will share) and prove the planner can produce clean top-level structure from the architecture spec.

**Why this is its own phase**: the schema is the most expensive thing to change later. Every subsequent phase reads/writes the same `Node` shape. Get it right here.

**Ordering note**: depends on E0 (need the `planning-agent/` directory). Children 1.1 and 1.2 are tightly coupled (1.2 cannot run without 1.1's schema).

title: P3-E4.1 frontend-build.yml: workflow_dispatch + astro build + wrangler deploy; Phoenix triggers via GitHub API; deploy-hook client swapped behind config
description:
## Why
- D3 fallback keeps hourly rebuilds (R1, ~720 builds/month) viable when Workers Builds quota falls short, on free GH Actions minutes (§3.2 build-minutes note). Pre-specifying it means §18 row 5 (quota exceeded mid-month) is a config flip with zero architectural change — the freshness model (states A/B/C, ConfirmBuild, /__build.json) never notices which executor built the site.

## What
- `.github/workflows/frontend-build.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` trigger; steps: checkout, install, `astro build` (with `BUILD_TOKEN` and build env), `wrangler deploy` (§12.3, §4 ".github/workflows" note).
- Phoenix side (`Immo.Edge`): deploy-trigger client behind a behaviour with two adapters — `DeployHook` (POST `DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`) and `GitHubActions` (GitHub API `workflow_dispatch` with a PAT scoped to `actions:write`). Adapter chosen by runtime config; `RebuildSite` step 4 calls the behaviour only.
- `ConfirmBuild` polling of `PUBLIC_SITE_URL/__build.json` unchanged (success when `content_snapshot_at` >= recorded; 30 min timeout → failed + alert).
- Secrets/env: GH PAT into the VPS env + §12.4 registry (adding an env var without updating the table fails review).

## Out of scope
- Changes to RebuildSite algorithm/builds table/ConfirmBuild; per-PR preview builds (existing CI path §12.3).
design:
- Workflow: on workflow_dispatch; steps checkout -> install -> astro build (BUILD_TOKEN + build env per §12.4) -> wrangler deploy (CF API token) (§12.3)
- Trigger: POST /repos/:owner/:repo/actions/workflows/frontend-build.yml/dispatches via GitHub API from Immo.Edge
- Deploy-trigger behaviour with adapters DeployHook | GitHubActions, selected by runtime config
- ConfirmBuild polling unchanged — architecture invariant (§3.2 build-minutes note)
- /__build.json emitted by the same build-info integration regardless of executor (§3.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- Phoenix-triggered workflow_dispatch runs astro build and wrangler deploy to staging successfully
- ConfirmBuild confirms the resulting deployment via /__build.json with no code changes (content_snapshot_at comparison still holds)
- Switching deploy-hook <-> GH Actions transport is config/env only; RebuildSite step 4 calls a behaviour, not a concrete client
- Workflow failure surfaces as builds row failed via ConfirmBuild 30 min timeout
- GH PAT scoped to actions:write on the repo; secret added to the §12.4 registry (registry-update rule)
notes: Spec: §3.2 build-minutes note, §12.3, §12.4, §16 P3-E4. Open decisions: D3 — only execute if P0-E2.4 quota verdict demands (quota < ~750/mo). Risk register: §18 row 5. Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: [Immo] P3-E4 — GH Actions build path (conditional, D3 fallback)
description:
## Why
- §3.2 build-minutes note: hourly rebuilds = **~720 builds/month**. If the Workers Builds quota on the chosen Cloudflare plan cannot cover that (D3 verdict from P0), R1 becomes unaffordable on the default path. The pre-specified fallback: **GitHub Actions** runs `astro build && wrangler deploy`, triggered by Phoenix via the GitHub API `workflow_dispatch` — free minutes, same architecture.
- §18 risk row 5 mitigation: "D3 verdict in P0; GH Actions fallback pre-specified" — this epic IS that fallback, so a mid-month quota surprise is a config flip, not a redesign.

## What
**CONDITIONAL: only execute if the P0-E2.4 quota verdict (D3) demands it.** Same architecture as the deploy-hook path; `ConfirmBuild` polling is unchanged.

- `.github/workflows/frontend-build.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` trigger; `astro build` + `wrangler deploy` (§12.3 frontend deploy; §4 workflows note "frontend-build.yml (D3 fallback)").
- Phoenix triggers via GitHub API `workflow_dispatch`; the deploy-hook client is swapped behind config (behaviour with two adapters) so `RebuildSite` step 4 is transport-agnostic.
- `ConfirmBuild` (P3-E1.3) keeps polling `/__build.json` exactly as before — success/timeout semantics identical.

## Out of scope
- Any change to RebuildSite algorithm, builds table, or ConfirmBuild semantics.
- Code-push CI builds (§12.3 Git-build path stays as-is for code changes).
design:
- Trigger transport: GitHub API workflow_dispatch on frontend-build.yml (§3.2 build-minutes note, D3 fallback)
- Same architecture: only step 4 of §3.2 (trigger the build) changes transport; ConfirmBuild polling unchanged
- Deploy-trigger client behind a behaviour/config: DeployHook adapter | GitHubActions adapter
- Build steps mirror CF Builds: astro build (BUILD_TOKEN) + wrangler deploy (§12.3)
acceptance_criteria:
- Executed ONLY if the P0-E2.4 quota verdict (D3) demands it; otherwise epic is closed as not-needed with the verdict referenced
- Phoenix-triggered workflow_dispatch runs astro build + wrangler deploy to staging
- ConfirmBuild confirms the deployment via /__build.json with zero changes to its code (architecture invariant)
- Switching deploy-hook <-> GH Actions is config-only; RebuildSite code untouched
notes: Spec: §3.2 build-minutes note, §12.3, §16 P3-E4. Open decisions: D3 (default = Workers Builds deploy hook; override trigger = quota < ~750/mo). Risk register: §18 row 5 (hourly builds exceed CF quota mid-month). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator.

title: P9.6 Patroni/managed-Postgres migration on scale (DATABASE_URL one-line move, §12.2)
description:
## Why
§12.2 accepts the single-box SPOF knowingly (an outage degrades freshness only — the static site keeps serving per §3.7) and pre-arranges the exit: `DATABASE_URL` is env-driven so Postgres can move off-box with a one-line change. When scale or revenue justifies HA, this executes that move.

## What
- Select the target topology (dedicated DB VPS / managed Postgres / Patroni cluster) based on the actual trigger.
- Migrate data (pgBackRest restore or logical replication), cut over via the `DATABASE_URL` change in Coolify, within a planned downtime window.
- Preserve scram-sha-256 auth and private networking; re-tune pool size and the §12.2 memory parameters for the new host.
- Re-establish backups + the restore drill (RPO ≤ 5 min) and re-point §14 alerts at the new topology.

## Out of scope
- App-tier HA / multi-VPS Phoenix (separate decision; §12.2 scopes this to the database); changing the freshness/SSR degradation model (§3.7 stays the safety net).
design:
- §12.2 escape hatch verbatim: "DATABASE_URL env-driven so Postgres can move to its own VPS later with a one-line change"
- v1 posture: single-box SPOF accepted knowingly — outage degrades freshness only; static keeps serving, SSR degrades per §3.7; revisit HA only on revenue (§12.2)
- Options: dedicated Hetzner DB VPS, managed Postgres, or Patroni for HA — choose based on the scale trigger that fired
- Co-location hardening rules carry over: never 0.0.0.0 exposure; private network or tunnel-equivalent between app and DB; localhost rule becomes private-VLAN rule
acceptance_criteria:
- Postgres moved off the app box (own VPS, managed Postgres, or Patroni cluster) with a planned, communicated downtime window
- DATABASE_URL is the only application configuration change (§12.2 promise verified)
- scram-sha-256 + private networking between app and DB preserved; Ecto pool size re-evaluated for the new latency profile
- pgBackRest (or provider-equivalent) backups + restore drill green against the new topology; RPO ≤ 5 min maintained
- §14 alerts (disk, backup failure) re-pointed at the new DB host
notes: Spec: §12.2, §3.7, §16 P9, §14. Open decisions: none pre-made (topology choice happens at trigger time; D12 backup target may be revisited). Deliberately deferred — do not schedule before launch; orchestrator wires p9e1 ← p8e4.

title: P9.5 Category-index SSR flip if product wants instant cards (D4 — config change via HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES)
description:
## Why
§3.6 accepts ≤ rebuild-interval lag on static category/city index pages (a new listing's detail page is instant via state B, but its card waits for the next build). D4's override trigger — product wants instant cards — is answered by design with a configuration flip, not code.

## What
- Set `RENDER_MODE=hybrid` (or extend the existing hybrid config) and list the category/index routes in `HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES` (§2.2, §12.4).
- Serve flipped indexes via SSR with `s-maxage=120` (§3.6).
- Verify the R4 hard rule held: no template/component edits; confirm origin load stays bounded via the `x-immo-serving` dashboard (§14).

## Out of scope
- Marking index paths dirty in KV (§3.5 deliberately excludes them — SSR-with-cache is the mechanism); flipping detail pages (they stay prerendered); /search (already an always-fresh island per §3.6).
design:
- §3.6 policy row verbatim: category/city indexes default static with ≤ interval lag; "if product wants instant: flip to SSR with s-maxage=120 via the hybrid route list — config change only"
- Mechanism (§2.2): hybrid mode — explicitly-listed routes (e.g. /search, category indexes) always SSR with short edge cache; HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES env (build store, §12.4) names them
- Index/category paths are intentionally NOT KV-marked (§3.5 path computation) — SSR-with-cache is the designed instant-cards answer, not dirty markers
- VPS origin load: bounded by the 120 s edge cache; watch the x-immo-serving ratio dashboard (§14) after the flip
acceptance_criteria:
- Category/city index routes flipped to SSR via configuration only: RENDER_MODE=hybrid + the routes listed in HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES (§2.2, §7.1) — zero component/template edits (R4 hard rule)
- Flipped index responses served with s-maxage=120 short edge cache (§3.6)
- A newly published listing’s card appears on the flipped index within the edge-cache TTL, with no rebuild
- Detail pages and other routes remain prerendered; freshness layer behavior unchanged
notes: Spec: §3.6, §2.2, §7.1, §12.4, §17 D4, §14. Open decisions: D4 (default static stands until product override). Deliberately deferred — do not schedule before launch; orchestrator wires p9e1 ← p8e4.

title: P9.4 PostGIS migration when radius/polygon search demanded (D7)
description:
## Why
v1 deliberately serves geo queries with lat/lng btree range predicates (§5.4) because bbox is all the map island needs (D7 default). §17 pre-defines the override: when radius or polygon search is demanded, migrate to PostGIS — this is that ticket.

## What
- Add the PostGIS extension and a GiST-indexed geometry on `listings` (from existing lat/lng).
- Migrate `/listings/geo` to PostGIS operators; add radius/polygon parameters per the product ask; keep the bbox max-span guard and the §6.3 GeoJSON FeatureCollection contract stable.
- Verify query plans with EXPLAIN on production-sized data; confirm the restore drill still passes with the extension in place (§12.2).

## Out of scope
- Search-island UX for drawing polygons (separate product/frontend ticket when triggered); replacing the §5.4 GIN attribute indexes (unrelated).
design:
- Current v1 design (§5.4, D7): lat/lng float columns + (lat, lng) btree pair; bbox queries are simple range predicates; PostGIS explicitly deferred
- Migration: add PostGIS, geometry column (or generated column from lat/lng), GiST index; rewrite geo queries to ST_* operators; keep response shape stable (§6.3)
- D7 override trigger (§17): radius/polygon search demanded — this issue is that migration ticket
- Mind pgBackRest/restore-drill compatibility after adding the extension (restore drill must still pass, §12.2)
acceptance_criteria:
- PostGIS extension installed; listings carry an indexed geometry (GiST) derived from lat/lng
- /listings/geo supports radius and polygon queries with index-backed plans (EXPLAIN verified) alongside the existing bbox contract
- Existing API contract unchanged for current clients: GeoJSON FeatureCollection with id, title, price, path, thumb (§6.3); bbox max-span guard retained
- Map island behavior unchanged for bbox; new search shapes exposed where product specifies
notes: Spec: §5.4, §6.3, §17 D7, §12.2 (backup/restore implications). Open decisions: D7 (default lat/lng btree stands until trigger). Deliberately deferred — do not schedule before launch; orchestrator wires p9e1 ← p8e4.

title: P9.3 /internal/freshness consistency upgrade if KV ~60 s lag bites (§3.5 documented alternative)
description:
## Why
§3.5 accepts KV eventual consistency (~60 s): an edit may serve the stale static at some edge for up to a minute. If product later demands stricter freshness (R3 tightened), the documented alternative routes the Worker's staleness check through the Phoenix API — the endpoint was built in P1-E5 precisely for this, unused by default.

## What
- Switch (or augment) the Worker entry's dirty check: call `GET /api/v1/internal/freshness?path=...` (render-tier token) with a 30 s edge cache on the lookup (§3.5).
- Keep KV available as fallback; preserve stale-beats-error behavior (§3.4/§3.7).
- Measure the origin-traffic increase on the VPS and document the trade-off + rollback.

## Out of scope
- Changing KV write paths (`MarkPathsDirty` stays as-is — markers still drive re-arm logic in `RebuildSite` §3.2); endpoint implementation (done in P1-E5 per §6.3).
design:
- Endpoint already exists from P1-E5, implemented-unused by default (§6.3): GET /internal/freshness?path= → {updated_at} or 404, render-tier bearer auth
- §3.5 alternative verbatim: Worker calls the endpoint with a 30 s edge cache — stronger consistency, more origin traffic; explicitly not in v1
- Trigger (§18 risk register): "KV eventual consistency confuses editors" — sustained editor-facing staleness complaints attributable to the ~60 s window
- Keep the KV path as fallback (stale-beats-error semantics of §3.4 unchanged)
acceptance_criteria:
- Worker staleness check consults GET /api/v1/internal/freshness?path=... (render tier) with a 30 s edge cache instead of relying solely on KV (§3.5)
- Edits become visible at all edges within ~30 s (vs the ~60 s KV eventual-consistency window)
- Origin-traffic increase measured and confirmed within VPS capacity; rollback path to pure-KV documented
- Freshness e2e scenarios (§15.4 edit/unpublish) still green after the switch
notes: Spec: §3.5, §6.3, §3.4, §15.4, §18. Open decisions: none — this IS the documented alternative, activated only on trigger. Deliberately deferred — do not schedule before launch; orchestrator wires p9e1 ← p8e4.

title: P9.2 Visitor accounts per §10.3 design note (HttpOnly cookie sessions, no JWT in localStorage)
description:
## Why
§1.3 excludes public visitor accounts (favorites/saved searches) from v1, but §10.3 reserves the design so the feature can land without compromising the static, cacheable architecture or R7's trust-path model. This implements that design note when product lifts the non-goal.

## What
- Phoenix login API endpoint that sets the session cookie `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Domain=.<domain>` (§10.3).
- Visitor-account model + endpoints (favorites, saved searches) on the public API surface with appropriate rate limits.
- Islands call `api.<domain>` with `credentials: 'include'`; Origin-header check on all state-changing requests (§10.3).
- Enforce the hard rule: no JWTs in localStorage; static pages stay anonymous/cacheable — only island calls carry the cookie.

## Out of scope
- Staff auth/RBAC (exists from P1-E1, §5.8); changes to machine trust paths 1–4 (§10.1); native apps (§1.3).
design:
- §10.3 design note verbatim: Phoenix sets HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Domain=.<domain> at login (API endpoint); islands fetch with credentials: include; Origin check on state-changing requests; no JWTs in localStorage
- Static/cacheable architecture is preserved by keeping auth entirely island-side — page HTML stays anonymous (R8 CWV + edge caching unaffected)
- Product scope from §1.3 non-goal being lifted: favorites / saved searches for public visitors (inquiry forms were the v1-only interaction)
- Builds on phx.gen.auth foundations (A8) but visitor accounts are a separate population from §5.8 staff users
acceptance_criteria:
- Login via Phoenix API endpoint sets a session cookie with exactly HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Domain=.<domain> (§10.3)
- Islands call api.<domain> with credentials: include; authenticated features (favorites/saved searches) work from static pages
- Origin-header check enforced on all state-changing requests (§10.3)
- No JWTs or tokens in localStorage/sessionStorage — hard rule (§10.3)
- Static pages remain anonymous and cacheable: HTML output does not vary on the session cookie; only island API calls carry it (§10.3)
notes: Spec: §10.3, §1.3, §10.1 (trust paths unchanged for machine tiers), §5.8. Open decisions: none (design note is pre-agreed). Deliberately deferred — do not schedule before launch; orchestrator wires p9e1 ← p8e4.

title: P9.1 Second-vertical rollout in dynamic/hybrid render mode (config + theme + content only)
description:
## Why
R4 promises the codebase is universal — the same code deployable as different verticals and render modes via configuration only — and R9 promises new verticals are data + templates + theme, not schema rewrites. The machinery (render-mode integration, view-model contract, theme tokens) exists from P2-E7; this item is the production proof on a second vertical.

## What
- Stand up a second deployment of the same code with `RENDER_MODE=dynamic` (or `hybrid` with `HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES` listing the always-SSR routes) per §2.2.
- Apply a `THEME` token override file + logo (§7.4 theme layer); set `LOCALES` for the vertical.
- Configure the vertical's `property_types` (keys, `url_segment`, `filter_config`, `schema_hints`) and load its content (R9).
- Confirm dynamic-mode operational profile: no scheduled builds needed, deploys only on code change, SSR responses edge-cached with `s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=600` (§7.1).

## Out of scope
- Multi-tenant single deployment (§1.3 non-goal — one deployment per vertical/brand); any component/template changes (forbidden by the §2.2 hard rule — if needed, that is a bug in the universality contract to fix upstream).
design:
- RENDER_MODE env flips route.prerender at build time via the astro:route:setup integration built in P2-E7 (§2.2)
- dynamic row (§2.2): no prerendering; every route SSR against the API; loaders skipped — build has no BUILD_TOKEN (§7.1); SSR responses s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=600 (§7.1)
- hybrid row (§2.2): prerender landing/category/detail; routes listed in HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES always SSR with short edge cache
- Theme layer (§7.4): design tokens in src/styles/tokens.css + per-deployment override selected by THEME env; LOCALES env as needed
- New vertical = data + templates + theme, not schema rewrites (R9): property_types rows with url_segment, filter_config, schema_hints
acceptance_criteria:
- A second deployment of the unchanged codebase serves a new vertical (e.g. land marketplace or rental site) in RENDER_MODE=dynamic or hybrid (§2.2)
- Zero component/template edits required — any PR branching template logic on RENDER_MODE or data source fails review (§2.2 hard rule)
- dynamic mode: no scheduled builds (deploy on code change only); SSR responses carry aggressive edge caching with s-maxage + stale-while-revalidate (§2.2)
- Theming achieved via THEME token override + logo + content only (§7.4); vertical content via property_types config (R9)
- One deployment = one vertical/brand (§1.3 — no multi-tenancy)
notes: Spec: §2.2, §7.1, §7.4, §16 P9, §1.3, R4/R9. Open decisions: none blocking (render modes are locked A1 design). Deliberately deferred — do not schedule before launch; orchestrator wires p9e1 ← p8e4.

title: [Immo] P9 — Post-launch backlog (conditional / deferred)
description:
## Why
§16 P9 collects the conditional / post-launch work whose triggers live in §17's open-decision override columns and §1.3's non-goals. Filing them preserves the design intent (each has a pre-arranged escape hatch in the architecture) without putting them on the launch critical path.

## What
The §16 P9 list, one child issue each:
- Second-vertical rollout in `dynamic`/`hybrid` render mode — the integrations exist from P2-E7; this is config + theme + content (§2.2).
- Visitor accounts per the §10.3 design note (HttpOnly cookie sessions, no JWT in localStorage).
- `/internal/freshness` consistency upgrade if KV ~60 s lag ever bites (§3.5 documented alternative).
- PostGIS migration when radius/polygon search is demanded (D7).
- Category-index SSR flip if product wants instant cards (D4 — config change).
- Patroni/managed-Postgres migration on scale (§12.2 one-line `DATABASE_URL` move).

**These items are deliberately deferred; do not schedule any of them before launch (P8-E4).**

## Out of scope
- Anything on the v1 launch path (P0–P8). Native mobile apps and multi-tenant single deployment remain non-goals entirely (§1.3) — they are not even in this backlog.
design:
- Triggers per §17: D4 override = product demands instant index cards; D7 override = radius/polygon search demanded; §3.5 alternative = KV ~60 s lag bites editors; §12.2 = scale/revenue justifies moving Postgres; second vertical = business decision (integrations exist from P2-E7); visitor accounts = product decision (§1.3 non-goal lifted)
- All items are config/additive by design: render-mode + theme are env-driven (§2.2, §7.4), /internal/freshness already implemented-unused (§6.3), DATABASE_URL one-line move (§12.2), HYBRID_SSR_ROUTES config flip (§3.6)
- §17 rule: implement the default unless the product owner overrides; do not block on undecided items
acceptance_criteria:
- Each backlog item is filed with its trigger condition from §17 defaults / §16 P9 (D4, D7, KV-lag, scale, second vertical, visitor accounts)
- No item is scheduled or started before P8-E4 launch completes
- When a trigger fires, the item is promoted with its spec sections re-validated against the then-current system
notes: Spec: §16 P9, §17, §10.3, §2.2, §3.5, §3.6, §5.4, §12.2. Open decisions: D4, D7 (defaults stand until override triggers fire). Cross-phase deps wired by orchestrator (p9e1 ← p8e4).

title: 9.2 (Later-stage) Recommendation ranking — NOT a launch blocker
description:
Replace the simple `recency * engagement_score` ranking from E7 with an actual recommendation model. Out of scope for v1.

**Files**
- `backend/ml/` (or Supabase Edge Functions with vector ops) — the ranker.
- `backend/supabase/functions/feed-discover/index.ts` — swap the implementation.

**Validation**
- Off-line eval against a holdout set of users: NDCG or a similar ranking metric improves over the v1 heuristic.
- A/B test against the v1 heuristic in production (feature-flagged).

**Agent**: code-puppy (or a data scientist if you become one)
**Notes**: this is explicitly out of scope for launch. Do not let it expand E7's scope. If you find yourself wanting to 'just quickly add a small model' during E7, file it here and move on.
